reviewText: xeport goal is to offer good quality earphones at a reasonable price. as far as quality and performance, the 3010-2 lies somewhere in between xeport's excellent xeport 5010-8 superbass hifi noise isolating earphones (with a free carrying case) and the not so impressive but pretty xeport 7010-0 ceramic hifi noise isolating earphones (with a free carrying case). at the time i'm writing this review the 3010-2 sells for a few dollars less than the other 2 models but i find it hard to justify buying something that's not the prettiest or be best sounding of the bunch. before enumerating the good-to-outstanding features, let me note the so-so ones: - bass is not as good as the 5010-8, maybe 'good' when compared with other makers' earphones selling for about the same price. - higher pitch notes sound good but, again, not as good as the 5010-8. - design and general looks don't even attempt to suggest 'high end'. maybe they should get a good mark for honesty :) - no controls. some earphones in this price range come with on-cord controls for volume and some have them for pause/stop/skip. xeport relies entirely on your player. not a huge deal but worth noting. now, here are the good parts: + pretty good noise isolation because they go deep down your ear canal. it's not 'noise cancellation' but the good fit successfully muffles everything else. + eartips in 3 sizes. + comfortable to wear. very little discomfort after wearing them for over one hour. + braided cord, a feature that i personally favor. + comes with a case. xeport's zippered hard, round case should keep earphones safe while not in use and adds significant value given that many earphones in this price range or even higher end come with no case or a soft pouch. my 3 stars (it's okay) mean that you aren't necessarily doing something wrong if buying one of these. you do save some money over the better xeport 5010-8 but i'd personally go with the better model. ___________________________________________ note: i'd like to disclose that i didn't actually buy these earphones myself. xeport offered to send me some of their products for review and i accepted their offer. it's possible that reviewing a free product affected my objectivity but i hope that it didn't. when granting three stars to this product i asked myself: "knowing what i know now, would i be buying this product if i wanted a not-so-high-end but good quality pair of earphones?" and the answer was 'maybe not' because there are better options out there.

i see opportunity for two improvements: iphones are not supported, though they play and charge through the fmcup, albeit with a lot of gsm radio static/feedback. i hear the verizon iphone has better results in this device (since it is not gsm). macally clearly states this isn't for iphones, so this is not one of those "they messed up" kind of things. it's just a suggestion. chances are if iphones were supported, wire shields and the like would run the price up a lot. i didn't get it for an iphone, but tried one out to see what would happen.

finally, the device in the holder feels "barely" in there. it sits high above the device and although the fitted tray hugs it at the bottom, a reckless child's reach for a cup or for the a/c control might knock it hard enough to cause damage. i'd feel better if it snuggled down deeper in there.

reviewText:
i've used many tripods over the years.  this is my favorite ball head ever.  the lever mechanism is definitely worth the few extra bucks.  a very positive attachment with a niftily designed safety latch that is simple and quick, but makes accidental movement of the lever very unlikely.  the attachment of the camera to the head is quite secure and very quick...nothing to line up so it can easily be done even in dark conditions.

the ball mechanism is smooth and remarkably easy to use.  in 10 minutes you will be completely at home with it, maybe even less time than that!  rated to hold 25 lbs, it easily manages a canon mark iii, battery grip and 70-300 lens.  i'm not a wildlife or sports photographer, so those folks will have to tell  you if a huge 600mm lens works well with it,, but i don't see a problem there either.  it is so smooth that it can work as a gimbal head.  maybe i should start shooting the snow geese since i could track them and snap picture after picture.  a moving toddler or dog will be no problem to keep in frame.  but when you get the frame you want, the camera stays still.  this is perfect when you are hiking and doing landscape work.  the composition is made quick and easy with this tool, and it is so secure that you don't get any jiggle or movement.  get the shot and move on.

the low weight (for the quality) and the great appearance make it useful in the field if combined with a good carbon tripod (i use the oben cc-2361).  the beautiful design makes it perfect in the studio...clients will note the professional gear.

though acratech suggests camera specific quick release plates, amazon mostly offers the universal plate.  that plate is easy to attach and is very secure.  i think you'll be quite satisfied with that combination.
summary: this tripod will be your favorite one

an awful adapter. it works -- when it wants to. there's frequently disconnects when all other wireless devices within the area have no issues. the adapter cannot tolerate the computer going to sleep. you will have to unplug and replug the adapter each time your machine hibernates or sleeps. it may appear to have a connection after this, but nothing will happen. at times it will connect to the wireless network but be unable to obtain an ip address. this too will require you to disconnect and reconnect the adapter.

reviewText:
i've owned two readynas products, back when they were still owned by infrant technologies.  i purchased my readynas without drives, as i was adding 3tb western digital reds at a later point in time.  the first unit i received powered on successfully, but began to shutdown on its own after just a few hours.  after getting the unit replaced, i was ready to roll! i added my drives, configured my nas for raid5, netting me just over 14tb of space.

i use my nas primarily to store tv shows and movies, and i'm able to stream them to the tv in the living room, bedroom or office.  since this model features a dual core intel cpu, i could install plex media server and stream videos and music anywhere i had an ip connection.  i regularly stream movies when we travel, and i'm very impressed by the performance.  nas units with arm processors just don't have the power to trancode movies on-the-fly, so this was the best option for me.

i highly recommend anyone looking to use plex on nas to consider the readynas pro models with intel processors.  don't bother with arm if you need to transcode - the encoders just can't use them.

reviewText:
this is a great monitor.  the color and the crispness and crazy good.  when i first plugged it in it was a little tricky.  it used some kind of stealth mode to report it was running the correct resolution, but it was not.  if you went into the menu on the monitor it showed you it was running at 1/2 the real resolution.  i had to use a different connection, my dual dvi output on my video card would not run full resolution at the correct refresh rate.

so i got it running and looking great.  amazing really.  problem is adobe illustrator cs6 does not "scale" when you adjust windows dpi.  so all my other programs adjusted their menu and toolbar sizes to the new dpi setting.  adobe illustrator cs6 would not. so my toolbars and menus were tiny.  almost illegible.  i bought the monitor to easy eye strain, and it added lots of eye strain.

so i returned the monitor and bought the 27" ultra sharp.  still a great piece, but smaller and therefore the toolbars and menus seem a little easier. because it is smaller i am able to put it closer.  if i put the 30 this close i would really have to strain to look at the edges.  for the first time in my life i downgraded to a smaller screen and a less cool technology purchase, thanks adobe.

how in the world does adobe not have this problem fixed.  are graphic artists not the folks using very large, highly dense monitors.  i love illustrator, who knows maybe they have this in their new subscription based products but i am not wiling to try those yet.

again, awesome monitor!

follow up:  it was my cord that gave me trouble using dvi on the 27" and 30".  i had a dual link card, the monitor requires dual link, but my cord was single link (see wikipedia on digital visual interface).  the screen came with the right cord, i had chosen to use my old cord to avoid having to cut tie wraps and re-route everything.
summary: great product, adobe made me return this

reviewText:
(i originally reviewed the r97 nov, 2013. this is a new review on 2/26/14 based on spending 4 months with the tablet)

i agree 100% with johnnied's review. the hardware is excellent for the money, especially the beautiful screen. the speakers are not great sounding and aren't very loud, but they're fine. the rk3188 processor is quite capable, the battery life is good.

the problem is that it comes with a terrible version of android firmware (also known as the rom). it is not optimized for the hardware/processor. out of the box (with android 4.2 that comes with it), the tablet is laggy, slow to register touch, and most frustratingly, once it's been asleep for a few hours, it often takes 5-10 minutes to fully wake up and be useable. it also completely crumbles with multi-tasking. for instance, if you're playing a game and an email comes in, the game may become un-playable.

but there's a silver lining! people have developed custom roms that optimize the hardware and make this tablet great. per johnnied's recommendation, i put the rom kasty-visture-v97hd-422-20131120-rooted4.zip on and it's a completely new machine. it's fast, smooth, and multi-tasks just fine. i haven't noticed any downside to the rom change. if you're willing (and able) to update the rom, the r97 is an amazing bargain for $200. if you just want a 10" tablet that's smooth and good out of the box, don't buy the r97--spend twice the money and get a well-known brand (e.g., samsung, nexus, etc.).

i found it quite difficult to successfully upgrade the rom, so let me offer some help. you'll need the rockchip batch tool to do this and need to put the right drivers onto your computer. the process will not work with a windows 8.1 computer (trust me, i tried everything). it works with a win 7 computer. google search kasty-visture-v97hd-422-20131120-rooted4.zip and the first result will get you both the rom and batch tool to download. once you download both, unzip them and remember the location.

the hard part for me was getting the rockchip drivers onto the computer. if you don't successfully do that, the rest won't work. try this:
1. turn your tablet off. (press and hold power button, when the tablet asks you if you want to turn off tablet, tap "yes")

2. with the r97 off, connect the usb cable. press and hold volume + button and the power button at the same time until the computer recognizes new hardware, then release all buttons.

3. a pop up question will ask you to install driver, or you can click on the un-recognized usb device icon in the system notification area to install the driver. if neither of these happen, on your computer go to control panel>device manager and look for the new hardware. right click and select install drivers. when installing the driver, select browse for driver, locate driver folder where you saved the rockchip batch tool>rockusbdriver and navagate to the proper driver for your computer. check the box "include subfolders", click "continue".

4. allow the computer to install the driver.

once you install the drivers, if you need a guide as to how to do the rest of the process, search for "rockchip batch tool installation guide."

good luck!
summary: only good if you change the rom

the hard part for me was getting the rockchip drivers onto the computer. if you don't successfully do that, the rest won't work. try this:
1. turn your tablet off. (press and hold power button, when the tablet asks you if you want to turn off tablet, tap "yes")

2. with the r97 off, connect the usb cable. press and hold volume + button and the power button at the same time until the computer recognizes new hardware, then release all buttons.

3. a pop up question will ask you to install driver, or you can click on the un-recognized usb device icon in the system notification area to install the driver. if neither of these happen, on your computer go to control panel>device manager and look for the new hardware. right click and select install drivers. when installing the driver, select browse for driver, locate driver folder where you saved the rockchip batch tool>rockusbdriver and navagate to the proper driver for your computer. check the box "include subfolders", click "continue".

4. allow the computer to install the driver.

once you install the drivers, if you need a guide as to how to do the rest of the process, search for "rockchip batch tool installation guide."

good luck! only good if you change the rom

reviewText:
i guess i'm having trouble really getting behind the concept of a chromebook.  they're basically a browser only laptop, combining the functionality of a basic tablet (but without touchscreen features) into the "keyboard and touchpad" aesthetic of a laptop.  do you only want to browse the web, stream a show on netflix, check your email and maybe write something in google docs but don't want to have to touch the screen?  then this is all you'd need and it's at a decent price point, all things considered.  this works fast and is easy to use (though the encouraged installment of the game "spelunky" didn't work on mine, darn character won't jump), but if i only want to hop on youtube or check my gmail i can do that on my phone or ipad.  if i need the greater functionality of a computer, i have a laptop with windows 10 that is way more versatile.  granted, both those devices cost me a bit more than $280 but they also do a lot more.

i guess know what you're getting into with one of these.  they're not a full laptop, they're only part of a tablet, but this asus model is well built and inexpensive so if you *just* need a device with a keyboard for basic internet stuff they're fine.  also, lots of kids need something like this for school these days so there's that too i guess.  i don't know.  it seems to occupy a no-man's land between tablet and laptop that really only does half of what you'd use either of those devices for.  that's why i'm left feeling ambivalent about the whole concept.  in the end, it's okay but i may not use this as much as i thought i would.
summary: if you need a chromebook this is nice and low price... but i'm still trying to figure out who needs a chromebook.

reviewText:
i ordered a few of these to test through my company.  i gave it 3 stars as it has a few quirks.

pros -
ergonomic.  it's a very comfy keyboard to use, i like it better than the wired ergonomic keyboard from ms.

function key switch is a great idea.  i never can remember on other keyboards which way i have the function keys toggled until i hit one and go "woops, i wanted f5 to refresh my screen not open search".  now i can visibly see which function on the function keys are active.

it's quiet!!  with the wired ergo keyboard from ms (and some of the logitech models) i can hear my co-workers in their cubicles around me typing away and the spacebar going clack clack clack.  with these sculpt keyboards, unless they're really pounding on the keys, i can't hear them at all.

it's compact, i like that it's smaller, i have more room on my desk now.

soft keys - they touch of the keys are soft, takes less pressure than the wired ergo keyboard to use.

cons -
it's wireless, and unlike some of the logitech keyboards i've tested there can be a delay with this ms keyboard.  if the keyboard hasn't been used for a while and i go to open say ms word to type, sometimes it will miss the first few letters until the keyboard "wakes up", but then it will perform normally.

mouse - i totally hate the mouse.  movement is smooth and precise, but the feel of the mouse in my hand i just plain don't like.  it's too round and just feels weird, i don't know how else to explain it. however, it does make a cool looking paperweight.  so there's a good thing about it i guess.

10 key pad "bugs" - i mentioned i like that i can move the 10 key pad around and save desk space.  they 10 key pad lag is even worse than the occasional keyboard lag i described above.  i have tried moving it to different positions on my desk, so it's been closer or farther to the usb receiver, but that didn't change anything.  i have to type a few numbers in the the 10 key then wait, and if i'm lucky i'll get 1 of those numbers displayed on the screen, then type a few more and use backspace to erase everything as it's all messed up, then it will start working and i can punch in the number i need.  but as i use the 10 key pad it will skip a number here or there.  typically we use 6 digit project numbers here, and 5 digit barcode numbers. i'll finally get a 6 digit number typed in and maybe 3 or 4 sets later it will skip one of the numbers i type in from the set, so i'll get like 13589 instead of 133589.  it's almost to the point of being unusable.  just typing those 2 sets of number here in this review was a chore.  i had to type the 5 twice to get it to display in the first set, and the 3's 5 or 6 times to get the 33 to show in the second set.

what i do like about the 10 key pad (maybe the only thing, other than it being not attached, but that's also it's downfall) is the backspace key on the pad itself.  in the week and half i've been using this keyboard i'm surprised you can read the "backspace" letters on the key.
summary: needs "bugs" fixed to be worth this price, but not a bad keyboard.

a few positive aspects of the nas would be that it is extremely easy to setup and configure for a simple file share. the bays are hot-swappable, and it has a pair of usb 3.0 ports.

it works well enough - no complaints there.  it is replacing a dead smc router which gave me about 4 years of good service.  i'm using both wireless (3) and wired (3) connections and everything is working fine.

i did not like the set up process.  i installed the set up application on my computer (gritting my teeth because i hate to add "needless applications") hoping it would make the set up go faster.  however, although there were nice (if useless) little graphics showing you how to hook things up, the router was never able to detect the internet through my cable modem.  i was getting pretty frustrated trying to get it working until i noticed that i did have internet access, the router was just misdiagnosing the connection for some reason.  and i was getting constant warnings from the set up app about my lack of internet connection.  so i uninstalled the app and all is working well now.

i also did not like how the set up app interfaced with the router.  i found it much easier to just go to the router directly (192.168.1.1) and set things the way i like them - way faster and more flexible.  so overall it is probably a pretty good product, especially if you trash the set up app and just do it yourself.

reviewText: i bought this tripod back when it was branded as ravelli, actually... the exact purchase page i used, is now an updated version of this item still branded as ravelli ravelli apgl5 professional 65" ball head camera video photo tripod with quick release plate and carry bag so it would appear that amazon asked the maker to brand this one for them, and the maker had to do a few updates/changes so their version and scale down amazon's version so there wouldn't be confusion between the two. (more on this later) in any case, i've had the original iteration of this tripod for a few years and i still think it's the best value out there. i have everything from ultra portable lightweight tripods, to heavy video tripods, and i still find use for this one right in between. here's the breakdown: -reasonably well made -feels sturdy/secure, mostly metal -legs click to lower positions for low angle -ballhead locks in tight, loosens properly -quick release plate slides a little forward to get balance right. -hook for hanging dead weight so overall, it's not a hunk of junk, and it's not a top end piece of kit. what it is, is an excellent value. i originally bought it just for the ballhead, because buying one separately was basically just as much as this package. i never thought i'd actually use the legs as much as i do, but they work!. the changes i noted between my original and what's now branded as amazonbasics, are that the ballhead's hard lines have been rounded out, and they removed 1 section of legs, mine has 3, this has 2. the updated version of the ravelli branded one also now has a removable leg to turn into a monopod, as well as super stylish blue accents. if i were to pick between the two, i would spend the extra 12 bucks for the ravelli linked above. regardless of which you choose, they are built on the same core, i could nitpick that i prefer fliplocks over these twist locks, and that opening closing the twist locks isn't buttery smooth, nor is the ballhead as perfectly rock steady. but all in all for 40 bucks (or 52), i have no complaints.
summary: still the best deal out there, have been using for 2 years

i was and still am a diehard xbox 360 fan. over the course of the 360 generation i bought 5 of them and currently still have 2 hooked up in my house. when microsoft announced he xbox one, i immediately pre-ordered it.

my first impressions of the console where, "eh, it's okay". there were definitely pieces of the os that were rough around the edges. the feb. and march updates have definitely smoothed some of those edges and added some additional functionality. however, i still would not call it a good console. a good console is something that i would recommend to everyone, and right now the xbox one is not that, at least in my experience. for me, the voice recognition is about 50% hit and miss and moving around the system without voice commands is still clumsy. you can tell this system was always designed with kinect in mind. when the voice recognition works it really feels like the future, but when it doesn't i feel like an idiot yelling at my tv over and over. imagine how frustrating it would be if the touch screen on your smart phone only worked 50% of the time.

after about 5 months of ownership my opinion of it has gone from "eh, it's okay" to "ugh, i should have saved my money". for now, mine is going back in the box to sell to someone else that wants to give it a shot. a year from now, this may be an amazing system, but for right now, i'll stick with my 360.
summary: it wants to be a good console, but it's still not there yet.

reviewText:
i bought this filter for my 70-200mm f/2.8 lens which is very sharp, so i wanted something that would not degrade image quality or induce ghosting/flare.  when i opened the package and took out the filter the first thing i did was held it up to my desk lamp to look for flaws.  what i found was that the entire filter looked like it had a dull white film over it (almost like severe water spotting or something).  i cleaned it with lens cleaner, then a micro fiber cloth, then a lens pen, then more lens cleaner, and still after all that you could see faint white spots/haze on the filter.  no matter what i did they wouldn't come off.  i took some test shots with and without the filter on and i didn't notice any difference in quality, but it still bothers me.

i'll give it an extra star because it did seem durable and the film didn't appear to impact image quality, but i think for the price that you pay for this filter you should be able to expect it not to be cloudy.

edit 08-22-2011

it was continually nagging at me that i spent good money on a "pro" filter that looked dirty all the time whether it noticeably impacted image quality or not.  i certainly can't see the white haze/spots being good for my photographs.  i was considering exchanging the filter, but amazon said that i could only return it for a refund, so they helped make up my mind.  after this experience and so many people (including professional review sites) claiming that the hoya filters are hard to clean i mailed this back for a refund and ordered a b+w mrc filter.  it was $20-$30 more, but i am putting it on a $1,400 lens, so the added cost is immaterial if the b+w is as good as everyone says.
summary: not sure if this is normal or not, but...

over the past month i have tried 3 different elite screens manual projection screens (135", 120", 106").

good:

problems:

summary:
1. manufacturer quality control is terrible.

2. amazon's excellent return policy is the only reason i continue to order replacements.  i'm hoping that i will get a good one eventually.

pros:
1.) very cool looking hub.

2.) no overheats, no matter how many devices of different types are doing transfers.  i have done as much as 5 usb thumbdrives  full transfers at once before.

cons:

3.) even when running at usb 2.0 speed, it cannot match regular usb 2.0 data transfer speed of you plugging a device directly into the motherboard ports.

4.) for some reason western digital mybook storage devices really struggle with this hub.  it maybe just my storage device?

cons:

*the led behind the power button malfunctioned after a day of use, but nzxt said they'd send me a new part in the mail.  fairly hassle free but it's taking longer than i'd like.

other thoughts:
i'm going to purchase a separate fan controller and see if i get some better performance out of it and wait for nzxt to send me a replacement led.

reviewText:
this is a nifty little device that adds some new dimensions to your home automation system. it allows you to set notifications and triggers based on a variety of environmental factors including temperature, humidity, light, sound and motion. i do not use apple's homekit, so i cannot evaluate that aspect of the device. the device was easy to setup...literally just plug it in, download the app and connect to the device...that's it. the application will ask you to register an account if you don't already have an ihome account, but it's very basic...name, email address and password. then the application will need a code number to connect to the device, this code is printed on a lable on the device and is printed inside the small manual that comes with it(which is nice because it allowed me to go place the device and then set it up from another room using the code in the manual).

once setup the app will show you the environment variables the device is measuring. you can adjust sensitivity of each of the sensors to your liking. you can then setup 'rules' to activate notifications and/or actions based on sensor input. this worked great together with my ihome wifi connected outlet adapters. i did run into some issues with the application though. for example, i attempted to setup a rule to notify me of motion detected between the hours of 2 am and 5 am. however, the toggle to "limit this rule to a time period" doesn't seem to work. i'll set it up, it looks right, but i'm constantly getting notifications all times of the day or night. when i go back to look at it again the toggle will be 'off'. i've tried multiple times to get this to work right without success. perhaps it's just my phone or installation, no way for me to know.

overall i think this is a great device to add some intelligent capabilities to your home automation.

i got this camera as a gift this christmas to replace my old fuji camera. before i ask my friend to purchase it, i did tons of research, because what i concerned most is 1st picture quality; 2nd, appearance; 3rd, overall size. at first, i planned to go for the canon sd450, however after i read many compliments from magazines, websites and consumers' reviews toward this panasonic lumix fx9, i decided to give this lumix a try.

on the day i received it, i first took several people portraits in the bright room, the pictures were nice. then in the night, i took it out for testing the night shoot. the night shot picture was not that good, too dark and tons of noise, until i used 60sec exposure, the picture turn out to be acceptable.

this week i took it to the la autoshow, which all the picture were indoor shoot. unfortunately, there was no indoor mode on this camera. i tried to use auto mode with auto flash, the pictures were totally disaster, too much noise with red blurs. after i turned off the flash, it seemed the picture is much improved. however, after i downloaded them into my computer, i find out the picture quality cannot even compare with my old fuji. be honest, the objects in the well lighten condition appear wonderful in the picture, e.g. the cars under spot lights, or the people under the sun light. on the other hand, all the pictures took in low light condition, the noise is just too much with tons red blurs.

in addition, lumix claims that it has imagine stabilizer, however, some of my pictures were still shaken and unclear (of course i hold the camera with one hand, but that is exactly the way how stabilizer shall work). and also, this camera is not as small as it looks in advertisment, it is still thicker than sd450 or t7, even bigger than most of today's cellphones.

at last, all i can say is although this is a fashionable look  camera, i lost my confidence with lumix brand, as it does not deliver what it promised in the advertisement, the imagine stabilizer does not work very well at all time, the indoor or low light picture quality is disaster with too much noise and red blur. now i am planning to get another really slim camera, because if all the small cameras do not perform well in low light condition, then i shall go for a really small one(sony or casio) which i can put in my jeans pocket, rather than this lumix one (nearly twice size as t7).
summary: a fashionable good looking camera, but the low light picture quality is too poor!

reviewText:
i got 2 of these units and tried to install them as an alternative to wiring a 200-foot ethernet cable from one end of my house to another.  i connected one unit to my verizon fios router and another to one of my cable set-top boxes in a bedroom.  the installation failed -- i could not get my apple airport express to see the router (there was a working ethernet connection between the apple device and the router, so my goal was just to use the moca adapters to replace the ugly ethernet cable strung from one end of my house to the other).

so, i tried to fix it.  the first thing i found out was that there was no documentation on this particular model.  using google to search the entire web, all i found were articles on the previous model of netgear moca adapter, which does not look like the units i got.  i looked at various reviews and articles on moca, but found nothing helpful.

worse, my entire verizon fios internet and tv setup suddenly failed.  while talking to the verizon tech support, i found out that they use moca for their routers and cable boxes.  the verizon tech support said that the moca signal was weak -- perhaps a side-effect of the attempt to install the netgear moca devices.  long story short, i had to disconnect the netgear devices or risk paying a hefty fee for verizon to send a technician over to fix our setup.  and, i had to be thankful to verizon for remotely fixing the problem caused by the attempt to install the netgear moca devices.

maybe the problem was not with the netgear moca devices.  but, with no documentation or help available at all from netgear, there was no way i could get it working.
summary: didn't work in my house, and no help

reviewText:
i like the old school analog tuner, which is easy to use and pulls in stations really well.  the audio quality would be great, except it has waaay to much bass.  we have ours on the kitchen counter, and even at moderate volume, the junk on the counter resonates when somebody is just talking on the radio.  a great radio should make it sound like people on the radio in the same room as you, not speaking over a pa system at the bottom of a well.

in fact, the bass was so objectionable, it was almost unlistenable.  i took a piece of packing tape and put it over the resonance port in the back, which took enough of the edge of the bass to make it marginally acceptable.  the only reason i kept this was that it's tuner is so good. i'd avoid this model, or any similar sangean model unless it had a tone control.

update: my wife found the bass so objectionable, she went out and bought a cheap clock radio to replace it.  to see if the radio could be salvaged, i opened up the box.  aside from the compact transformer based power supply, the radio is contained on two circuit boards, one in front containing mostly radio stuff, one in back containing mostly power amp stuff and back connectors.  amplification duties are handled by a single, unmarked ic in a heatsinked, single inline package. this is possibly a tda1010 or similar, which is mainly targeted at the car audio market.

there are two issues, i think, that cause the objectionable "boom" sound.  the first is the speaker, which is a rather massive 3.5" unit similar to those used in car audio.  replacing this with a different unit might help, either a cheap unit with less bass capability, or a more expensive one with an aftermarket crossover.

the second issue is the cabinet, and some people might find this important for different reasons.  the cabinet is not "wood" except by the most liberal definition of the word.  it is a wood resin composite -- something like bakelite.  there's nothing intrinsically wrong with this, but the material is extremely dense and the cabinet is definitely resonating.  theoretically covering the resonsance port would make this worse, but it seems move the boom to a less objectionable frequency.  it might be possible to add weight to the case to shift the resonance lower.

in any case, this case is certainly not "walnut", it is wrapped in tough synthetic sheeting with walnut grain printed onto it.  she sheet is actually overlapped on the bottom of the cabinet, and if you actually look at the "wood grain" you see it twists around the corners in ways that wouldn't happen on a real wood cabinet.

that said, the fact that this is not actually wood isn't necessarily a problem, it's a high quality plastic cabinet.  in this case it seems poorly matched to the speaker, which is perhaps too much speaker for a cabinet this small.  the more i think about this, the more i am convinced the best course of action would be to replace the speaker with a more appropriate one.  it's not that the speaker is bad, far from it.  it's just too much for this cabinet.

second update: i soldered in a 220 microfarad non-polarized capacitor in series with the speaker.  given that the speaker is 4 ohms, this should result in a low pass filter with a loss of 3db at 180hz, 9db at 90hz, 15db at 45hz etc.  the objectionable "boom" is actually subsonic; you can feel it in other parts of the house.  although the radio is still bass heavy, the boom seems somewhat attenuated.  i've ordered a 7.0 mh inductor from parts express using amazon.  putting this in parallel with the speaker should net no noticeable reduction above 200hz, 3db at around 130 hz, and 12db/octave thereafter, yielding a 15db reduction at 64hz, a more dramatic reduction of subsonic boom.
summary: great tuner, way too much bass

update: my wife found the bass so objectionable, she went out and bought a cheap clock radio to replace it.  to see if the radio could be salvaged, i opened up the box.  aside from the compact transformer based power supply, the radio is contained on two circuit boards, one in front containing mostly radio stuff, one in back containing mostly power amp stuff and back connectors.  amplification duties are handled by a single, unmarked ic in a heatsinked, single inline package. this is possibly a tda1010 or similar, which is mainly targeted at the car audio market.

there are two issues, i think, that cause the objectionable "boom" sound.  the first is the speaker, which is a rather massive 3.5" unit similar to those used in car audio.  replacing this with a different unit might help, either a cheap unit with less bass capability, or a more expensive one with an aftermarket crossover.

the second issue is the cabinet, and some people might find this important for different reasons.  the cabinet is not "wood" except by the most liberal definition of the word.  it is a wood resin composite -- something like bakelite.  there's nothing intrinsically wrong with this, but the material is extremely dense and the cabinet is definitely resonating.  theoretically covering the resonsance port would make this worse, but it seems move the boom to a less objectionable frequency.  it might be possible to add weight to the case to shift the resonance lower.

in any case, this case is certainly not "walnut", it is wrapped in tough synthetic sheeting with walnut grain printed onto it.  she sheet is actually overlapped on the bottom of the cabinet, and if you actually look at the "wood grain" you see it twists around the corners in ways that wouldn't happen on a real wood cabinet.

that said, the fact that this is not actually wood isn't necessarily a problem, it's a high quality plastic cabinet.  in this case it seems poorly matched to the speaker, which is perhaps too much speaker for a cabinet this small.  the more i think about this, the more i am convinced the best course of action would be to replace the speaker with a more appropriate one.  it's not that the speaker is bad, far from it.  it's just too much for this cabinet.

second update: i soldered in a 220 microfarad non-polarized capacitor in series with the speaker.  given that the speaker is 4 ohms, this should result in a low pass filter with a loss of 3db at 180hz, 9db at 90hz, 15db at 45hz etc.  the objectionable "boom" is actually subsonic; you can feel it in other parts of the house.  although the radio is still bass heavy, the boom seems somewhat attenuated.  i've ordered a 7.0 mh inductor from parts express using amazon.  putting this in parallel with the speaker should net no noticeable reduction above 200hz, 3db at around 130 hz, and 12db/octave thereafter, yielding a 15db reduction at 64hz, a more dramatic reduction of subsonic boom. great tuner, way too much bass

reviewText:
these were an upgrade from a very pathetic cheap set of headphones i was using to listen to music on my first generation ipod with.

i didn't know that the other headphones were so pathetic until i plugged these in.

i immediately noticed the "huge difference" in the richness of the bass in the songs i was listening to and the crystal-clear fidelity coming through these things.

i won't ever give these up and go back to the ones i was using without dying first!

unfortunately, i find the 10 feet of cable provided to be "too much" and i am forced to keep all but 3 or 4 feet of it "bundled up" (using a garbage bag tie) into an awkward "knot" that is a little bit too heavy and it frequently gets in the way.

however, i am forced to admit that the long cable does have a certain advantage in that i can plug the thing into my stereo or my television and listen from across the room as i lay in bed.

the leatherette ear pads (replaceable) are very comfortable and they fit my average-size ears perfectly; but i get the feeling that someone with rather large ears could possibly encounter difficulties wearing them.

also, the fact that these are not adjustable with respect to head size might give someone who has an extra large mellon on his shoulders some trouble as well in that these might squeeze just "a little too tightly". a solution to that might be to very gingerly stretch the headphones open very wide over and over, not to the point that they would break or damage the plastic, but the stretching just might alleviate their default tension.

conclusion:

this is one of the best things that i have spent money on in the longest time.

i recommend these as a great investment!
summary: absolutely wonderful sound coming through these!

reviewText:
pros: good construction, nice user interface, simple setup.
cons:  it basically doesn't work.
i set up two users, and 5 shared folders with a variety of protocols and rights.
everything came up fine, and i started moving data to it.  later in the day, i could not browse the drive on the network.  using the discovery tool i could get to the drive, and map the shares to logical volumes, but cifs just would not see the drives.
the next morning it was back, and i thought everything was fine.  i went to the drive control interface to set up more shares, and found the permissions were all screwed up.  i was puzzled how i could have screwed them up so badly, but it would explain why i couldn't browse them on the lan.
as i was readjusting permissions, i saw that changing permissions on some volumes would delete permissions on other volumes...okay, that's bad.  i emailed seagate, and 24 hours later they recommended reinstalling the latest firmware and a reset.  done.  no improvement.
so i exchanged the drive with another.
no improvement.
it isn't a win7 problem, when it isn't working it also fails on my networked tv, my sonos system, my mac, win xp machines and 3 win7 boxes.
it isn't my network, i have other cifs file servers that work fine.  the seagate works fine intermittently, then it doesn't.
it is the seagate nas.  i decided to return the drive, so i needed to delete the data on it.  i went to the ui to do that, and then it showed there are no users at all (although the non-existent users still have permissions on the shared folders)

i returned the drive for good.

i would recommend not buying this.
summary: i could not get this working properly on my home lan. (windows, linux, mac)

reviewText:
pros: asus really knows how to manufacture quality hardware. they have done it well here (i hope so! for a $400 mobo). the moment you open the package, it screams of quality. oc panel is also very high quality. lcd on oc panel is wicked.

cons: the issue i have with asus motherboards is really not with the hardware.

first the bios:
- lets be honest here, asus is lagging in terms of their bios uefi interface. it feels dated. look at the newest gigabyte uefi (albeit with some mouse lag), evga and msi. they are all very well organized and provide as much information as they can display on the screen. asus has large fonts, lengthy scrolling in the "extreme tweaker" menu and tons of non-intuitive ui elements. for example, we have buttons that look like you can press them, but they dont. text input is not intuitive...i often ask myself, is it really greyed out or i can type something here? i am indeed, nitpicking but i am going to be spending a lot of time overclocking and these things bug me.

- ai suite 3: this is good if you are a casual overclocker, but i prefer old school bios overclocking. ai suite overrides everything the moment you install it. it conflicts with the bios settings. ok, i can uninstall it, right? no. this software leeches on your os like a...well, a leech. you have to go to "task scheduler" and turn off the asus com management & hs com management to get rid of this software.

- oc pane: cool hardware. very gimmicky and something that i just look at and say "oh yeah...thats my $400". i couldn't do much with it and there is no user manual provided with the board for the oc panel. the connector is the worst part of the oc panel. you have to keep it connected to the motherboard with a sloppy connector that comes off easily and a cable that is 2 feet long. the connector is similar to a front-panel connector on the motherboard. there is no "lock" or "snap". so, you constantly worry about the cable coming loose. i wanna put the oc panel on my desk, but guess what? the cable is too short. i have to sit on the floor and use it.

other thoughts: i returned it and going to get an msi board.
summary: great mobo hardware, gimmicky oc panel, terrible software, horrendous service

- lets be honest here, asus is lagging in terms of their bios uefi interface. it feels dated. look at the newest gigabyte uefi (albeit with some mouse lag), evga and msi. they are all very well organized and provide as much information as they can display on the screen. asus has large fonts, lengthy scrolling in the "extreme tweaker" menu and tons of non-intuitive ui elements. for example, we have buttons that look like you can press them, but they dont. text input is not intuitive...i often ask myself, is it really greyed out or i can type something here? i am indeed, nitpicking but i am going to be spending a lot of time overclocking and these things bug me.

other thoughts: i returned it and going to get an msi board. great mobo hardware, gimmicky oc panel, terrible software, horrendous service

i bought this to revive an old upc ups we have in the chemistry department.  while this cable has an rj50 male connector on one end and a standard usb connector on the other, the cable i received was not an apc 9827 connector according to many pinout sites.  when i plugged it into my bx1500lcd, i got a usb error -- the device was not recognized, and the device manager reported a faulty usb device.  the "standard" poinouts for an apc 9827 are (rj50 -> usb): 1 -> 1, 4 -> shield, 7 -> 4, 9 -> 2, 10 -> 3.  the cable i received was: 1 -> 1, 4 -> 4, 7 -> shield, 9 -> 3, 10 -> 2.

while this cable was essentially useless as is, i was able to cut it and reconnect the lines using the correct pinouts.  now it works fine, but considering that it took about 1/2 hour to identify the problem and correct it, the total cost was way more than $10 if you include my time.  would not recommend.

reviewText:
people complain about the live reception, and while i would like live reception, i'm willing to give that up for what this device offers. however this device fails on basic design levels... i'm highly disapointed.

the designers spent so much time on bells and whistles, they obviously forgot what people really want.  it's not about the flashy design, or a color display, it's about usability.

however, before i bash the unit, i'll tell you what i like about it:

likes:

- i like the integration as an mp3 player.  i can store my favorite songs and cd's.  depending on my mood, i have the flexibility to listen to what i want, when i want.

- love button is a nice feature.. however you can't use it on scheduled programs. you have to be live, or listening to "my sirius channels" while in the dock to use it.  prerecorded programming is the same as on the xm2go.

- sirius programming... i generally prefer it to xm

- dock mount has a flexible mount so that it will fit curved interiors and dashboards.  you can put the unit where you want it.

- ability to mix/match sirius and personal collection into playlists

- i love the "my sirius channels" function. it records even when you're using the mp3 player. however, as a drawback, it only records when you're on one of your three most used channels..  and it has to be on to record.  it only records what it's tuned to..  being that it only comes with a car dock, if you have a 40 minute commute, when you get to work, you'll have the same 40 minutes of programming you just listed to!

now, my dislikes.

- no presets:  yes, the amazon description says that it provides for up to 30 "one touch" presets.  not true! presets are like a favorite channel lists.. you can set up to thirty channels to "browse" through.  you have to use that bulky knob(or the buttons on the remote, which i prefer) to browse through your 30 favorites one at a time.  this is like having a sportster and skipping all the channels you don't like, then browsing through them. in short, there are no presets on this device. i had hoped you could use the numbers on the remote as one touch presets, but this is not the case.

- to get to your presets, you have to hit the magnifying glass button three times.  your system does not remember this, you must do this each time you turn it on, so the "skip channels" actually works better for me.  just a plain horrible design, even the starmates offer this sort of functionality! just horrible!

- no "multiple line" list of what's playing - another feature i love on the sportster and xm2go units is the ability to list your channels to see what artist/song is on 6 at a time by presets or genre.  this is how i use a sattelite radio, i list all my favorites on the screen at once(well, you do have to scroll down to see 7-10) and select from there.  take this away, and it takes away a lot of the functional fun of sat radio.

- knob is a pain to use, and feels cheap.  the heave click feel when rotating slows down tuning(not fast like on the sportster). and why not use this thing like a joystick?  no, you have to rotate the knob to make menu selections.  i can get around this by using the remote control, which i use the knob design is so poorly used.  the whole unit is not very intuitive.

- why have talking navigation? i care more about what's playing than what channel i'm on. if i had presets, i wouldn't need to look to know where i was... and by the time it tells you, you've already seen/heard that the song is one you like or not.  it gets in the way.  i'd rather have cut this functionality and added something useful(presets? live reception?)

- color display:  looks nice.. but why?  at this time you can't show video, sure you can customize your startups or backgrounds.  the negatives are big.. it eats battery live, and it has to shut itself off to conserve powere. a b&w lcd could be on all the time.  and it's all i want or need.  an expensive and useless gadget. spleaking of conserving power:

- battery life sucks

- lack of ability to "love" a song from the my sirius channels option when out of the dock.  when i hear something i like, i have to dock the unit and find it again to save it.

- the unit will lock up at times.. mine hasn't been as bad as some others, but often when "undocked" the system won't shut down.  i have to reseat the battery to get it to shutdown at times.  if i don't do this, the battery will drain before i'm ready to use it.

- i have to say it... i knew it wasn't there, but everyone wants live reception. where i work, i have a very strong sirius repeater. i could listen to it at work.. live.  i've used an xm2go at the same location, and it works great with a weaker signal.  to claim as sirius does that this it's not what consumers want is crazy talk.  the idea that they wouldn't have such a unit available with howard went online was a poor decision, and will end up hurting them.  they are offering internet streaming, but this is often against internet use policies.

all this being said, though i'm firm on my 2 stars, i'm considering living with it for the ipod functionality. however, i'm also considering just using a sportster and getting an ipod for less money.  i've very disapointed in sirius, they just don't get it. xm had a better feel for what people are looking for in hardware and it's a shame because sirius has a better idea of what programming people want.

purchase with care!

reviewText: i love the power saving feature of this surge protector. it leaves the little "standby" light on all the time on my tv, which is plugged into the "master" outlet. this is the only vampire power that i am wasting now. all of my gaming systems and other connected components only turn on when the tv is on, so i am saving a lot of power. it also has an on/off switch if you want to completely cut power to everything, and it has nice indicator lights to show you if the outlet is grounded and if your devices are being protected. my one complaint is that the configuration of the outlets makes it hard to use all of the outlets available. i also might be willing to sacrifice some of the "always on" outlets for more power-saving outlets. that being said, i doubt that any surge protector can anticipate and satisfy the needs of every user. i have never had one that perfectly fits my needs. there are too many oddly shaped plugs that take up too much room on a surge protector. and it is hard to anticipate how many "always-on" vs power-saving outlets people will want.
summary: pays for itself and works great. full of features and high quality.

reviewText:
i have used the sto-fen onni-bounce with my canon 580ex ii flash and it fits perfectly. note that this is for the 580ex and not for the 430ex which is somewhat smaller. the diffuser is easy to slip on, is snug and will stay on tight unless it's pulled off. no need for tape or sticky velcro pads. the diffuser merges into the form of your flash.

the sto-fen diffuses your flash's light so you get a softer and more spread-out look to your flash. no more "deer in the headlight" look. this has a more "natural soft light" look. it can be used indoors or out. i highly recommend it for indoor use, because you'll want a soft flash with it being the only light source, and the omni-bounce spreads out the light so you are better able to light up the scene and room. this diffuser works fine, works best for individual portraits or rather close shots.

i keep it in my canon bag. it's light weight and is great in a "pinch." installs in seconds! great product! can't beat the price.

let's face it, the puny 128 mb players are expensive and worthless. that is why we are moving up to the bigger leagues. well there has been big competitors trying to run the 20 gb market. dell has one, rio has a nice smaller one than ipod, neuros, archos, and **creative**. now why did i stat creative? first i will explain why i gave the ipod 2 stars.
first off, i have two 20 gb mp3 players. i have a creative labs nomad jukebox 3 (same thing as the zen) and a 20 gb ipod.
good:
setup was simple and transferring files to the ipod was fast. it comes with a nice docking station and yes it is small.
bad:
let me uncover the truth about the ipod that no one knows about and that people never will say because they are now stuck with the pod like me. apple will tell you i believe when you open the box that the pod is meant for your computer only. that means you can't go over to a friend's house and copy your friends music. ok well that isn't legal, but no matter what there are people who want to do that everyone knows that will happen, so what move on. so you are limited to only your pc. now here is the tricky thing that no one even think of. take my computer for example. i had the virus that spreaded across the net and i like to reformat my drive every year to give it that nice fresh start. ****warning**** if you reformat a drive or actually try to install ipod on another computer, every single thing will be erased!!!! that is what happened to my ipod. see when you reformat a drive, you have to install the software over again because everything is erased off the computer. so when you reinstall it on your pc or a friend's pc, the ipod does not like when you try to copy so the software has a reset in it and will wipe out everything you have. i have 2,000 songs and 4 months of work (because i have other work to deal with) gone down the drain as if i never touched the d*** pod. secondly, unless there is some way to change the settings, every cd burned, ipod makes a copy of each song in the library making you have to erase each copy which becomes extremely annoying because it makes a copy of it on your ipod which is so stupid. unlike the creative, you can't change anything directly from the device, only on the computer which isn't good either.
now back to the creative. i have the jukebox 3 which is the same exact thing as the zen. zen has a different style so that is why it is called that. to prove it is the same, check the prices at comp usa and other stores. they still sell my at the same price as the zen. plus all the firmware and accessories are made for both devices. the creative allows you to use it on anyone's computer and it is compatible with everything. apple is known for having there products strictly work for them. the drastic windows change didn't change that much. apple you are limited to there firewire and usb attachment and you must have every wire that comes with it or else you have to buy it again because you can't just go to a normal store and buy any usb or firewire because it won't fit your pod. creative will work with anything. you can go out and purchase any cable for it.
next is the firmware. it comes with a simple easy to use program where you can see everything on your computer and see your device on the other screen. the scrolling is great and the sound quality is superb. you can choose some great accessories for it. i purchased a $68.00 fm tuner with built in microphone and mini display with the play, stop, fast forward, and rewind all on it. the biggest difference is the price of the creative. it is $100 cheaper than the pod and it has more features and works well. ipod has gotten so much publicity when i feel it shouldn't. creative has been knocked down just because it isn't white and a couple inches smaller. creative truly is better. it isn't as if i wanted to advertise it because i am a creative fan because this is my first product i purchased from them besides the standard soundblaster built into home pc's. i have both the ipod and creative labs and i would take creative over ipod any day. my mother went with the hype and bought the ipod and i took the creative going with my instincts and a lot of reviews. look who came out as the winner. i still have my songs and less of a headache. don't make the same mistake like my mother.
summary: either back up every song you have or never reformat your pc

reviewText:
ok, so i can't figure it out - some people report that their 30gb video ipods fit perfectly in this skin, and some say it's a bad fit...

i, for one, think this is a terrible fit for my 30gb!  i've put in the insert it came with, tried pulling and pushing and everything i can think of to make it fit -- but the case just will not lay flat around the screen protector! it "peels away" on the top and sides of the screen, leaving a big gap for dirt to get in.  not to mention that it looks awful fitting that poorly.

it also doesn't lay flat against the clickwheel...so not only is the clickwheel not protected, but there's a big gap there for dirt to get in as well.

it fit my friend's 60gb ipod very well, however.

i think this case was designed for the 60/80gb ipods, and the 30gbs were just an afterthought...that rubber insert is just not cutting it.

even for the thirteen bucks i paid for this on an amazon sale, it's just not worth it.  bummer.
summary: it just will not fit my 30gb properly

reviewText:
this is an older design i think.  it hooks up to the wireless in your house or office to play internet radio.  it automatically finds thousands of internet radio station around the world and you can search by type of music or geographic region of the world to find it.  the bottom 5 buttons let you program a station for quick access. i use this to listen to background ambient/enviornment music in my office while reading.  there are a few stations that play music without any commercials.  the speaker on the front is good enough for background music.

now the problems.
1 the "sleep" mode is a lie.  if sleep mode is disabled, it will still turn off after several hours.  the purpose of this devide should have been to always have music without paying attention to it.  it has to be turned back on at least twice in 8 hours.  if you want a music device that you must constantly fix, just play music on your computer or smartphone.  a sleep mode that can't be turned off is either a mistake or the result of another idiot "user experience" expert, aka techparasite.
2  it has no memory.  if there is the slightest drop in your internet connection, it will cut out.  a better device would save a couple of seconds in memory and play from that.  such tech is decades old, but sangean does not have it.  this might have been fixed in later designs, but i doubt it.  this thing is laden with useless features, so it is probably designed by a user interface idiot.
3  control designed by idiots who think you are dumber than they are.  there is a single twist knob, but it does not control volume.  it controls the menu, which is used on on first set up.  an annoyance.  see techparasite above.  also, once you accidentally put it in menu, you can not get out of it with the back button.
summary: acceptable, but only just barely.  cons: 1. it is always on "sleep"  mode.  2. no memory.  3 controls designed by idiots.

reviewText:
i am no audiophile, but i've had my share of premium headphones and these earbuds caught me by surprise.

first off sound quality- i was surprised how these sounded around it's price range. they include an equalizer built in with 3 sound presets normal, bass, and treble depending on what you like and they can be switched by holding the volume + and -. the clarity and the bass is nice but i found some of the really high notes can scratch a bit but they will have to be uncomfortably loud to get there. i love loud music with alot of bass and have personally used some equalizer apps to get these things to hit a little harder with the bass and they do deliver. i've compared these with the beats urbeats and these match up nicely. bass can get strong if you really want it to and sound good while doing it. not quite to the standards of a $200 pair of sony mdr950bt's but with the bass booster app set to more basses along with google plays equalizer settings to punchy i found these to have a wonderful listening experience. tested with rock, hip-hop, r&b, dub step, and even some older titles.

build quality- these earbuds by all means do not feel cheap. the speakers are housed in a nice cold feeling aluminum casing with some decently strong magnets that are strong enough to keep them together when you need them to. but not too strong pulling them apart. the cables have a nice feel to them, soft yet strong. the controller has a plastic body but doesn't feel too cheap. the buttons are very responsive with a decent click and although some of the functions can be a bit tricky it is easy to get used to.

accessories- nice durable case the feels durable enough to carry in your backpack or pocket worry free, that is if you don't sit on it on a hard surface or set a 20lb dumbbell on it. even then the earbuds feel durable enough to survive such an occurrence. eartips included are your standard rubber eartips, wingtips, and memory foam. all of the eartips are comfortable enough for long listening sessions although i found the ones that sound the best and seal out the most sound are the memory foam tips. there are 2 shirt clips that attaches to the cable that are pretty strong and works well. in the same bag are some cable management clips to help make the cord a bit shorter if it is too long for you, although i have had no issues with the length of the cable.

portability- better than ever. no worries if you are someone who has forgotten earbuds in your pocket or have fear of ever leaving them in your pockets to only go through the washing machine. i personally have laid them around the back of my neck and attached the buds via magnet and wore them like a necklace. they are sweat proof so worry not if you decide to stuff them under your shirt. the included clips will help you keep them secure if you decide to part take in sporting activities. i myself have witnessed and had personal experience with playing sports with earbuds around my shirt and neck only to have it tugged by my opponent either on the field or the court. i play hard in a game and often leave with scratches and or bruise's so it's a big deal for me to say that i could safely wear these under my shirt with the included clips clipped on to my shirt to know they will stay in place and will not get snagged by another player in the game.

final verdict- great sounding headphones at a very decent price that is portable enough to endure the hard life of any sport player out there.

if any problems occur with the earbuds i will leave an update.

reviewText:
a 17" mac book pro or powerbook fits nicely in this backpack, and there's plenty of extra room for the power supply, spare batteries, cables, thumb drives, evdo cards, etc.

brenthaven changed the design a few months ago.  my wife has an earlier one, which has a less comfortable handle but a removable inner sleeve that velcros closed.

the newer style does not have the internal velcro closure, and this was a very costly omission for me.  my backpack, containing my 17" powerbook, tipped over, fully zipped, and fell approximately two feet to the floor, with the top of the backpack striking pavement.

fearing the worst but hoping for the best, i removed the computer and was horrified to discover that it had slid right through the internal flap and taken the full brunt of the impact, massively denting and dislocating the side of the computer and damaging the pcmcia slot.

applecare does not cover this sort of damage, so i ended up eating a multi-hundred dollar repair bill.

the backpack is comfortable and capacious, but the lack of protection for a top impact was a deep disappointment.
summary: a large-capacity, comfortable backpack for macs that doesn't provide as much protection as it should

it would be tedious for me to list all of the positives (this device is awesome) so i'm going to focus on the negatives i've experienced.

- battery life

you will only get somewhere between 3 and 5hrs of life during typical use. this is extremely low for a tablet but pretty good for an ultrabook in this price range (with this much power). if battery life is a concern you will definitely want to invest in a surface pro 2.

- weight / ergonomics

the only really positive thing i would like to add, that isn't always mentioned in other reviews, is that this thing is extraordinarily durable... it is vaguely reminiscent of the iphone 4 with it's almost full screen of glass w/ clean edges but it shares almost nothing in terms of durability with that device. rock. solid.

i have an isole watt-stopper power strip with a motion sensor that shuts down power to the strip when it hasn't sensed motion for a while. i use the watt-stopper for all my displays and speakers. the watt-stopper works fine on wall power through the cyberpower ups, but when i cut the wall power the watt-stopper's "wiring" warning light comes on and nothing downstream works. i suspect that the grounding is not carried through or simulated by the watt-stopper. my apc ups i was replacing worked fine with the watt-stopper, so i'm considering using the apc ups for just the watt-stopper loads even though it's battery is near end-of-life.

the "new plastic" smell is still kind of strong after 18 hours but not unbearable. i wish i'd installed this during better ventilation weather so i could just leave the windows open all day.

update: the "new plastic" smell went away completely within a few days. i placed the unit in my garage over the weekend with a small load, and cycled it a few times so it would burn off whatever made the smell.
summary: working, but not for all loads

if you want to power phones like the samsung galaxy s5, you'll need the 2a board. the 1a version just doesn't cut it. the only thing i got to charge with the 1a board was a gopro battery and an old ipod mini.

this board can be powered with 3.7v cells in parallel, but doesn't seem to work properly as the led glows red indicating that the battery voltage is low when it's not.

one big thing to note is that when you're not using this board, the led will continue to draw power from your batteries, so you will need to install a switch. drok should add an auto on/off feature when devices are plugged/unplugged and when battery is near depletion.

another big thing is that this board doesn't like to be connected with a 3v lithium battery charging board like the jbtek one. charging will not work if you connect as follows 18650 battery>jbtek charging board in>jbtek charging board out>drok usb converter. just separate the two boards and connect each directly to a battery.

reviewText:
i am a big fan of the ergonomic keyboards.  you know the ones with the split keys.  and my wrists hurt at times from typing at work.  well, i have to say that i've been using this keyboard for a week without wrist pain.

i think that the flat design helps my wrists as i no longer need wrist supports.  my wrists are flat with the desk and the keyboard.  so that helps an awful lot.

this comes with all the batteries that you'll need to get started.  the mouse will recharge.  the keyboard won't.  the keyboard needs 4 aa batteries.  so far, i have no idea when it's going to die but i keep spare batteries in case.

the feel of the keyboard is more like a laptop keyboard than a traditional keyboard.  there's very little down stroke when you press a key.  no too springy either.

the function keys on the top are not really keys but a small depression that you have to lightly touch.  that took some getting used to.

i'm not 100% sold on the design.  i use the arrow keys a lot at my work and they're much smaller than most of the old keyboards i've used.  there are times where i've thought about returning to the old keyboard just because of that.  but i still like the feel enough to give this a chance.

the mouse works fine.  it's a mouse.  it's no logitech laser mx but it's not bad.  the action is fine.  it's nice to have the keyboard and mouse drive off of one little bluetooth usb key.

overall, i'd recommend this with a few reservations.  if you're super sensative to the ergonomic keyboards and don't like regular keyboards, avoid this.  also, if you need a 10 key or use the arrow keys a lot, this is not the keyboard for you.  beyond that, you've got a stylish cool keyboard with a good mouse.

reviewText:
the visual quality of the photographs when viewed thru this frame are really beautiful, and i expected as much given that i have a view sonic computer monitor.  however, you can only either display photos in portrait view or landscape view if you want photos to run a slideshow and not have half of them laying on their side.  you can stop the slideshow and rotate a photo, but it will not be saved in the rotated view and will go back to its original view.

i purchased this frame to give to my sister with her wedding photos as they wanted to run their photos in a slideshow. about 1/3 of my shots were shot in portrait view, 2/3 in landscape view.  i have pulled out about half my hair experimenting with cropping and resizing my portrait view photos so that they can be read by the frame as a landscape dimension, but the frame cannot deal with that at all, and there's no way to predict how the frame will deal with a crop or resize until it is loaded into the frame.  my computer monitor can certainly deal with displaying a photo in any view, why can't this?  in fact, the frame will manually rotate a photo by making an intelligent crop, but you can't save it like that.  if you recrop the photo in the very same way the frame did and load it back into the frame, it treats the photo like a close up [even if you size to accommodate the lost pixels]!!  it's sheer crazy making.  i am now needing to decide if some of my favorite shots stay out of the frame or if i return it and try something else.

if somebody has any suggestions, i'd be appreciative

update:  july 20, 2010

regarding the problem with vertical/portrait view shots, i found that if i cropped some and rotated them 90 degrees clockwise, that the frame would load them properly but only with the 3:4 view.  so this squeezed the horizontal/landscape view shots a bit, but an acceptable compromise.

however, the slideshow craziness is not acceptable.  you can set a "shuffle" option to avoid the frame running from the very beginning of the photo set each time, but after sitting with 150 pictures for over 20 minutes, the frame would run some of the same shots multiple times and never get to others.  if i then go thru the menu to see the photos one at a time by choosing a shot from the thumbnails and then clicking to forward thru them, sometimes the frame will just start a slideshow again, taking me far afieild from the photo i was next planning to look at....really nuts and completely annoying.

a commenter in the digital frame forum here on amazon stated something very true, that all frames seem to have two fundatmental flaws; dealing with shots on the verticle, and lousy slideshow performance.  this frame has big problems on both those points.  it also tends to caste a bit too much of a warm temperature [yellow] on shots that have a certain amount of gold light in them.

i've since gotten the linksys modem (befcmu10) and stacked it with the wrt54g router and it works fantastic!!!  be sure to call your isp with the modem's mac address and/or serial# to get online.  you won't get connected otherwise. my isp had me up and running within 5 minutes.  also some isp's give you a discount if you supply your own modem.  check it out. a great product!

reviewText:
i am happy with my 2013 purchase of my new hp p7-1430. over all a very good computer for the price. you can find better but look at the price tag. if you want a computer that should last for years with out blowing $1000+(after monitor and speakers) i think you should consider this one.

i will now give you the good, bad, and why some people gave bad reviews.

the things i liked:

- price vs. performance is great for this class of computer. the envy is better but hey, it costs more.

- hard drive is fast for not being a solid state drive and large(2tb). good luck trying to fill it any time soon if you are using it at home.

- all the standard ports that you need for todays computer you can find on the tower including usb 3.0

- cool quiet running. i press my computers gamming and have not ever seen the computer get hot at all.

- plenty of room to add more memory later.

- office programs were included on the one i got. my last computer had no ms office programs with it so this was a plus for me.

- windows 8 is efficient at running programs and can run some older programs but not all.

- cpu will over clock it self. this feature is becoming more standard on newer computer.

- graphics card on the mother board is adequate for gamming as good as most gddr3 1gb cards. though i bought a way better card the gigabyte radeon hd 7850.

- system stability is good.

the things i did not like:

- only one pci express 16x.

- inadequate keyboard and mouse. the batteries on the keyboard run out too fast and the mouse lags. there was no way i could use them for fast paced gamming. i'm sure most people using it for basics tasks may be some what satisfied with there performance.

- windows 8 start screen. it is annoying but that is not hp's fault. we can blame ms for that.

- windows 8 portability. i already had a solid state drive and found that it would be very hard(way above my comfort level) to port the os to this drive. again not the fault of hp but microsoft yet again.

some reasons for the bad reviews:

-it has a dual physical core with a quad logical architecture. this is causing some people confusion. the fact is many new computers are rated now by logical cores not physical cores, a quad is physically two, a six core is really three. the function is about the same but physically there are less cores.  it's what the processor manufactures are doing. intel computers don't even tell you how many cores there are now.

- windows 8, yes the new hated windows. after learning my way around the os it is really not bad and far more efficient running programs on then other versions of windows i have used. the renamed "metro" opening start window is annoying but the trade off in performance is worth it and it only takes a second to move the desk top or you get software to avoid it all together. there are potential drawbacks though with windows 8 as mentioned above.

i'm a bit torn. on the one hand, i loved my flex. it tracked activities well, it was water resistant, with a good battery life, and easy to use. i especially loved the alarm function.

on the other hand, my first flex lasted me just a year before its battery died horribly. its bands wore out every 2 to 3 months and had to be replaced. this is down to the fact that to recharge it, the user has to bend the band backwards to pop out the flex, putting a lot of wear on the little seams at the bottom. the replacement bands aren't cheap if you buy from fitbit and generic ones fall apart with a sneeze.
