reviewText: i've had this bag for two years or so, from the start when i first got my canon eos 60d camera. it's been with me ever since, going on trips to family gatherings and acting like a storage space for my gear when i'm at home. over the years, i've expanded my personal photography collection by adding a 50mm prime lens in addition to the 18-135mm kit lens, a canon 430ex ii speedlite, extension tubes, remote triggers, cleaning kits, rechargeable batteries and their charger, lens caps and so on. all of the above plus more fits in snugly without issue. this bag is great for it's purpose - it holds a lot. though i'm no pro, i carry around all of my equipment that can fit in the bag, plus accessories, software, booklets and more. the only things i cannot jam in it are large items like my softboxes, tripods and props. while i haven't treated the bag roughly enough to vouch for its superior sturdiness - it has not gone hiking or anything strenuous - mine is still in good condition. no zipper breakage, fraying, tearing. to wear, it's very comfortable, and a plus side to the design was the strapped front which allowed me to jam water bottles and snacks in the front for easy snacking while on the go. i do not use the straps underneath or on the sides for my tripod (a sunpak 620-750tmbb platinum plus tri-monopod, silver which is pretty hefty). it's unwieldy and the weight of the tripod causes it to sag on one side, and potentially slip free of the straps. three of the issues i had with this backpack: 1.) i originally wanted a bag with a hammock system, such as the case logic slrc-203 large slr camera bag (black). the hammock really appealed to me as extra additional protection against sudden jarring. however, at the time i purchased this backpack, that sort of bag was not available. this backpack allows the camera to be placed at the top with the lens facing down, but it's not a hammock style and it is not, in my opinion, securely contained. especially when i have my short 50mm prime lens on, the camera can shimmy loose and move around and potentially fall out. 2.) i also wanted a bag with a stable base. be warned - this canon backpack is not stable. especially considering the bag can be top-heavy from the camera being placed on the top, it can and will fall over. this has always been my biggest concern, and i always take care to prop the bag up safely, or lay it down to prevent damage. more than anything, using a bag that causes me more need for concern than assuaging it, is a big loss in points for me. 3.) should the bag fall forward, there is little to no padding on the front to cushion the fall. i've taken to putting booklets, dvds and cleaning cloths in the pockets to help the padding, but it still makes me wince to see the bag tottering over. in short, after a few years of usage, i've finally put in the money and purchased a kelly moore mimi bag (black). i wanted something to protect my gear while looking sophisticated enough to take out for social gatherings and family shoots, without branding the bag as a camera bag with lots of theft goodies in it to nab (that old canon logo sure is obvious on this backpack!) that said, i will be keeping my canon backpack at home to store items that i don't need for my every day use, and for those long trips where i need a bag that can carry some weight comfortably. and if it comes down to it, a bag that i won't mind scuffing up.

first, i would like to mention that sylvania is great at manufacturing light bulbs, but the dvd players they are producing is by far not the best product they have. please do not be confused by many positive and negative reviews, the product itself is not very good or very bad, it is just cheap and poorly designed. even though dvd players were working for me, judging by the overal quality, i doubt will last longer than 5-6 months. both dvd players are completely identical, so if you need just one, you can keep the second one as a spare, and wait for the first one to stop working, should not be too long. i have noticed that sound quality is not good, screen quality (colors, resolution, etc.) not good, many controls are available, but it seems that changes of settings produce little difference; buttons are not responsive, controls and buttons are not positioned conveniently,  dvd's doors open in the wrong direction, and is not wide enough, remote is a joke (made by somebody who seems have never seen how remotes should look and work). i have noticed that loading dvds takes very, very long time. sd card readers works, but are useless. it takes way too long to load 5-6 mb images from camera, and lcd screen does not have enough resolution to display photos at any acceptable quality.

well, i realise that the device does play dvds, and is fairly cheap. considering that dvd technology is going away and a selection of portable dvd players is not huge any longer, some people may consider this product to be an attractive choice. i completely disagree, since  this device to my opinion is a piece of junk from almost every angle. i would never suggest this device to anyone. if you need portable dvd player, look for left overs from sony or other reputable brands while still exist.

reviewText: i was extremely excited when i saw this camera.  i said to myself, "finally a small compact camera with a large lcd display."  when i received it, i was even happier. it looks fantastic and the controls, menus and ease of use are incredible. and with the ipod case (it fits perfectly!), it is extremely portable. "well," i thought to myself. "let's see how the pictures look." here's the story. in daylight, the colors are dull and lack-lustre; kind of faded and washed out. i use iphoto and the "enhance" feature takes care of most of this problem. where the t1 really misses the boat is with it's built in flash. if your subject is more than 5 feet away, (yes, just 5 feet away) the flash just doesn't illuminate enough for a good picture. in fact, the flash photos are terrible! they're extremely noisy and the colors are way off. i've seen better flash photos with a 1.3 mega-pixel camera. i really wanted this camera to work for me. i tried every setting and even called customer support. but ultimately, i returned it. to me, if the pictures aren't good enough, the rest really doesn't matter. hopefully, sony will fix these problems and then maybe, they'll have the perfect digital camera.

i got the backbeat go 2 bluetooth earphones after trying the beats powerbeats 2's (which sounded great, but kept dropping out - update: tried another pair of powerbeats 2, and they've been working out great).

they were easy to charge. i expected just a usb charging cable, but the included ac adapter was a pleasant surprise. a red light on the earphones turned white (i believe) once the battery finished charging.

pairing the backbeat go 2's to my iphone 6 was easy. i saw the earphones on my iphone and selected them to pair.

then i tried them on, and that's where the party ended. they were just not comfortable - too large for my ears. i also did not like the sound. at about half the sound level, the sound was extremely distorted. i didn't expect great sound, but for me, it wasn't even in the realm of acceptable.

this was the last pair of in-ear bluetooth earphones on my list to try. i am sticking with my true and trusted wired etymotic in-ear monitors.

i would still like a pair of bluetooth earphones, but i may have to look to a circumaural design. they won't be as portable, but they will hopefully not have drop outs and sound good! perhaps the new parrot zik 2.0's?
summary: highly distorted audio, and not a good fit for my ears.

reviewText:
this yamaha is a pretty decent receiver.  works well with most stereo-type speakers.  it has lots of inputs for speakers, digital, component, and composite.  the front panel is simple to use, with a big volume tuner and orange/amber color display.  yamaha has imbedded some decoders so that you can set how you like your receiver to sound like (game, movie, music etc).

some drawbacks i found was the remote controller.  it's a bit clumsy and comes in black which doesn't quite match the silver receiver.  the buttons on the remote are also a bit tiny.  this unit only has 5.1 channels so it will work well if you just want a 5.1 set up.  if you're looking for 6 or 7.1, then you'd have to look for another unit.  another drawback i found was that if you just hook up stereo speakers, the bass seems quite weak even if you boosted the "tone control" all the way up on the bass.  you would definetely need a powered subwoofer to maximize this receiver.

other than that, it is a pretty good system for the price, worth a look.

reviewText:
bought this no-frills mobo to go in a work pc and read about them being reliable. originally purchased from another retailer (that other pc parts retailer) and had to rma - the rma process takes horrendously long so ordered another w/ next-day shipping from amazon. amazon gets 5 stars as usual.

the problem with this motherboard is the 'cute' uefi bios doesn't always... load. when i scrolled through items (ram clocks, sata mode, etc), some text fields were missing entirely, others were invisible (could still select, but couldn't see what you were selecting). all of this is a horrible sacrifice just to use a mouse in the bios - everyone's moving to this, and these companies' programming abilities aren't up to snuff to produce this functionality reliably. i figured i needed a bios update, done this several times, used the company's @bios software - failed, no diagnostic messages. loaded bios to usb drive and loaded it in bios... bricked the motherboard. horrible. got a new one from the zon and resolved not to touch anything, use standard bios settings, just because it's a work pc and i need to... work. also, i had already installed a ton of software on my c drive and didn't want any hiccups. as a result, i have downclocked ram, etc. do not buy this unless budget is the only consideration.

that said, i've built ~8 pc's in the last 2 years and i couldn't name a reliable mobo manufacturer with a no-frills stability mentality. maybe intel? that's >$100 for same functionality as the overseas companies, and i've had a few fail on me as well.

***edit 12/29/14*** - this motherboard has a known defect involving the 'a2' diagnostic code that is shown pre-bios. google 'msi motherboard stuck on a2' to see what i'm talking about. about 3-6 months in, the motherboard fails to recognize attached sata hdds/ssds and hangs before you're even allowed to see the bios. resetting the cmos, pulling various sata devices, none of this works, and all the ssd/hdds were connected to a spare pc i have in the back and they all worked flawlessly. the only solution i've found (this has happened to me twice now) is to replace the motherboard and plug all your devices into their previous slots - the pc then boots right up. because this is a work system, uptime is critical and i will never buy another msi product (i currently own 4). i tried submitting a tech support ticket the first time it happened (in april) and they got back to me at the end of summer. their support forums are full of msi reps giving the standard 'did you test your power supply? did you run a memory diagnostic?' endlessly in circles while people eventually just buy new components. spend an extra 60-100 and get whatever good asus/evga is out, their qc seems to be leaps and bounds above msi's.
summary: 8-month edit: do not buy, see below update

reviewText:
after doing lots of research, reading reviews of this and other telescopes, i decided on this one.
the people on the astronomy forums are snobs and hate anything that isn't a dobsonian.
i'm not necessarily saying being a snob is bad as i was a snob with cigars, but they would answer almost every question about should i buy this or that reflector or refractory scope with, neither buy a dobsonian. their reasoningfor the most part made since. however, i did not want to spend the money for a dobsonian that can also track, not for my first telescope.

unlike many people who reviewed this telescope, i watched the assembly and usage videos before purchasing. i also watched the assembly video while i assembled it, so for me, assembly didn't take long at all.

the usage video also showed me how to balance the scope on the mount, as well as aligning the scope with the view finder. fortunately mine arrived in good shape, so i did not have to collimate it, but watched a video on how to do so.

the first time i took it out was last night 8/15/17. i spotted what i believed to be saturn and unfortunately all i saw was a dot. i used the 25mm, 10mm, and barlow lens, and nothing but a dot. i was very disappointed and wondered how long i had to return it.

the next morning, i checked the scope and view finder alignment, and set it again.
tonight 8/16/17 i took it out again. when i spotted what i believed to be saturn, i set up the scope, targeted the dot with the view finder, and looked through the 25mm lens. i saw a circle. then i put in the 10mm lens, and there it was, saturn.
i was so happy. then i saw jupiter, though i couldn't get a good view because of the trees.

at this point i am pleased with what i have seen and look forward to seeing more. i'll eventually get more powerful lenses.

many reviews of this telescope complain of the vibration using the eq2 mount. unfortunately that is very true. while viewing saturn and tracking it, it repeatedly lost focus due to the motion from turning the scope. it also gave the same visual vibration when turning the focus.
that is one of the many reasons the telescope snobs recommend dobsonian telescopes.

overall, as my first telescope i am pleased. i know spending $300 and seeing visual vibration doesn't sound pleasing, but i am pleased with the view of saturn and jupiter, as well as being able to track them with this telescope.

unlike many people who reviewed this telescope, i watched the assembly and usage videos before purchasing. i also watched the assembly video while i assembled it, so for me, assembly didn't take long at all.

the usage video also showed me how to balance the scope on the mount, as well as aligning the scope with the view finder. fortunately mine arrived in good shape, so i did not have to collimate it, but watched a video on how to do so.

the first time i took it out was last night 8/15/17. i spotted what i believed to be saturn and unfortunately all i saw was a dot. i used the 25mm, 10mm, and barlow lens, and nothing but a dot. i was very disappointed and wondered how long i had to return it.

the next morning, i checked the scope and view finder alignment, and set it again.
tonight 8/16/17 i took it out again. when i spotted what i believed to be saturn, i set up the scope, targeted the dot with the view finder, and looked through the 25mm lens. i saw a circle. then i put in the 10mm lens, and there it was, saturn.
i was so happy. then i saw jupiter, though i couldn't get a good view because of the trees.

at this point i am pleased with what i have seen and look forward to seeing more. i'll eventually get more powerful lenses.

many reviews of this telescope complain of the vibration using the eq2 mount. unfortunately that is very true. while viewing saturn and tracking it, it repeatedly lost focus due to the motion from turning the scope. it also gave the same visual vibration when turning the focus.
that is one of the many reasons the telescope snobs recommend dobsonian telescopes.

overall, as my first telescope i am pleased. i know spending $300 and seeing visual vibration doesn't sound pleasing, but i am pleased with the view of saturn and jupiter, as well as being able to track them with this telescope. my first telescope.

it's also cheaply made but a good design, which is why it works.

the fitbit is pedometer, with a bluetooth connection. its major functions are counting steps (which it can only show you in increments of 2000) and storing that information in a place where you can later view it by a better piece of technology. the fitbits battery life is advertised as up to 5 days. in my experience, its about 1-2 days. thats right folks, this thing you need to charge every night (if you want reliability).  the indication of how much battery life is only visible when plugged in to the usb charger (at which point it can not count steps). its up to 5 dots. it says that it should charge in 3 hours. my cell phone charges in less time then that, but when i put the fitbit after sleeping for 8 hours it is usually at 3 dots. so perhaps it changes in 16 hours (i don't know, i have other things to do in my life). when the fitbit runs out of battery sometimes it sends you and email, most of the time it does absolutely nothing except have the dots dance at you instead of show you the number of steps you have when you check. when you see the dancing dots, the fitbit is telling you that whatever steps you think you have gotten have been lost to space and time. those steps have gone to a far away land never to been seen or heard of again. the fitbit usually syncs with your phone, but many times it doesnt. instead your phone simply gives you a red icon and tells you that you need to be more active because you have 0 steps.
all in all this product is a disaster. it took at most $3 to manufacture, and boy you can tell... sadly i couldn't tell within the 14 day return policy at best buy.
summary: pedometer with a bluetooth connections (except unreliable)

to sum things up, stay away from this gps, invest a few more hundreds and get a newer version.

reviewText:
first of all, i have opened up this stereo and discovered it uses the tda7387 amp chip which is 41 watts per channel, not 60w as advertised. this is a 164 watt system being advertised as 240 watts!

the audio streaming over bluetooth is tinny and compressed, with harsh treble, from what is likely a low bitrate or poor d/a converter. plugging in through the aux is the only option for decent audio. the built-in mic picks up more engine noise than anything else. luckily i am an engineer and willing to crack it open and run an external mic. just about the only thing this has going for it, and the main reason i bought it, is the simple interface--why do all aftermarket stereos have to look like some flashy techno device from blade runner?

cheap plastic everywhere, slow interface, middling sound quality, and unabashed product misrepresentation. do not buy.
summary: you get what you pay for

this and its corded (usb) twin are apparently the only trackpoint keyboards available new at this time, and that's a shame. i'd kill to have this keyboard with a number pad - and with a more reliable wireless connection. for now i'll make do with this, because i have to. but i eagerly await lenovo's next generation of trackpoint keyboards!

i want to describe my experience with this tv even though amazon does not currently offer it. (perhaps with good reason.)
my television worked fine for two weeks. then it developed the buzz at start-up that others have described. after a few days it would not turn on. i purchased this from cr*tchfie*d (four thou). i am going to find out if they really honor their 30 day money back guarantee.
the picture quality with hd broadcasts was superb. quality for sd directv broadcasts was only fair to poor. some channels appeared muddy or out-of focus with an overall smudgy appearance. even the best sd channels were worse than my old 50 inch pioneer rear projection tv which never failed to turn on in ten years.
this was actually the second tv that i received. the first came with several cracks running through the screen image and a heavily dented chassis.
the manufacture date for my set is december 2003. the problem with the buzz comes from the television's very expensive (two hundred fifty) halogen lamp. the lamp is either no good or something in the television's circuitry is causing them to burn out prematurely. sony rates them to work for approximately 1 year of average viewing.
in searching the internet i have found dozens of complaints similar to mine. some people report exchanging one tv only to have its replacemnt develop the same problem. there was even one who had three televsions develop this problem. i have seen posts that claim that sony is aware of this problem and has taken steps to correct it with recently manufactured televsions not having the problem.
in a way a problem that presents immediately is better than a problem that appears after several months when the only option left is to be at the mercy of sony's guarantee and face several weeks of waiting for in-home repair visits. i present this review as a warning to others so that they can avoid this painful experience.

reviewText: first off, you should know that for some people this will be a very good subwoofer.  if your only concern is with spl, i.e. having a sub that causes hearing loss, head-aches and makes your neighbors yearn for your death, then this is a fantastic choice.  however, if you are actually concerned with the musical quality of your bass then you need to look elsewhere.  this sub doesn't play deep, it doesn't play clean, it simply eminates a tremendous quantity of bass that isn't worth hearing.  the bass reproduced by this sub sounds simply like power converted into sound and not an actual element of music.  i'm sure people who own this sub are very proud of how much it makes the rear-view mirror rattle, as well as the amount of attention they are able to garner as they cruise past wal-mart with the windows down; but i fail to believe anyone really truly enjoys the sound that is created by this discus of decibals.  in short, if you want loud (and all you want is loud), consider getting this sub. if you want a sub that actually sounds good, try kicker/rockford/soundstream/audiobahn/boston or some other brand that realizes bass isn't simply a frequency that makes your trunk sound like the apocolypse is beginning, it's an actual element of music.

reviewText:
well tom tom doesn't really need to make the gps units anymore because those have become obsolete in a way, so there is this item a golf watch.

1.  what's in the box?:  you receive the watch, also an instruction booklet, and a usb power charger.

2.  aesthetic?:  the watch is sleek and nicely done for an electronic watch.  it has a nice square face, with a smooth band, a double clasp, and a button on the inside for the wrist.  the watch is nice and pretty sleek looking.  when used for time, the digits are displayed in a nice interesting manner.

3.  set-up?:  the watch does not carry a charge, so you will need to charge it with the power cable.  after that, the watch comes on and away you go.  the watch goes through the initial set-up (use the arrow on the wristband) and this is pretty intuitive.  when i tried to set up for a golf session, the gps initially took a few moments, but it readily identified the courses near me.  i chose a course i am readily familiar with near me and it is pretty easy to navigate around.

4.  use?:  to use this on the golf course is easy.  i turned on the unit in terms of airplane mode being off and after a few beats, the watch finds the nearest gold courses and away you go.

i didn't believe the claim this would register the golf swings and understand practice swings, but this device does. as to understanding the placement of shots, this is helpful, although i am not skilled enough that understanding where i should go is how i will go if you catch my drift.

the information is easily findable using the button on the bottom, although i am constantly tempted to think of this as a touchscreen.

the lack of a color screen didn't bother me too much, frankly.  perhaps with more use that will change, but i think not.

the information provided is excellent with the app and provides great data that helps (it helps me understand i stink, but that's another story).

overall:  as i continue to use this powerful device, i will update my review.  at this time, i really like the watch.  it is a terrific tool for the golfer.  the entire concept is frankly, pretty amazing and i enjoy the 'gee whiz' aspect of the technology.
summary: cool concept, easy to execute, powerful metrics.

reviewText:
pro:  low cost
con: not easy to work with
.  deceptively thick wire but with a very small conductor
.  unspecified conductor gauge

at first glance the unstripped wire looks like ~16 gage but the conductors are actually much smaller, 24 gauge at best. i used them for some short strips of led lights and they work fine, but the unspecified small gauge wire certainly won't safely handle more than an amp or two.

the conductor are stranded copper and the assembly comes with very short (~1/16" - 1/8") prestripped/tinned leads.

the insulation is very thick and hard to cut /strip.  i have no idea what the actual insulating material is but it is definitely not normal pvc.

the wire is very difficult to strip. the insulation is much thicker than the conductor and the waxy plastic material does not cut cleanly. i also had to almost always cut off the pre-tinned portion of the wire since the cut piece of insulation won't slide off the wire end with the extra thickness of the solder on the lead.

if this modem would work with my isp it would be easy to set up. i use both windows and mac and tried to set it up on the mac first (manual), then i ran the install software on windows which provides three methods.

1) automatic: the software tries to discover the details of your dsl connection and program the router. needless to say this failed.
2) by isp: the software provides a list of isps (verizon, century etc.). i tried every one and it was unable to connect to the internet. i might point out here that it did get a dsl connection when i first turned it on which meant that the phone line and so on were ok.
3) manual: i set up the dsl parameters according to my old modem and it would not connect. i finally used a static ip address (my last known good one) which my isp doesn't want you to do, and was able to get the internet light to turn on for the first time. however, i could not access any web pages because the dns servers were blank, and there was no way to enter them manually. i would also like to say that that the number of options  available is severely limited.

 so, i sent it back to amazon and they provided their usual no hassle postage free return - amazon, a great place to do business with. in view of the fact that my isp is different from all those the actiontec provides for, i elected to get a bec technologies modem (at almost twice the cost) from my phone company. it has lots of bells and whistles the actiontec didn't, and works flawlessly over 50% faster than my old modem.

i purchased this player off ebay a few days back (as it's no longer sold - toshiba basically replaced it with the zune).  i will not review the original firmware, as i wiped it immediately and replaced it with rockbox ([...]  the rockbox firmware is not complete yet, but it is functional.

i have used rockbox with the gigabeat f series, but this s series is a major improvement.  the s series is small (smaller than an ipod video), light, and has a nice screen and excellent controls.

as for hardware mods, it's very easy to open (5 screws).  the hard drive is a standard 1.8 inch zif based 8mm size, and i added a 120gb drive to expand the storage.  removing he battery requires removing 2 more screws, but it can be done.  being 700mah, i suspect upgrading to a 1000mah will give me an improvement in battery life, but i haven't done that yet.

as for the sound - that's been the only drawback for me (updating this review, because of this).  the sound quality is sub-par, to my ears.  comparing it with the sansa clip, cowon d2 and the zune 30, this player comes in dead last in sq.

so, if you are a tech geek who uses rockbox and wants a good player (sans the sound quality) that supports it, look no further!

reviewText:
i received this laptop today so this review is limited to just one topic:  the damn touchpad "tapping" function cannot be disabled via the elan touchpad control options.  i purchased this laptop primarily for very fine video editing, which would be impossible with the ultra-sensitive touchpad "tap to select" function operational.

fortunately i found a solution that someone named "rakulia" posted on-line.  the solution, however, requires editing of the pc's registry file--something that i hesitate to attempt but fortunately the change went well and, after a restart, worked perfectly.  now i can have full control over the touchpad without accidentally initiating unwanted actions.

for those who need to disable the touchpad tapping function, go into "regedit" and make the following changes:
1.  select registry file to edit: hkey_current_user\software\elantech\smartpad
2.  then change tap_enable to 0 and tap_activate_enable to 0
3.  then reboot

if this pc provides the blazing video editing capability that i need, i may add ore info to this review in the future.

update:  as of sept 10, 2016, this laptop has been working very well and i've increased my rating to 4 stars.  still not 5 due to the touchpad issue.  my primary requirement for this laptop is video editing.  i use cyber director for editing and the laptop speed is very good.  previously the audio and video were out of sync when previewing editing changes, which made precise editing very difficult.  this laptop is able to provide previews that remain in sync.  additionally, final production times have been cut almost in half.  a 15 minute video now takes only about 20 minutes to produce.

the look and feel of this laptop are also both excellent.  amazon describes the case as satin gold, but you have to look vary hard to perhaps see the slight gold tinge so it has a very nice satin look.  the case, keyboard and overall feel of this laptop are all excellent.  it feels very sturdy and well designed.  it also seems to have excellent heat dissipation since the heat is directed out the sides, which reduces the potential for being blocked on the bottom.

update:  dec 10 2016,  after using this pc to do more than just video editing, i find the space bar can cause text editing errors.  after entering a paragraph of text, i've noticed that there are sometimes errors due to the lack of a space between words.  after doing a little testing, i've found that the far left and right areas of the space bar do not always work properly.  i can fully depress the lower left and lower right areas of the space bar and (sometimes) no space is produced.  pressing the center of the space bar will always produce a space, but the lower left and right areas do not.  perhaps this is an issue with just my keyboard, and it is only a minor annoyance, but for someone who does a lot of keyboard work it may be a more significant problem.  otherwise, i remain very happy with this laptop and plan to start using it as my primary laptop.

1.  select registry file to edit: hkey_current_user\software\elantech\smartpad
2.  then change tap_enable to 0 and tap_activate_enable to 0
3.  then reboot

if this pc provides the blazing video editing capability that i need, i may add ore info to this review in the future.

update:  as of sept 10, 2016, this laptop has been working very well and i've increased my rating to 4 stars.  still not 5 due to the touchpad issue.  my primary requirement for this laptop is video editing.  i use cyber director for editing and the laptop speed is very good.  previously the audio and video were out of sync when previewing editing changes, which made precise editing very difficult.  this laptop is able to provide previews that remain in sync.  additionally, final production times have been cut almost in half.  a 15 minute video now takes only about 20 minutes to produce.

the look and feel of this laptop are also both excellent.  amazon describes the case as satin gold, but you have to look vary hard to perhaps see the slight gold tinge so it has a very nice satin look.  the case, keyboard and overall feel of this laptop are all excellent.  it feels very sturdy and well designed.  it also seems to have excellent heat dissipation since the heat is directed out the sides, which reduces the potential for being blocked on the bottom.

update:  dec 10 2016,  after using this pc to do more than just video editing, i find the space bar can cause text editing errors.  after entering a paragraph of text, i've noticed that there are sometimes errors due to the lack of a space between words.  after doing a little testing, i've found that the far left and right areas of the space bar do not always work properly.  i can fully depress the lower left and lower right areas of the space bar and (sometimes) no space is produced.  pressing the center of the space bar will always produce a space, but the lower left and right areas do not.  perhaps this is an issue with just my keyboard, and it is only a minor annoyance, but for someone who does a lot of keyboard work it may be a more significant problem.  otherwise, i remain very happy with this laptop and plan to start using it as my primary laptop. beware of touchpad "tapping" issue

so i got the vizeri (which actually says "tank007" inside the tube) based upon the excitement here. i'm not excited.

first of all, it's not even tactical! a tactical light works with a soft-press of the switch from the off position. this needs to be completely switched on to work...and then...changing modes by half-pressing the switch doesn't always work. it usually needs to be half-pressed twice in every mode, before it changes the mode.

with all due respect to those who are impressed by the vizeri's brightness...you ain't seen nothin' yet! by comparison to the majority of flashlights on the market, 230 lumens isn't terribly bright. many are over 500 lumens. in fact, i have a flashlight from zebralight that is 3" tall, less than half the diameter of the vizeri, operates on 1 aa battery, and is just as bright (if not brighter) than the vizeri!

the vizeri also displays pwm (pulse width modulation) when operating in medium and low mode. the effect of pwm is seen when a fast moving object is being lit by the light. the object appears as a blurry, multiple image. if you only operate this light on high...you'll never see it. the cree xr-e q5 led was a technical breakthrough almost 10 years ago. it's not a bad led, but it doesn't have the capacity to offer much more lumens than is already coming out of this light. it cannot drive a light as hard as the newer xm-l led's. on the plus side, it has good throw. and the manufacturers have seen fit to not drive it hard enough to cause excess heat and premature burnout.

what i admire most about this package, is the accessories. they're quite generous. especially the diffuser.

if you've never owned an led flashlight before, or only had a really cheap one, then the vz230 will seem pretty impressive. for someone like me, who owns many lights, it's pretty average and doesn't hold a candle in terms of convenient size or lumen output that most of my others do.

it's not a bad light, but it has some issues. the zoom works well and can be set at any interval you choose. the beam of the led when zoomed out, is only useful when pointing at something 100ft or farther. this is due to the 'squared shape' of the led which is seen in that mode.

you can use nimh rechargeable batteries instead of disposable aaa's. you can also use lithium rechargeables; 2 16340's or 2 18350's. disposable cr123's can also be used. interestingly though, in my visual tests, i can't see any noticeable difference in lumen output with the lithium vs. the nimh aaa's. in other words, it doesn't appear any brighter with lithium batteries. that surprised me.

i don't generally like or recommend "zoom" flashlights. name-brand non-zooming lights can be bought for about the same price as this one. the beams on those lights are far more useful to me...and much brighter too!
summary: it's not all bad...even though it has pwm!

reviewText: i like this strap and use one for each of my cameras. however there are a few things you may want to know before deciding to purchase it: (+) it is very comfortable: wide and soft and slightly elastic which makes a big difference when carrying a heavy camera + grip + lens + flash. (+) it features an array of anti-slip rubber balls in the center, which i find not just efficient but even comfortable (~) its shape is not symmetrical, being curved to match the neck. this means it is much less comfortable to hang my cameras around my neck upside down as i used to do so that the long lenses hang against my body instead of protruding. i considered attaching another female uni-loop to the battery grip to connect the strap between the top right and bottom right anchors but then the camera grips are not easily accessible. (-) it is quite short. i am 6' and it is just a little tight for me wearing it around my neck. this would be a no-no if i had not replaced the attachment straps. (-) if you use the provided attachment straps, as soon as you disconnect the neck strap itself the camera has these two long straps dangling on either side. some people like that you can attach one to the other and it provides sort of a handle. i for one find these long straps silly, especially since i like using the op/tech usa slr wrist strap (black). more on that below. (-) it has a very prominent op/tech usa logo in white on black. it might not bother you but i usually avoid doing advertizement unless i am paid for it - i even have tape over the brand and model of my cameras so as not to attract undesired attention. as mentioned above, i replaced the straps that attach to the camera. i procured a pair of op/tech usa system connector uni adaptor loop - regular which provide me with the following benefits: * slightly longer - still i can pass both a shoulder and my neck through when carrying a small camera, and it is long enough to comfortably hang my main body around my neck (with long lens and flash as needed). * can be disconnected very close to the camera body for transportation - no need to have the strap in the pelican case, it is already full. * the wrist strap already mentioned attaches to the same uni-loop on the right of the camera * i attached the removed male attachment straps to the d rings of my camera harness (opteka mch-25 multi camera carrier harness holster system for dslr cameras) to use as safety straps, attached to the left side of the camera. so here it is: each camera has two very short, unobtrusive connectors one on each side, which can be used to connect the neck strap this is all about or a wrist strap or the safety line when using a harness. this neck strap + uni-loops is also compatible with a shoulder strap extension (op/tech usa system connector sling strap adaptor) however i can't get myself to entrust the weight of but the lightest of my cameras to its plastic sliders.
summary: works best with the extension - not just for the size

i bought three of these for various locations throughout the house. i wanted actual surge protection and not just a power strip. after mucho reading of reviews i went with tripp lite. i have some other tripp lite strips at home, and they seem durable and nice. and the components inside are allegedly top-notch (although i wouldn't personally know).

this is a new style of super7. i have an older style super7 and there are two main differences.

the first is that on the new style the side plugs are closer to the end of the strip. my old style has them smack in the middle. that should not really affect anything at all, except for maybe aesthetics.

the one major gripe, though, is the on/off switch. the old style was this strong, stiff, bulky thing that required work to turn on or off. a good thing considering strips are often in the area of accidental kicks and shoves by one's feet.

unfortunately, the new super7 features a week on/off switch that can easily and accidentally be turned on or off. you now have to pay special attention to the location of the strip. even my cat could accidentally flip this off. not good when a computer is plugged into it.

two stars off for this new "feature."

reviewText:
so i had wanted a way to hook up my playstation 2 to my hdmi-only computer monitor. i tried a few converters, with varying results. this one works pretty well, though.

however, there is one caveat, but i'll get to that.

i plugged my ps2 via component cables into the box, and the audio cables into the box, and then the hdmi cable into my monitor (asus vh236h in case you're wondering).

i got picture and sound perfectly via the single hdmi cable, which is great. zero perceptible input lag is also great! i could play hot shots and shadow hearts (which require split-second timing) perfectly. yay!

but now the downside...

because the converter is also an upscaler, it upscales all 480i/480p ps2 signals to 720p. that in of itself is not a bad thing, as it really does look good. the downside is that everything is output in 16:9 widescreen. yes, even games that are not widescreen. for games that are widescreen, this isn't an issue. but... well..., i personally don't like stretched games. on my asus monitor, i cannot set the screen to display it in 4:3 non-widescreen with this converter box connected because it's a set digital signal. boo.

anyway, if you can live with it stretching non-widescreen images, you'll be fine.

4 stars out of 5.
summary: if you're a playstation 2 owner, mostly good results with this.

my original belkin f5d7010 ver 3000 card died in mac os x 10.4, tiger. this version uses the ralink chipset, and there is no currently available software for this card with tiger (see my f5d7010 review).

i then purchased this f5d7011 card, which utilizes the broadcom chipset (as in airport cards), and it it works in tiger using the airport software in my powerbook g4 (dvi, 667mhz). oddly, the normal 'airport setup assistant' application did not work, but the 'airport setup assistant for graphite or snow' hooked up just fine.

others have claimed similar success with f5d7010 ver 1000 or 2000, which also utilize the broadcom chipset. these should also work in tiger, but i have not tried these directly and cannot confirm the findings.

i'm very happy with the new setup. no more buggy ralink software, and wireless access while in os x 10.4. hope this works for you too.

reviewText:
the quality of sound coming thru my computer speakers is critical to me. the sound that comes from the "built in" sound devices on most mother boards today may provide the latest in 7.1 technology, but if you listen to music critcally as i do, there's just too much inherent noise. the answer is an add-on sound card. i prefer the ease of connection from the front bay interface that the creative card provides. all the connections for audio are there, digital and analog, except the xlr type. if you need those, other external devices can provide that. now, i'm not a gamer, so you may ask "why did you purchase a 'gamer' sound card?" well, the quality afforded  this card is not lost on me. my studio is capable of producing 5.1 surround mixes of the music i record. to mix them down i need an exacting device with stellar specs. my choices were few in the price range i wanted. the front access drive bay was the deciding factor.
this sound card connected to my logitech z-5500 speakers brings my listening experience to new heights of clarity. the built-in "crystalizer" adds impact and clarity and has a wide range of adjustment.
of course it can be shut off too, but once you hear the difference, you'll probably choose to have at least some level of enhancement. this is the best sound card i've ever purchased, and as long as motherboards provide a pci slot, any upgrades i make, i'll be swapping this sound card over. amazon.com's price with the free shipping was my deciding factor where to purchase. my local stores wanted 199.99 for the card. amazon beat that by 25.00.

i received my e250 on christmas and was quite pleased with how it worked and the life of the charge-- until today, precisely one week since i first laid my grubby mitts on it. after loading it with music and leaving about 80mb to spare, i turned it off. i get to work tonight, turn it on, and this infernal machine informs me that i don't have enough free space left to build the database and that 6mb need to be freed. even if the e250 provided a feature to delete music through the player itself (which it does not), it wouldn't matter because it won't show you any of the files. the files are there, of course, you're just not allowed to see them! i then tried to reconnect it to the computer to free up space, but the player didn't register on any usb connections unless it was in msc mode. too bad you have to be in mtp mode to have your removal noted by the player. i then went to sandisk's website to update my firmware-- the only thing that needed updating wasa *manual*-- not software! i then downloaded the sansa data recovery tool from sandisk's website-- this tool refused to recognize the sansa and told me to call customer support. i decided to cut my losses and do a hard reset of the player by following the instructions on the website-- holding down the reset button for 15 seconds. by the tone of this review, i'm sure you can figure out where i'm going with this. right, no hard reset. now i'm left with a worthless pile of cables and an equally worthless mp3 player that decided to brick itself. i know i'm not alone with this sort of problem, either.
---edit---
called sandisk tech support, and they were most helpful. they resolved my problem in under five minutes and gave me tools to fix it myself if i ever have this problem again. having nice, competent tech support goes a long way in raising the score, and i consider it a wonderful feature.

the instructions that come with this weather radio leave something to be desired in their clarity and completeness. while one can defeat some of the alarms, not all of the alarms that noaa provides are listed as one scrolls through available alarms to defeat, which is not described in the instructions. in addition, the first radio i received had some garbage readouts when i was looking for alarms to silence, and also in the county codes selection (one can set it so one only receives warnings for their area). midland customer service took awhile to get back to me, and when they did, just said this was how it was supposed to be. however, when i told amazon that i was concerned about the function of the radio i had received, they shipped me another asap without my even asking. the replacement radio had none of the idiosyncrasies of the first unit (though there is no "tornado warning," etc listed in the alarms one can defeat - this is what is "supposed to be" so one cannot turn off critical alarms). so thanks to amazon for resolving this. as an aside, note that midland charges you $7.95 to exercise your warranty if you so choose. what a deal. with the replacement radio, we are satisfied. seems to work as advertised, though we have not received any warnings as of yet, other then the noaa test alert. amazon customer service is why we give it 4 starts; it would be 2 if amazon had not intervened.
update 2/5/12: the weather radio part just stopped working, but there was no indication is was not working and no errors in the display. when i noticed the usual wednesday test today did not illuminate the "watch" light, discovered the wx radio was dead. not good. we just recently had a tornado warning in this area but this midland 300 did not emit a peep or light a warning. should have known then. i reduced my rating to two stars for midland. amazon remains at 5+ stars.

reviewText:
i live in an older house and neighborhood with old overhead power lines and transformers. voltage sags when people run their air conditioners and these units work well for boosting voltage.

i own six of the older model ss1200 which has the rectangular case. the newer ones have a trapezoidal-shaped case. i have not had any problems with the older models, but i would have to say that the capacity is rather low and it is worthwhile to consider the ss2000 if you're planning to plug in more than 5.5a total draw. the ss2000 uses the same case and has a heavier-gauge power cord, although it still seems to be the bare minimum for the rated 9.1a. however, i ordered 2 of the newer ss2000s and had problems with both (see my review of the ss2000 for details).

the last ss1200 that i bought had a cracked rear panel but is still safe to use as the crack is in the mounting hole. this is due to how these units are packaged and handled during shipment. the cord and plug are packaged at the back of the unit, and if it's dropped during shipment on the back panel, the weight of the transformer causes the plug to crack the panel. i suspect that the type of polymer used in the case has changed.

also, if you get a lemon, amazon cannot take these units back even though they are not a ups and do not contain a lead-acid battery. amazon sent a replacement, but after the second one was also a lemon, they referred me to the manufacterer which i would have to rma and send back for repair at my cost.
summary: newer models seem lacking in quality

i am reviewing only the charge case here. it works great, and has made so i can leave out of town on business travel and never need a wall outlet to charge my headset. i like that i can charge from just sitting my headset on the top charge port the let's the headset rest in a secure way, while charging on a desk. i open the case and store headset in case when i need to protect it. charges the headset quite rapidly eather way. best thing out there to protect and charge your headset on the go.
updated: after a couple months of use, the case has become unreliable. at first this only happened when setting the headset on the top charging port. but, now it is doing same thing when the headset is seated inside the case. i put the headset in the charger at night, before i go to bed. when i wake up, there is a 50/50 chance that headset will either not be charged any more than it was when you inserted it, or only charged a little more than it was. sometimes it charges perfectly. i do the same procedure every night. i seat it in securely, and confirm the indicator lights come on. this is a real problem for someone like me, who uses headset every single day for business. i have just not had long term success with plantronics products in general. i used them in the past with units falling apart within the first year. i hope this headset last longer than this charger case. disappointing, to say the least.

reviewText:
well, the 10" sub is not 5.14" deep, its 5.50 (5 1/2). i didn't think it would be but that's a bigger difference than i though. so this won't work for my original plan. that's the reason for the missing star.

update.. i have the 10 inch version installed in a 1 sq ft sealed box, pushed by 500 rms watts at 2 ohm from a boss armor 1500 watt amp and it sounds great. ill be gentle for a few weeks and then turn it up and see what it can really do. great for rock, country and some hip hop. i might add another one soon, and run both. not the best sub , but under 40.00 bucks you can't go wrong. good for adding  little boom to your ride, don't expect earth rattling bass . im pleased with it. great little sub.

update: july 3rd 2015:  i just installed the 12 inch version and it slams like a beast. i put it in 1.3 cuft ported box running the same amp, a boss 1500 watt armor that is putting out maybe 500 rms @ 2 ohms. wow, what a diff form the 10 inch sub. if you are on a budget then this is it.

i put the 10 inch in the other car, running on an old kenwood amp pushing around 300 rms at 2ohms and it adds a little boom to the ride. im impressed and pleased with both the 10 inch and 12inch subs. buy the 12inch subs they are great.

update: july 29th

i sold the 10 and replaced it with a new 12. the old 12 is still slamming away. great budget sub's. just remember to keep the amps power around the rms rating and you'll be fine. i may upgrade to a better amp soon. don't get me wrong the boss armor 1500.1 is doing a great job. both are great budget equipment. well enjoy all.

update: 08/31/15

the 12 inch sub, is still slamming away. great budget sub, glad i bought it. i now have a rockville m2 800 rms amp pushing the crap out of it.

update 05/19/2016
great budget subs, wow!!!
gave both 12 inch subs to my sister and they are pounding away. installed the subs in a 3cft vented box tuned to about 34 hz on a belva 1200 watt rms amp, and it's just sounding great. i went and bought two qpower deluxe subs and they are great budget subs too.
summary: lanzar 10 inch and 12 inch maxp subs ::::::)))))

reviewText:
these are very similar to other bluetooth headphones as far as features go, however where they stand out is the incredibly snug and comfortable fit.  they are easy to re-seat if they work loose; the earphone tips are mounted to the "tube" with the clip on it and it's just a matter of grabbing that tube and using it as a handle to readjust the position or seal.  of the wireless bluetooth headphones i've tried these are definitely the most comfortable and i have been able to wear them all day without any irritation or pain.  as far as sound quality goes i am very happy with the evenly balanced bass/treble, there is enough bass without it being so strong as to overshadow the other frequencies.  --these headphones are not something that you would buy because they have tons of bass, they are in-ear headphones that form a seal with your ear to block out a lot of the noise around you, and part of that effect is that is to limit the amount of bass a bit.
battery life seems to be around the 8-hour mark, as expected.  i did notice one odd effect when the battery was very low: the headphones would constantly disconnect/reconnect from the phone and since it uses a synthesized voice it would say "connected to phone"/"disconnected" over and over.  not a big deal, just a little odd.

my only gripe about the sound is not related to its quality but because when you adjust the volume it sends commands to the phone/tablet you're connected to, adjusting the system volume instead of leaving that as-is and allowing you to go in several steps from complete silence to the current system volume.  the main drawback is that (for me anyway) it's not possible to adjust the volume below a what i consider a fairly loud level-- it's that or mute the audio completely.  maybe for others that is as low a volume as they would want to listen to, but i have fairly sensitive ears and it's annoying not being able to adjust it to a lower volume than that.

overall these are really excellent headphones and i look forward to using them in the noisy environments i sometimes work in.  full disclosure: i received these headphones to evaluate after having some problems with the ones i originally purchased (a different model); taotronics was very helpful and responsive in resolving the issue.
summary: great quality headphones for a great price

reviewText:
defective.  if you own one of these, you *will* experienceeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee stuck keys.  why it will happppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppen to you constantlllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllllly.  what is happening is the bluetooth connection is dropping immediately after a key-down signal, dropping the following key-up signal, leaving the os to think you are holding the key down.  or alternatly the keyboard's firmware is lagging hard perhaps buffering.  then when it re-connects it sends the key-up event from some kind of buffer or a  reset commend stopping the repeat string.  which, i wouldn't overly upset if this if it was a rare occurrence, but rather this happens to me about every 8-10 minutes of typing.  that is a lot of deleting characters you never wanted to enter.  i've used this on two windows 10 computes, and even tried using two different bluetooth adapters.  i even attached the bt adapters on the end of a 3 foot cable in case usb port noise was the problem. nope, still happens when the bt dongle is touching the case of the minila.

yes it has mx cherry brown switches, which are very nice and just what you expect them to be.  but its also got:

no usb plug,  its bt only, and that's a killer with the faulty bt implementation.  it can't even fall back as a wired keyboard.
printed keycap legends.  in my experience they rub off
cheap abs keycaps.  these get worn down and shiny over time. the good keyboards are using something called pbt.
no backlight options, unlike every competing product i've seen.
and usb 3.0, which is the core of its problem.

which is a shame, i really wanted to like the unique layout with its fn switches on the thumbs.  it also has removable batteries, an utter rarity in this age of disposable tech.  its like you know guys, you can buy rechargeable aa batteries.

honestly these problem might have been worth tolerating at a much lower price point, but considering how much i paid, i expected much better.  i returned mine as defective.
summary: the only thing going for it is that its got cherry mx switches.

reviewText:
i am a delivery driver and the radios installed in our vehicles are quite poor. i have issues pulling in all but the most powerful local stations with them. i love listening to npr and unfortunately i was unable to receive my local affiliate. after getting tired of driving in silence for 8 hours a day i decided to have a look at portable units with excellent reception. this seems to be the best.

the built in antenna is not great, but usable if you like to listen to powerful commercial stations that are close by. plugging in a pair of headphones improves things a bit as the unit uses the audio cable as an antenna. things really get impressive when you use the dedicated external antenna that is included with the unit. it's a simple wire with a standard 1/8" jack. to give you an idea of the reception capability with the external antenna, i have had no trouble at all pulling in welh, a 4,000 watt station from over 20 miles away. typical commercial stations are normally 10 times more powerful. your results will obviously vary due to terrain and other factors.

a smart choice by c-crane here: there is a switch to select between the speaker, and stereo or mono sound through headphones. this means you can use a pair of headphones solely as an antenna and have the the audio sent through the built-in speaker. in other words, plugging in headphones does not automatically mute the built in speaker. you have to select that manually. the built in speaker is adequate for talk radio but i find it poor for music. it's also slightly too quiet for my liking. i'm basically nitpicking here, though. this is a pocket radio!

build quality seems good. the edge is rubberized but i'm not sure how effective that is. i have dropped it once and the batteries popped out but there has been no damage. the unit is quite light so if it's dropped from a short height i don't think much damage will be done. unfortunately it's rather bulky. i didn't like the feel of it when using the belt clip. this is most likely a trade-off between performance and portability and i'm quite glad that c-crane opted for the former. what's the point in a sleek radio if it doesn't pull in stations you like?

the button layout is intuitive. the lock switch is a great feature if you're going to be putting it in your pocket. it disables all button functions, including the power button. i would have preferred a switch for the power button, as it's rather easy to accidentally turn it off if you have it unlocked (which i prefer, so i can easily switch between preset stations).

shuffling through the preset pages is rather odd. only 5 presets are available at any one time. to enable more memory presets without having an overwhelming amount of buttons, c-crane opted for digital memory "pages". to access these pages, you must press and hold the band button and then select a page using the preset buttons. in practice this is rather cumbersome, especially if you want to select a preset station without looking at the screen. i would have preferred some sort of system where you could cycle through the preset pages sequentially.

now that i've been using the radio for a while i can comment on the battery life. with the speaker on full volume, playing 8+ hrs a day, the battery has lasted just up to two weeks. that's impressive. i'm down to one bar now and i could probably go a bit longer, but i think reception isn't as good with the weak batteries (but maybe i'm imagining things). with headphones i assume the batteries would last much longer, as those tiny speakers aren't as difficult to drive.
summary: probably one of the best pocket radios out there

reviewText:
the local computer superstore did not have an ordinary mechanical kvm switch available, so i went with the belkin on the strength of their reputation.  unfortunately, certain assumptions are made in the design of this unit that cause it to be poorly suited to use with my setup; i'm trying to control a docked dell d600 laptop and a compaq desktop from the same keyboard, mouse and monitor.  there are several issues involved which the instructions don't take into account.  first, the kvm switch wants to use the same keystroke as part of its selection sequence that the laptop wants to use as a control signal emulation; the "scroll lock" key.  this caused the need to select a different key for the laptop's control signal, which had its own set of issues as a result.  second, it turns out that the kvm switch is picky about the timing of the two keystrokes needed to swap from one system to the other; lag too long between keystrokes, or try to swap back too soon, and the sequence gets ignored.

i wish i had saved the packaging and receipt; this purchase would be going back to the store if i had, but some of the problems didn't become apparent for a couple of weeks because one of the computers involved wasn't present right away.

i'm going to replace this gadget with a mechanical switchbox from a different source.

spring loaded jaws to hold your phone expand to a max of roughly 3.4 inches. so probably holds most phones, but maybe not a galaxy note or similarly large "phones" which are more like mini-tablets. the octopus arms are cheap plastic and sometimes dislodge from their joints and have to be popped back in. also the minimal friction in the joints makes some of the joints looser than others, which can lead to inconsistent stability when posed. lastly, it has difficulty staying well gripped to other objects. best to place it on top of or hanging from other objects, but it seems to sit still for the most part. horizontally extending the apparatus from an object doesn't work too well (would need duct tape for that).

if you're a professional, i would suggest going into a store and actually trying this out to see if it's for you. also, most of the companies selling this on amazon are asian companies, so expect a very long wait for shipping and possible shipping complications. caveat emptor. the quality you get is the quality you pay for. in the future, i may buy a better constructed alternative brand of this. for basic purposes, this does fine, and the price was right.

i provided a photo of the blue version i received (i ordered purple) with a pen for size comparison.

i can't tell you how anxious i was to get this unit. so anxious in fact, i mistakenly ordered it twice.

i own the previous model (dvpcx985v) and have been very satisfied with it. this unit, the dvpcx995v, enticed me with its hdmi connectivity. this ability would enable me to add this unit to my existing home theater with no worries--so i hoped.

well, once i looked at my online bank statement and realized i had ordered two units, i had to make arrangements to return one. needless to say, both units arrived the same day, and i returned one.

and wouldn't you know it, when i hooked up the unit, i had a problem with the hdmi connection--incredibly bad banding.

i had bought a $110.00 monster cable and refused to believe i had a bad cable, so i went and bough another one. i still had the same problem. so, i hooked the unit up to another hd television with both cables; and the problem was still there.

the worst part was that, through the banding, i could tell that if the connection was good, the image quality would have been outstanding--and then i thought; what if i had kept the unit i returned?

to bring my long woeful story to an end, i figured out a way to connect my cable box with the hdmi cable and used the component connection. i must admit, even though i get a good picture, i noticed that the hdmi connection does produce a superior image. and just for those who wondered, i used startrek tng: nemesis for testing.

i set up a very simple moca network and the connection wasn't fast enough.  upgraded my splitter and added a poe, point of entry, filter.  still hold a solid connection.  after buying the poe filter i realized it was a complete waste since i am connected to a verizon fios service.  my cable connection does not continue outside the house as it might with a traditional cable tv provider.  i suspect the cable that someone ran years ago between the downstairs tv and the upstairs bedroom is of very poor quality or has a barrel connector or other connection in it that doesn't support the moca standard.

i have moved to a power line ethernet adapter which is not a suggested connection method.  it works much better than the moca network but still occasionally drops.  my power line network uses fairly old gear so i may upgrade it to the newest/fastest standard and see if that helps.

why no wifi?
summary: hard to get a good connection to my main tv box

the battery charger is considerable smaller than the chargers than came with my camera or the other batteries i have purchased.  the led display is a added nice feature that lets me see the charge state of my various batteries.

so far, i would great this a good value and a great buy!!
summary: can't go wrong with this battery charger.

i purchased the old lacie external hd a long time ago with no problems. this year i added the new d2 case when i needed more space.
the aluminum enclosure is very classy. it's small and very quiet. there is no internal fan and power supply, which avoids noise and heat build-up. the case itself dissipates heat from the hard drive. some people find the external power source a disappointment, which is baffling to me. it helps reduce the extra weight. if there is something wrong with the power supply, then at least you can easily replace it without opening the case. it comes with a very heavy metal stand which one should connect when being used alone. it is not needed when adding to another d2 unit for stacking.
i use these hard drives for dv editing in my mac. i have never come across with any bad sectors or problems, whatsoever (knock on wood). to be fair, lacie does not manufacture the hard disks, they only make the [cool] enclosures.
i have to be honest, i was disappointed with their old enclosures which were very much plastic and came with poor quality. i also have an external cd-r/rw from lacie in the old design and it did not stack up well with my old lacie hard drive. moreover, both were very noisy. they were only recommended by professionals, that's why i made the purchase.
now they solved the problem with these great d2 cases. you won't believe how quiet and sturdy these enclosures are. it looks unbreakable and expensive.  a must have especially if you were to own one type of external case.
summary: best external enclosure you will come across!

i was given this hub by a friend who bought it from amazon for me. it's maybe nine months old (in my possession), and today it has simply stopped working. it's plugged in, as always, but i leave the ports off unless i am using the devices plugged into it. now not one of the blue lights comes on when any of the four buttons is depressed.

i just don't know enough about the technology to guess at why it has stopped working. usually things with moving parts are most susceptible to breakdowns, but except for the buttons that activate and deactivate the ports, nothing else moves or has changed since i hooked this up. i have had a couple of power outages recently, but they have occurred when my mac has been asleep. perhaps there have been surges, but none of my other equipment has had problems.

i'll be buying a new hub, but i won't be buying another one of these, even though it's amazon's favorite.
summary: hub simply stopped working for no discernible reason

reviewText:
efun products are: a waste of money and time.  buy a kindle fire to get a real brand name behind the purchase (for whatever that's worth these days)

i purchased one of these for my high school daughter for lesson plans last august.  she used & enjoyed it daily through christmas, but then the headphone jack died.  i told her to live with it as the unit worked for the stated purpose and the speakers still played (always very low).  in march the unit started sticking in a boot loop.  i brought it up in diagnostic boot and found the internal memory had stopped functioning so the os was not there to load.  i called the warranty number but nobody in california ever answered (just hold music).  i'd get a call back the next day and an answer to emails, so i assume that required daylight in china not 9-5pst as stated.  they were nice.  after two weeks of email, i did get a repair ticket & i mailed it back.  they did replace it last month on the 24th.  fair enough and any small electronic can be bad.  this unit was a newer operating system and faster  --but ---

within 10 days the unit no longer functioned at all, not even diagnostic boot.  i will probably just trash it or crack it open to see the poor assembly quality out of curiosity.  many of these are assembled with masking tape inside.  that's 2 that are bad.  the 2nd one worse than the 1st.
summary: completely unreliable, no quality control in production

there is a small but growing community of people world-wide who are using this device as a very low-cost, low-power linux box.  if you are buying this for that purpose, it's a great product.  i love it for what it is.

i would not recommend this to anyone who is not a linux hacker enthusiast or a professional network administrator.  mine did not work at all until i plugged in a new usb 2.0 flash drive (it didn't even appear on my network with just a usb 1.1 external hard drive attached to it).  the documentation, such as it is (mostly on the cd that comes with the device), frequently defaults to such helpful suggestions as "if this doesn't work, see your network administrator."

in my experience, it is a lot easier to buy a second hard drive and install it in your pc than to setup one of these on your home network.

i did not buy my xps 2720 from amazon but rather from dell. it was purchased in october 2013. the first hard drive failed in november 2014, three weeks after the warranty expired. i paid dell to replace that failed hd. then that hd failed within a few weeks after i got the unit back. then it really went south when early this year i began the most frustrating, maddening experience i have ever had with any company. dell shipped me a "refurbished" replacement unit. the cpu fan in the refurb unit began squealing like a pig. so dell sent another refurbished unit. same thing (squealing cpu fan) with that second refurb unit then, believe it or not, they shipped a third refurbished unit. the cpu fan squealing was evident in that unit as well.  all of theses units, including my original purchase, were mid-2013 manufactured win 8.0 models. dell had me ship the third replacement back to them in houston to "fix" the cpu fan. the fan was out of stock. but eventually they "repaired" it. i got the third refurb unit back about three weeks ago. it has the same loud, very noticeable and very annoying noise as each of the refurb units. throughout the six months i have dealt with this i have wasted countless hours installing and re-installing software, os updates, file replacement, accommodating fedex deliveries, etc., etc., etc. it has been the absolute worst customer service and product quality failure i have ever had...for any product. and i'm a long time dell customer.

i think dell has lost their way. they farm out all customer contact to their overseas contractor. these days i recognize that that is not all that uncommon. their off shore service people are polite to a "t" and of absolutely no value in solving real problems. after five months of this i finally
wrote a personal letter to michael dell on the 22nd of may. i had to resort to that because there is no way to actually talk to or exchange emails with a live dell employee in round rock. the company has so intentionally insulated itself that it is impossible to contact anyone there other than by snail mail. i did not ask mr. dell to intercede. i simply asked him to have one of his people give me a call or email me. so far nothing.

i suspect dell makes some good products. they certainly used to. but based on my experience i think you're playing the lottery if you hope to get a quality made product. so i would absolutely, positively stay away from them if you value customer focus, customer satisfaction, after sale support and your time. from a design standpoint the xps 2720 is a gem. you won't find another desktop all-in-one that compares. but quality, reliability and and customer satisfaction has, at least in my experience, taken a back seat. design means nothing if the product doesn't work. i loved my xps 27 for about a year. but who has $2500 to throw at a new computer every year?

these sound pretty good, considering they are wireless. most people won't be able to tell the difference between a wireless vs. wired headphones. if i was mixing audio professionally, i probably wouldn't use these. if i'm watching a movie, or listening to tunes at my computer while i work, these are great.

if you take off and walk away from the base, you'll get crackle and fade. this is kind of a no brainer, i don't see why some reviews make this an issue. if you live next to an airport, a secret military installation, or the seti array or something... then you'll probably have a lot of background noise...but for most people these are pretty good on the noise/greatness ratio.

pros

----

-no cords.

-good sound.

cons

----

there is this really f***ing annoying "beep" tone that happens whenever there is no signal being broadcast. so if you put these on before you click play, you get this annoying, repeated "beep" tone. it reminds me of some of those retro games: when you're low on energy the beep was so annoying you'd look for places to kill yourself just so it would stop, the headphones have this whenever there is no broadcast signal.

all things considered, i would recommend these.

reviewText:
(using canon rebel xs) i purchased this lens last year (2012) and i'm very pleased with it. the one i have is made in japan, but was still at a low cost price.

i originally purchased mine because i wanted to experiment with snowy landscaping compositions, and it also can make a glass snowball effect. but, since i'd purchased it in autumn, i couldn't help being curious as to what it would look like if i tried some autumn foliage experiments.

it has a unique glassy distortion effect around the edges.
it doesn't quite warp your photo as much as other fisheye lenses might, but it's very fun to play with.

i would recommend using this lens with a uv filter because the glass refraction causes many images, especially when shot at noon or mid-day, to look too white-washed. using a typical uv filter will solve this problem.

i recommend using this in dimmer times of the year, especially winter (outdoor), and especially post autumn equinox, but also pre-spring equinox.

not so great for indoor use.

i bought this product at sams club when going to buy groceries, isually i always buy at amazon but this was at a smokin hot deal at $9.99. i knew the router was crap when buying it but that was not the point. at home i have a high end enterprise network setup and did not need this router. however, when i bought it i when into flashing dd-wrt to do sone cool tricks. i decided to use this for a project called mobifi. i know awful name, but i spliced the wires and grabbed a usb cable and ghetto taped them together. i hooked up the router to my powerbank and to my laptop which is intercepting internet through clockworkmod tether from my phone. when using this router for this project i noticed that when using both 2.4 and 5g on wide ht, t
the router kept boot looping. based on my troubleshooting and close analysis of dd-wrt,
's system status, the cpu isn't powerfull enough to sustain both 2.4 and 5g networks. thus boot looping. so, if you bought this router, do this:

-flash dd-wrt. its easy to do and extremly hard to mess uo.

- setup the new os with nothing connected to wi-fi and have your pc or laptop hardwired. there are many tutorials online.

-head into wireless, set 2.4g wireless network mode to disabled.

- under 5g, set wireless network mode to n only,  and set the channel with to wide ht 40 20+20.

-save changes and you're done.

** some devices only support 2.4 g and may not see the wifi netowork if you perform what is above. this is typical with really really cheap phones or legacy devices.
