reviewText:
i returned these. got them very cheap in a cyber monday deal, and that part was great. however, they were not what i was looking for. partly due to some possible too-high expectations for such a low price point, and partly due to the fact that these do not truly go over your ear, unless you have tiny child ears, maybe. i notice that currently they don't say over-ear anywhere in the listing, but they showed up in a search for over-ear headphones. so i fault that to amazon i guess.

first issue: over-ear size
the ear cups on these are round, not oval, and they will overlap and press against parts of your ears. i was specifically looking for over-ear headphones to avoid this, as i find on-ear headphones to be less comfortable for long durations and they usually leak more sound. so i was quite disappointed to find that these still smashed my ears, even though they do have quite a bit of padding.

second issue(s): build feel and quality
these have a lot of metal in them, yes. a lot of people seem to equate that with quality and durable construction, and that might be true in part. but they're extreeemely heavy. i can't imagine that being very good for long term comfort. also, only the headband is metal. the ear pieces themselves are plastic, and very cheap sounding plastic at that. when taking them out of their travel pouch or just moving them in general, the plastic rattles and clacks loudly against the metal and sounds extremely cheap.
the controls on the outside of the right ear piece are also a problem due to the plastic. when you press any of the buttons (they're all under one plastic piece that presses wherever you push it, like an apple mouse) with the headphones on your head, it's insanely loud as the clicking sound of the button travels right through the hollow plastic and into your ear.

third issue: sound quality
i will say my expectations were probably too high for headphones at this price point. they do have a lot of bass which is nice, but the sound is like swimming in mud because of it. and the "3d sound" effect sounds terrible.

even if my expectations were too high, this low cost is not worth it to me. i'd rather spend more money and be pleased with higher quality than spend all my time rationalizing something that sucks by saying, "well, it was really cheap though."

use these for cooling down my audio receiver and power amp.  i am hoping that by using the fan, i can at least avoid heat issue and possible prolong the life of the receiver.

about the fan itself, i only use it at less than half of the power.  else, i could hear the fan.  however, using less than half power, it is sufficient to keep the receiver from getting too hot.  so far only warm to touch or cold to touch, depending on the sound level.

one fan is plugged to the tv's usb port and it will turn on the fan on the receiver each time i turn on the tv and use the receiver to play the digital audio via hdmi arc feature.

the other fan is plugged to the blu-ray player so that each time i use it for playing music loud, it would cool down my emotiva power amp.

i am also glad that the cable itself is long enough to span 2+ feet.

although this fan works fine, i am taking one star away since anything more than 50% power causes noticeable noise in my setup.

yeah, it's made of plastic.  don't throw it down the stairs then.  just put it where you want it and enjoy it.  now that i've got mine set up where it can pick up stations and i've got the volume and tone set the way i want, all i do with the controls is switch between the same two stations on occasion.  so i suspect this radio will last a while.

these radios are especially useful if your home office is partially or completely below ground, like in a finished basement.  or, if you work in a metal framed office building and you want to listen to talk radio.

am signals are directional.  you need to find the location of the transmitting tower for the station you want to listen to, and then point the radio toward the tower.  that's what i did and i can listen to radio in a place where nobody else can.

it's also a good general purpose portable radio for sitting out on your deck listening to the game or music or whatever.  it's not as bulky as a "boom box" but it's got better speakers than most portable radios, so it just sounds better in return for a slightly higher price.

postscript:  in all fairness to those who comment on the build quality, i will say that my radio stays in one place tuned to one channel and maybe tuned to a second channel on occasion.  i hardly adjust the controls at all.  so, maybe those who are complaining about the construction quality have a point.  i'm just not using this radio in a way that involves moving it or manipulating the controls much.  it has a very easy life.
summary: get good reception in difficult areas without spending a fortune.

reviewText:
overall, i love asus. the products i've bought from them and read the reviews on has made their name basically synonymous with quality products for low prices. upon getting this monitor, i was rather impressed... a high-contrast, large, 144 hz monitor for this cheap? unfortunately, as a student, i don't have the extra funds to get anything more impressive than this, and my experience with asus told me that it would be worth the price. overall, it absolutely is.

the software isn't too clunky, frames are consistent, contrast is utterly fantastic for the price (although you should find the optimal settings from another website, such as this one (...)), blacks and brightness are well done, there doesn't seem to be any bleeding, and the colours are (once calibrated correctly) exceptional for a monitor like this.

unfortunately, a single pixel came stuck on arrival. this wouldn't be a huge issue if it were a dead pixel, as it's not shining in your face all the time, but it's always glowing red against basically any dark backdrop. i have tried things that have worked for me in the past (undead pixel (udpixel), works by cycling a 1x1 or 5x5 area of your screen through various colours very quickly in an attempt to unstick it... this has worked occasionally for several minutes, but inherently ends up failing. i've also tried pressing lightly against the spot with a soft but firm surface, like a pencil eraser (hasn't worked either)), but they fail as well.

overall, i absolutely love this monitor. if the pixel becomes permanently unstuck i'll bump it up to a four star rating, but so many monitors getting to customers with stuck pixels is uncharacteristically bad for asus. if you're one of the (majority of) people who gets a monitor with no bad pixels, i would say that it's a 5/5 monitor that you shouldn't pass up. however, if stuck pixels bother you to that extent, you may find this monitor to be a bit of a risk.

as i said, this is a fantastic monitor (aside from the stuck pixel issues people seem to have), and i want to wholeheartedly recommend it... but i can't due to this issue.
summary: nearly perfect, but just like every other critical review, i have a stuck pixel.

reviewText:
perfect for younger children or those that want a simple tablet and don't need all the bells and whistles of an ipad or even a kindle, the genesis prime is a solid, entry-level device.  the genesis runs on the android jelly bean 4.1 os, comes with a 1.1 ghz processr, 512 mb of ram and 4gb flash memory.  a micro sd slot allows you to add up to 32gb of additional space.  the hd player supports 1080p and of course is wfi capable.  it also features 5gb of cloud storage.  the box includes a usb cable, wall charger, earphones, quick start guide, and manual.

the display of the genesis prime is surprisingly clear and sharp.  the tablet comes loaded with google play which gives you access to thousands of android apps as well as movies, tv shows, e-books and magazines, and music.  if you don't already have one the initial setup will require you to set-up a gmail mail account.  initial setup was fast and easy although the first couple of times i tried to access google play i lost my connection to my wi-fi but after that initial hiccup i have not had a connection or signal issue since in the month i have been using it.  it features apps to play your music, movies, and books, along with a calendar and contact manager.

while you can stick with the google chrome browser that comes loaded, the processor isn't quite robust enough and chrome can be slow and lag a bit.  i would strongly suggest downloading the opera mini browser which condenses web pages before loading resulting in faster browsing.  ive used youtube and several game apps without issue.  the speaker is on the weak and tinny side to be sure but sounds just fine with headphones or a speaker like the braven hooked up to it.

the tablets camera can take either still pictures or video but, and this is a big one, is only front facing which badly limits its usefulness.  thus if you want to take a picture of something other than yourself you cant see what you are shooting.  i don't understand if you are going to make a tablet with a camera facing only one way why you would not want to have it back facing.  just makes no sense to me.  the tablet with last about 4 hours on a single charge which is mehok but certainly could be a lot better.

ive read some poor reviews of the genesis prime but those reviews seem to forget the key point that the tablet is a mere $70.  the fact is you are going to be able to do a lot of the same things with this that you can with any of the yop of the line tablets for a fraction of the cost.

reviewText:
sketchy, slow, read further to know why.

on first boot, noticed it was slow, but.. knowing that typically the first boot has many processes going on in the background, after a sysprep image is launching.

first realization there was an issue, could not connect to wifi, on any band, and with multiple access points/ routers.  troubleshooting: connected to lan fine, tried statically assigning ip/ dns for wlan, helped to connect but disconnected quickly.  then proceeded to www.support.dell.com where i learned that dell doesn't support windows 10 for this model of laptop.  i.e. if you have any hardware related issues, and need to download drivers / firmware, you are sol.  see screenshot from dell's support site, where it shows windows 7,8,xp, etc, but not windows 10.

2nd issue, windows wouldn't auto activate.  license key on bottom worked, but that is not something that a "re-certified" pc would have happen.  to be classified as re-certified, the pc needs to act just as it would shipped straight from the manufacturer.  this is most likely an issue with the sysprep process, the seller uses.

3rd issue, slooooooooowwwwwww.  ok, here is the tough part for the seller.  the laptop works, and looks decent, but most reviews note how slow the laptop is.  here is why.  the hard drive passes basic testing (smart testing/ western digital quick tests), but fails extensive tests, and it is obviously a drive that has bad clusters and or read write head mechanical issues.

these laptops ship with a platter based / "spinning" hard drive.  laptops are notorious for hard drive issues, as they are moved around with much more frequency than a desktop.  spinning platters spin between 4.2k and 7.2k rpm's, so anytime you move your laptop while it is reading/writing data, or even when its not powered on, you risk damaging the read/write head or in this case, significantly slowing down the capability of the hard drive.

spinning / platter based hard drives usually average between 80 and 120 mbps read/write speeds (think miles per hour, 80 miles per hour, etc), with an average of 80+ (when new).  over time, with the issues related to the drive being installed in a laptop as noted above, those speeds gradually drop.

first test w/out a load (nothing running, just chrome open), this hard drive tested w/ an average of 20 mbps (again, compare to miles per hour, driving hoping to get 80mph, and with the pedal to the floor, only getting 20mph).  as a tech, i recommend replacing hard drives that test w/ an average lower than 40 mbps.

2nd test, ran under a load/ with basic operations running.  office, quickbooks, chrome, etc.  yeah.. this got a whopping 2.3 mbps average read/write speed.

so, we have a laptop with a failing hard drive, not supported by manufacturer w/ the version of windows installed, oh, and with a non manufacturer/ non oem power supply (explains why another customer noted that their charger stopped working after a few weeks).

in summary, this computer fails to meet the most basic re-certified / refurbished standards.  i have had luck with dell refurbished laptops before, i usually just purchase straight from dell, but was on a time crunch w/ this one.  positive note, the seller shipped it via prime, and it did arrive fast.  however, with all the issues, simply not worth the hassle.  slapping a ssd in this one, and using the devid of the wireless card, found factory firmware updates and drivers for windows 10, which fixed the network connectivity issue.
summary: do not recommend...not fully refurbished/recertified.  tested/ benchmarked by tech w/20+ years exp.

reviewText:
well they support music playback and have a mic, that's about all that is good about them. the actual performance of these headphones leaves a lot to be desired. the reason i purchased these was because of reviews claiming of good audio quality (on earphones and mic), as well as the quoted 7 hour battery life. my intended use was for work, to go seamlessly from listening to music to a google hangout or skype conference call and back multiple times a day. i need high quality audio with noise cancelation, these don't deliver that in any way.

if you are just listening to music, it will sound decent, but noticeably worse than even cheap wired earbuds. once you activate the mic for a phone or conference call, it's like going back to a 90's era cell phone. the product description claims bluetooth aptx support, but connected to my mac and using the bluetooth developer tools i'm unable to even force aptx codec use (necessary for good quality wireless audio over bluetooth). paired to my iphone, listening to music and going onto a call exhibits the same audio quality issues.

oh, that microphone on these headphones doesn't exhibit any noise-canceling properties at all. in the office i expect it to only pickup my voice, maybe some overly loud background noises, but what i found out in testing was that even faint background noises were being picked up and transmitted to the receiving party. outdoors on a quiet neighborhood street i had to shout to be heard above what was at most a 5mph wind.

in both sound quality departments, these are far inferior to the apple earpods bundled with every iphone going back a few years. guess i'll have to try a different product.
summary: look elsewhere if you want quality

reviewText: i bought the sennheiser hd555 from amazon this week, exclusively for use with my ipod touch. i already own the ue super.fi 5 pro canal phones and they are great indeed, but i was wanting a set of headphones for both work and home that were easier to put on and take off.  the super.fi pros take a few moments to get the seal right.  i must say that i was rather disappointed with the hd555.  so much so, that on the following day  i  purchased the bose on-ear headphones. yes, the sennheiser hd555 have a more defined midrange and more pronounced high's than the bose on-ears do.  but why is it that i was so unsatisfied when listening to them?  i listened to the bose headphones, and enjoyed their presentation far more than the hd555's.  i played a orchestra/vocal mp3, "gollum's song", with emiliana torrini, and recorded at 320 sampling rate rate, and the hd555 sounded better than the bose, so i will add my confirmation to the others, that for classical and orchestrated music the hd555 will noticeably outperform the bose on-ear's.  ...but.  the bose did quite well with that and other orchestra pieces too and just gave such a more well-rounded performance on all different types of music than the hd555 did. amongst many other songs, i listened to the beatles' "come together" and the hd555's disappointed badly there, and i had to turn the eq bass booster on to get any satisfaction at all from it. the bose were very nice with no eq, just the right amount of bass, both felt and heard.  not muddy at all, but deliciously warm. if the sound that came out of headphones were edible, i would say that the hd555's are fat-free vanilla ice cream.  the overpriced bose on-ear's are creamy chocolate truffles for your ears.  on the physical side of things, the sennheiser hd555's are quite comfortable, but leak a great deal of sound and it is clear by the rather large audio plug that not much thought was given to the design for connecting it to an ipod.

the batteries are sigmastek that i just received.  i am not sure how the brand will stack up, but they are about half the cost of a genuine rbc7.  keep in mind this listing/product has had various sellers over the years.  the current seller is batterysharks.com and you can buy these $3 cheaper on their site (not sure if it ships as fast though, i have prime).

it's a simple process to setup the batteries...place them so the connectors are in the middle (one positive will be next to the other's negative).  pop the terminal covers off your original battery (held on by 4 pieces of double-sided foam tape).  if you have double-sided foam tape that can be used to tie the batteries together, but you have be accurate...and easier method is to hook up the fusible link and then simply run a piece of packing tap across to top width-wise and then a couple pieces around the sides and bottom....make a 3" tape flap at the fuse end so you can pull the battery out next time.  connect the power leads (make sure positive and negative are correct)...pop the two terminal covers back on and as you have it about ready to slide in connect the plug inside the ups to the new battery....pop it in and you are back in business after a couple screws and putting the cover back on.

with smart ups 1500's and ibm 2130r5x/ups1500tlv's these can be done without turning off the ups and without having to power down any connected devices (hot-swapable).

even with my genuine rbc7, i am lucky to get 2 years out of a battery set as i am coastal and the power flucuates constantly turning the day.  if i get more than a year out of these, i am still ahead.  they come in a sealed factory box as well, some vendors ship used batteries that are almost impossible to tell from new (other than getting much less life) or batteries that have been sitting on a shelf for a year+ which also will have shorter lives.

reviewText:
i just finished building a htpc/gaming pc but with my space limitations i had to be very careful with what components i chose but would give me the best bang for my hard earned $ & look right on top of my entertainment center. i found & ordered this after looking for @ 2 weeks of searching.

the case has very nice/clean lines and 2 usb3.0 connectors in front, a fold  down cover so you don't always have to see the optical drive or usb connections, a switch on the bottom to dim or completely hide the red & blue hdd & power lights (i actually disconnected the red hdd light), enough space for m-atx motherboard, room on the right side for up to 3 80mm case fans & enough room for a full size atx psu ( more on that in a bit).

the components i chose for my build (& very happy with my selections) fit except my bd-rw drive - there simply was not  enough room for my lg drive & a full size psu so had to find a modular small form psu! even with 90 degree sata cables & psu adapter it would simply not fit the case!

the only drawbacks i can really think of is that the motherboard connectors (power switch etc., internal usb3.0 header cable & audio cables) are just too long in my opinion - i was able to do a lot of cable maintenance/hiding/cable tying duing the build but you can only do so much & the fact that it has silveerstone in white letters on the front

i had to buy a sata power splitter because the way i have my pc setup is my ssd in under my optical drive & my 3.5hdd in mounted in the front by the 80mm case fans - not a bad idea though, this way one fan is pulling the heat off the hdd !

my build consists of the following components:
intel i5 4690k on stock settings
coolermaster gemini 2 low-profile cpu cooler with a 120mm noctua pwm fan
gigabyte ga--z97mx gaming 5 m-atx mobo
8gb hyper-x fury memory
3 noctua 80mm pwm fans for cooling
samsung 840 256b ssd
seagate 4tb 3.5hdd for media
intel 180gb m. 2 ssd for game storage
zotac nvidia 750gtx low profile video card
lg bd-rw burner
silverstone 450watt sfx modular psu

the system stays very cool & quiet & from @ 15 feet away i cannot hear it!

if you decide to purchase this case for a new build i would highly suggest checking the component fit & plan out your cable routes before securing everything down

good luck!

reviewText:
mixed feelings over this product. for it's price, the specifications are outstanding. but i'm not sure of the component quality and i'm less than happy with the much touted 3 year warranty.

within a few months of purchase, the sound system started acting buggy.  the pc is connected to a tv via hdmi.  in order for the audio to pass to the tv, the tv had to be turned on for a few minutes prior to the pc being powered on. checked the cable, tv hdmi input by using another pc and it is definitely something to do this product. emailed support and was met with a "never heard of this before, did you try a different cable? type of response. decided to just always turn in the tv first as a work around.

about 1.5 years along, the hdmi has gone out all together and a fan sounds like its about to die.  did all the normal trouble shooting. - ie changing cable, different hdmi input choice, different pc, etc and it's definitely this machine. opened it up to see if i could just replace hdmi - nope, it's part of either the mother board or card. not sure as i didn't dig around as i didn't want to void the warranty and i'm not a computer whiz so none of this is instinctive.

contacted support and was told to use an air can to blow out the fan as that's usually the problem with fan issues.  and for the hdmi problem, aaron told me that i'd have to reformat the entire machine since it's probably a bad driver. when i responded with, "no, that's not normal process for a corrupted driver."  aaron insists that i have to reformat the entire machine first.

um, no.

so, if you need a cheap no name pc that works decently for 1.5 years, this will be fine.  i'll use it as a backup machine until it dies as the vga connection works fine.

for htpc (always on and used 16 hours a day) it didn't work for us.
summary: decent but will not buy from seller again

reviewText:
the tripod is not all bad. but it's not all good either.

pros;
-bubble level on the head.
-quick release uses a nice, easy lever.
-the head rotates nicely to the vertical (portrait) position and is still quite stable.
-locks for the head tilt, the panning and the column seem to hold fairly well.

cons;
-there are no position locks for the legs. this means that the legs have to almost go to a horizontal state. there is nothing to keep them at a higher angle like a normal tripod. so, if you have a very small working space like i did once, you will be out of luck. you will need a minimum of 9 inches across when the legs are in the shorter position.
-the suction cup is useless, but that's not a surprise.
-the head and panning mechanism are not exactly small.
-another proprietary quick release.
-the height the column adds is negligible and almost nil, because of the way the legs lie nearly flat you have to have the column extended just to have a stable tripod. if it's lowered then the legs won't flatten out, so it will be unstable. so you gain maybe a 3/4" with the legs in the extended position, and only 1/2" in the retracted position. the other reviewers are maybe over-estimating the benefit of extending the legs or they are attempting to use the tripod with the legs at a steeper, less stable angle.

reviewText:
i agree with the reviews that speak of the good features of this tripod... it is lightweight, easy to set up, compacts to a reasonable size, and is not difficult to carry.

i purchased this tripod in 2004 but have never used it with my video camera; it always held my still camera. this year, i began using my video camera and a tripod was needed for smooth panning and tilt for an hour-long shoot. the subject was a corporate trainer whose motions did not follow a predictable path.

the first taping, i found the joints a little sticky, even though the clamps were loosened. to prepare for the next taping, i attempted to lubricate he mechanism. that is when i realized that the design and construction was the cause and not that the tripod needed the lubricant.

the construction of the joints had large clearances thus the tradeoff was keeping the adjustment snug or allowing the maximum freedom to eliminate the stickiness. on the second taping, i loosened everything up and was more careful. some erratic movement could be edited out and some was compensated by the video camera's steady-cam features.

while i like this tripod for my still pictures i would suggest evaluating other tripods for video use when panning, or tilt is needed.

reviewText: this is my first ever pair of bluetooth headphones so i don't have anything to compare them too. i normally use the koss wired ones with the foam inserts that i had replaced with the howard leight foam earplugs that i wear at work, but with holes made in them for the sound. i found the rubber plugs to be hard to get used to and don't block sound as much as a foam plug. the design will keep me from changing that over till i have time to look at them on the work bench and make my own modifications. the sound is much better than my old $30.00 wired ones by far. i like the fact that the headset tells you when it is on, what the power level is when turned on, and whether it is connected. on the negative side, i have found that the headset will tell you when the power level is half way but, at least on mine, it will say it is low and then turn off. i'd rather have a little warning time on that. i have read that the bluetooth function on the phone is somewhat limited and i have not tried that, but can say that when listening to audiobooks the distance is quite good. it will work around corners and metal cabinets in the factory like the phone is right in your pocket - impressive. another negative is that the sound is always skipping a beat, kind of like a record (for those of you that are familiar with that) that has an occasional skip of the beat from lint or a minor scratch. that drives me batty and does it no matter where the phone is located on my person or on a table in front of me. mind you that i have not tried this with music and it could be the formatting of audiobooks but i don't hear it when played on my desktop pc. don't know if i should return them for this reason or not. they will run all day on a charge which is nice. i have used them when working sometimes but because i have to tilt my head i am always pausing and starting at inopportune times so now i just turn them off if i have something to do. i wish the buttons were designed a little different from this standpoint because if you were outside doing house maintenance you would always be pausing and starting from your neck or chin pressing the control. i also purchased one of the aftermarket covers and found it a good investment when using this type of product if you are active. i will update if i have anything else to add. update 10-32-14:after having the unit for several months i have gotten used to the ear buds somewhat but after extended use they still make my ears sore. that being said i have not had any playback issues with any of my recent audiobooks. don't know what was causing it except it could have been the mp3 book i was listening to. that said i don't like the position/tactile response of the buttons. when i have these on and am working i have activated some of the functions with my chin or the side of my jaw when leaning over to so something. that's frustrating! but i guess it works for those that don't have to lean their heads over to do their job. the battery will report the power level when activated and all i have heard is fully charged and medium. from medium there is no warning that the battery is low and the unit will just shut off, another disappointment. all in all it is not a bad unit but after living with it for so long i don't think it was worth the premium price i paid. i think the present price is closer to a fair deal for this.

i received these as a christmas gift  ( otherwise i would have returned )  my loved one begged me to tell him exactly what i wanted. without hesitation i said "jabra smart halo " i have wanted this set for weeks. my dream was to have a set of bluetooth headphones that had amazing battery life and sounded great for phone calls and all day listening of podcasts. then i tried them...

here is what i like about them :

*  battery life is amazing !!! yes,  they deliver on the 17 hour promise. i wear at work for my entire 8 hour shift and i can go two days without a recharge. the charging port is on the collar. there is a small rubber attached cover, its a mini usb but the included cable fits it best. these cannot be used while charging. fully recharge is 1 1/2 hours.

* connection is instant and stays connected. range is about 30 to 50 feet in real world conditions ( work room floor)

* sound is very good. i mostly listen to podcasts. for podcasts the sound is more than acceptable, very clear and rich tones to voices. with music again very acceptable. i think they need a little bit more bass.  do i dare say my skullcandy smoking buds 2 wireless sound better for music?

* the collar is good. i am a small person and it fits perfectly . they stay on my neck. i have a very physical job and these stay put.  the buds are magnetized ( just barely ) so when they hang down they are secure. you can also pull the buds apart to answer calls or put them together to end calls <--- i find it a little hard to do before my call goes to voice mail. most of the controls are on the right side of the collar. they are raised so you can quickly learn to feel for them rather than having to take the collar off. the left side has the siri/google button <--- i don't use this feature.

* the buds themselves stay in my ears perfectly ! i have small ears so these work well for me. again i have very physical job and these have never fallen out yet.  i have already lost one bud cover... comfort wise they are good.  i wear them for 8 hours ( very little out time ) i wish the portion that goes in the ear was longer. its very short and the business part of the bud kind of pushes up against my ear.

* volume is excellent.**** update *** left side started decreasing in volume at almost the 2 month mark. now almost completely silent and garbled on left side....  overall volume was decreasing with use

* build quality is excellent. we have an older set of jabra wired over the ear headphones that still work beautifully after 3 years of daily commuting on the train. i am hoping these have a long life too.

* vibrate feature is excellent, these vibrate with off/on and with incoming calls.

now here is what i hate about them  !

phone calls are horrible on these !!! i love to talk to my family and friends while i work. my callers can instantly tell i'm not on my usual set. the microphone picks up everything in the background and presents it loudly to your caller. i work with paper my friend can hear me moving paper around... they can hear my coworkers in the background ( i work with  normal people not yellers )  perhaps if you make calls from a silent location these might be for you. one of the main reasons i purchased these was for quality phone calls... they are advertised being able to take calls anywhere. pretty much useless to me for phone calls. did i get a bad set ?
summary: useless for phone calls !!!! defective and jabra will not support !!! no warrenty coverage

reviewText:
as a user with lots of usb devices and limited built in ports on my machine, a good usb hub is a must.  i've been using an older usb 2.0 hub for a while in spite of having upgraded to numerous usb 3.0 capable devices (most notably a couple of external hard drives).  having finally made the move to a 3.0 hub i am extra pleased.  as far as usb hubs go, this one has pleased me in a number of ways.

size - from time to time i've been given some free "swag" usb hubs by vendors wanting to promote their company.  some of these were insanely large for the number of ports and capability they provided.  this sabrent 7-port hub is similar in size to a pack of playing cards.  it takes up very little desktop space but is still large enough to have something plugged into all 7 ports without trouble.

speed - naturally, the main benefit i saw immediately on upgrade was speed.  going from usb 2 to usb 3 is fabulous.  my hard drives can now transfer at full capabilities.  my phone charges much faster.  it's lovely.

power switch - when i first got this, i wasn't sure why i would necessarily care about having a separate power switch for each port on the hub.  then i remembered experiences i'd had with an older hub where having multiple high power usb devices plugged in at a time would result in some of them not being recognized (due to not being served enough power to run).  in the past, i would have to unplug on or more devices to get another one to run and then i'd have to find the plug and plug it back in later.  being able to leave the cable plugged in and just press a button is handy.  it's still not a feature i use a lot but it's kind of cool.

overall this has been a great option.

****
4.5 out of 5 stars

reviewText: hey, it's 2014 now and this product came out over 10 years ago. the reviews here are mixed for various reasons - but the key point probably should be - this was the top of the line, super expensive unit in 2004 and about the best in the <$500 consumer market. but technology has changed considerably. it's pretty easy to get a good $100 or less model that does everything a consumer would ever need for driving. i lost the mount, cradle & power cords on a trip 7 years ago and eventually replaced the unit with a new model because the missing parts cost more than a new one. those lost parts just turned up this weekend - and after 7 years i pulled it out and used it. the first time, it took about an hour for the disk drive to release and start working and the unit to figure out where it is - but after that it worked just fine - and as a good as it did 10 years ago. please, nobody buy this unit any more - probably at any price but certainly not above $50. i just saw 7 magellan models: 5220-lm, 5230t-lm, 2220-lm, 5045-lm, 1700-lm, 2240t-lm, 2255t-lmb are all available around $150 or less and refurbished units often $50-$75. i think the -lm means lifetime map updates - so as new map updates become available (which isn't all that often) - you can update the unit with them. my newer  units are in the 2000 & 5000 family - and both work good. the size and pretty minor (imho) feature differences are most of the differences. if you can figure out how you plan to use it and what features you feel are essential - i'd suggest buying the cheapest roadmate that does that. if you're just an occasional, get it out to find a new location - definitely any of the modern $100 units will be all you need.
summary: the time for this model has come and gone.

reviewText:
i use an ipad pro for work with clients off-site, and a keyboard (and machine protection) is a must-have. this combination case is as good as we've found, but the detractions were far too great for me.

first, the positives. the case weighs about as much as the ipad, so together you're looking at about two pounds. for some that detracts from the levity of the machine, but the alternative, for me, is a light laptop--so i'd be looking at two-pounds either way, and likely more. when the case is closed, the ipad is totally protected, enclosed inside the hard plastic that's as tasteful as plastic gets. i felt confident enough just slipping the whole unit into my briefcase until in-field work time. also, the magnetic catch system works well to hold the ipad up for viewing or typing.

but the most important aspect of a keyboard, to me, is the typing experience. and after trying four other portable bluetooth keyboards, i'm not impressed with what i've found so far because important keys are often moved about to save space. on this belkin keyboard, for example, the return/enter key, the right shift key, the (right) semicolon/colon key, the apstrophe/quotes key, and the right quote key are all at unexpected places or too near/too far for me to easily get accustomed to.

if this were the only keyboard i used, i supposed i'd become acclimated to it, but switching back and forth between this and standard keyboards just won't work. i never get used to the layout of the belkin keyboard. it's extremely frustrating to have to lift my hands off the keyboard to check where the above-mentioned right keys sit, or if i think i've finally gotten the feel of the keyboard and type without looking, to find myself returning-new-line instead of inserting an apostrophe or shifting...

the feel of the case and keyboard is about as good as i've found, and the protection for the ipad is outstanding. but i couldn't get used to the belkin's layout. to contrast, i bought the original ipad six to seven years ago and paired it with a logitec bluetooth keyboard. that keyboard's layout so effectively mimics a standard keyboard's that today, years after my original ipad has ceased working, i still use the logitec keyboard, pairing it with my phone or my lenovo tablet or even my laptop when i take it into the field for presentations, so i can type while a group is viewing my files.

at least i've concluded that any keyboard that changes the orientation of the main keys--including shift, return, apostrophe/quotes, colon/semicolon, cannot compensate with other desirables. one final note:  if possible, especially with these high-tactile devices, try to borrow one from a friend for a week or so to see if it will work for you. you should know in a few days. if i'd bought this from a local best buy, i'd have returned it within 48 hours.
summary: terrific ipad protector, but poor right-keys orientation may create significant typing liability

i am a highly technical person, and have used print servers in the past (they are not very complicated).

the print server got an ip address from the router without a problem. the software installed fine, and i was able to browse to the server ip address and configure options. there was just one problem: print jobs never went through. as an alternative, i tried setting up my printer as an ipp printer (as one of the reviewers suggested), but no no avail.

customer service/technical support is a joke. the manual, the "read me first" card and the telephone greeting all give different hours for technical support. i waited on hold for about 20 minutes, until the recording finally said they were transferring me to a company representative, who would take my contact information & i would receive a call back (this was purportedly being done to avoid any further wait time). i was then transferred to an extension that never answered (it just rang and rang).

note: my printer (samsung scx-4100) is on the list of compatible printers.

my advice: don't waste your time with this device.

reviewText:
in short, i'm glad i waited.

our harmony 880 finally started to die on us after years of service. not sure what it was that was killing the ir, but it finally wouldn't control our devices. we had been putting off the upgrade because:

at first, the harmony one was getting long in the tooth. we knew there were newer ones coming, so we waited.

the harmony link seemed cool! then we heard that it required an always-on internet connection to work and the settings were all stored online. if the server went down, a connection was temporarily lost, or your internet so much as looked at you sideways, it would stop working. this was unacceptable, so we waited.

the harmony touch seemed to be a bad layout with no other benefit over the harmony one, so we waited.

all the while, only one device could be associated with one account. that's nearly inexcusable. a different email address for each device is required? who thought that was a good idea?

the harmony ultimate solves all of these problems except for one, which i will get to in a moment. your configuration is stored locally on the hub, so if your internet connection goes down, it is no longer an issue! fantastic! when you use the app (which is phone only, not tablet. i hope this is fixed in the near future) it pulls the configuration and information from the hub, and the hub keeps all devices in sync as opposed to a server online. moreover, all devices remain aware of the current state of the home entertainment system and devices. if i turn on watch tv with the remote, the phone says watch tv is active and so on. fixed the link's problem!

the ultimate is the newest model, with what appears to be a super-reliable charging cradle. so while the one is good it shows its age in comparison to the ultimate. i just set the hub where it can see my whole entertainment center and it no longer matters where i'm sitting. no more doing the volume dance where i try to find a line of sight to the stereo with the remote that's in my hand. i just hit volume, and the hub sends it no matter where i am. fixed the one's problem!

also, your account now allows multiple devices! fixed that too!

here's the one thing they didn't fix. vs the touch, the screen still sits below the play/pause. when i have to hit those buttons, i have to carefully avoid hitting the touch screen, which is now a gesture control which could accidentally fast-forward or such. this was a horrible decision they haven't yet fixed. that said, it's no dealbreaker as i can still use the remote; it's just more difficult. this is the sole reason i give it 4 stars instead of 5.

other than that, the remote is surprisingly small. smaller than the 880, so my thumb can actually reach the whole thing if needs be. the tilt sensor is vastly improved as well, so when i pick it up, i don't need to shake it to make it wake. very nice.

my only suggestions for future improvements are as follows:

move the play/pause/ff/rew below the touchscreen. for the love of all things good, do this in the next iteration.

and two, now that a website is synced with the hub... let me control the entertainment center using the app remotely. i don't mean from somewhere in the house. i mean when i'm not in the state. i know it's a weird thing to ask for, but when we're visiting family, it would be nice to turn on animal planet for the dog to keep her from barking all the time, or set a schedule that turns the tv on like an alarm clock, but only on weekdays or such. also, it would be great if we could turn the whole system off when we realize we're going to be gone longer than we thought that night. we could also turn the tv on as a "we're home, don't break in!" measure remotely. these are all nice-to-have compared to moving the screen though.

lastly, please provide a tablet version of your app for both ios and android! maybe a window 8/rt/phone app? and please, please, please put it on amazon's app store. there's no reason not to, and there are probably millions of kindle fires out there that could be remotes for this awesome hub!

i can not say enough good things about this remote though. it is the first suitable replacement for the one or the 880 that i have seen to date. very well done. if you have fewer devices, the less expensive $129 will only have 3 activities on the remote, and i don't know if it limits the app, but it also has the hub. (which is awesome)

i would have given it 5 stars, but i spent more than 2 hours trying to figure out what i have done wrong, after completing the wiring and connecting the unit, i turned the ignition key to on but the unit did not program itself. after re-setting the unit and observing the led flashes feedback to see which wires were connected and what radio brand the unit was connected to (as indicated in manual), it showed that there were 4 wires connected out of seven when it should have shown only two, and the correct radio (kenwood). i then tried to do a manual programming but was unable to do so
i proceeded to re-check the wiring and it appeared that the wiring was ok (as indicated in instruction). i view that i remembered reading a review in amazon that the green/orange was really yellow/green, i reviewed the installation manual and noticed that i connected the green/orange wire (which is pin 4 from the aswc-1 connector) to the pin 7 wire of the car connector (toyota solara 2007) as indicated in the connection instructions downloaded from the manufacturer website, but the right way to do it was connecting the yellow/green wire (pin 3 of the aswc-1 connector) to the pin 7 wire of the car connector.
once i had the correct wires connected, i reset the unit and immediately programmed itself and all the steering wheels control bottoms work as designed. the manufacturer needs to revise the wiring instructions!!!!

reviewText:
i have to laugh at myself when i realize how hooked i am to this gadget.  i remember having a conversation with a woman in my exercise class who was walking and listening to her ipod.  i asked her what the benefit was to having an ipod over listening to a radio.  she said you can listen to what you like and not to what the dj decides to play.  i could not relate because i just thought "so you change the station".

i bought a palm tx and decided to venture into using the mp3 feature just out of curiousity.  well, i became addicted.  before i knew it i was searching for a good buy on a 1 gb sd card because i had use up my 512.  then i spoke to a friend who said that an mp3 player gives you more space and you don't have to buy expansion cards.  so, i was on the web reading reviews and searching for the best player.  i searched and compared for a couple of weeks and bought the creative zen micro photo 8 gb black.  i was amazed at how small it is compared to my palm.  but, i was impressed with the capacity of this player.  it sounds great and was not hard to figure out.  the touch pad is a little "touchy" but i feel that i will adapt. my greatest criticism is the usb charger/sych cord, it is much to short making it awkward to access when transfering music (this is why i gave it 4 stars).

i was leary of using yahoo unlimited and had in fact previously canceled my trail subscription because it was giving me more challenges than i needed.  i was using napster and was pleased with the service.  curiosity got the best of me so i inserted the cd that came in the zen mp box and downloaded the engine.  right off i notice that there were updates added. so, i was encouraged that the bugs may have been addressed. i also found the transfer of music to the device to be very simple.  you don't need wmp to do this unlike napster.  also the "to go" version is cheaper than napster's as is the costs to burn a cd.

i am truly into my zen mp.  i feel good about not getting caught up in the ipod madness.  i read many of the reviews and believe i made the best choice.  in nearly a week i have transfered 200 songs. i look forward to exploring for new songs.  this is a great player at a good price.

i installed the seagate slim (for mac) 500 gb (model stcf500102) on my
imac 3.2 ghz running os x 10.7.5. it is plugged directly into the usb
port on the back of the imac using usb 3.0.

the unboxing went well: the packaging was minimal, the build quality
appeared fine and the drive case was very compact. it came with a rather
short 18" usb cable but this wasn't a problem for my imac setup.

after installing and powering up the drive, i ran the apple disk utility
"verify disk" which turned up no obvious disk problems.

i'd already installed the seagate dashboard software (this software was
present on this drive) from a previous seagate installation. since i
encountered problems using the seagate dashboard and drivers from that
previous installation, i did not reinstall it for use with this drive.

i copied some rather large mp4 files to the drive and ran them using
quicktime player. the files ran fine so basic disk operations worked
fine for simple tasks. the drive was very quiet during the copy and play
operations. i did not run any other significant benchmarking tests so
can't comment on performance of this drive.

pros:
  * solid build
  * quiet operation
  * minimal packaging

cons
  * buggy driver/dashboard software which appears to negatively impact
performance
summary: good quality but has software flaws

i was looking for a bag that can handle my 17" dell, 40d with battery pack, and several lenses during travels. it's my fault that i didn't bring along all my gears when i bought this from a local store.

negative points:
1) when i place the camera in the middle slot and push the drawer/rover system, the plastic clip in the middle scrathes the lcd screen of my 40d.
2) contrary to my initial expectation for the "rover" line, it's not easy to put out your camera from the bag to shoot a fleeting moment; i bought a crumpler 6m usd home just to supplement this purpose.
3) the slot for the 17" laptop is still cramped. although sufficiently foamed, space is not really slotted for a laptop. (perfect envelopes and folders though)
4) 40d with battery pack seems too big already for the drawer compartment.
5) 70-200 lens is already cramped as well.
6) in general, bag is too big to look at, but surprisingly cannot accommodate much.

i think the -trekker system (gears placed in vertical array slots) is still better in the end. consider the computrekker aw (even not "plus," still can handle 17") or vertex line if you want one bag for camera + laptop, or just buy a separate bag for laptop and separate for gear--something big like phototrekker to provide for that 500 mm lens that you're eyeing.
summary: consider the computrekker or vertex model instead

reviewText:
i have been running two d-link dcs-1100 wired ip cams for over three months now.

pros: this is a reasonably priced, solid camera with a fairly broad range of functions. i have successfully used the ftp feature to upload images every few seconds to an archive server on the both the lan and wan sides of my cameras. in general the camera tends to keep working and not freeze up. the streaming video image is best viewed from the home page of the web based control interface.

cons: my biggest problem with the dcs-1100 is that the web based control interface cannot be used at all in firefox and tends to freeze up in safari. if you're like me and you don't use internet explorer for security reasons (especially all those active-x goodies), you're likely to have difficulties configuring and managing this camera. also the ability to insert streaming videos into a web page doesn't seem to work reliably or consistently for anything other than ie, and even then there are some issues. finally the light range is adequate at best which means that in order to get any night vision at all, i am obliged to suffer a bit too much brightness during the day.

one of my two ipcams replaced a usb webcam, but since i didn't have the option of continuing to run a usb webcam, my best guess is that, notwithstanding its faults, there is nothing better than the dcs-1100 for anything near to its price range.
summary: dcs1100 ipcam works best with internet explorer

reviewText: this iogear 2 port kvm switch (gcs612a) is a great switch if you have simple needs to share a monitor, speakers, keyboard, and mouse with two desktops.  i bought this to help with the upgrade process when i recently bought a new pc but kept my old monitor.  it is very easy to use, and the directions that come in the package are very straightforward.  there are clearly marked inputs for each component with a corresponding set of connectors for each desktop.  after connecting everything, a simple double hit of the "scroll lock" key seamlessly transfers control between the two machines.  after reading some negatives on sound quality, i decided to do a test and compare the sound on my new pc between using the switch and directly connecting the speakers to the desktop.  my speakers are nothing to write home about, but i could not tell any substantial difference between the direct connection and going through the switch.  you mileage may vary depending on your speakers.  one item to note is that the switch only workers with externally powered speakers.  the speakers on my old pc plugged in through a special port that powered them so they did not work.  luckily i already had another set that had its own power source.  the one thing the switch will not do is connect the microphone on my monitor.  i really don't use it so this is not a problem for me.  when choosing a kvm switch, you should make sure that all of the components that you want to share have a connection on the switch.  overall, this is a very solid product for the limited scope that i needed.

i purchased two of the aj130 alarm clock/cd/radios on december 4, 2007,
from another online retailer, and was excited to do so, as my wife and i are owners of other philips clock radios with the "gentle wake" feature (she has the aj3965 and i have the aj3980).  my intent was to buy two matching, smaller, sleek models with similar functions to the ones we were replacing.  both of us really like the "gentle wake" feature of the philips line.  i set both of the clocks up, and, to my dismay, the gentle wake feature, which is advertised as included on this model, does not function.  i figured that, perhaps, one was defective and that i might have to return it, but then when the feature didn't work on either of them, i thought better and wrote to philips, asking them whether or not he gentle wake feature, said to be one of this model's features, actually exists in this model.  a phone call solved nothing -- upon my suggestion that they consider bench/lab testing this model for that function, the tech support guy told me that they weren't able to do that.  how about that?!?!  the manufacturer of the darn clock can't even test it.  makes you wonder.

really, my only complaint about the unit is the fact that both new units lack the touted "gentle wake" feature.  it is not a misprint or an error on the website -- it is advertised on the unit's packaging.  i'm also very familiar with how the feature works.  on the other two models i mentioned, the gentle wake gradually increases the volume of whatever the wake-up setting is (radio/cd/buzzer) until it reaches a maximum level.  in fact, on the aj3965, you can even set what the maximum level you want it to reach is.  on the aj130, the gentle wake is only applicable to the buzzer setting, so cd and radio do not gradually get louder -- they stay at whatever level you have the volume set at before you go to sleep.  when the alarm goes off, though, if you have it set on "buzzer," the volume goes straight for the jugular -- there ain't nothin' "gentle" about that "wake."

it's a sad situation, because philips makes good products, but i think they really goofed with this one.  it might turn out that they just happened to manufacture a "bad batch" of them, but i have a feeling that this is more than just a bad batch.  i question whether or not the gentle wake feature really is supposed to be promoted as included on this model.

i've written to philips consumer electronics about this problem.  i'm somewhat leery of sending them my clocks for an exchange, as i'm afraid that the two that i receive in return will lack the same functionality, and what's more -- i'll be out whatever it cost me to ship them.

i don't know.  buy at your own risk.  i only say that i would not recommend it to a friend because of the fact that the feature is absent when it is supposed to be present.  if they fix that issue, then i would recommend it.

reviewText:
i bought this headset for use with dragon speech recognition software and skype. i've been using both programs with a variety of microphones for many years. this is the first microphone that failed.

even with the maximum volume, people were barely able to hear me over skype and many words were missed in dragon speech recognition. i have been using dragon for four years and this is the first microphone that failed so spectacularly. most microphones give you a wide range of adjustability when it comes to microphone input volume or at the very least a "microphone gain" option.

unfortunately, andrea chose not to make its own drivers for this headset but instead opted for generic usb audio drivers. these generic drivers do not have a microphone gain option. as a result, you cannot set the volume of the microphone to a usable level.

for those wondering, i did try every possible microphone boom position short of swallowing the damn thing. i also scoured the web for any possible solution to that the aforementioned generic drivers and found nothing. in short, this thing is going back!
summary: be warned -- maximum microphone volume too low! unusable!

reviewText:
got these as a possible replacement for the jaybird bluebuds x (which keep shorting out because -apparently- my sweat dissolves plastic)...not so much.

good
 - bluetooth works pretty well

so-so
 - control module feels bigger than it needs to be

bad
 - fit isn't great, even with comply tips
 - little 'wings' on the earbuds to help them stay put are too short/too flimsy to work well; they pop out of my ear frequently and, if i'm sweaty, barely stay in at all
 - cord is way too long and heavy!  feels like it dangles halfway down my back and i can feel the weight of it pulling on the earbuds even when i'm not moving
 - finish/texture + length of cord = big problem. it gets caught on fabric. and skin. and t-shirt collars. and dress shirt collars. and jacket collars. once it gets stuck, it tugs on one or both earbuds when you move - up to yanking them out altogether

for half as much cash, you could buy a small bt receiver clip thing and use your favorite wired headphones...you still have wires that way, but it doesn't seem too different than using these.

if you want to go bt completely, i'd recommend upgrading to the bluebuds x (more expensive than these are, but still a better deal all around).
summary: less convenient than they should be

reviewText:
i have 2 freeagent go external hard drives, one at home and one at work. i originally only purchased a single dock which i used at home and i liked it enough to purchase a second one for work. there is really nothing too special or fancy about it, it's just handy to be able to quickly grab the drive and go (after safely ejecting in windows, of-course). additionally, i believe that having the hard drive standing up improves airflow and ventilation allowing the drive to stay cooler than when it is lying flat.

i only have 2 gripes:
1. the dock has a built-in usb cable with 2 male usb a connectors, one for power and one for data. depending on the system and port, it would probably work with only the data cable connected - but i haven't tried.
2. i really wish the dock came in black, considering that the drives are black. the white makes it look like an apple product.

also note that there are 2 variants of this product.
1. the freeagent go dock+ has 3 powered usb ports, effectively making this a usb hub for only a few dollars more.
2. the freeagent go dockstar also has 3 powered usb ports as well as a network/ethernet port which effectively turns this into a nas that can be accessed from any computer on the same network. this model, however, is substantially more expensive.
summary: handy dock for my portable hard drives

reviewText: i purchased the 4 year camera accidental protection plan ($3,000 - $3,500) in feb 2016 and had a failure of my sony a7rm2 in july 2017. it was past sony's manufacturer warranty period, so i made a claim on my smartguard warranty on july 26, 2017. i made the mistake of making the claim through live chat. i was told a shipping label would be sent to me by email to ship my camera to the repair company. i had to call warrentech several times to request the shippping label. it was a week after my live chat before the shipping label arrived. i finally was able to ship the camera to united camera in il for delivery on aug 4. after a few days, i called united camera and they told me they could not repair the camera and had to send it to the manufacturer, which i assumed meant it was sent to sony. i spoke to united camera on aug 23 and was told that an estimate for repair was given to warrantech on aug 18 and approved by them on aug 21. i was told that my camera was expected back from the manufacturer on sept 5 and that the camera would be shipped back to me on sept 8. i spoke to united camera on sept 7 and was told the camera was received from the manufacturer on sept 5 but had not been inspected yet by united camera. i spoke to united camera on sept 8 and was told that they had an error in their system. my camera had not been repaired yet because a part was on order and my camera was not expected back now until sept 20. i also found out that my camera was not sent to sony, but to precision camera in ct. i don't know why warrantech didn't have me send my camera to precision camera directly. i also don't understand why it took three weeks to update the repair records to show a part was on order. i asked united camera what part was on order and what exactly had to be repaired in my camera and they said they did not know. i never had my camera repaired before, but i think 2 months is a long time for a camera repair. the length of time has been exacerbated by having multiple parties involved and having the camera shipped multiple times. hopefully my camera will be restored to good working order, but don't count on this warranty to get your camera repaired quickly and plan to have backup equipment around for use.
summary: hopefully my camera will be restored to good working order

reviewText:
this is a very interesting kettle of fish...

i should also note upfront that i don't use wireless streaming (even though i have wireless-n) because i had planned ahead and run a gigabit cable to the wall behind the unit.

in general, it does what it does pretty well, but there is a lot it doesn't do (and doesn't even try to do).  as long as you know what to expect, it is a decent unit, but certainly not a perfect media player.

for example, just straight-up playing videos over the lan is fantastic.  quality of video and sound is excellent (assuming the video source is also good)
however, trying to navigate through the video to points is frustrating or just bizarre....for example:
- chapters don't work.  if you try to use the next/previous chapter buttons on your control you'll end up jumping to the next/previous media file not chapter.  needless to say this is maddening.
- you can skip to a percentage of the video by pressing the 1-9 buttons, which will jump you to that 10% of the file.  e.g. pressing 7 will take you to 70% of the way through the movie.
- ffw/rwd only go at double speed.  nothing more, nothing less, and when you press play again you often end up playing up to 10 seconds away from the point you pressed the button at.
- pageup/pagedn.  yup, when watching a video they jump you forward 30 seconds or backwards 15 seconds.  useful but peculiar.

audio is again good but the unit's slow interface can make this a bit of a chore.  the sounds quality is fantastic (depending on your speakers of course, and also assuming a good quality of the ripped file)
however, once again the system makes you jump through hoops or struggle to figure out how best to use it....for example:
- browsing to a ripped cd through the album option gives the album tracks in a different order than when you browse to the album through the artist option.  one is in alphabetical order, the other is in the correct album order.  why on earth would you want album tracks in alphabetical order???
- there doesn't appear to be a way to just play randomly/shuffle across your entire collection (or even a subset of it).  surely this wouldn't be hard to implement?  i find this strangely lacking.

other observations:
1) while waiting for my new hdmi cable i initially ran this over component.  don't do it!  the ratio on many of my video files was wrong and vertically stretched.  relatively speaking this was only out by an inch or so, but the result was that everything looked weird.  as soon as i sent the output over hdmi it went back to normal.
2) i use a master-switching power strip for most of my electronics.  if you're unfamiliar with them, when one specific device is turned off, it powers off the other sockets on the strip to save energy.  however when i ran the 520 on one of those switched sockets, it would routinely reset itself to factory defaults!  i have no idea why this was happening, perhaps it was something with the way the power trigger interacted with the power on signal to the device from the remote, but i was minutes away from sending it back before i decided to try it on a 'real' power socket.  i haven't had any issues since i did that, and it was resetting about once per day before.
3) it does play some video formates not listed, but only to an extent.  for example, i was very pleased to see it play vob files which is a common format for just ripping dvds.  the only problem is that a dvd ripped to vobs is actually stored in a number of 1gb vob files.  when it reaches the end of one vob file, it stops and doesn't move on the the next file in the movie.  its not a big deal for me since i know this wasn't even supposed to be supported, but its sooooo close to working right that its just a little frustrating.
4) there are a number of video or audio formats i would like to have seen (e.g. divx, even iso perhaps).  i knew these weren't supported so they don't affect my score as such, i just mention it as part of my reasoning for why its 'not a perfect media player'.

overall, i like the unit, and i got it at an excellent price.  i would not have paid more for it, but i would recommend it if someone can get it for about a hundred after rebates.  i anticipate that this will be a short term thing for me (a year or two), before i get a newer generation one that has as more rounded set of features.  just be aware of the limitations and you'll be fine.

hopefully future firmware updates might fix some things, like the shuffle to the music or the album track listing order problem, but its been a while since a new one has been released so i get the feeling dlink are moving on to newer models and leaving this behind.

for testing purposes i have an ortek mck-142 pro mechanical keyboard that is a favorite throughout my office. it is an at model with a ps-2 output. in addition, i added an ibm kb-8923 and a dell sk-8100, both pure ps-2 keyboards. i want to use these on a modern desktop computer with 2.0 and 3.0 usb ports. in researching for a way to do it, i realized that there is a difference between an adapter, which is only a wiring solution and a converter that has electronics to assist in making it work. the problem is that there are many brands and items available and no real way of knowing whether any or all of them will work. so i took the proverbial bull by the horns and bought one of each to try out. this resulted in ordering 9 items for a cost of about $77, not too bad for my purposes.
i purchased: usb to dual ps2 adapter convertor  white by saitech it; monoprice ps/2 keyboard/mouse to usb converter adapter, black (110934); tripp lite usb to ps/2 adapter - keyboard and mouse (b015-000); trendnet usb 1.1 to ps/2 converter, tu-ps2; adesso ps/2 to usb adapter, connects 2 ps/2 connectors to 1 usb port/hub (adp-pu21 ); sanoxy usb to ps/2 adapter (this one has wires); startech usb to ps/2 adapter - keyboard and mouse; radio shack ps-2 female to usb-a port adapter 26-723; and sanoxy ps2 keyboard to usb adapter (this one is a little block).
i tried them one by one. all were recognized on the usb device manager as a keyboard, yet all, but one, failed to allow the keyboards to be recognized and function.
the only one that worked perfectly for all 3 keyboards was the sanoxy ps2 keyboard to usb adapter  the one that is a little block. this being amazon, i immediately returned the other 8 and ordered a bunch of the sanoxy's. thought you might find my experiment helpful. sanoxy ps2 keyboard to usb adapter

reviewText:
sony makes a very reliable blank cd-r that can handle up to 80 minutes of music or 700 megabytes of data. moreover, these blank cd-rs are capable of recording data at high speeds. (i looked at one older sony cd-r disc to help me write this review--would you believe it didn't say the speed at which it records? sorry!!!) the data i record onto these cd-rs has now lasted for over three years, proving the test of time. i have used these as data discs and discs to record audio. i almost never got a coaster. great!

the cd-r discs are compact and easy to store. while the discs are still blank, store them in the circular case on the spindle that they came in. after your burn data or music onto them, i would recommend storing them in slim jewel cases instead of paper sleeves. it's just better protection for your cd-rs that have anything stored on them. don't store these discs, burnt or blank, in rooms that become very hot; this causes damage to any brand of this type of disc and you could lose data over time.

there are two caveats that many other people note about any brand of this product: when you are burning the data onto the blank disc, don't be surprised if you see that the data is burning at a rate slower than the packaging advertises. this can happen if your burner doesn't have the capacity to burn faster, or it may be a quirk. i am not a professional so i cannot be certain of precisely what causes this phenomenon; but i assure you that the extra minute or two (tops) that you wait to get your cd-r completed is worth the wait. in addition, don't write on these using sharpie ink pens. the ink can seep through the top coating of the cd-r disc and slowly but surely compromise your data--and you wouldn't want that, now would you? if you need to label the discs, label its' jewel case using a post-it note. at least that's what i do.

overall, sony blank cd-r discs store data reliably over the years and i believe that an extra minute to burn the data onto the blank disc is well worth it in the event that it doesn't actually burn at the very highest speed advertised.

use them in good health!

reviewText:
i wanted a new case for my asrock z87e-itx motherboard because the old one was a bit large for the vintage buffet that i'm using for an entertainment console. i also wanted a case that would let me install a slot-loading blu-ray drive. there aren't a lot of choices out there, so i was really happy to find the ml-06.

construction is solid, as you would expect, and there were no surprises when it came to opening up the case.  i was pleased to see that silverstone hadn't used any oddball fasteners; they were all philips-head screws. however, i thought it was odd that they used silver screws to attach the top panel and the power supply given that the case is black.

i had silverstone's sfx power supply in the old case, so i just moved it over along with the motherboard. power supply goes in first, and you will need the modular cables for it, because space is at a heavy premium when you get everything installed. the motherboard drops in and attaches with 4 screws. i moved the pair of 2.5" hard drives from the old case into the drive cage (i also have an msata drive attached directly to the motherboard). although silverstone says you can put 4 drives in the cage, poor placement of one set of holes (at least in my unit) means you can really only put in 3. and given the lack of room in the case, you can really only put 2 drives in the case because you need the space in the cage to stuff some of the wires.

i attached my blu-ray drive to the bottom of the multipurpose bracket, and then went to put it back in the case. i was disappointed to find out that my zalman cpu cooler, which i though was pretty low-profile, is too tall; the bracket will go back in on its own, but not with the drive hanging from it. dang! i guess at some point i can get a new cpu cooler, but for now, i'll go back to using the blu-ray from an external box.

the case has space on the right side for a pair of 80mm fans, but i didn't bother. the psu and cpu fans provide enough exhaust, though if i do install the blu-ray drive, it will block the cpu fan's access to the top vent, and then i might need at least one of those side fans.

the front audio and usb 3 ports are on the right side of the case, which is a bit nonstandard. if the space you're putting the case in is a little tight, this might be a consideration for you. for me, it's not an issue.

after i reattached all the cables, i put the top back on, attached the power cord, the usb wifi, the usb transmitter for the wireless keyboard, and the hdmi cable, and it was off the races! everything is working fine, and the ml-06 fits great in the available space in the console. i'm a happy camper!

reviewText:
i am supplying power to both my dac and phono preamp with this power supply.  there are noticeable improvements to sound quality upgrading from the wall warts--a veil is lifted for each.

the phono preamp i am using is a bbe and it wants 12v dc, so i just connect it directly to this pyramid power supply.

for the dac, i have the fiio d3.  it expects an input voltage of 5v dc (normally powered off a usb bus). so what i did is buy a few parts from radio shack for a few bucks to make my own voltage regulator--a 12v to 5v voltage regulator ic, heatsink, small perf board & little project box.  i just place this diy voltage regulator in between the power supply and dac.

love this power supply--hugs & kisses.

i am a hobbyist and only comment as one here - this is the best lens i've used so far as far as iq goes. on top, it's light weight, discreet, not too expensive. somehow i felt the af on this is not as quick as my 70-200/f4 non is zoom. maybe just me. but the iq (color, contrast, sharpness) on this one simply blows me away, wide open or not. i use this lens shooting in-door head shots of my little 4-yr old. she simply springs to life from this lens! the 200mm on 40d is even better than 5d because it gives the kid more room to be herself. the af on this lens is not the best in low light. this is true with 40d, 350d rebel, and 5d. 24-105l under the same condition works much better. this is true even with the build-in flash emitting af assist beams. with the 580ex however, af is instant. and so does most other lenses i use. i suspect this has to do with this 200mm lens being of a much older design while the 24-105 is far more recent.

update april 2011 -

after some years of use mostly on 5d mk1, i get to know more about this lens:
- iq is great, but not the best. actually, both 100/f2 and 300/f4l is seem to be better in many cases. af is not the quickest either, worse in normal indoor light. flare can be a problem for this lens if shooting with a bright window in the background. 300f4is is quite a bit better. 100/f2 is much better. but under normal light, this prime is great.
summary: the best lens i've ever had so far

i am an it in california who purchased two of these units new at fry's because i like sabrent, having purchased many of their disk enclosures in the past.  but sabrent really deserves to be skewered for this case design because it is too small to house a hitachi (hgst) travelstar 2.5" sata disk.  i have mechanical skills, but it took me a half hour just to get the hgst to go inside the case.  the case comes in three parts: two flat metal sheets that cover the length of each side, and one flimsy rubbery piece of plastic that surrounds the disk once enclosed.  the problem is that the plastic boundary is deformed so as to block disk insertion.  there is no straight in path for the disk; one must insert the disk into the usb electronics at an angle; the required bending alone is enough to destroy the circuitry.  using a spudger, to move plastic case boundary aside, destroys it.  there is 0 tolerance in the case design; no wiggle room at all.

and then, sabrent thinks they are doing us a favor by incorporating a nonstandard usb cable that is incompatible with all previous sabrent usb case enclosure products.  take a close look at the photos to see the nonstandard female termination.

the dumbest thing about this case design is that it has two buttons on the side of the case that release it.  the problem is that if you press those buttons accidentally, the case comes apart in your hands.

of course, after all this work getting the disk in, the sabrent usb interface was dead.  that was confirmed by verifying a fully functioning hard disk after its extraction.

i must say, to whomever is responsible for "designing" this disk enclosure, you should leave the mechanical engineering profession and seriously consider the food and beverage industry as your next career choice.

reviewText: when i purchased them i was wary of the reviews calling into question the build quality, but i needed right angle adapters behind the living room media console so that it could be pushed flush with the wall, and in the bedroom where, with two small kids in the house, i didn't want an enticing cable sticking a few inches out from the wall. so i bought two of these and installed them behind the media cabinet and in the bedroom, and they have performed as expected and keep cables out of the way as advertised. a couple of notes about "signal strength." signal strength is measured in decibels (db), a logarithmic scale (each 3 db of loss reduces the signal power by about half). connectors typically introduce ~ 0.01db, or less than 1% power loss. even poor quality connectors usually keep loss under 0.1db (about 2% power loss). comparatively, a 100 foot rg6 cable loses ~ 4db (it varies between the high and low ends of the broadcast spectrum range). so compared to the loss in your cable run, a connector is likely to be a negligent factor in signal quality. it is of course possible for a connector to push the signal over its tipping point, but this would be the exception rather than the rule. it is also possible to get a bad apple that slipped passed qa. there are other manufacturers of this component as well, such as cable matters and mediabridge. quality connectors are also available from mouser.
