reviewText:
this is a cute, inexpensive bluetooth speak that works great.  it's not going to put out the volume or bass of a much bigger, much more expensive speaker but on the other hand this one will fit in a pocket in your backpack and really improve the sound from your phone.

as a bonus it works as a speakerphone, it has a built-in microphone that will let you use your phone as a hands free phone in the car or while sitting at your desk.  it paired up easily with my mac and with a nexus phone.

it has an aux audio input jack, a micro usb port for charging and four simple buttons on top (power, pause/play, back and forward).  two of the buttons also serve as volume up/down buttons.  i'm not real fond of the volume buttons, you have to press and hold to use them as volume buttons, if you press and release they'll act as forward/back buttons which will likely result in you either restarting a song or skipping to the next one when you don't want.

i haven't had it long enough to determine how long it will last on a charge.  there is a dual use led that is blue when connected over bluetooth and alternates with a red flash when charging.

i received this new trent product at a reduced price in return for a fair and reliable review based on my user experience.

update:
after making sure the speaker was fully charged i ran it for 8 hours last night playing white noise at low volume, this is not an accurate test of longevity for music played louder but i did want to see if it lasted all night.  white noise helps some people sleep better.  the result was it was still playing after 8 hours.

update 2:
i was able to get 8+ hrs of music at a moderate volume.  however, when used to watch a movie there was a lag between that audio and video that was noticeable to the point of being annoying.  i repeated the test with a bose soundlink and the lag was nearly imperceptible.  of course the bose was > 10x as much.  in addition the audio would cut in and out when used to watch a movie on an apple computer, i didn't experience the same dropouts on the bose.  it may be that the speaker is designed to reduce power when no audio is playing but if that is the case it isn't doing a good job.  normal music is fine, no dropouts.  i took off a star for the dropouts, not really planning on watching movies with it so not important to me.

lastly, i opened the case to examine the components.  a standard lion battery is used, if you have soldering skills you can replace the battery.  the speaker is a 4 ohm, 5w speaker.
summary: small, compact, good sound, reasonable price

reviewText:
i had an "inside" robbery at a second home which i discovered a month ago.  i say "inside" as opposed to outside---i have also had an outside robbery of large patio furniture which i pretty much ignored. this time i knew i needed an alarm system.  my house is in a very good neighborhood and no one saw a thing either time.  i live alone so i really was upset to know that someone had been in my house and really might come back.

i looked into all the big systems---like adt (my friends have that and they get all sorts of false alarms, so they never turn it on) and i met with the reps.  i looked online at everything i could find.  i found out about smash and grab, where a thief finds the control panel while the system is beeping and smashes it before the alarm sounds. obviously, having it connected to your phone line is a problem because the thief can cut that.  and you have to have a battery back-up.

i didn't want to pay for monitoring.  my neighbor said she saw a prowler around my house and called the police and by the time they got there, he was gone.  so i just wanted something really loud to scare off the intruder immediately and wake up my very nice and responsible neighbors so they would call the police and come outside.

i decided on ordering this system.  i did not get the dialer, because of the "cutting the phone line" issue.  i did read another reviewer's thoughts on smash and grab and bought two control panels.  i also bought two alarms.  remember, the idea is to wake up the neighbors who, imho, should be grateful to know a robber is around.

unlike adt and all the big companies, all the extras with this company are cheap.  for $20-$30 you can get extra door sensors, motion detectors, and alarms.  this was something i considered because i have 5 exterior doors alone and lots of windows at ground level.  most systems give you one motion detector and two door alarms.  and the last thing i want is someone wandering around in my house until he happens to get to a sensor somewhere.  so i bought sensors for all the doors and two motion detectors.  (i am going to get some for the bedroom windows too).

so far so good.

i get the box which i expect to be huge, and it really is small and weighs ten pounds, maybe less.  so i open it and start reading and wow---not easy at all to put this thing together.  it's not just the instructions either---the door sensors did not look anything like the ones i saw a woman install on a promtional video for another company.  she just peeled off the tape and positioned them on either side of the door and off she went.  this had little parts and wires and screws.  so i looked again at the instructions.  don't even believe that reviewer who put this thing together easily unless you are super good with electronics.

so i call a ****brilliant techie**** college kid i know and he comes over and expects to spend an hour.  four hours later he leaves with the instructions. get my drift!  but he does have up one of the motion detectors (with the double sided tape) because he does not have the right drill bit for plaster.  he also has up another motion detector secured to wood and half of all the door sensors are in place.  the problem with the other half of the door sensors (the part needed to sound an alarm) is that none of my doors are flush with the molding.  they have to be flush.  he did not act like this was a big deal--something about buying and screwing rubber under it, etc.  but *i* and perhaps *you* wouldn't know how to do this.

we tested the alarm and if you are beside it---wayyyy loud.  disabling loud!  however, i have plaster walls and if you are two rooms away---you hear it, but it is no big deal.  not what i thought it would sound like.  the alarm then would only be a deterrent in that a robber would *hopefully* think it was alerting someone somewhere to do something.

my brilliant techie never did figure out how to get the thing armed right and neither did i.  i wanted the instant alarm (no delay).  i know it will do that because it says so on the control panel, but we do not yet have that figured out.  i did get it to work on delay and we had up the two motion detectors so i felt good with that level of security.  however, for whatever reason, the second alarm and the second motion detector would not work with the control panel.  i think add-ons take some time to get going, based on what another reviewer said.

here comes the good part.  you should enjoy this at my expense.

ok, so remember i have been robbed recently and i am not feeling safe in my very nice house in my very nice neighborhood.  i am on edge during the day, looking for anyone suspicious driving about and *really* on edge at night.  but now i feel much safer because i have a partial alarm and i have my key chain remote (which works fabulously btw---ignore people who want it coded so you know which is the off button, as this is not something you would want someone else to figure out right away).

at 5 a.m. this morning (while i was asleep and it was very dark outside) i hear a distant thud in a nearby room and then the beeping of the alarm starts and i grab the key chain and push the panic button to make it go off sooner.  yes, it did seem coincidental that this was all happening the day i put this alarm in, but who wants to take chances.  i called 911, barely able to breathe---remember, i did hear that thud and i have been robbed.  so the alarm turns itself off, but i keep pushing the panic button on the keychain(4 times because it keeps turning itself off) to make it come back on, and it does, until the five policemen show up and take their flashlights and go around my house.  no robber and no sign of entry.  one comes inside and goes through my house.  nothing.  have i ever done this before---the answer is no.

so they leave and i am wondering what the thud was and what is going on.

then i spot the culprit.

remember the sticky tape on the motion detector---the thing fell off the wall.  i locate it behind a piece of furniture and as i am standing over it, the system starts beeping again, ready to go off.  so the system does work---just don't use that tape, even overnight.

now here is the big thing.  remember my super responsible and wonderful neighbors---i'm sure you see them all out in their robes, standing in their yards, worried sick.  not exactly.  no one, no one woke up---not with the four times the 110 db alarm went off nor with the five policemen walking around my house.  my lapdog didn't even bark.

are the houses far apart---no!  i have a neighbor on one side whose house is about 20 feet away.  the others are a lot farther, but the alarm was in the bedroom closest to his house so he would wake up.  nothing.  the police did not use their flashing police car lights or sirens---i don't even know where they parked (this would be my fault as they could not find the house since i don't have up the house numbers--but my neighbors do, so they did have some idea).

would i buy it again?  i originally said yes and now i say no.  it is important to note---i was pretty sure the big time expensive system alarms are 95 db---which is less powerful and who would want to pay an extra five hundred dollars to get a second one.  so, i bought a few more alarms cheap.  i thought i could find something for outside---a big horn or something like my neighbors have.  if you have drywall (as opposed to brick and mortar walls---a builder built my house for himself so it is made quite well) then you are going to have a different experience.  probably a very loud system for an apartment.

pros:  1)inexpensive for the starter sytem and really inexpensive for the add ons.
  2)it apparently has different levels that will allow you to set a delay so you can enter and turn off the alarm or you can have it come on instantly if you are asleep and there is an intruder.  it also has some sort of zone programming which, i assume, will allow you to be at home with certain zones on (like the doors and windows) but not the motion detectors.
  3)it looked comparable to other, much more expensive systems and the alarm is actually louder than some of the expensive ones i looked at.
  4) the key chain remote works well and is truly cool.  other systems don't give you this or charge you $100 extra for one.  it has a red panic button and the other three have raised dots.  one dot is to arm the system and the three dots are to turn it off.  i don't know what the two dots are for.

cons:  1)instructions are difficult to understand.  impossible for me.
  2)the control panel is of no help at all in programming the thing.  it just has lights to tell you if the thing is armed and what zones are armed.  thus far, the lights do not tell me how it is armed---whether it is chime (it has a chime mode) or delay or instant.  there is no window with words that tell you what is going on.  that one thing would be a vast improvement!!!  are you listening skylink?  and the battery back-up light turns *on* if you have a low battery.  that is a big flaw!  because when the battery goes out, the light will go out and you won't know if the battery is good or bad.  it should be just the opposite.  it should be if the battery light is out, you know you need to replace it.
  3)installation is not that easy---remember the door flush issue and the wires and screws and plates.  but considering the price of the system, it was worth it to me to find some help.  a comparable system would have cost me well over a thousand dollars and i would have had to pay the monthly monitoring fee.
  4)it probably is not going to wake up your neighbors, unless you live in an apartment.
  5)i had another false alarm---police came---i was embarrassed---no thud, no double-sided tape issue.  i have no idea why it went off.  the only thing active was one motion sensor and no one had been in the house and the dog was with me.  no one in my neighborhood woke up.  i even asked them---just if they heard it---no, they did not.

update:  more robberies in my neighborhood this summer, so i am really on edge and i totally regret buying this system.  it would be fine for an apartment, but it is not loud enough to wake even my next door neighbors.  my neighbors alarm across the street went off last week and it woke everyone up in the whole neighborhood.  and i thought they were all just heavy sleepers---no, mine is not loud enough.  it just isn't.  so i totally regret it.  what's the point if it doesn't get someone to do something---mine is not connected to that dialer thing because that's no good if the phone is cut.  i want my neighbors to get up and call the bleepin' police, like i did when his went off, so i can go back to bed.

the other big negative with this system is that it only stays on 3 minutes and then turns itself off.  that's ridiculous.  so, i would return it if i still could.  the only thing it is going to do is wake me up, assuming i am here.  that's worth a star.

reviewText:
this is a surprisingly well-built and versatile radio.  i had expected much worse when i bought a two-pack of them (bought two in case one was doa).  instead, i have solid audio, good transmit and receive, solid heft and tactile impression, and accessories i had not remembered were included (headset, belt clip).  it is not as intuitive as radios used to be, but if you have ever tried to program a yaesu vx-3r, it takes a user's manual as well, and the latest batch of offerings have more in common with this little radio than with those "old days" hts that actually were intuitive and easy to use.

i think this radio must have a history of being applied to business radio and other "disposable" environments before it found its way into the ham market.  it is clearly evident that effort has been made to address durability and ease of (pardon the phrasing) dumb-monkey use (ie. push the button and talk.  don't touch anything else unless you're told), while the user interface for hams, who require much more access to their radio's operation, seems... less well thought out.

i would not hesitate to recommend this radio to new or experienced hams in need of a 2m or 7cm ht.

capture quality is currently a little blurry at all but the highest bit rate settings and when recording a shooter their is distortion when turning left and right. most software encoders give a better video quality but to get that quality you'll probably not be able to play the game on the same system that you're streaming with. this video shows off 720p at 400kb/s. you can get higher quality with faster bandwidth but i don't have any extra bandwidth. still it's completely watchable and in the top end local recording modes it's a flawless "like your own computer"

reviewText:
first of all, i did not buy this from amazon, but i know some people here will value the review if your comparing to the surface pro 4.
i bought both because i could not decide. i had a couple days to compare the two first hand.
the bottom line is that the surface pro is a higher quality machine and you can tell they spent a lot more time refining it. they also did not cut corners to try to lower the price and compete with another product. the acer seems to be a good machine and if you cannot afford a surface pro 4, then get this one. if you do, don't play with a surface pro 4 long or you might wish you spent the extra money. the small difference add up to a more refined and pleasant machine to use.

these statements will be about the acer in comparison to the same spec surface pro 4 (i5, 8gig, 256ssd).
-the touch pad is not as smooth and your finger does not glide as easily. it is also lower quality with curved up edges.
-the keyboard rattles when you type on it (highly annoying)
-lower resolution screen
-screen is not as bright
-screen is smaller even though the outer dimensions are about the same (more wasted bezel space)
-its heavier
-its a bit thicker
-the keyboard back lighting is on or off, not adjustable intensity
-it is infested with bloatware and a bunch of acer stuff. the surface pro is lean and mean with no junk to spend a bunch of time figuring out how to get rid of
-the initial setup is not as good. for example the surface sets up the camera to log you in right off the bat
-kickstand is a little harder to find a spot to grab and pull out, but it is a nice kickstand. you can grab the surface pro anywhere and there is enough lip to get it without going where the indentation is
-the charger connection is the old school type that tend to get broken. its the round plug in type. the surface has a very nice magnetic one that goes in either direction effortlessly and will just pull off if it gets jerked.
-no pen included
-no display out connection without buying a dock
now for the better:
+3.1 usb vs 3.0
+has a usb-c, not sure what needs this yet though
+passive cpu cooling (if it works better i am not sure)
+price (the only reason to get it over a surface pro 4 in my opinion)
summary: lower quality surface pro 4 alternative. great for the price, but not as good as the real thing!

reviewText:
i'm reasonably happy with this stand.  i just wish they did a smaller version specifically for 7" tablets like my nexus 7.  it works ok for smaller tablets, but would be nice to have a smaller stand package to go with the smaller tablet.  and like other reviewers, i'm also not sure that the "just force it" plastic ratchet mechanism is going to last.  but i'm not dinging them on rating for either of those things.

my main criticism is the lack of space for charging connection at the bottom of the tablet.  i had read this in other reviews, but thought that the low profile, right angle connector i use would fit.  it doesn't.  yes, you can flip the tablet upside down, but that then makes it much more likely for the tablet to be knocked off the stand if anything happens to snag or move the cable, which has already happened twice in the two days i've been using it.

overall it's a functional stand, and for the price it's hard to beat.  i just feel that properly accommodating charging connections is a fairly basic requirement for a stand, which is typically going to be used during heavy power consumption scenarios like watching movies, or sitting on a bedside table overnight being charged.

if anyone knows of a design of micro usb connector which does fit, i'd be interested in knowing, so please leave a comment.

reviewText:
i have owned my inreach se for 2 days so far.  however, i have previously tried the original inreach and had used a spot for the past 8 years, so i consider myself somewhat of an expert on these type of devices.  i have spent several hours playing with and testing my new play toy, and had done many hours of research prior to purchasing.

the thing i liked in the other two units that is lacking in the se is a really good waterproof seal.  the others had cover screws that you could tighten by hand to form a really super tight seal.  the se just has a rubber flap over the charging port which has a very insecure feel to it.  i have little confidence in the seal and it looks like it will wear out and be less secure over time when opened and closed each time i top off the battery.  what i don't know is if getting water on the connector will allow water to get into the rest of the unit.

i really like almost everything else about the inreach compared to my prior experiences.

the biggest advantage is that when you send a message with the inreach, you know if it got through or not.  this is not true with the competition.  in fact, with my old unit, i had an experience where messages i sent were delayed many hours before being delivered.

this unit easily pared with my android with one disappointing feature.  with an emergency device, you want as many backup options as possible.  i wanted to pair it with both my android and my wife's android, and expected it to just lock into which ever one was turned on nearby.  however, in order to pair with a second device, you have to unpair from the first device using the tiny screen and the few available buttons.  not a super big deal, but in an emergency, it could take some time you might not have.

the good part of the cell phone link is that even though it is an easier interface to use, you don't need it.  the inreach will perform it's functions totally without any cell phone, which is a good thing to have in an emergency device.

advantages of this unit at as follows:
1.  confirmation that you message has gotten through.
2.  two way text communications (others are only one way).  this seems especially good if you needed to communicate with sar people, or just need to coordinate with friends on shore (my primary use is sail boating).
3.  longer canned messages.
4.  built in screen interface provides much more information and functionality than just having a few buttons and lights.
5.  much better sensitivity and coverage.  my old unit would not work inside my house or inside most buildings.  i was able to get gps lock and sat communications sitting at my computer in my office.  covers more of the earth.
6.  quicker communications.  has access to more sats than competition, so time to lock onto a sat is much shorter.

the earthmate android/ios app is free if you have a registered inreach.  it not only makes things easier to do while paired with the inreach, it acts as a gps map device.  most gps mapping apps in cell phones are useless when you have no cell coverage.  however, this app allows you to download topo, marine, street, and aerial maps for any areas you select.  once the maps reside inside you cell phone's internal storage, you no longer need a cell signal to use the mapping features.  a warning, maps can take up significant space.  if you have an sd card, set the option to put the maps there before you start loading maps.  if you don't have a lot of available storage, be selective in the areas you load and they type of maps you select.

i don't know how long this device will run on a single charge.  delorme list about 100 hours with 10 minute position reporting, but if you are not using continuous tracking or expecting people to be sending you messages that are time critical, i recommend turning the unit off when you don't need it.  it does not take long to power up and be ready to communicate.  you could also pick up a solar charger for long trips through the wilderness.

the last thing you need to know about is the service that you need to subscribe to.  these devices will not communicate at all unless you sign up for service.  however, delorme, unlike the competition, offers some lower price plans for people who only need service a few months per year, or who don't need to send a lot of messages.  they also don't tack on meaningless extra fees on to you bill.

overall, i am very happy with my purchase.  i would have given 5*s if not for the flimsy cover over the data/charge port.
summary: far and away beats the competition.

reviewText: if you have old tapes and records you would like to be able to archive, put into your computer or other mp3 player, and/or burn cd copies of, this is the the portable media player/ recorder for you...but it has one major flaw* a line in jack (odd 2.5mm, but adaptable) is a very rare thing on a portable media player/ recorder, and this has one...add to that it's vu meters and it's close to perfect for making digital copies of any audio source including your old analog recordings. that's right it actually has a line in jack and vu meters..how sweet is that? with an adapter ( audio adapter - rca - mini-phone stereo 3.5 mm (m) ) you can jack it right in to your stereo system..with the included 2.5mm to 3.5mm cable you can jack into anything with a standard stereo 3.5mm headphone/ output jack. recoding is encoded at 128 or 160kbps wma..ok so it.s not high end top notch audio, but it's just fine for cassettes,lps, 45s, radio, and yes even your old 8-track cartridges. 320 kbps would have been better, but 160 is adequate. it also has a built in mono microphone that makes decent sounding recordings. ..and yes it'll play your audio and video files, and display pictures too... just like everything else, bla, bla ,bla. nothing new there. audio output is not very loud, but it does have a real user adjustable five band equalizer. battery life is about 9-12 hrs...uh... battery..battery...where's the battery? * the battery is not user replaceable. imho that's inexcusable. when it goes dead on you and you're away from home you're sunk. likewise when it'll no longer hold a charge. the only way to replace the battery is to literally pry the case apart or have it replaced by a technician! as a recorder i'd give it an 8/10. as a portable media player i'd give it 2/10 because of the battery issue alone...where it not for that i'd say 7/10.. sounds good for what it is, but i wish it had more output power.
summary: outstanding portable recorder... with one major flaw.

reviewText:
i recently bought a laptop and had to go wireless with my network. i saw the 108mbps and looked into the routers. i read some favorable reviews and bought it.

it auto-detects if there is new firmware available and will install it. just a tip though... don't do this. i ran into some troubles and netgear tech support said to disable this feature.

the setup of the router is fairly straightforward. if you have your wan settings readily available, you should be able to get it on-line without much trouble. it did take a bit to get the wireless up and running because i tried to use the highest encryption available without realizing that this is some sort of pay service. i set it to the basic wep and my card connected fine.

it seems to work fine everywhere in the house. i have yet to test it's limits for distance, but it seems to cover any area around the house where i'd use it.

my speed seems fairly good, but it's no 108mbps. my hardwired systems are quite faster. for my uses the wireless is fast enough, though i do plan to get some test software to see what my real throughput is. file transfers are somewhat slow, but since i don't do much of that from the laptop, it's no big deal.

the big issue i ran into was with a firmware problem of some sort that screwed up my port forwarding. if i setup more than one port forward, anything in the list past the first setting was unreadable and unremoveable. if i went to modify the setting, the ips came up wrong and the name was in gibberish as well as the port numbers. tech support had me download and manually install an older firmware version. that solved the problem. on occasion, changing a setting brings me to a blank ie page instead of returning me to where i made the change. the changes i make do to take though, so this is not a major problem.

having the built-in four ports is nice because it allowed me to easily plug it into my current setup. it was also nice of them to include a decent sized cat5 cable so i could mount the device away from my other computer equipment. (emi is a common cause of connection problems with these devices.)

aside from some minor irritants, this router has performed well enough for me to recommend it. novice users may have more trouble with it than others. netgear's tech support is not that great by any means, but it was effective enough for me to get my troubles solved. be sure to register on-line before you call or you will not be able to get support. this is my first wireless router so i don't have anything to rate it against, but based on my experiences, i had my office order one for their 802 network and so far we've had no troubles with it. (granted, i knew about it's weak points by then.) i gave it 4 stars, but consider that as really 3.5, based on the tech support. there were a couple moments where i felt i knew more about their product than they did.

reviewText:
for the price this is a fairly remarkable light. my wife has a $200 focus light and i also have a sola 1200 ($400). with fresh batteries this is similar to the 2 more expensive lights on medium setting. but, this does not have the same quality of driver/electronics. where the other 2 maintain brightness during the battery discharge this one becomes slowly dimmer. with a good battery (i suggest a decent 26650 or high end 186650) the light will easily go an hour. seems solidly made with good anodizing, well cut threads on the tail piece, 3 o-rings to seal, and the switch seems to work fine.
just got done using it on a 30 dive tropical trip with several dives to the 120' level. no problems at all.
for daylight use in clear tropics the light is somewhat weak, but then there is enough light to focus anyway. works fine at night. broad even light spill. i didn't find the red light strong enough to be useful at all, even at night.

for those getting the short bolt...unfortunate, but not too hard to replace.  mine was fine. hopefully they will fix that issue.

follow up a year later:
the switch is not suitable for saltwater use at all, which is completely unacceptable for a dive light. the switch on 2 of them became non-functional. you can take it apart with #5 torx bits. it's a simple magnet switch, but the spring and the magnet are both simple carbon steel and rust badly in saltwater. the spring broke in 3 parts. the magnet and switch were a mess, as well as the track the magnet runs in. with 0.25-0.50 cents in decent parts this could have been a pretty good product. i can no longer recommend it.

i bought this product...for my brother...he wanted a way to transfer files from his desktop computer to his laptop from work...it failed to install on his laptop.  the instructions say it works with the default drivers from windows 2000, but when it was plugged in, a driver installation wizard appeared because it couldn't find the drivers.  we tried a bunch of things with the supplied driver disk to no avail.  the usb-to-ide adapter inside the unit is a scanlogic sl11 chipset so we got the development kit installation off the internet (which was the same as the drivers provided by dlink)  but got no further.  we gave up on the laptop.
i took a crack at it and successfully installed it on my powerbook g3 and uploaded a song to it to try it out.  it seemed to work okay.  i went back and deleted all the files i put on it but apparently took some of the driver files as well by accident.  the unit was now crippled and wouldn't work at all.  i think there's a way to reload the software from a pc--except that we couldn't get it to connect to a pc. i was pretty disappointed that the "firmware" in the unit was so frail that a little overzealous deleting and you end up with a paperweight.
in all the process a nightmare. i did get a refund and eventually got him a usb powered hard drive instead.  the selling features are very strong--a battery powered usb hard drive that can be expanded with larger laptop hard drives and also doubles as a portable mp3 player.  pretty cool ... if it only worked.

reviewText:
i am addicted to music. in college i studied chemistry with a cheap pair of headphones on and the soothing sounds seemed to help me concentrate (bach and chopin, not rock). i have reviewed a few head sets for vine and for most, i loved the sounds but hated the cord. i wear an ipod when i work in the yard because it's a job i hate and music and smart pod casts make the drudgery less awful. but, the darn headphone cord keeps getting in the way. i either pull one out of the ipod or pull the headset off my head! it's even worse with apple ear buds. they fall out easily as soon as i start to sweat... can a guy get a break? that's why i jumped for these wireless ear buds. the bluetooth feature and motorola brand name lured me in. here's what i found.

first, the packaging is clever. the charger is also the carrying case. it connects to the usb port on your computer or to most every phone / tablet chargers. next, the design is just as clever. the size and shape is rounded, without sharp edges. this ensures a comfortable fit. finally, the battery lasts long enough to allow me to finish mowing the lawn. so far, so good...

the reason for only 3 stars? the ear buds fall out... fall out a lot. even when i push them in with various tips included they never feel secure. then, a quick head motion - again, especially when sweating - they fall out. so far, i have been able to find the missing bud when it winds up in the lawn but i am worried that i could run over one with the mower.

as mentioned by a few folks, they are large. the size may work for some, but i found them intrusive.

the sound is good. surprising base tones but in my head, i can hear bone conductance when i move my jaw. i have to really crank up the volume to drown that out. maybe it's just me - other reviewers - please comment!

i have decided to use these buds to watch my favorite tv shows on my ipad while my wife's watches her favorites. ha, earbuds marriage promote harmony! that makes them a real bargain.

clever packaging, good battery life, decent sound, some issues with fit.

the product felt strong, solid, and well put together. the glass was clear with no visible tint or imperfections. although this and another filter (same type different size) both arrived with smudges on the glass. the smudges were fairly easy to wipe off, but i suspect the items are either not cleaned before packaging, or i received someone's returned item. however, i had to return this item since they don't contain any anti-glare/reflective coating on them. when shooting towards a light source (light bulb, tv, sun, etc) a green reflection of the light source would appear on the recorded image. the green reflected image was caused by a reflection bouncing off of my lens's green tinted anti-glare coating which was bounced right back into the camera by this filter. if your lens isn't coated in an anti-glare coating the result will be even worse.

instead i picked up quantaray filters from a local wolf camera that were coated with the anti-glare. they only cost a little more, and the green reflection is now gone. make sure you look for a filter with the anti-glare

after installing the card correctly making sure it was properly seated and plugged into a spare sata power cable i had, i downloaded the latest driver only to get a "fresco logic usb card not found" or some such. only after a reboot did windows 10 see the intateck and i was able to install drivers but upon every reboot or waking form sleep the inateck was not found. i would literally have to reboot my pc for windows 10 to see the card, so on a recommendation i uninstalled the fresco drivers and used the windows 10 default drivers. this made the intateck visible in windows 10 upon any reboot, however i would get warnings about needing to update my drivers in the oculus software.

i removed the card and filed a refund. i have no idea how this card is recommended by oculus as being the best because in my experience its literally the worst piece of hardware i've ever installed in my pc. maybe its an issue with asrock z77 extreme4 owners, but i would totally not recommend this card whatsoever.

reviewText: since nikon no longer manufactures the batteries for my nikon coolpix 8700 camera, i resorted to searching on-line for a new battery.  the original nikon battery lasted 7.5 years.  based on previous reviews for this item on amazon, i decided to order these batteries.  i followed what any manufacturer would tell you to do and that was to fully charge the batteries before use.  i used the original nikon battery charger that came with my camera.  batteries charged fine.  my only complaint with this particular en-el1 battery manufacturer is that the batteries are somewhat difficult to get in & out of my nikon charger.  very tight fit!!  the first battery i charged came out of charger fairly easy.  however, when i charged the second battery of this set (just tested to make sure it worked before 30-days had passed), it was extremely difficult to remove the battery from my charger.  i am not willing to purchase a new battery charger to accomodate these batteries.  i figured out a way to get the second battery removed but it wasn't easy.  suggestion to manufacturer, please consider making the width of the battery to accomodate all chargers designed for this model of battery.  otherwise, these batteries work very well and i may order another set for spares as it was difficult to find this model of battery.  even duracell or energizer don't have this type of battery available unless you order via amazon.  overall experience with these batteries is good.  only gave it four stars because of the difficulty i had in removing the batteries from my nikon charger.

ok, i am switching out a failing wndr4300 (wireless signal drops and will not come back until you perform a factory reset) that is less than a year old. but i have used netgear routers for more than 6 years so i decided to stick with the brand and go for the n6100. it was at a nice price and it still had all of the functions that needed from previous netgear routers (wmdr3700 and wndr4300).

everything worked well out of the box, and then i updated the firmware (as netgear suggested). things still worked fine, until about 20 minutes later. wifi signal disappeared, as in, completely disappeared from the list of available connections. i checked all settings, i even made sure the ssid was being broadcast (i never turn that feature on but i wanted to be sure). i reset it multiple times and after the 6th reset the wifi signal finally came back. after that it would disappear or would be there and connect to wireless devices but those devices could not connect to the internet. the wired devices worked fine, until 2 days later when even they started giving me issues.

overall i had more issues with the new router than with the current router. i have ultimately decided to return it to fry's electronics where i purchased it from. while i have not given up on netgear (1-2 routers cannot shake 6 years  of good products, although 3 might), i am a little weary of my next choice (wndr4700).

reviewText:
everyone here has said everything about these headphones and all of which stand true. they sound great for music and are a steal at $20. but i got them for practicing guitar at night so i can crank it up and not get phone calls from the neighbors.

for that purpose the hd 202's are great. i can turn it up nice and loud and get a nice sound through them. whether it be a detailed clean or heavy distortion, these provide excellent sound. i hooked them up to my line 6 amp with the included stereo plug adapter(some reviewers say it isn't included but it is) and they took all the volume i could throw at them and then some. at least, as loud as i could handle. they sound great on all settings and the 10 ft' cord makes them perfect so i can stand back and work the pedals.

i did hook them up to ipod as well though and was very impressed by the bass i heard through them. i used some of my deepest trance and electronica tracks and they handled them easily. they also sounded great when listening to metal and classic rock. they're much better than my in-ear, more expensive ear phones. i'll use these instead from now on for my ipod except at the gym.

they're solidly and stylishly constructed. they don't seem to have any weak spots and the padding on the ears and on top of the head make them very comfortable for long listening periods. i don't see them falling apart from normal wear and tear.

these are great headphones at at great price. i did some shopping around first and they rank far and away the best over others in their price range. it's actually shocking that they're only $20 here at amazon. yeah, they're that good. for whatever you want them for, you will not regret buying these.

reviewText:
i use this camera quite often and it seems to work pretty well. my pc is pretty powerful but it seems sometimes the video is a bit choppy which is a little disappointing. also, the video and audio get out of sync depending on what you choose to encode your video as.

1 thing i particularly do not like is it seems the microphone is constantly on. i have a creative labs sound blaster audigy platinum zs2 internal card which i like using the 'record what you hear' feature quite often and i noticed that on one of my recordings room ambience included in my recordings. it took me a while to find that culprit was this camera. i unplugged the usb cable because i couldn't find an option to shut the microphone off when the camera was not recording, but was unsuccessful. i'm sure there is a way, but i looked for a good while and just winded up unplugging it instead.

the lighting seems to auto-adjust which can be good and bad at times. i believe this is also an option to shut off, but like i said, it is good in most cases. sometimes when you move too close to it, it locks into a lighting setting and could take a while to re-adjust back to a good setting.

you really have to play around with the setting to get a good recording, but if you are just using it for normal conferencing i think you should be fine.

overall it is still a good camera. i bought this a couple years ago, so im sure there might be better ones out there now. just do you research before you buy and if you can get a good price for this one then go for it.

i bought this for less than $60 in oct 2014. that was a fantastic bargain. the price changes a lot.

i got this to pair with two tiny energy micro speakers (leftover from a 5.1 system) and it is excellent for music even with the sub cranked up to the maximum crossover (150hz) to compensate for the poor low end of the energy speakers. i am using the high level inputs since it is driven by an old receiver without a sub out. the bass is very tight with plenty of low end for a wide variety of music. it does look exactly like the pioneer model which usually sells for $150. i trust the audiosource brand since i have used a few of their amps for various purposes at work for years, such as for conference room audio systems, and never had a problem.

if the price of this is much over $100, though, i would probably just get an 8" polk or pioneer for $100, which would be comparable, assuming they had the same features as this one.

i purchased this drive last year hoping it would do exactly as it said it would. i use a macbook pro and travel often.

this drive has been nothing but a headache. pretty to look at, but so far it has required me to use 'datarescue' 4 x in the past 6 months alone just to find the files i have stored on it.

it seems a regular occurrence to be shown the dreaded 'drive not recognized' error when i attach via my usb port. my feeling is that it is far too fragile to travel with, despite advertising to the contrary and within that somewhat attractive exterior lies a very defective interior.

if you do choose to purchase this drive, you may wish to use it as a unique paperweight then back your data up with another device - one that actually works and doesn't lose everything on an all too frequent basis.

in this day and age, who has time for this?

i used to be a big linksys lover, but my experience with several of their products (both here and at work, where i'm the it guy) makes me seriously think that their quality is suspect.

my experience at home is with the befsr41.

as far as featureset and stability, it's great!  no problems and the functionality is excellent.  i'm very happy in that regards (which is why i gave this a 3 instead of a 1).

as far as quality goes, though, i have a different experience.

i leave these on 24 hrs a day and have several computers hooked up to it.

my first one died, unexpectedly, after 13 months.  they wouldn't replace it (out of warranty), but my credit card company did reimburse me (the credit card extended warranties do work!)  so, i went an bought another one.  6 months later, it started freezing up and required an unplug/replug.  it started happening more and more.  so, i saw that there was a firmware upgrade... i upgraded and it died.

so, it's under warranty and they offer a great exchange policy (i know, because i had to use it with their wireless router at work -- it too just died one day), so i will exchange it for another one.

but... after seeing 4 of their products die unexpectedly (i also purchased their vpn router at work and it stopped working after around 18 months), i can honestly say that i am no longer on the linksys bandwagon (hence my foray into netgear).

so... my opinion is that this is a great product... until it dies.
summary: had two - great functionality, but both died

reviewText:
as one who could consider themselves a videophile (i've had vcr's since 1977 (beta and vhs), svhs since 1988, laser since the mid-80's, and dvd's for four years), i have been waiting for dvd recorders to crack the $1000.00 barrier.  when i started seeing them being listed on amazon.com, i knew it would be only a matter of time before i bought one.  the reviews by consumers of the recorders on amazon.com were great, once you separated those who expected the dvd recorders to be like a low-maintenance vcr from those who followed methodical steps when using a new product, the philips dvdr985 looked like a good deal.
...while i'll honor amazon's policy of not telling you what the price is until you put it into your cart, trust me, the price is even lower now than it was four months ago. and shipping was fast.  it left their store within two hours of the order and was delivered 1000 miles away in two days with standard shipping.
philips makes good equipment, and this one is very versatile.  i have it hooked-up to svhs/rca inputs and outputs on my receiver to record from svhs, laser discs, beta, and satelite.  i also have it hooked-up to the 75-ohm lead from the cable.  as a recorder of video programs, it puts vcr recordings to shame, even those with flying erase heads.  while recording a live program, one can make a noise-less pause to omit commercials, and the problem with the creeping clock seems to have been resolved.
recording quality depends on the quality of the source.  trash-in yields trash-out, but if it's a good source, you'll have a great long lasting image. you can record at over 500 lines of resolution at the 1-hour and 2-hour settings per disc, and svhs quality at the 3-hour setting.  the 4-hour setting is a little less, but much better than vhs.
the manual could be a lot better.  someone's suggestion of reading the whole book first is a good one.  the quick start pages leave out the part about "finalizing" the dvd after finishing your recording (finalizing makes the dvd playable on other dvd players).  when reading the manual, have a couple of pages of note paper nearby.  label one "steps in recording (including setting the timer)," another "setting recording speeds," and another "setting recording inputs."  once you have that knowledge, you can begin recording and enjoying the equipment while reading the rest of the manual.
dvd recording is the future.  with the philips dvdr985, the future is now!  if it came with a better manual, i'd say this one could be used by anyone, but until so, only someone who doesn't rush into recording should get this one.
would i buy it again.  yes.
summary: great recorder!!!  fair manual.. wonderful price!!!

reviewText:
let's start with the box. this is a rather harsh review, but i feel it must be done so because i've had more issues than anything with it.

it's unfortunate that i have to give these headphones a 2 star, but if we were to divide the attributes, this is how it would be below. i must also add, these ratings i'm giving it, are very harshly affected by the comfort of the silicon tips. they are what provides the fit & they provide the sound because if it's not in right, it won't sound complete.

quality wise, i believe these earphones are great. definitely worth the price, but as mentioned above, they have a terrible fit. if you have larger than the average ears, these would fit quite nicely (as my friend told me, who is in that category). also, sound wise i like full bass. however, these deliver well but a bit lacking in that department.

durability is also pretty good, but i'm disappointed that the cable gets tangled really easily and the fact that the cable appears thin or weak.

the comfort level of these earphones is astoundingly horrendous. not only do they not fit properly, but no matter how you put it in, it starts to hurt after a fairly short period of time. the reason being is that they push against the cartilage slightly below "root of the helix" (flexible yet tough, feeling like a soft bone that sticks out). it becomes a major annoyance, and that's when you constantly have to try to arrange the earphone so that it doesn't crush that poor part of the ear. this was a big deal breaker, and why i went back to re-buying (4th pair, i lost all the others) a pair of bose for their comfort.

design is... rather poor. i'm amazed at how bulky these things are. they sound good, but they definitely weren't made with the average person in mind i do not think. one of the reasons why these earphones went to the garbage bin for me, is because i lost a silicon tip. this goes hand in hand with maintenance below.

and lastly, maintenance. unfortunately, there is absolutely none. you can't get smaller tips, and you can't get replacements. if the thing gets caught on clothes and you pull hard enough (let's say you wrap them around your neck, and it gets stuck on your t-shirt), you'll lose the whole thing. good luck finding it after, when it's hundreds of feet behind you before you notice it's gone. the fact is, pioneer didn't think much about it. now, all i have to ask: why is it that the silicon tips are removable in the first place? what about loss of sound because sound does escape through silicon? how about replacement? why so bulky? why are there no choices for different sizes? we can only wonder...

so... pretty much, here's how i would grade them:

quality of sound highs: 4.5/5
quality of sound mids: 4/5
quality of sound lows: 4/5
durability: 4/5
comfort: 1/5
design: 1.5/5
maintenance: 1/5

reviewText:
i've had the carbon for about a year now. works as advertised and described in the other reviews. i use it for audible.com files and rips of books on cd. easy. great battery life, too.

as far as durability is concerned, i've had better luck than some of the other reviewers. like an idiot, i kept this in my back pocket a couple of times and noticed that i squished it together (it's stuck that way now with a slight lip all the way around but still plays fine). i keep it in my side pants or front jacket pocket now and it's been fine.

i use this thing daily, usually for two-eight hours and it has been problem-free except for one thing...

every once in a while it acts (non-acts?)dead. i have a feeling this might be caused by a few things...

1. the device not being "stopped" before it's taken off my usb connection with my laptop. not rio's fault; this is a problem with lots of usb stuff.

2. moving through sections of audible.com files too quickly.

3. one person metioned a low-power cause for freezes, too. i haven't seen that.

the reset is easy but needs a thin paper clip, the hole is tiny. (note that the hole in the front is not the reset. that's the microphone. the reset is on top near the wheel.)

so,i pop a paperclip in the little reset hole as the instructions advise. the device comes back every time.

the carrying case is useless. i have not yet found one that fits well, and i have been looking pretty hard.

all-in-all, it's still worth your hard-earned dollars, i think, and the price seems to keep dropping.
summary: still happy after after a year

reviewText:
i bought these cans based on the reviews everywhere that said they were magnificent. and they are - for the most part. they represent an incredible value at the price listed on amazon (~$250). soundstage is marvelous, and the sound quality is extraordinary. so why the "but?"

well it seems that during the week they were designing these puppies, the ergonomics department was on vacation. the sonics are great, as noted above, and the appearance is also first rate. but the comfort - not so much. some reviewers have said that after a few hours these headphones get uncomfortable. i think they are being way too kind. after about 5 minutes wearing these things, it feels like someone is pressing down in the middle of my head with their thumb. it's really uncomfortable - almost painful. (and, no, i don't have a really big or small head - just your average noggin.)

and it's not surprising to see why. they seem to be manufactured using all the best materials and knowledge from the 1950's. have these folks ever heard of memory foam (vs. hard leather)? or distributed pressure? the leather looks good - but it is fashioned just the way headset cushions were designed in the 50's - a series of hard bumps attached to a pretty leather backing. each of these hard bumps actually exerts greater pressure on the head than a simple flat headband would.

i could go on all day, but i won't. what's most annoying is that these are great cans for the money. they really do perform. but since comfort is such an integral part of listening to headphones, it is disappointing to have to cringe every time i think about having to wear them. it's not pleasant at that point - it becomes work... and that's not good for high end headphones, imo...

reviewText:
1. these headphones sound different using different headphone amps. on apple products, they sound hard and sharp. on mostly anything else, they sound much softer and smoother. it's night and day difference. all eq's off, no sound enhancements on anything. frequency response is the same on every headphone amp i've tried. same amount of treble and base and mids. the sound hits your ears differently depending on the amp.
2. these resonate at 240 hz the most. there is a big boost on vocals. it gives an illusion that the mids are louder then they actually are.
3. bass is a+. very multi dimensional and textured. the extension could be better though. sounds like a sub tuned at 38hz.
4. no one had mentioned how they handle extreme cold and heat. i would love to take these with me in winter. not a good idea for expensive headphones.
5. these do sound different when broken in. break them in like a subwoofer. the drivers are extremely high mass for a headphone. i used a fiio e17. bass at 10, volume at 35(0db gain). it takes about 5min of some bass. after, the treble extension improves dramatically, and bass extension improves too. the 240hz resonance goes down just a little.
6. final note! these make everything else sound and feel like trash. even off an iphone. and their loud af! 50 percent volume on an iphone is pretty loud.

reviewText:
i purchased this keyboard (4000) from staples to replace a 1999 natural keyboard that had finally given up the ghost (i still have my original 1994 natural keyboard which surely part energizing bunny, it keeps going, going...).  the 4000 went back to the store the the next day and i replaced it with a natural keyboard elite.

the problem, that would be the space bar.  i really liked everything else about the product, but could not get around the space bar. it does not engage when pressed, usually on either of the outer areas at the corners.  i am a touch typist and this space bar significantly dropped by speed and increase my error rate.  i tried to train myself to press more to the center of the space bar which worked just fine, but time and time again i would find myself pressing one or the other of the "little wings" with the result of no action and no space produced.

i have used the natural keyboard for 18 years and would choose nothing else.  but this keyboard is just very poorly designed for a touch typist.  a newcomer or hunt and pecker would probably not have this trouble with the space bar.

i would have given it only one star but liked the other functionality of the keys and especially the raised lip on the bottom of the wrist side of the keyboard.  i have been using a negative angle on my keyboards for many years and just find that is the less stressful way to type.  (negative angle is when the edge of the keyboard where the space bar is,is higher than the further edge of the keyboard, where the function keys are).  this position allows the fingers, wrists and forearms all to be in a natural straight line, there by decreasing at least one of the causes of carpal tunnel syndrome.

reviewText:
i have been using traditional docking stations with my last couple of laptops. i like being able to connect the computer to a monitor, mouse, keyboard, and speakers with just one click - or undock it with one click so i can take the laptop elsewhere. i had ordered a new laptop that was going to require a dock like this one - it's actually less of a dock and more of a port replicator. instead of nesting the computer in a dock. you plug the unit into the computer via a usb 3.0 port. this anker model got good reviews, so i gave it a try. i initially set it up with my older windows 7 computer. as soon as i plugged in the usb cable, the dock went to work setting up drivers and identifying all the peripherals it needed to work with. it took about 5 minutes, and i really didn't have to do anything once i had plugged everything in. easy-peasy, and it worked beautifully right away. then the new computer arrived. that didn't go as smoothly. it's a windows 10 model, and while the anker dock tried to do its thing when plugged in, the video display was wonky, and there was no sound. when i called anker's customer service, a rep told me that i needed to go to their site and download a driver for windows 10, which i did. you don't get any indication that installation is complete, and there is no instruction on what to do next, but i figured out that i needed to reboot. once the computer started up again, everything was working beautifully.

i miss a couple of features of the traditional docking stations. there is no power switch on the dock, so you have to open the laptop to turn it on. this unit does not supply power to your computer or charge the battery, so that's one more cord that has to be connected. this unit is less obtrusive than a standard dock, which is nice. it comes with a stand so that you can position it vertically (as is pictured) or horizontally without the stand. it has plenty of ports for all your computer peripherals.

it's a good gadget that does its job.

reviewText:
we have a small country home, the bedroom thats 9 x 10. this was a perfect solution, we weren't interested in having it flat to the ceiling, we mostly just want to tilted enough so that the closet door can open, but if we are watching a longer movie we drop it down so its square to our viewing angle. we mounted a sound bar on the ceiling just in front of it. its really cool, and i love motorized things anyway.
i wouldve given it five stars, except for one issue that couldve been a nightmare. when we mounted it, it was a quarter inch too close to the wall, since we weren't planning for it to be flush, i didn't think too much of it (bad decision on my part). the problem is, and they should warn you of this, because we all mess up now and then, the device when first plugged in the only thing you can do is hit ok which causes it to move the tv to the ceiling, nothing will stop that until it reaches flush to the ceiling, except unplugging it. by the time i got it unplugged the tv was jammed against the wall. we could find no way to reverse the device, being nearly flush, not quite, we had to look at a way to dismount the tv from the device. fortunately the visa mount was large and the two bottom screws were accessible. i found some 2 inch screws that matched the half inch screws that were there, it allowed me to remove one screw at a time and install the longer screw dropping the bottom of the tv down just enough so that it could completely a full close and then you could tell it open again.
manufacture, you should warn people of this maybe add to the instructions that before you activate the motor, push the bottom up manually, to make sure it clears the wall. there should be some option for emergency release.

perfect stand for a cell phone.  i have a samsung galaxy iii s, and the charger hangs off the bottom perfectly without getting smashed at all.  it's all metal, very stable, and i like the mesh.  these little electronic things are inclined to throw a lot of heat, and the mesh and the stand allow for more circulation around the phone.

i have used this for my samsung tab 3.  it works, but i'd like something just a little larger for that.  if i didn't have it in a fairly heavy / thick cover, it would likely work better.

i would definitely recommend.  i'm thinking this may be on the "christmas gift" list for family and friends next year.

reviewText:
this is my first tablet. i've had it a couple of weeks now. i got it to purchase college ebook textbooks because it was more affordable than paying for the physical books. i am not impressed by any means.

cons:
*it is very slow. it locks up and crashes constantly. trying to use the browser is a test of patience i cannot pass. in the time it takes to load a webpage on my tablet, i could have already did it several times on my laptop (even something as simple as a google search.)
*the battery life is terrible. you might as well just leave it plugged in at all times.
*the camera quality is terrible.
*it has a little weight to it and makes it uncomfortable for long periods of use. forget playing any type of game that you have to tilt the screen for.

pros:
*if you have patience, it will function for what you need.... eventually.

if for whatever reason you do get it (not everyone can afford an ipad, certainly not i), you will need the following additional items:
1. a pack of styluses- the constant lagging and angrily dragging your finger across the screen to unfreeze it will get old and your finger will start to hurt.
2. a case that stands up- as mentioned before, the weight will get to you after a while
3. a micro sd card- the internal memory sucks
summary: what do you expect for a $50 tablet?

reviewText:
i do like my new router, but was disappointed, especially after 3 days of working with my backup software and many chats with about 6 company tech support folks to discover the following:

the firmware does not support full access to the usb-attached drive.  sure, you can map the drive and write to it and read from it, but you don't have the level of access necessary to adjust the attributes of the files.  (for example, you can't unset the modified attribute and the file timestamp you get when you xcopy the file will always be the current time, not the original timestamp of the file.  this renders many backup solutions useless.  (a senior tech at the company finally explained -- after many hours going 'round and 'round with 3 different firmware replacements -- that this is a known "product limitation" and she pointed me to the nslu2.
summary: storage link has limited utility, only supports r & w.

reviewText:
shopping for a dvd player is something i've dreaded. it seems every dvd player model i've seen fails. my dad got a brand new sony combo vcr and dvd--it skips on new movies. my brother got a used samsung--same thing. my friend's xbox spins up and never plays, just starts grinding. my friend's philips will sometimes read movies and sometimes won't--how scratched they are or not has little impact, except that they're slightly more likely to confuse it if they are. but brand new dvds without a spot on them still confuse it. it got so frustrating that i finally caved and decided i needed to replace the thing, as much as it was nice to be able to watch movies (sometimes, at least) for free (albeit with lots of headaches).

when i ran across this panasonic, there were no serious negative reviews. no total red flags. the price was good and the features were suitable.

but the very first time i tried to load a dvd, the tray withdrew as the dvd was half in--it extended to its full open position and hovered there for a split second when it reversed course. the dvd, which it snatched from my hand in the process, got stuck, and i feared it would be destroyed. but i pressed the eject button and it came out. but again, the tray withdrew very quickly. i looked in the manual--nothing. inexplicably, one time it stayed open like other dvd players i've seen--long enough to put in or take out a movie and then some. but then it reverted back to its spastic opening and closing behavior. and sometimes when you press open (or click it on the remote), it didn't actually open, it just stuck out a little and said it was open. and then horrible grinding noises came out of it. and then i clicked close and it closed, and then i clicked open and it opened--and then withdrew. the grinding noise stopped. and once it a while it worked fine--i think maybe 3 or 4 times out of dozens of times opening and closing it, it actually did what i asked it to do.

putting a dvd in is like trying to draw a gun faster in a duel: you watch intently and you keep your trigger finger ready, but if you're off by a fraction of a second, you're a dead man. it's completely unacceptable, which is a pity, because i was going to give panasonic a chance. now i'm thinking of hitting a couple other brands and seeing if any actually work or if all dvd players are doomed to bugs like these.

ironically, so far it has had little trouble actually reading the movies and playing them. the remote works fine, although as other reviewers mentioned it's a bit small without much finger space. and there's no separate pause button, which is annoying because sometimes i accidentally hit pause.

i'd order a replacement of the same type since feature wise it's perfect, but a bug like this right up front just doesn't give me any confidence the replacement will not also fail soon. and since dvd players seem to only have 90 day warranties (on labor, which they'd likely bill it as) most of the time, i'm not confident the manufacturer has any confidence in their product lasting longer than that. so, i've decided to return it.

reviewText:
i did not buy this board from amazon, but so frustrated at the board i wanted to comment everywhere i can.

this board got my attention due to the number of hot swappable sata ports, although i don;t overclock i prefer boards that do, and the easy overclocking genie seemed easy enough to do light overclocking.

be sure to read several forums on this board and the problems people are having. i had to rma mine after 30 days and no longer under exchange days. i paid for overnight shipping and had to wait 4 weeks to get a replacement. the replacement came and it too is bad and now i have to rma the board, msi has no customer service and refuses to refund the board. i can't afford to pay shipping again wait 4 more weeks for another board that "might" work. i had to buy a competing board.

if i had searched the internet first instead of just going by feedback i would have realized several people are having issues with this board.

it has a lot of features and if you get a good board the first time it probably rocks. but if you get one of their bad boards, they will start making accusations that you have done something to the board. i have built computers for probably 20-25 years and have never had to return a motherboard that was bad.

next time i will make sure i order the motherboard last, so all of my components can be installed before the 30 days are up and you can get the rma from amazon or other retailer.

reviewText:
acer's aspire s13 is pretty close to being a really, really great portable. as it is, though, it's merely very, very good, and that's a tiny bit of a shame.

but let's start at the beginning.

the unboxing is pretty standard fare. just the laptop, a power cord, and a teeny bit of literature, in a generic cardboard box. peculiarly, my s13 wouldn't even power up the first time without the power cord plugged in. this led me to believe that the battery was dead, but it wasn't. 88% full, in fact. bizarre! after the first boot-up, no further power-related oddities to report, but it definitely threw me off at the start. it might just be a programming choice to make sure the user runs through the initial setup plugged in to make sure no shut-down issues arise while configuring the system the first time...

first hardware impressions are mixed. the screen has a sizeable bezel around it, and it's quite plastic-y, which is a bit disappointing (especially compared to the stunning dell xps 13). tapping away at the keys before booting left a much more favorable impression, though. these ultra-portables tend to have very shallow keys which can make fast typing a bit tricky. i'm pleased to report that the keys on the s13 are actually very nice to type on. not too shallow at all, and certainly deeper than the 12" macbook. the keys are full size, and i took to typing on it speedily within minutes. the function keys along the top are a little small, though not as often used, and the arrow keys - as with many laptop keyboards these days, are too small for my liking, but so it goes. disappointed to not have transport keys (i.e. play/pause/next track/previous track). the power button is in the top right, above the backspace key. thankfully, you need to hold the power button down for it to do anything, so you won't accidentally put your system to sleep or power it off. in any case, i've not hit it by mistake at any point anyway.

when the system boots, you're immediately greeted by a fine-looking display. it's good to see ips displays finally becoming more mainstream in this space as high-resolution laptops become more of the norm. the viewing angles are very nice here. this non-touchscreen aspire s13 features a matte (yay!) ips display, and this has its pros and cons. for one thing, it's nice to not have to deal with reflections like i do with my imac and other portable apple devices. however, the trade-off is not quite as vibrant colors like you get with glossy displays. in addition, there's a reasonable anti-glare coating at play here, giving the screen a slight shimmeriness, most noticeable on white or light backgrounds. it's not as bad as some displays out there, but if you're sensitive to this you might want to bear it in mind when choosing a laptop.

setting up windows 10 home included here was very simple, and i was up and running within minutes. at this point, a quick trip to control panel revealed a bunch of bloatware that i had to uninstall. disappointing to see a bunch of nonsense apps forced on the user, but thankfully it was easy to remove them all one by one.

at this point, and with some proper playtime with the system, here are some observations:

1.) there is just one, small fan cooling the system. under normal usage (casual browsing etc) it's either completely off or running quite slowly. the system is actually very quiet compared to other laptops out there, and it runs quite cool, too. however, there's definitely an up-and-down tendency to the fan. it prefers to spin up for as long as needed and then immediately slow down/shut off. this repeats with predictable regularity, so if this sort of thing you're sensitive to, it's worth bearing in mind. compared to a macbook pro which just runs its fans constantly and quietly, this is much more sporadic in nature.

2.) the two downward-facing speakers are surprisingly good, and loud. i wasn't expecting this. there's even a touch of bass here. no, it's not thumping, but that there is any bass at all is quite a feat. go in with low expectations and prepare to be surprised.

3.) keyboard backlighting has three settings: low, high, and off. the backlighting isn't as uniform as on a macbook/macbook pro, but it works well enough. some light leakage around the keys, and some keys are brighter than others, however. again, it works, but it would be nice to see a tidier lighting system. also, it's a little frustrating that the backlighting turns off after 30 seconds if no keys are pressed, and that's not customizable. i was hoping that interacting with the trackpad would at least light the keyboard up again, but nope... in the dark you'll need to fumble/press a key, and that will re-illuminate the keyboard.

4.) this is quite a zippy system. it's a standard fare core i5, 8gb, 256gb ssd (middle of the road kingston), but it feels quick enough for an everday system.

5.) the intel 520 gpu isn't exactly gaming-pc-grade hardware, but if you temper those expectations you can get reasonable framerates on some games with low settings. at 720p, with graphics settings set low, diablo 3 gives me 50-60fps on high-level rifts. sure, it's not exactly a feat, but it's more than i was expecting. at 1080p, those framerates are more in the 30 range. again, the noise put out from the system isn't even particularly intrusive at this point, either.

6.) the power brick features a really tiny, seemingly fragile connector. i'm interested to see how this holds up over time, but it really does feel a little puny. the port it goes into in the system has some play designed into it, so it may hold up better than i expect, but it's not confidence inspiring...

7.) wifi and bluetooth both work brilliantly here. i connect via 5ghz ac wifi to my latest-generation apple time capsule router, and have had solid connectivity without issue. speed tests confirm i'm maxing out the connection to my provider, and my local connection to my other systems on the network. bluetooth has been great, and i'm happily using sony bt headphones to play music wirelessly.

8.) the trackpad isn't anything special. yes, it's multitouch, and yes, it's large, but it's not anywhere near as responsive as a good macbook trackpad (apple is simply unbeatable at trackpads). it works, but i wish it were less... flakey. friction for one thing isn't perfect, and my fingers tend to get a little hung up at times. having a glass trackpad like with apple's systems would alleviate this issue. i was also surprised to see no native chrome two-finger navigation back/forward a page, something every other laptop with multitouch has, - that i've ever used!

9.) very pleased to see two usb 3 ports, a usb-c 3.1 port, and absolutely no legacy usb 2.0 ports, finally! the sd card slot is nice to have, but it would have been nice to have ethernet, too. just can't beat a good wired connection for reliability!

10.) the 720p webcam features hdr (high dynamic range). this is impressive. the 720p resolution isn't anything too special, but the camera handles both dark/light areas of the frame really well. e.g. if you're sitting with a window behind you during the day, this can cause issues for a lot of webcams, but but this one really does a nice job, exposing well despite the massive subject exposure difference. a green led lights up next to the camera when it's in use.

11.) i like that there's not a massive amount of leds indicating power/disk activity etc. there are just a couple on the side of the system. they're never in the way, and you can barely see them unless you make an effort to look at the side of the machine. this is great! no distractions!

12.) sitting in bed, in the dark, typing on this machine, i really like the blue-light reduction setting in the acer software. it really takes the edge/harshness off of the display when you're trying to wind down for the night...

13.) battery life is solid, though i cannot see how you'd ever attain the advertised 11 hours of battery life unless you had the brightness all the way down, wireless off etc. i get approximately 6 hours at medium brightness, browsing the internets etc.

14.) boots outrageously quickly from cold. it's up in just a few seconds.

overall, this really is a solid laptop from acer. some build quality/trackpad issues are a bummer, as is the large and plastic bezel around the display. but the core functionality is there, built around intel's solid skylake processor line. great sound, good thermals and a lovely ips display are the things that set this system apart.

alternatives: dell xps 13, asus zenbook ux300 series.

4 stars out of 5. recommended.

*update august 10, 2016*

this really is a lovely laptop for watching movies on. the ips screen has no clouding or hot spots, and contrast is remarkably decent for this type of panel.

however, be sure to go into the intel graphics properties and disable all false contrast enhancement/skin correction. in addition, uncheck the 'display power saving technology' setting in the power options part of the intel graphics properties. leaving this enabled means the backlight is constantly adjusting depending on what is displayed on screen, which i personally have found quite distracting. it's most obviously distracting when you're viewing dark material and then moving to bright material. you can see the backlight pumping very easily. thankfully this was easily disabled. *note* you will need to remove acer's rather useless "power management" software. first, it takes up space, and consumes memory, and second - it interferes with the above setting. so even after you display the "display power saving technology" setting in intel's graphics software, acer will actually reset this setting to being enabled again, which is rather frustrating. after removal of acer's software, this is no longer an issue.

*update, august 11, 2016*

if you haven't updated your new aspire to windows 10 anniversary update, which was just released, i highly recommend you do not. after the update, the trackpad becomes near unusable, stuttering across the screen randomly. external mice remain unaffected. a fresh reinstallation of windows 10 and the anniversary update showed the same issue. only a fresh installation of the pre-anniversary windows 10 resolved this. a real shame.

*update, august 15, 2016*

i do a lot of photography, so i was curious to see how accurate out of the box this ips panel is on the aspire s13. surprisingly, after a calibration with an i1 display pro, there was very little difference between the uncalibrated image and the calibrated image. very impressive, acer! this is a great, well-calibrated display out of the box.

*update, august 31, 2016*

still no fix for the trackpad issues introduced with windows 10 anniversary update.

*update, october 23, 2016*

still no fix for the issue introduced months ago with the trackpad. at this point, i'd recommend you buy something else. it's a shame because the laptop is great, but it's clear acer is not supporting it as well as they ought to.
summary: a solid entry to an overcrowded ultra-portable market.
