reviewText: first off, i've used my spot in real life situations hundreds of times for work and pleasure. these included coast to coast states, every rocky mountain state and a month in new zealand. i've used it in, deserts, forests, an 18 day float trip through the grand canyon, etc. generally i have been pleased, primarily because i have not often depended on it as my sole communication device. it is typically reliable and i do not expect perfection. however, the worst sin you could have with an emergency transmitter is if it indicates a message has been transmitted when it actually has not. for my device the battery indicator light is not sensitive enough to tell if the signal is strong enough to actually register with a satellite, even in a wide open prairie. for approximately 30 sent messages and a multi-week backcountry canoe trip my wife did not receive a single message, even though the all the lights flashed green, indicated a quick gps lock and message transmission. i had spare batteries with me the whole time, but no reason to think they were needed. i reported my problem to spot thinking that given the hundreds of dollars in subscriptions fees they've gotten from me that they might try to make it right (offer to fix my unit, extend my current subscription, etc). what i go was the equivalent of "man, that's a bummer. oh well. hopefully it works next time".
summary: beware the low battery light and spot customer service department

reviewText:
spend your money elsewhere. the one thing that i hate is that the bands on this suck. they just break for no reason other then stress related. i have now had mine for a little more than a year and i am on my third band. at $15 a pop i now have to decide whether or not i should continue to buy bands that are made of garbage or if i should abandon this device and go with a fit bit. albeit a fit bit was certainly 3x as much for the one i wanted (with a readout because i do not have an android to sync it to, but i have a pc...) but it is now getting ridiculous. i can buy a band on here at amazon and pay for shipping, or, because i am cheap, i will buy other things that i need to make $36 or whatever the rate is now and get free shipping and feel like i won. or i can go to ebay and pay some fool $15.00 so that he can come to amazon and use his prime account and buy the band for $12 and have it shipped to me... i hate doing that even more because now the people that do that have flooded ebay with the same items that you can buy here but they all fight to make a few more pennies than the other guy.

and i am done talking about the things that annoy me, back to this. this device is a decent device but if you plan to wear it you must continue to buy bands for it or i have no clue why this company has not taken any hints from casio or timex and made a band that can withstand everything that it gets handed to it. i am not a super active guy. i barely hit 4k calories burned each day. i do not run, i mostly sit on my butt. but the performance of the device itself has now become overshadowed by this stupid band snafu. if the band was good i would not be reviewing this poorly. but i hate subscribing to a band of the month club to continue wearing this (yes that was sarcasm). this device needs a band to hold it against your skin so that it can measure heart rate for all of those times (seven) that i wanted to know what mine was last year. it then probably uses that to count the steps and see how many calories you have burned plus if it has the built in pedometer then it is probably counting the steps i take based on my movements...

i apologize for being brutally honest about one aspect of this device but when i see things like this it just makes no sense why a company will make it and release it unless it is planned obsolescence.  that is where an item is made with the intent that it will function for a specific amount of time and then break and thus, forcing the consumer to buy another one...  i hate things like this.

stay away from this. it will end up costing you more in the long term and after about a year or two, you will be like, damn i wish i bought a fit bit instead...

i was not given this. i paid for it with my own money so that i could give you an unbiased opinion. beware of any reviews in which people were given items. i think they are full of crap a bit much when every review that is positive says they were given that item in exchange for an unbiased review, meanwhile all of the people that paid full price give an honest review with less than 5 stars...

reviewText: i used to own one of these and when it is aimed directly at the source, it gave good reception. the problem is if you live anywhere where there is more than one station, you live in an area where the sources probably come from different directions. i also found that it worked best near a window aimed at the broadcast source. i am only about 5 to 10 miles from most of the broadcast antennas, and about half of them are grouped relatively close together. antennaweb dot org has a great utility to help you locate the broadcast source for the stations you are interested in for your location (just click the "click here to start" button). the base of the unit is small, and this antenna is easily knocked over as it's a little top heavy. it is fairly well balanced, as long as there is no one very close to it moving about. after using this antenna for a while, i got tired of having to re-orient it based on the station i was watching. i finally replaced it with an earlier version of this rca antenna: rca ant1250 uhf/vhf amplified indoor antenna. the rca antenna worked far better with a minimum of adjustment. i would also recommend not buying into the hype of buying a hd antenna. any antenna will pick up the digital signals, it's not magic. finally, i upgraded to an external antenna (for about $50) and installed it in my attic. it works far better than any other antenna i have owned. if you have an attic that is accessible, i highly recommend going this way.

i've owned other cirago products and was pleased with them.

this one, however, is junk.

the bays are larger than a 3.5 inch drive. they are open with the sata connector sitting toward the rear as is normally the case. the problem is that.the bays are so large and the sata connectors apparently a bit short that the drive may not retain contact and go offline! absolutely unacceptable. also, of minor concern, is the front bay is b and the rear a: backwards from normal configuration. there is no ejection mechanism which is a sure invitation to problems when trying to remove one drive while leaving the other in place.

drive recognition appears to take longer than on my other docking stations.

i didn't even try cloning since that isn't one of my concerns.

overall, i warn potential purchasers away from this unit. for a few dollars more, you can go with startech, thermalake or another brand with higher quality.

jerry

reviewText:
my largest concern with this product was the level of assumption; let's start by what it does:

it does indeed connect to a computer, and with a desktop app you can see what the camera sees, pan/tilt, and hit the "fire" button.

unfortunately, beyond 10 feet, the projectile arcs so far down, it's hitting below the bottom of the video feed, so you cannot even see where it hits.  i guess i assumed it had pressure similar to a child's nerf gun.

tilt and pan are by hitting a button, so of course it's by hops (think of a watch with a jumping-second hand rather than a continuous sweep).  the "gunner" needs to choose whether to hit the far left side of the target, or the far right side.

the projectile fires roughly 6 noisy seconds after the launch command, so stealth or quick shooting... they don't go to the same parties and events as the oic.

the extra "over internet" requires an outdated windows pc and uses the old windows messenger tool (i think it's the one already turned off, not the one turning off in april); the good news is that because i tested on a mac, and cannot use the oic feature, i won't see any features disappear.  your mileage may vary.  i would love to see an opensource oic for this.

as a cute way of breaking things up in the cubicle farm, it works; as an actual usable turret for cubicle defense in the event of an office dust-up (stuff of legends, just like the non-existent tech-intern), no good... unfortunately, it's now a $47 paperweight.

i had some expectations for this (involving dogs who should not jump up on sofas but know when people are watching) but the range, responsiveness, and herky-jerky pan/tilt kinda blew it for me.
summary: does as advertised, but range/distance isn't advertised

tilt and pan are by hitting a button, so of course it's by hops (think of a watch with a jumping-second hand rather than a continuous sweep).  the "gunner" needs to choose whether to hit the far left side of the target, or the far right side.

the projectile fires roughly 6 noisy seconds after the launch command, so stealth or quick shooting... they don't go to the same parties and events as the oic.

the extra "over internet" requires an outdated windows pc and uses the old windows messenger tool (i think it's the one already turned off, not the one turning off in april); the good news is that because i tested on a mac, and cannot use the oic feature, i won't see any features disappear.  your mileage may vary.  i would love to see an opensource oic for this.

as a cute way of breaking things up in the cubicle farm, it works; as an actual usable turret for cubicle defense in the event of an office dust-up (stuff of legends, just like the non-existent tech-intern), no good... unfortunately, it's now a $47 paperweight.

i had some expectations for this (involving dogs who should not jump up on sofas but know when people are watching) but the range, responsiveness, and herky-jerky pan/tilt kinda blew it for me. does as advertised, but range/distance isn't advertised

i've had this camera for almost 2 weeks now--and so far i just love it.  i bought it to replace a 4-year-old minolta dimage digital, which while it took good pictures was clearly outmoded, had a small screen that was unusable in daylight, an inadequate rangefinder viewfinder, and lousy battery life (even with ni-mh rechargables).  so i was ready for something new and more advanced.

after doing lots of homework reading specs and customer reviews, i settled on the z612 kodak.  what initially attracted me was the 12x zoom, which i couldn't be happier with.  but the other features are equally good.  the lcd screen is spectacular and i can't say enough for the electronic viewfinder, which is bright and clear (i generally am used to the "put the camera up to the eye" mode of picture taking, so i love the evf).  so far i've only taken photos indoors, mostly of my cats and husband, (which means with flash) but they have all come out sharp, clear, and with terrific color.  after finally figuring out how to work my fancy-schmansy hp photoprinter, i printed several 4x6 prints in 6 mp that are now hanging above my desk and are just amazing.  i can't wait to get this thing out of doors.

i love the different shooting modes.  the controls are very intuitive and easy to reach with the right hand while i have the camera up to my eye.  the symbols for each function and mode in the viewfinder and lcd screen are easy to read and understand.  i'm still learning, but have recently figured out burst mode, which will be great when i'm shooting from moving boats in switzerland this summer.

so far battery seems find, but i will have to do more shooting to find out how long a charge lasts.  i love that the battery and charger were included in the package.  that's $20-30 right there in savings.

my only quibbles, not enough to downrate the camera is that i wish they'd included the full manual in the box.  i had to download 90 pages and print them on my computer, which was a pain--and a waste of paper and ink.  the little start-up manual that comes with the camera is not all that helpful, not to mention that i misplaced the english version and had to try to read the spanish version.

the only other complaint is that the manual and website contains little information on what kind of memory the camera needs and how much it can handle.  i took a leap of faith and bought a 2gb sd card, and, thankfully it works with the camera, but i had little to go on.

and finally, the price on the kodak z612 cannot be beat -- in fact it was nearly half what i paid 4 years ago for the minolta and is at least twice the camera.

all in all, i love this camera.

reviewText:
no doubt about it, this is a nice looking remote. great color. back-lighting. sleek design...but then there's some problems.

first the positives.

it's really nice to have a remote that can hook up to the computer, download information about the remotes and devices that you have and have a lcd to display the buttons that it wouldn't always have. no doubt about it.

it looks really cool and if everything is okay, performs well, as well.

the cons.

this not only happened to my, but my neighbor as well. to recharge the remote you set it in the cradle right? no big deal. except sometimes it just doesn't catch and by the end, it wasn't charging at all. i would leave it on the charger (one beep means it's connected and charging, two means it's disconnected) and it would beep. the next time i used it, it said that it needed to be charged with a red battery indicator. i even set something on top of it, licked it to ensure a connections...everything. it just stopped taking the connection and stopped charging.

i didn't have the receipt because it was a gift (that i wanted) so i found out that the lcd screen is sensitive to being smashed by my fist. repeatedly.

the other down point. the remote lags when given a command. example: i point it at my dvr and rewind to catch something i missed and it takes a moment. it's there, so i press play and it takes another couple of seconds to respond, missing what i wanted. sure you get used to it, but it becomes annoying when it just feels like it lags.

for the price and the charger....i wouldn't recommend it.

reviewText:
the thing to remember if you're looking to buy a case for a gen 2 nexus 7 is how flimsy the new n7 is.  it's nice to have a tablet that's so thin, but it's also extremely fragile.  i had mine in my back pocket without a case and the screen snapped like a twig when i bent over a little even though i am a thin man and had baggy pants on and it only put a very small amount of pressure on the glass.  i own the 1st gen n7 and never had the problem of worrying about bending the screen.  that being said, this case offers very little in the way of reinforcement of the n7.  the front cover is very flimsy and offers hardly any protection at all.  when you fold the front cover into a stand it doesn't work well at all.  the only thing that keeps the cover folded is a tiny magnet and any movement will make it come undone.

i would say the only person i would recommend this to is someone that doesn't want to buy a screen protector and doesn't plan on taking their tablet out of the house, but i noticed the other day that when i open the case it has a habit of sliding the metal part across the screen. i would assume that will eventually scratch the screen if you do not have a screen protector on it.

it's not so bad as to deserve 1 star.  i gave it 2 because it's not complete trash.  it would be an ok case for a tablet that was more sturdy i guess.
summary: if you have a gen 2 n7, get something better that will support how flimsy the n7 is

i'd like to be able to replace it and buy extras of good quality. after shopping for days trying to find decent quality universal-fit pc android tablet accessories such as a keyboard, screen protection, power cords (the one that comes with the tablet is only about 3-and-a-half feet long) and etc i finally contacted tabletexpress through their ebay store, to which they replied that i can buy accessories for $15 each, payable through paypal; that's it. no other information. not a website from which to purchase or get support, no help at all. to speak to them directly you must call them in maryland. judging by the dismal quality of their e-communications, i hesitate to try and speak to them on the phone, and i really think i should be able to buy a tablet screen protector for less than $15. i have found, however, that universal-fit tablet cases sized for 10.0-10.2 inch tablets work fine. i purchased some here on amazon: case logic etc-110 folio for 10-inch ipad/2 and new ipad 3rd generation tablet (black) case logic enst-110 7 - 10.2-inch laptop/ipad/netbook sleeve (plaid) another con of this tablet is the battery life; i've had these headphones for years.  they sound better than most headphones i've owned.  the bass is accurate and full, yet not hyped, and the other frequency ranges come through cleanly as well.  the protective hard case is very clever and protects the headphones well, but can be a bit of a challenge to use quickly.  there's no isolation from outside noise, so they aren't good for some environments, but they give a faithful reproduction of what i'm listening to.  i have other headphones for other purposes (in-ears for travel/airplanes, noise-blocking for environments where isolation is important, etc.), but these are the ones that are the most convenient to use (other than getting them in and out of the case).  they are lightweight and easy to put on and adjust, and it's not hard to forget that you are wearing them.

i recommend these, and if mine were to suffer some accident, i'd probably get another pair.
summary: excellent sound, useful hard case, great value

reviewText:
i am very happy with this case, it is very quiet.  i bought it to build a quiet machine for my media room which includes podcast recording.  combined with noctua fans, it is very quiet, can't usually be heard much at all except when playing games and everything heats up and fans are blowing at high speed.  it meets all my requirements and has more than enough space for all the things i want to put in it, even a 280mm radiator if i ever want to.  power supply can be mounted inverted or regular side up, whichever is which.  4 hd trays.  front door is switchable.  usb 3.0 ready.  2x 140 filter spots in the front.  140 and 120 fans included, though not pwm.

downsides: can't use a 280mm radiator with the top panel on, corsair had to replace the bottom fan filter because it was warped, but they did so nicely, fan filters are restrictive to air flow, but that's the nature of fan filters.  one thing that i was disappointed in was the lack of variability in putting fans in the front.  you can't just install whatever fan you want in whichever place, you have to use corsair's screws, so no silicone fan holders.  i've been thinking of just drilling out the screw threads and using quiet silicone ones.  doesn't really matter if you're using double 140mm fans in the front though, only if you want to mix with a smaller fan.
summary: very good quiet case for the price.

reviewText:
this was my first digital, and a wonderful introduction to the world of digital photography.  i'm sure i've taken more than 10,000 pictures sincei got my s330 last spring, and i've recommended it to three friends who have bought the same camera.  i routinely put my travel photographs on line, and the reviews have been very positive.  the camera has proven to be durable and reliable, and i'm totally hooked on digital photography.  i kept my old point-and-shoot film camera for the first few months after i went digital, but have since given it away and never missed it.  it's all digital, all the time for me.
on the plus size, the camera is very compact (easily fits into a pocket), easy to use, and takes good quality pictures.  it also has a very wide range of manual adjustments to increase the flexibility of your picture-taking, and the controls are very well thought out.  the lcd display is very high quality, bright and sharp.  i carry it with me everywhere, and wind up taking many pictures i would have missed with a larger camera.
there are some quirks and weaknesses i do need to point out for this camera.  color reproduction is uneven, depending on the quality of the light and weather, and on the color and type of subject.  many of my outdoor photos, particularly those taken on overcast or cloudy days, have a noticeable "cast" to them ... bluish or greenish.  this is despite fiddling with the manual settings for "overcast."  the camera loves red (you should see my pictures of the barns of coastal maine) but hates green.  i have never been able to take a picture of a lawn or tree that is anything near true to life, again despite attempts to adjust the manual settings.  on bright days, again despite working with the manual settings, highlights are inevitably blown out (although i hear this is a problem with most digital camera).  in addition, the flash is no more than could be expected from a compact camera.  flash pictures always look ... well ... flashy!
when taking digital photographs, you'll tend to take many more pictures than you would with a film camera, and erase the ones you don't like in the camera.  so i'd recommend at least one additional battery (i have two) and 256 mb memory card if you're going to be doing travel photography without access to a computer to download the photos as you go.  (i get about 360 pictures at highest resolution from a 256 mb card,)  more tips:  digital photography is much easier if you have a mac (it really is as easy as they claim in their ads to download and edit pictures); adobe's photoshop elements 2.0 is incredible (and an incredible bargain), and shutterfly.com is a great site for ordering prints.
i've got my eye on a 5 megapixel 8x zoom for early next year, but i'll keep my s330 for its compact size and ease of use.

reviewText:
i purchased this and received it yesterday. i was skeptical about ordering it because most of the brackets state they do not work on camera's with battery backs, but figured what the heck.
let me say that this fit on my nikon d60 with battery pack with no problem in regards to clearance.
there are several drilled holes in the mounting bar that allow adjustment of clearance for your finger grip if you want. i went with the center one as set up out of the package as it fit placement of the flash best and left ample room for my hands.
the rotating bracket screw seems plenty tight for night, though based on other reviews i will keep an eye on it and cary and allen wrench in my camera bag just in case.
things i did not like about it:
the single screw in the bottom sticks out way too much. i will likely replace this one with one that folds like for a tripod plate.
the single screw does not keep the bracket stable in terms of rotating on the bottom of the camera. there is some textured grip stuff on it that seems to be more for looks then actual tact. i solved this issue by placing two small circle pieces of velcro on both sides of the screw and then also on the bottom of my battery pack. they are small and no obtrusive and hide under my tripod plate when i am not using the bracket.
over all i think this is a good investment and think i will be happy with my purchase.
summary: good bracket with a little modification

reviewText:
i purchased this unit about 2 years ago. since then, i've literally made thousands of copies. anywhere from 1 hr to 3 hour dvd's. at roughly a hundred bucks, this thing has paid for itself many times over. i purchased it mainly to record movies off my satellite. picture quality is very good, generally as good as the source you input into it (non hd of course). it will only record onto dvd+-r discs (i've been using -r) but i've had no luck using dvd+-rw (even though the manual says it does i can never get the player to read these rewriteable discs). it will not record onto dl (dual layer) discs aswell. recording times range from 1 hr (hq), 2 hr (sp), 3 hr (ep), 4, 5, and to a max of 6 hrs. but picture quality suffers with the longer recording times. i've found 6 months into using this unit the clock setting would disappear after setting the auto record function, so at times the recorder would record my program, at other times i would find the unit with no recording. and this unit has a problem recording multiple events at different times onto 1 disc, so if your the type to wanna record 6 shows in one day while your out, you'll likely come home to find out maybe only 2 were actually recorded. yes the remote buttons are fairly small and unlite, but after using this unit regularly i had no issues navigating my fingers around the remote.
the unit may not record certain vhs tapes or dvd's with copy protection on them (you will get an error message on your screen).
just recently my player has been spitting out error messages more often than not when finalizing my discs ("error, cannot record onto disc"). so much so i have to power off the unit, reinsert the disc, have it take a minute to read, try to finalize again, and get the same error message. now if i can't finalize my discs i can't watch them. not sure if the motor or the laser in the unit is on the way out, but it's definitely not working properly lately. unfortunately, i have 200 more unfanilzed discs stacked in spindles i have yet to get to. so, even though it's been 2 years and a couple thousand discs, i can say this unit has worked fairly reliably and has certain paid for itself.
now, i'll need to purchase another new unit to get to my unfinalized discs!
summary: a workhorse for a budget price!

i bought this grip several months ago and have had no complaints. sure, the batteries don't last as long as the official canon ones, and the grip is a little flimsier than the official canon one. but no complaints given great quality for the price.

however, this week, my camera started intermittently shutting off and then died completely. batteries were charged, nothing else seemed to be the problem. it took me a while but i finally realized that the little tab at the base of the "column" of the grip that slides into the battery slot on the camera was no longer depressing the tab inside the camera to tell the camera that a battery was in place. this is the same tab that is pressed down by the battery door without the grip. if the tab is not pressed down, the camera won't turn on. so if your camera mysteriously stops working, put a small piece of duct tape or similar over the little protrusion at the base of the column and slide it into the camera. it should fix the issue. this is documented online in one thread where a camera mysteriously would not turn on and it eventually came out that the user had a knock-off, after market battery grip installed. so this is a known issue.
summary: read this if your camera won't turn on after installing this grip.

reviewText:
i was attracted to the garmin street pilot i2 based on the garmin reputation for high quality gps units and the bundled city select north america mapping software. i have two cars that have dvd navigation systems (nippon denso) built in and have come to appreciate the convenience and routing flexibility this technology provides. i also have three other cars that don't have gps systems and find that i miss having access to the navigation reassurance i experience in my other cars. when i saw the price being offered by amazon on this unit, the features, software bundle, portability and garmin brand i was hooked to take a closer look. the garmin information and the reviews on this page indicated the unit was a superb value and would give me the ability to move the unit from car to car and small enough to throw into my briefcase for out of town travel where i am frequently lost on first visits to new towns. the unit also has frequently updated points of interest (poi) that lists, among other things, numerous restaurants by proximity to where you are currently.

upon actually receiving the unit i was impressed with the small size, the accessories and the build quality of the unit. i followed the start up instructions and booted it up. i did note that the i2 does take longer than other gps units to acquire satellites - strangely much longer on initial boot up and less time on subsequent start ups. the instructions are not very precise on the set up options and i learned a lot by going through the detailed manual on the garmin web site. the i2 is intuitive to use, so kudos to the garmin engineers on having thought through the user interface. the unit is also accurate and provides good directions both on-screen and audibly. battery life is about 6 hours on two aa batteries and garmin includes a car power adapter so this is great. using the scroll wheel for data input is a bit more difficult than my nippon denso touch screens but not bad once you get the hang of it. the i2 lost a star in my rating due to excessive time to acquire satellites, lack of easily accessible documentation for advanced set up and difficult to navigate garmin support web site.

couple of negatives that i needed to work around.
1-there are warnings on the garmin web site that california and minnesota do not allow devices attached to the windshield. i didn't want to put the included permanent attachment disc on the dash as that would lock the unit into one vehicle and likely diminish the resale value of the car at some later date. work around here is to obtain a "type s universal holder" sold on amazon that is intended for ipods and cell phone attachment to dashboard airvent clips. i glued the permanent attachment disc to the holder and it works great. (i did end up putting some thin rubberized electrical tape on the metal "prongs" to increase the friction of the prongs to the plastic vents - now it stays put on bumpy roads.)
2- the garmin i2 memory holds several states on the included 128 mb transflash memory card. i serached the garmin site and found references that other garmin units had been tested successfully with up to 2 gb cards. i ordered a 1 gb card from amazon for ~$40 and it should allow me to hold most of the us (otherwise you need to hook the unit up to your computer - delete states from the memory card you don't need currently and then select and load the staes you want to add) we'll see and i'll post an update if it works successfully (it does! i was able to load all of the us, canada and puerto rico on the 1 g transflash card - only downside is that it takes about an hour to download into the unit from the computer - but i shouldn't need to again until the software is updated).

overall i would rate the streetpilot i2 as a great value from a respected company in gps technology that will provide the accuracy, portability and flexibility that i desire in a gps navigation system.
summary: super value that will get you there

i have been using sony clie pda/samsung uploar sprint phone as my mp3 players. and because of the limit of the memory size, 256mb & 32mb, i was looking for a better replacement.

 i did not like the craze of "ipod" because of the high price you pay and the bulky size you get - my clie pda with memory sticks was not too big compared to ipod/ipod mini, and, hey, sony clie has a color touch screen with all other utilities to play with. and super light. and still cheaper than ipod. these are my arguments with any ipod manias.
  with 4-40gb scratch hdd, some might say that they want to carry all their cd collections in the handbag as if they will never update mp3 files again, and that it could be an alternative external 20-40gb hdd, but to me that would be an expensive choice when you can get 250gb ext. hdd at around $200.

 so, i knew i would like 1gb tiny little mp3 player, hopefully with fm radio as a bonus so that i can carry it anywhere and it could stay in my pocket all the time. i would say this is the smallest/lightest 1gb mp3 player. and the grey/chrome color looks quite "sleek" in my hands.

 originally, i was looking at lexar jumpgear/jumpdisk sport 1gb (approx. $120) but this black plastick thing did not apeal to me much although anyone who anticipates for a future upgrade to 2gb or higher would need this when a bigger flash memory is introduced.
 and i also looked at cheaper but sharp looking chinese oems, there are 3-4 different designs, similar looking to iriver/samsung yepp - but all coming with exactly same monitor screen - directly sold from hk on ebay and i could not trust the quality and it was only 20 some bucks cheaper($85~90) plus s/h ($30+)with no guarantee of after sale services. and i would not bother wasting time bidding on them.

 the new ipod shuffle is no comparison to this at all. no monitor to read/search files, a blind mp3 player? files are shuffled? no way!! is it cuter than other mp3 players? i personally think none of ipod models is good looking, except that they are all white or pastelly. it is like watching people dressed in all white and that is all. kind of looking like a mac groupie to me.

 i paid for this sandisk mp3 player at $143.54 from amazon.com. amazon is the cheapest vendor at the moment with free shipping-ups-in 3 days.

 after 2 hours of listening to music, i have to address some "minor cons". i know sandisk needs to improve this mp3 player a bit.

 1. grey armband with clear mp3 player holder - looks cheap, but it is free!
 2. voice recording volume is too low and it starts 1-2 seconds after pressing rec button and poor hissing background noises when played.
 3. during usb connection to pcs, if you delete old files and add new files, you have to go and check "disk cleanup" as the old ghost files still sit in the flash memory and would not let you add new files until all removed.
 4. fm radio is superb but i found that i could receive more stations in korea setting- the factory default setting is usa.

 5. "b/i/g  d/r/a/w" - the basic operation instruction is not all printed in the quick guide manual, and you have to read rather "lousy" pdf file on the monitor instead. this was painful to me, too many pages to pagedown. but i  finally manage to follow it better second time.

 6. i wish it came with internal usb socket. it could be handy to plug it to any computer for file backup/transfer. the provided us cable is bulkier than the actual mp3 player. some of the chinese oem i mentioned above has an integrated usb socket and it is ready for a file transfer.

 indeed, i love this mp3 player as i expected. the file transfer was super fast. some people complained about the biggie earbuds but it works fine with me. actually, this tightly sits in my tiny ears and does not fall out. it sounds quite true to the original recording sound without the exaggerated bass - very crisp!

 the reason i gave 4 star verdict is because 3 & 5 above. these should have been imrpoved before sandisk introduced this cool player to the market. other than that, i am very  happy with this little thing - smaller than two fingers together. see the pictures i uploaded. good investment!
summary: good design/value/sound - but not easy to follow manual

reviewText: i ordered this system from staples because i found a 10 percent off coupon which brought the price to $182.  the first one i received had a tweeter loose and rolling around in the soundbar.  i brought it back and they sent me another one.  i set this one up and it sounded awesome when it functioned properly.  i really liked the surround sound setting as it worked pretty well for sports and movies.  all the audio had a very clear and crisp quality overall. something i didn't like was that there was just a bass and treble setting for the sound adjustments.  no separate subwoofer setting. so the bass control brings the bass of the soundbar as well as the subwoofer.  i placed the sub next to my seating area and i did notice sometimes it would cut out or get distorted if i walked in front of it.  only 11 feet away line of sight.  after 5 days the subwoofer stopped paring and ultimately never paired with the soundbar again.  i really had faith in phillips seeing as they helped create the first cassette tape and compact disk but there seems to be some quality control issues going on.  if you get a non lemon i think you will probably enjoy it but not for 250$ as it is priced now.  this seems more like a $180-$200 soundbar system.
summary: two bad experiences but it sounds great when it works.

reviewText: i've had my imation atom for about 5 months.  i bought it for both storing files and for playing mp3's using my car stereo that has a usb input on the front.  i had trouble with the other mini usb flash drives that are out there that don't have a full usb connector staying in the usb ports in my pcs, and especially in my car stereo where some keys are hanging off it.  the atom fits nice and snug in both.  after i had the atom for about 2 months, my car stereo started displaying read failed when i inserted the atom, however it would read my other flash drives fine.  i finally ended up copying all the files off, reformatting it, and copying all the files back onto it.  that actually worked, and clearly lead me to believe that it was actually a problem with the atom.  about 4 weeks ago the same problem cropped up again.  i don't have prblems with any other flash drives in the stereo.  about 2 weeks ago, i noticed that the plastic usb plug on my atom had actually melted and deformed.  i'm assuming it was from being in a pc where the port got really hot.  now the top side of the usb connector has completely broken off.  they should have made the usb connector out of metal, and not cheap plastic.  so, i guess i'm going back to my sandisk cruzer micro skin.

reviewText:
this is a tough review to give because this pair of headphones does so many things right but it has an inherent issue that breaks its usability.

first the good:
the headphone's sound profile is really good. the highs are clear, the mids are punchy, and the bass is booming. this is one of the best sounding headphones around, specially for its price. active noise cancelling works well and as it should. the controls are intuitive and located in easy to reach, logical places where you can make adjustments without taking the headphones off. padding on the cups are really, really soft. this adds a lot of comfort for the listener which is great for long listening sessions, but is sadly counter acted by a design flaw.

the bad:
unfortunately, these headphones suffer from a major flaw, and that is audio sync. there is about a 1.5 - 2 second latency when paired via bluetooth. this makes it impossible to use the headphones for anything other than casual music listening. a few other issues have to do with build quality. for the price, you can't expect great materials, but the plastic and finish used for the arms of the headphones feels and looks really cheap specially with the fake chrome finish. the arm also features a swivel mechanism that allows you to fold the headphones flat. unfortunately, this swivel mechanism has been implemented backwards and locks in the opposite direction that would provide better comfort. without the ability to swivel the cup towards the neck, the front of the headphones put a lot of caliper pressure near the temple. it's uncomfortable.
summary: good for music / bad for video

i overall do not like this case, especially given the price, and will be going back to the combination of the apple smart cover with additional sleeve when needed.

reviewText:
unless you have a lot of money ... and want to go ahead and get it, i would recommend holding off on this unit.  i have tested it and returned it because of several things that are wrong with it, but, could easily be fixed in future generations.
  if you just want to record from cable/uhf/vhf, then, you shouldn't be disappointed with this model.  i found no problems with recording from cable or in its audio and video quality.  however, copying from vhs input, the main selling point for me on dvr's, is where i started to dislike this unit.
  on vhs input, it suffers from signal drop, skipping over dropped out audio and video.  if the vhs tape was damaged, then, i could understand, as it's a tracking problem.  but, this happens in certain specific areas of certain tapes, but, never exactly in the same spots, just the generalized area.  plus, i tested two different vhs inputs, a philips dvd/vcr combo and a go video vhs.  there was still signal drop from the go, but, this just amazed me, there was more signal drop from the philips!  the input and output sources were devices from the same company, yet, the results were worse.
  also, be aware that this unit while it will play some dvd recordable formats it doesn't write to, it won't play pressed dvd-rom, e.g. the dvd movies you buy in a store!  the video keeps skipping, with no audio.  also, dvd+r, the write once/read many (worm) dvd disc format, is only just now coming out, and, the entire dvd+ format is more expensive than the traditional dvd- format used in most other recorders.  the dvd+ format was made to capitalize on a market without standards yet, so, don't be pulled into it.
  if you just want a cable signal recorder, then, if you can spare the money, this unit is a good choice.  i'd wait until they work out the bugs in it, though, before buying it myself.

i own a nikon d5100.  this was my second lens.  this was a big decision for me.  i got this lens to take indoor pictures of my newborn, now toddler, son.  i noticed that the pictures were constantly soft.  initially i thought it was due to the lens being wide open and no vc.  even after stepping up to 5 and plenty of light, the pictures were soft.  then reading through some forms, i thought it may have been my auto focusing technique.  about 2.5 years later, i posted the complaint with some pictures on an online form and someone mentioned that the focus seems to be sharp right behind the object i meant to focus.  after learning that, i googled a focus test and learned that my lens had a back focus problem.

i sent it into tamron for repair and it is covered under warranty.  the positive is that they will re calibrate and send it back.  but i am very frustrated.  this has been my primary lens and for the last 2.5 years, i have been taking soft pictures of my son and family.  i have thrown away a lot of possible good pictures due to bad focus.  this will be the last tamron lens i will get.  i would rather pay a bit more and get good pictures than to save a bit money and gamble.  especially for a enthusiast like me who is still learning what a good picture should look like.

i've had this unit for about 9 months now.  i've had nothing but frustration with this unit.  another product that was rushed through r&d to market.  i have trouble dubbing from hd > dvd with 'selected' shows (failed).  the tv guide feature doesn't not work correctly with all cable systems.  i'm an engineer in the cable tv industry so i know how the technology works for this unit.  some cable systems inadvertently strip the data (vbi data) from the signal which is where the data is carried for the tv guide feature to work.  in addition, the timer recording (manual setup or schedule setup) has just vanished on it's own more than once.  in other words, i'll have 4 shows programmed for record.  they'll record no problem for 3-4 weeks and then for some reason, they all erase (as if the unit reset itself).  i then need to go back and reprogram all these shows over again.

i called sony support in regards to the tv guide feature and they transferred me to several customer service reps since none of them could figure out what was wrong (or even understand the problem for that matter).

this unit's going on ebay very soon!  i don't recommend this to anyone.  i figured i'd give the unit some time but 9 months is enough!

reviewText:
first thing's first, when i was researching this keyboard many users were complaining about the spacebar being too stiff. i've been using it now for two weeks and have determined that the problem is due to the curvature of the keyboard. the farther away from the center of the spacebar you that you tap it, the stiffer it is and is thus less responsive. if you happen to tap it closer to the middle, then it's fine.

i'm a programmer and i type all day long and use the entire keyboard (function keys and all the puntuation that comes with writing code). after i had a chance to use an ergonomic keyboard for a couple months w/o any pain, i finally purchased the ergo 4000. i love it.

as for a couple specifics, the last ergonomic keyboard i used had an enlarged delete key. the home, end and page keys were normal size. i never got completely used to it and was glad when the ergo 4000 came with a normal cluster as i use those keys alot.

also, as is typical, this keyboard has a function lock key that can toggle between the standard function keys and special programmed shortcuts. i use the function keys alot and never use the special functions, so i was also pleasently surprised to discover that function lock is turned on by default. so when i first boot up and login, i don't have to remember to turn the function lock on.

the only con i can come up with is that there is only a single "windows" shortcut key located on the left side. i also use this key a lot and my last keyboard that came with my gateway had the shortcut key on both sides and i tend to prefer to have the key on the right side. but i can live with it. i hope this helps others.

reviewText:
okay sooo then i love my laptop but it's my "desktop" full service machine basically and i hate using the built in trackpad.  at home i have a full sized mouse but i was going to be away from home for an extended time and wanted to pack light.  well i was one grumpy girlie when i realized oh yeah, extended trip without a mouse = grrr.  so while out picking up things we needed i spotted this.  perfect as i always have limited space and it was cheap cheap and i don't need to buy a good expensive full service mouse for where i am when i'll just have to give it away when i leave.

now there's the good - it works fine.  it's comfy.  clicky clicky and the cord is all wrapped up (only once with months of daily use did it get caught / tangled in the process and it was minor and worked out easily).  it's affordable.  i plugged it in and it worked.  great.

then there's the bad - you do get what you paid for.  it's not going to hold up to daily use long term.  a few months in and it's dying fast.  it sort of works now and then, but it just doesn't want to be recognized.  ahh yes, the oh so pretty light is out.  or no!  it's on!  nope just kidding.  oh yup it is!  i suspect it's just the cable not holding up and it is starting to look tattered at both ends  - frayed isn't the right word, tattered probably isn't either.  just worn.  it's tired of being used.  i wasn't even unplugging it often, just winding the poor thing so that my cats couldn't eat the cable.  yet yeah, that looking tired cable / thinner in spots cable = now i have to wiggle it around for it to work, etc.  it's a pain.  i tested other things plugged into the same slot, it's the not computer, everything else is hunky dory.  so, yeah, it just doesn't hold up to the abuse of daily use and one to two cord winds a day over a few months time.

i would recommend it for short term uses or to keep around as an easy to store emergency mouse.  for regular use or daily use?  it's just not going to hold up for long and you'll be replacing it often.  i've not looked to see if there is a wireless version, if there is, i'd be thinking of that even though you'd surely pay a bit more.
summary: for what you pay, it's great... but...

reviewText:
first of all, this system cannot be expanded - i discovered this after purchasing the listed add-on camera (lw2731ac1) and attempting to sync it.  the lw2731ac1 camera would not connect at all, and i'm not sure what camera will - the lorex web site does not even acknowledge my monitor's model number ("wl2730" instead of "lw2731") on their accessory compatability page, and attempts to contact tech support about the issue have been in vain (finally wound up returning the add-on camera to amazon for a refund).  i am not prepared to purchase every single camera lorex sells to try to find the one that can sync!

with that said, this is a nice camera system.  good day and night visibility - can see clearly to the end of my driveway (about 60' from the camera).  good color during the day, and the night vision is very clear.  features multiple sensitivity and recording settings, though it is almost too sensitive - it turns on in response to leaves blowing across the driveway, changing shadows from the trees, or even moths flying in front of the camera at night.  reviewing 100+ five-second clips that were captured throughout the day can be tedious at times!  the video files are stored as .avi files, and both windows media player (version 11.0.6002) and realplayer (version 16.0.0.282) can play the files. real time video is smooth, but playback can be jerky.

this system would benefit from a touch screen to help navigate through the menus as the buttons below the display are not very responsive.  also, viewing the images remotely requires a connection to a pc and an active internet connection, so checking the cameras while you're away on vacation requires your computer to stay on the whole time as well.  remember the camera needs to be plugged in (and a longer cord would be helpful).  running an extension cord through the attic & routing the camera power cord through the eaves wasn't too difficult, and since it's wireless, i don't need to run a signal cable all the way back to the monitor.  i have had no connectivity problems between the monitor and the camera.  my monitor is approximately 40-50' from the camera, & the wireless signal passes through two interior and one exterior wall (wood frame construction/vinyl siding - you may have different results through brick/stucco walls).

installation of the camera was easy - three screws secured the base to the house, and the camera screws onto the base.  it was very convenient having the monitor screen with me while making those final camera adjustments for the proper field of view - imagine having to come inside to view a tv or computer monitor after every adjustment!  syncing additional cameras is supposed to be simple - select sync from the menu, select an unused channel, then press the button on the back of the camera within 30 seconds.

overall, i'm pleased with the camera.  this whole camera sync problem is just making it difficult to expand the system like i wanted to.  if i had to do it again, i would have simply purchased the one that already included the additional cameras!
summary: nice system, but can't seem to add extra cameras.

reviewText: this is a basic 5.1 sound system with integrated wi-fi; it won't blow you away and fill up a home theater with movie theater sound but it does a fine job in an average size room. i'm using it in a 16 foot x 18 foot room with a 32" tv. that seems to be a good room size for these speakers. fyi: 2.1 means that there are 2 speakers and a subwoofer. 5.1 mean that there are 5 speakers (2 front, 2 rear, 1 center front) and a subwoofer. setting it up is not too complicated. all the speaker wires & the connections on the back of the receiver/blu -ray player are color coded so it's pretty easy. the included directions are minimal and the owner's manual is on a disc. i went to the lg website to get the owner's manual instead of just randomly pushing buttons on the remote while watching a blu-ray to figure out how to adjust sound, etc. i wish they had included the owner's manual with the system; other thoughts

reviewText:
i was excited to get my hands on this lens and spent the last 3 days taking pictures of everything and anything. in arizona there is no shortage of sunshine, so these pictures were under "ideal" light conditions.

first few shots taken from the office window looked pretty fuzzy. i set the camera to full auto and they seemed better. over the next few days i experimented with various settings and found the lens rather hit and miss with focus. items that should have been obvious point of focus were not always so. a few "difficult" images of mesquite tress came off with nothing in focus. comparing to the stock lens, and similar pictures i'd taken with an ef-s lens i'd had, i was rather peeved with it's out of focus images. it was much slower than a canon usm lens and had real trouble in low light finding a focus point too.

i was impressed with indoor shots of fruit using flash, very detailed.

people have remarked on the focus ring turning while you hold on to it, which it does, but you learn not to. the reverse thread is also something you pick up on quickly, so neither of these are an issue i feel.

also found when comparing photos with the stock 18-55mm my canon xti came with there was a distinct red tinge to the outdoor pictures taken with the tamaron lens. nothing photo shop won't fix but a bit strange. both lenses had b&w uv filters.

conclusion, i may have had a bad lens, it did work well when it could focus. build quality was also quite good. it's going back and i am going to spend a few hundred more and get the canon. 6 year warranty was nice touch, but i'd probably stick with a fixed focus tamron lens on a future purchase.
summary: some good results, but red tinge and focusing are a problem

reviewText:
the acer c7 has a very upward battle to fight among the google community and in people's mind. the samsung that just came out before it has been getting excellent reviews and has been labeled the better computer, but is it really?

i was a bit shocked when i got my acer at the small size of the product. let it be stated that these are possibly the most portable computers when it comes to wanting a real keyboard. this computers weighs in at a little over 3 lbs but honestly you wouldn't think so as my wife can lift it easily with one hand. the overall casing is solid enough to give you enough confidence to carry it around without the feeling of breaking it but still not a full laptop/macbook quality when it comes to overall durability.

what stands out when you open it first is the keyboard. people have made this statement over and over but this little $200 system has the keyboard of a decent laptop. the keys are really responsive and nicely spaced, honestly it feels like a full keyboard most of the time. two of the place where the laptop falls short is the track-pad and camera. the camera is very good compared to the samsung but really doesn't give you any options when taking pictures (adjusting brightness, contrast, etc) this can be done on the back end with a photo editing program but not during. the track-pad is okay at best. you won't be raving over it but your not going to be giving it praise either. the screen resolution is overall very good, i watched netflix this morning on it and i was very happy with the overall look and sharpness of the screen.

differences between this and the samsung are simple. this computer carries a 320 gig spinning hard drive and the samsung has a solid state 16 gig hard drive. both come with 2 years of google drive 100 gig service for free which is more than enough for most people. the google community as a whole prefers a solid state as it has no moving parts and it follows google's overall vision of the machine. but unlike the samsung the acer has a removable hard drive and can be installed with an ssd (same with ram and battery).

this computer also uses and intel chip which means it can run things that the samsung can not just yet. example netflix. the samsung machine will eventually be able to but currently can not. this computer also has a fan as the arm process runs cool enough to not need it, however if you are used to the fan of a full sized laptop then unless you are in a completely quiet place you'll never notice this fan.

the google's os works about as good as expected. there are many things that you will not be able to do that you could do on a windows/mac/linux machine that is a given. they are working very hard on resolving these issues. right now i would say you if you buy this machine you are pretty much a beta tester. i could easily recommend google chrome for writers, children, people who travel a lot, and people who generally work on the web (you know who you are). i am happy enough with the os as it's fast and just works. i use it for both personal and business and i have encountered very few issues that couldn't be resolved with a google search.

pro's
removable ram, hard drive and battery - which can lead to replacements or upgrades after/during warranty cycle.
glossy screen (better for movies not better for outside)
ethernet and vga ports (the samsung does not have this - it is only wifi/3g)
quick start-up (22 seconds on average for me - not as fast as the samsung but windows users know this is fast!)
netflix works (samsung still being worked on)

con's
not the fastest chromebook (samsung is faster start up, 550 is the best performance.)
small webstore (chrome's web store is pretty small with that being said they still have many programs that you would normally find on windows. quality will get better as more people purchase the systems.)
netbook size (this computer is small, that doesn't mean it's bad but i'd like to see a big computer down the road)
os development (the os is still being worked out so you should be prepared for things to change - however if you like change there is nothing more exciting than being part of the process.)
battery (4 hours max - 3:30 to 3 on average needs better battery life or extended battery option)
summary: a few miss hits but overall worth the value

reviewText:
bought this last november to use as a tv mostly in a darkened room at night. not the right set for that because viewsonic left off a crucial control for any lcd tv - backlight adjustment. the backlighting is so bright you cannot get more than a gray for blacks. try to adjust the "brightness" and you crush the blacks in the image into the gray.

the lcd panel is 16:10 not 16:9 as stated in some viewsonic info. this is typical with this size tv. however viewsonic did not provide a 16:9 aspect ratio with the picture settings, so everything is slightly squeezed with geometric distortion, and the limited "zoom" modes are useless to correct for that.

also the panel is very inconsistent with the amount of light leakage and hotspots all around the edge, and bad light leakage at the top and bottom of the panel. the tiny (tinny) speakers can barely keep up without an odd resonant buzzing. they are very weak. no auto volume, limited tone controls, no "surround" mode.

another real annoyance for late night viewing is the bright blue power indicator light behind the power button on the front. no way to turn that off in a menu setting. i had to put a piece of black tape over it to make it tolerable.

i just bought a samsung ln19a330 to replace it. the samsung has adjustable backlighting, a 16:9 display ratio with other useful picture settings, and the audio is much better. i will be selling the viewsonic at a loss. i will give viewsonic credit for one thing, they did offer to swap it or give me trade-up credit for another viewsonic tv, but i would have to go to a much larger size to get adjustable backlight, and i need a 19" size to fit in a limited space.
summary: not so good tv unless you are in a bright room!

reviewText:
most reviews are about how well scratch out works (or fails to work), so i thought i'd add a little info about the product itself. there are a few things to be aware of:

1. it smells like paint thinner. the fumes were strong enough to give me a pretty bad headache. buffing out scratches requires you to get pretty close to the disc to examine it, so be prepared to hold your breath while using it.

2. the tube is mostly air. it comes puffed up and sealed, so it seems like you are getting a lot of product, but once you pop the seal off it deflates and it turns out that the tube is 3/4 empty. on the shelf the size of the bottle made $5.97 seem like a good deal, but as soon as i opened it i felt completely ripped off.

3. the product itself is kind of like runny toothpaste. it pours out easily, but makes a huge mess when using it. it also dries really quickly. once you smear it on the disc it almost immediately starts hardening up. that makes it difficult to know how much "buffing" you're supposed to do, or how hard you're supposed to press down (the directions aren't clear on that).

my results:

i tried scratch out on a dvd and an audio cd.

1. the dvd played fine up to chapter 5 in the movie, at which point it would then freeze. the disc had a small scratch (approximately 1/4 inch long) that wasn't deep. i don't know that the scratch caused the problem, but i assumed it did and wanted to see if scratch out would fix it. it didn't. i tried following other people's advice: work radially outward, try multiple applications, & immediately wash with dish soap. after ten applications the scratch was still there and the disc still froze in the same spot. the only improvement was that the movie would skip to the next chapter and keep playing, whereas before it would completely freeze and i had to take the disc out. after ten applications the disc looked as though i had washed it with steel wool. it was completely covered in thousands of small scratches. while that didn't affect how it played, i didn't like how destroyed the disc looked. why use a product that creates a thousand scratches when i'm just trying to get rid of one scratch? and since scratch out didn't remove the scratch or fix the problem with the disc, i'm calling this one a failure. to be fair - maybe the disc had a glitch in the way it was manufactured, or maybe scratch out just didn't work. i don't know either way. but it didn't work well enough for me to risk damaging other dvds that still play (with minor skips/freezes).

2. the audio cd wouldn't play at all. since the disc was essentially worthless, i gave scratch out a try. the disc looked perfectly fine (no scratches at all), but neither the computer nor the cd player would read it. i did one application of scratch out on the entire disc and immediately washed it. the entire cd now plays fine and it ripped to windows media with no problems at all. so - with this disc scratch out worked great. it was a cd that i really liked and had looked at re-buying. cost on amazon: $10.99. cost of scratch out at walmart: $5.97. to me that means i got the cd i wanted for basically half the price i would have had to pay to replace it.

to sum it up:

while i'm happy it did work on one disc, i think the product causes as many problems as it fixes. if i could do it over i would rather re-buy a scratched/unplayable disc than deal with the headache that comes with using scratch out (even if it does work).
summary: mixed results and a bad headache

reviewText:
i purchased this ahead of a roadtrip, during which i had my gopro rigged for use while driving.  as a result, i had occasion to use 2-3 batteries a day, over a 4 week period.  i've had good experience with wasabi batteries and chargers in the past, but these did not seem to be up to the task, at least not such heavy use.

the 12 volt adapter fuse blew.  it appears that it was a 2 amp fuse.  the closest replacement fuse i could find on the road was a 5 amp fuse, and that blew almost immediately.  (i didn't have problems with any other 12v electrical devices i was using.)  i ended up needing to use a 12v inverter i had with me to use the charger in the car for most of the trip.

then also, it's pretty easy to not snap the battery in place quite completely, or for it to come unsnapped (perhaps due to car vibrations), resulting in the battery not chargiung, or not charging completely.  however, the charging indicator with no battery/contact is identical to a fully charged battery, so it's easy to not realize that you haven't fully charged the battery.

finally, after several weeks on the road, it seemed clear (though i didn't time it) that the oem battery life was significantly longer than both of the wasabi replacement batteries.

if you have less demanding uses, these batteries, and this charger, will probably be fine.  but be aware that it is not up to oem quality.
summary: some significant issues mar performance for heavy use and car charging use

i really cannot endorse this product due to its limited functionality and the fact that two of the three outlets were bad out of the box.

i'm actually a strictly-nikon shooter, but this backpack got good enough reviews and was in my (cheap) price range, so i took a chance on it.

when it arrived i was surprised that it was as compact as it is. i expected it to be a tiny bit bigger, but it ended up being a good size for me. i am able to carry all of my gear in it (minus my tripod, but i easily hook that on the front) and can easily access it when i need to. it sits comfortably on my back and i feel secure when hiking with it. i carry all of my lenses, batteries, battery pack, cords, cleaning supplies, white balance tools, flash drives, and any other miscellaneous bits and pieces with room to spare.

i was hopeful it had enough room for me to slide my laptop into the main compartment, but sadly it doesn't (15 inch macbook pro). it might fit the 13 inch, but the 15 is too big. granted, the backpack wasn't made to carry all of your gear + your laptop, so this was just me being hopeful. i have a habit of carrying everything on me while out and about shooting so cutting down 2 big, bulky gear bags into just one backpack would have been awesome. maybe next time!

overall, i like it. it's not 100% perfect, but it's darn near close. good for amateurs, hobbyists, and budding professionals who have enough gear to fill it, but not enough gear to require a crazy amount of space.

when i first saw this camera, i thought to myself, "kodak has finally gotten it right." ever since they started making digital cameras, kodak has had, in my opinon, some of the best picture quality available. the metering has always been dead-on and the pictures, although somewhat over-saturated, have always featured deep, sharp colors and extraordinary clarity. the only thing that prevented me from buying a kodak digital camera was the fact that their bodies were cheaply made out of lightweight plastic. then they moved into the easy share line of cameras geared to the entry-level market and things went from bad to worse with the camera styles getting progressively larger and the bodies getting progressively cheaper.

but with the release of the ls753 (and its 4 mp younger brother the ls743), kodak finally smartened up and made an ultra-compact, sleek, attractive, sturdy camera geared to the mid-level user. and the camera is every bit as nice as it looks on the internet. the ls753 is a slick little device. weighing in at just under 6 oz. (without battery) and measuring just larger than a deck of cards, this camera is small enough and light enough to easily fit in your pocket or comfortably fit on your belt. the body is made of high impact plastic and features a metallic front that gives the camera a sturdy feel without making it too heavy or bulky. it's finished in a metallic silver with just a hint of blue tones which, in my opinion, makes for a very attractive color. ergonomically, everything is exactly where it should be and the camera feels very comfortable in your hand. one of the nicest features is the inclusion of a button on top of the camera to quickly change flash settings. also, the camera features a small dial on top, right in front of the shutter button, which allows you to change camera modes. the default setting is always automatic so you never have to worry about accidently setting the dial somewhere you don't want it and then having it in the wrong position when the camera starts up. all in all, this is a perfect design. but, unfortunately, the positive features end there.

as i said, i was fully expecting that this camera would have taken beautiful pictures, based on my past experience with kodak. i mean, with today's technology, picture quality should only be getting better, right? wrong. here's why:

1. the pictures, although clear and crisp in bright light, are far too dark when taken with the flash. but the problem is not consistent and it has everything to do with the automatic iso and speed settings that the camera uses.  at equal distances, some of the flash pictures will be far too dark and some will be acceptable. it seems that the shutter is very fast, but maybe too fast for the size of the lens and the power of the flash. it seems to me, for the majority of the automatic flash pictures, that the camera is not letting enough light in. in fairness, you do have manual control over some of these settings (exposure and iso) and i'm sure, with some tweaking, you can get closer to the right mix. but, for this size camera, why should we be concerned with such things? this is a point-and-shoot, and you expect to be able to do just that.

2. the flash is far too small for the camera and, more often than not, you will find that it will light up only the very closest objects. this gives the unpleasant effect of having only half of your pictures illuminated. coupled with the problem above, the bottom line is that flash pictures are not at all acceptable for this price camera. when compared to my canon s40, which is a similar compact camera, there just is no comparison. the kodak is just not acceptable for indoor use.

3. the camera features a 1.8" lcd display which is crisp, sharp, and easy to see even in bright places. however, it has one major flaw which is that the pictures appear much more dull and dark on the lcd screen then they do when viewed on a computer. (even the ones that actually are dull and dark as described above are far worse when viewed on the lcd screen). this can actually be a difficult adjustment in the beginning because, when previewing pictures on the screen, you may be inclined to discard pictures that you think are too dark, only to find out that they would have been acceptable (or close to it) when viewed on a computer.

4. the low battery indicator is not at all obvious, with just a very small flashing white icon in the far bottom corner of the lcd screen. maybe i'm not paying enough attention, but i almost never see it. and it seems to comes on just before the battery actually dies. the end result is that the battery dies and the camera shuts down as a surprise. and not a pleasant one.

5. the autofocus is terrible, particularly in lower light conditions. you will find that you have to discard about 10% of your pictures because of blur, even with the most steady of hands. this is beacuse the camera was made to point and shoot very quickly without having to wait for the camera to autofocus. and, 90% of the time, it does fine. but for the other 10%, it is very frustrating. i would rather have the camera autofocus for a second or two and beep when it is in focus so that i know the picture is ready to be taken. not having to wait is a nice feature, but you have no idea what the end result will be. i have also had problems with the camera focusing on the wrong subject. for example, just today i took a family portrait using the auto-timer and the picture was blurry. obviously it had nothing to do with movement because neither us, nor the camera were in motion. it just has to do with, again, bad internal automatic settings.

is it all bad? well, not really. as i said, the design is great. and if it had better guts, the camera would be perfect. one thing i love is the comapct battery charger that plugs right into the wall. i wish more camera/camcorder manufacturers would catch on to the fact that we consumers like to remove the battery and put it into a separate wall charger without having to lug around wires, an ac transformer, etc. kodak has gotten this part right. i also recommend the separate custom made leather case that they sell. this fits the camera snugly and offers a lot of protection in a very compact package. one last positive note is the battery life. i had one fully charged battery last through approximately 150 flash pictures and it had plenty of life to spare. this is a very positive feature for this size camera.

in fairness, i have not tested this camera with the docking station or with any of the easyshare software which is supposed to be a major selling point of this kodak line. i am just not that type of user. i prefer to remove the sd card and load my pictures to my computer using a card reader where i can manipulate them. but, even if these easyshare features are flawless, it would not make up for the lousy flash pictures and the all too often blur. nothing, not even ergonomic design, can make up for bad pictures. and, unfortunately, that's just what this camera takes.

what if you only use it outdoors? well, then this camera would be a winner. but, i'll go out on a limb and say that the majority of the point-and-shoot market will not be limiting themselves to outdoor shots. that said, kodak really missed the mark on this one. which is really dissapointing to me because they passed up a golden opportunity to make the perfect digital camera.

back to the drawing board...

we have used plantronics headsets in the past with great success.  bought this model to replace one that was quite old and starting to show some signs of wear.  however, when we first tried this headset, while it was easy to hear conversations, it was very difficult to have others hear us, especially when on a three way call.  with a simple two way call, it appeared to work okay.

we thought it was a defect with the headset, so returned and go another one.  same result.  we even switched phones, but the same issue was there.  so, if you are going to be doing only two way calling, this would be a very good headset.  however, if you do a lot of conference calls, it may not be the one for you.

while it functioned well and the key presses were nice and crisp and it did not miss or add many characters when typing it was just awkward to use.  the main reason for this was the touch pad being on the right and shifting the keypad to the left.  holding it in two hands to type (using it a ouya box for trying in xbmc) i was always kind of stretching with my right hand to hit keys and felt cramped hitting some of the far left keys with my left hand.

overall ok and maybe a little different for people with bigger hands (mine are average sized for a guy) but for me it just didn't feel good typing on it for more than anything that short bits.

i ended up returning this one and getting the older hausbell mini h7 (similar if not the same as some of the rii and ipazzport mini keyboards) and keeping it even though there were a few things about this one i liked better.

it's a 2.5 out of 5 for me.

nice crisp key presses
back-lit keyboard
decent battery life
nice size and feel holding it

cons:
offset keyboard felt awkward to use
felt a little light and cheap but i think it would have held up

reviewText:
once again, i must highlight that you need to have bluetooth built in to your computer for this to work.

i first tested it on my laptop with windows 7. i went to devices and printers, clicked add a device, windows scanned and immediately found the mouse and automatically brought up an installer to setup the mouse. i let it install and it worked. what a great experience.

in windows 7, it has the standard left, right buttons, scroll wheel and button (with horizontal scroll as well). the difference with this mouse is the windows button on the left thumb that is primarily designed for windows 8 (which i'll get to). in windows 7, it pops open the start menu if you push the button. if you swipe up or down on the button, it will move your browser back or forward. this is a nice touch (haha).

in windows 8, i hit windows-i and clicked "change pc settings," then "add a device." the mouse appears and i clicked it, which installed it. i had to go to the action center to finish installing the special software (optional). in windows 8, the mouse is set by default to go to the metro start screen on pushing the thumb button. swiping down pulls in a tab from the left that show all open apps in metro, which you can then click to open. swiping up switches between recent apps directly. i found that i really missed the ability to "go back." with premium mice over the last ten years, you generally have a back button on your thumb, and even in windows 7 with this mouse, that is the default behavior(with a swipe). many of the metro apps act like a website where you click items and you have a top left back arrow, so it seems more important in windows 8 to have a back button than windows 7. in looking in the microsoft mouse & keyboard center software, i don't see a way to change the windows button functionality, so i set the swipe down to be a browser back command (also works in metro apps). another useful feature on the mouse for windows 8 is the horizontal scrolling with the wheel since many metro apps are designed to scroll to the right. in my testing, it was just way too touchy and it would fling the app left and right too fast.

as for comfort, i like the fact that it's not too bulky, yet not a mini mouse (it's wide, heavy and not too tall), so it still fits ok in a laptop bag. it feels good and comfortable in the right hand, but a major design mistake by placing the windows button too far forward. in my hand, with my fingertips at the end of the mouse buttons, but thumb doesn't touch the windows button, so i have to pull the whole mouse back in my hand to be able to touch the windows button.

microsoft markets this as more convenient because you don't need a usb transceiver, but it adds a level of complexity that isn't involved in a regular usb version (and all the new usb mice have tiny transceivers these days anyway). when i tried to move the mouse to a different computer, the only way i could figure to get it to work was to delete the mouse and re-add after putting the mouse into pair mode. in other words, if you are going to use it on multiple devices, it's a pain.

reviewText:
this is a good scope - not great. would not recommend. the focuser was sloppy, too much play. disassembled it, added more teflon shims, relubed it with silicon and tightened the gear. the tripod, despite it's rugged looks is flimsy. if you have even a moderate breeze expect your image to be shaky and blurry.

the finder scope is cheap, awkward and poorly mounted.

as an aside - i bought a 70mm mead refractor ($50). is easier to use, less bulky and gets just as good an image.

updated comments: i have had this scope for about a year now. still not happy with it and will use my recent acquisition, a 40+ y/o sears stargazer refractor, rather than set this thing up. i have been to star parties where there are terrific celestron scopes being used - all schmidt-cassegrain - with superb images.

my rating has not changed and my humble opinion is that this telescope is not worth the money. i have had the mirror out, cleaned it, have a laser collimater, keep the scope protected in a padded case, yet despite my tlc cannot even get a decent view of saturn's rings. forget the details in the orion nebula!

if all you are interested in is the moon . . enjoy.
