i have a couple different brands of dash cams.  i thought this model offers lots of features for such a low price.  the gps info is pretty cool as well.  it is pretty easy to use and navigate menus.  the customer service is top notch. prompt replies back to emails and they go the extra mile to make sure you are happy.  the only issue i dislike is the mount.  it is of a thin plastic.  if you leave the camera on or off but keep it in your window it may damage the mount that colds the camera.  the weight of the camera along with the type of plastic can cause the mount (which is in a u-shape) to expand.  if this happens the camera doesn't fit snug.  you can heat it back up with a heat gun or hair dryer and rubber band it more closed and as it cools it may be good-to-go.  my advice is to never leave the camera in the mount.  you can leave the mount up all the time but always take the camera out of the mount in hot weather.  some want the camera up and rolling all the time to record even when the vehicle is not occupied.  however if you do this in hot weather i think you are going to run into the same issue i did.
again....great camera, good quality footage, great customer service, excellent value.
summary: lots of features for a low price.

unbelievably poor installation design and instructions.  no operators manual provided...i thought they forgot to package it but was told one is available for around $35.00,  despite reports of poor screen durability raymarine fails to provide either a sunscreen cover or a carry case...they sell these items for approximately $22 each...manuals, and screen protectors are standard with garmin and other manufacturers.  after one use all got was a series of vertical lines with blue background on the fishfinder.  i cleaned the transducer etc., etc., nothing worked.  next morning it functioned as normal.  raymarine published a uses manual online...a lot of good that does when one is seaward!  for otherwise intelligent engineers, raymarine has become a bunch of money-hungry jerks.  i spent over $725 for the dragonfly and suncover and regret every penny. i will never buy another raymarine item...stick with garmin or even hummingbird...companies who care about their recreational customers.

as of this writing (10/06/14) my dragonfly is at raymarine's product repair center in nashua, nh.  on my boat it would only show vertical white lines on a blue background and would not even provide depth numbers.  at the suggestion of raymarine tech support i did factory resets on the unit and even dismounted and repositioned the transducer.  the gps, water temp and speed work fine but negative on the bottom/depth reader. so sorry i was lured by the big name high dollar unit after having had so much success with garmin and hummingbird all these years.

reviewText:
we installed this ssd in our 2008 imac and for several hours we were happy, but then descended into a pit of freezes and a kernal panic. ended up replacing the hard drive, running diagnostics, found that a memory module had become bad - odd coincidence?
in the past weeks i had relegated the ssd to stay in a jacobsparts hd series hard drive docking station and act as a backup( for the three versions of osx) - connected directly to the imac usb2 port, no hub. but, it has started being unreliable in that role. three times now, carboncopycloner has declared i/o errors on specific files in two different target volumes on the ssd. also, it continues to sometimes block the imac from booting, in one peculiar session, holding option while booting, the ssd partitions showed at first, then disapppeared, and the imac would not boot without a restart (with the external disconnected). reports on the jacobs seem all positive. i guess i'll have to return the ssd.
more data - we tried to run this ssd in a maxtor onetouch iii external, to use the firewire 800, in an effort to isolate whether the jacobsparts dock was a problem. but the mac could not see this ssd at all - apparently this crucial 500m is not compatible with the oxford 924dsa chip - beware, many external drives use this.

this is my first laptop, but i think it is heavier than most and the battery life seems to be about average. i shut off the touchpad which i found awkward to use and added a wireless mouse. this setup works for me because i don't intend to carry the laptop around very much, but may not work so well for someone who intends mobile use for it.

one thing i didn't expect was the cooling fan developing a loud noise after a couple of months. if it weren't for sony's excellent service, i would have rated this a star or two lower. they actually sent a tech to my home free of charge to replace the fan !

the only other complaint i have is the windows 8 operating system which does not reflect upon the computer itself. this seems to be a common complaint with this microsoft "upgrade".

the good: they are actually headphones. they do fit in your ears. i haven't had any issues with them falling out.

the bad: (you might want to get a cup of coffee, you are going to be here a while). most importantly, there is no bass. with my ipod set to the highest bass setting, there was no more bass on a song by dmx than there was on a barney children's tune. all in all, the sound quality can pretty much be equated to the sound quality on am radio, except you are probably using them with your $[...]+ mp3 player, not your grandparent's car.

go with something else. all in all these are not quality.

i purchased this item for vacations, and as an alternative to the much more expensive gorillapod product. it was/is my intent to use this product with either a sony nex camera or a canon 6d, as the description of the product indicates that it would support the weight. i haven't used this product enough to have a definitive opinion as to how good or bad it is. i did try to wrap my 6d around the handle of a bike to see whether this would hold it upright, and i noticed that the camera and tripod started to slowly creep down. this suggests one of two things: (1) this tripod cannot handle the advertised weight or (2) i wrapped it around the bike handle incorrectly. when used on a flat surface (where the xit is used like a traditional tripod), however, it appears to work as you'd expect a tripod to.

unfortunately, i have not had an opportunity to really take this tripod out and to put it through its paces. based on the number of reviews on amazon, however, i fear that it may not be sturdy enough (or built well enough) for me to risk using it w/ my 6d out in the field.
summary: haven't used it enough to put it through its paces

reviewText:
this camera takes great photo's and has a lot of great features. it has many features that you'd find on a more expensive camera. i'm an amateur photographer and i bought this as the look and the feel of this camera reminded me of the older more quality made camera's like my old pentax. i purchased this mainly because of the 18x zoom and the 10 megapixels. i'd recommend this camera for some wonderful close-up's.

though, at times the stabilizing feature doesn't seem to work as well as i'd like, the shutter speed sometimes is slower than i'd expect on certain settings. though, it could be something i'm doing wrong.

the other thing about this camera i was a bit disappointed in was that it didn't come with an instruction booklet. you can print off the whole booklet but, when you purchase this nice of a camera i think it should already be printed and in the box with the camera. i don't want to use all my printer toner just to print an instruction booklet and it isn't user friendly to look up the info on your computer. i bought a cheap samsung digital camera and it had a nice book with it, so i expected there to be one in with this camera.

overall, this is a great camera for the money and takes really good photographs.
summary: great camera, but, doesn't come with an instruction booklet

reviewText:
i've had the 40gb version of this player for about 3 months now.  mostly, i agree with the previous reviewers, it's a great player.

the reviewer who was frustrated by the "3 bar" battery indicator should read the manual, however.  it states that 3 bars is fully charged, 2 bars is 60% full, 1 bar is 30% full, and no bars (battery outline only) is 10% full.

i'm consistently getting 18-20 hours of use per charge.  i typically have it set in shuffle mode, select a genre and play for 4-6 hours at a time.  i suspect that more frequent pushing of buttons would use up battery power faster.

sound quality (going through sennheiser cx300's) is excellent.  i'm listening to albums i've had for years, and hearing new things - making out lyrics, hearing background instruments, picking up subtleties i've never heard before.

the only (minor) gripe i have is the touch-sensitive bar.  i've tried the various settings, but i still frequently overshoot once or twice when scrolling with it.  however, i think this is a minor annoyance with an otherwise excellent mp3 player.

reviewText:
i chose this product over the garmin 60cs based on the sd card and rechargable battery... i am feeling very nervous about my choice...

first off...

one downside of the "pc style file system" is that it can get corrupted.. mine did and a search on the internet revealed that i was not the only one that it happened to.. there is no supported method for an end user to reload the basemap to the system if it gets corrupted. contacting the technical support team (we will get more into that later) revealed that i would need to send the unit back to them to restore the map.  this is crazy. i can't believe they are so paranoid that someone will buy an eu unit and load a na basemap into it, that they are wiling to cause what i think is a great inconvience... this was after owning the unit for three days...

also, my joystick did not work. it would not let me move the cursor in the up direction. the customer service (cs) rep said that it could just be that i was pushing the stick wrong... bad design or bad quality control in my mind.

then i get to road and topo maps.. i went to a large sporting goods store (between a target and a best buy and just as big) and they sold explorist gps units and had a us road map and na topo map for magellan receivers.. previously i had gone to the magellan site and clicked on a link for mapsend compatiblity, and for the explorist, it said "yes" for everything... the software to load maps is called the "magellan conversion manager"  this is also my first gps unit.. keeping this all in mind i bought both maps... i get home and find out that they are not compatible with my unit... there is  no way to make them work... they were magellan maps but for the older meridain gps unit...  when i mentioned this to the cs rep, they said that their manager recommended to me that i either try and sell it on ebay or try to return it to the store... i can't think of any store that accepts returns on software... i don't buy or sell on ebay. i told them that i believe that they need to put somewhere on the compatibility chart a mention that the explorist is not compatible with their older software.

so now i am waiting for them to return my gps unit... they let me upgrade the software i had purchased and i will end up paying the equivalent as list price for the topo and road maps... more than i would have paid if i had purhased the maps on amazon...

i talked with some other gps owners and they are reassuring me that it will all work out...

also a note, i use a mac as my primary machine. the device only has a usb interface, which is generally good, but don't expect to get nmea data directly from the gps unit to use software like macgpspro.... the garmin 60cs has both a serial and usb interface. and when using an sd card and the usb interface, you can only access either the sd card or the internal memory at any one time.. you need to switch which one the unit presents over usb to the host computer to change from one to another.

i would think carefully before buying this product... go to a decent store and look at the available software and prices for magellan versus garmin... look at third party software support for nmea data... i find that garmin has better support, at least where i have been looking...

if you like the sd card, this is a great device, but the 60cs can hold a goodly amount of map data in its internal memory.. and if you are going to be away from power for more than 17 hours or so, aa batteries are cheaper than proprietary rechargeable batteries.

reviewText:
this does what it is supposed to do but and this is a big but for me; it drops the voltage too far. i'm using this to send a signal from my dac to two amps.

my original setup is as follows:
dac to passive preamp to amp.

these adapters were installed at the dac to allow one set of cables to run in the above configuration as well as a second set straight to my other amp that does not require a preamp.

when these adapters are installed my main amp loses a good amount of signal which ultimately means my amp does not have the robust sound i'm used to. where as before using these adapters i could run the preamp at 1/4 to 1/2 gain and get beautiful sound...with adapters i have to push the gain well over 1/2 to get it as loud and at the same time the body of the music is diminished. it just doesn't sound as full bodied.

i think this happens because i use a passive preamp and the 3 volt line output of my dac that usually sends a nice clean signal to my amp is now about halved and the amp doesn't have enough to play with. so even though my second amp is powered down the adapter still splits the signal and i suppose it is just enough to lower the output voltage that my main amp receives. what i lose in this exchange is bottom end is weaker, amp gain has to really be cranked to reach same output without this adapter and the sound output is just weaker and less robust. music sounds thin and uninspiring. as soon as i removed these adapters music was full, loud with less gain and very full bodied. so yeah..these adapters won't work for me. in another configuration i'm sure these would be fine especially if i used a powered preamp but i'm not willing to add any more color to my sound. the passive preamp i use is fantastic.

all in all and in the right setup i think this would work very well but not with my gear.
summary: it works but halves the signal ultimately gimping my amps.

reviewText:
my work requires periodic sessions of massive downloads and when it's working, this device makes good use of my broadband connection.  my connection averages about 13 mps, and the download sessions generally run at 1.5 to 2 mps.  that might not seem like much, but without this unit, the download sessions run at less than half that speed.  no one on the network has noticed any erosion in performance during download sessions, so i'd say it was a success in that regard.

the problem is that that whenever there's a hiccup in the connection (brownout, router or switch reset, unknown gremlins) the unit does not reset itself, as does the router, the switch and all my other network equipment.  it must be manually disconnected, the broadband feed restablished in the router, then manually reconnected.  this is not anything that the dlink suport staff seem to be aware of.  nor is it particularly intuitive (or logical for that matter).

if you can live with this and need focused broadband, place the unit in an easily accessible place and go for it.

reviewText: got this for my small boat, it was on sale at west marine and listed as 'waterproof' (who wants a boat radio that's not waterproof?). takes multiple power sources, does dual watch, weather band, and the price was right. after it charged up it worked great. we used it several times for coordinating activites without incident. until, while helping trailer the boat, my friend slips on some seaweed and this 'waterproof' radio hits the water. it was in maybe a foot of water for half a second, but that was enough. the ptt button was stuck on, the button would physically push and release but the circuit stayed active and the radio kept transmitting- salt water had shorted the ptt switch. turning the radio off and on was no help- it refused to power up with the ptt switch held down (just made a beeping noise). further research reveals that this unit is rated jis4. according to [...], jis4 means 'splash resistant'. most of the other marine portables are rated jis7 (same as ipx7)- can be submerged under 1 meter (3 feet) of water for 30 minutes with no ill effects. some are rated jis8 (indefinitely submersible up to mfr. specified depth). many of the other units also float, and most aren't that much more expensive than this one. you might check out the uniden mhs75, which is actually cheaper, smaller, and is jis8 rated. it also has same weather radio alerts, which this doesn't. i'm giving this 2/5 stars because i think a boating radio, to be used on the water, should be more than just 'splash proof', especially when nearly all the competition is jis7. and had me and my friends been stuck on the water instead of on the boat launch, the unexpected failure of this unit would have put us in serious trouble.

reviewText:
first of all, i know that if you're interested in this lens you'll end up buying it anyway cause it has raving reviews anywhere you look and it's cheap.

anyways, i wanna give my 2c about it because i don't agree with much that i've read here.

i'm using it with a brand new canon t2i that takes amazing pictures with the kit lens (18-55mm). i bought this lens hoping to take some nice portraits and for it's ability to blur nicely the background, since it has a very wide aperture (f 1.8).

i can say that at least 70% of my pictures are off focus. i'm using single manual focus point in the t2i (center point) and even tough i always focus on my subject's eyes, their entire face seems way off focus in 70% of my shots. this doesn't happen at all with the kit lens. i don't know if i got a defective unit, it doesnt seem to be the case, but that's just the way it is.

people say it's not sharp at 1.8 and they are not kidding. its really, really, really soft. for the pictures to be usable i have to use at least 2.8, wider than this you get a very soft picture. and i'm not even a pro, they're really unusable.

it does have a nice ability to blur the background, but forget about taking any landscapes shots with this glass, because 50mm on a t2i or similar is very "zoomed in" if you know that i mean ...

if you just bought a dslr and its your first lens after your kit lens, please keep in mind that this is a fixed focal lenght lens, wich means it doesnt zoom in or out like your kit lens (wich goes from 18 to 55 mm). and remember that on cropped bodies like the t2i, t1i, etc, you have to multiply the focal lenght by 1.6, so this actually means you're buying a 80mm mens. in my experience it's very hard to take indoor pictures with this lens because it always seem it's "zommed in" ...

if you really wanna know how it behaves, get your kit lens, zoom it to 50mm and pretend you can't zoom out. try to take pictures with it for a day like that and see if you find your shots usable ...

reviewText:
i wish you could provide a zero star rating, just know that's how i would rate this.

the shelf itself is fine, but the attachment hardware is horrible.  m6 lag screw with a hex head and a philips.  for some unknown reason, the hole you have to insert the fastener through isn't large enough to put a socket through.  so, the only way to attach this is with a screwdriver.  well, it's nearly impossible to drive a lag screw 2" into a stud with just a screw driver, even with the proper pre-drilled hole.  before i attempted to install the bracket, i pre-drilled, then drove the lag screw with my socket in hopes of making it easier to drive.  i should have stopped right there, because at that point the hex head had already started to deform (yes i was using the proper 10mm socket).  i attempted the install, started the top screw, then started the bottom, and i drove them as far as i could until the socket reached the outer hole.  from there i attempted by hand, again as far as i could.  i eventually had to resort to a drill driver on the lowest torque setting i could get to still drive the lag screw.  well... prior to getting the lag screw tight, the philips head stripped out.  this happened on both bolts, leaving me with a shelf support that isn't secure to the wall and no real way to remove the bolts now.

i attempted at first to drill out the larger hole, but even with a step bit, you don't have enough depth to work the bit through to open up the hole.  i then attempted opening up by using a smaller bit and working it around the hole.  i gave up on that, and went to the hardware store to purchase an extractor bit (which cost me as much as this shelf).  that worked like a charm, and i got this piece of crap off my wall.

time to order something different, please don't waste your money on this.  even if you started with good fasteners, you have no way to drive them tight.  the outer hole isn't large enough to get a socket through, and you can't buy wood screws large enough to properly secure this.  other seem to install just fine, but the hole diameter is 1/16" smaller than the outer diameter of a 10mm socket.

i got this unit because it fit my entertainment center. great price, great picture. sound was ok, but i was hooking it up to a home theater sound system anyway, so no big deal.

after six weeks it developed a bright blue line from top to bottom any time a large red or orange object appeared on screen. then the nightmares began. the seller refused a return for exchange, saying that all warranty claims had to go through the manufacturer. the manufacturer at first refused a return claiming that i must have damaged the unit. then they agreed to a replacement but only if i shipped it back to them at my expense, they checked it out and confirmed the problem was not my fault (a four to six week process) and if it was determined defective, that i pay to have a new unit shipped back to me. the total for shipping both ways with required insurance would have exceeded what i paid for the tv, and even then, they still reserved the right to declare it was my fault and refuse replacement at any time during the process.

needless to say, the 55" i subsequently bought for my bar is *not* an olevia.

addendum. a couple of years down the road and both the manufacturer of the tv and the retailer i bought it from are out of business. i'd like to think it was karma, but to be honest if they treated all their customers as they treated me, it was just a natural and expected business outcome.

reviewText:
it mostly works as intended for me thus far, after daily use for a few weeks.  the unique feature that makes it particularly appealing to me is the inclusion of a simple standalone remote - an important convenience as in my particular use case it's not in an easily accessible location, and pulling out a phone to simply turn it on or off via an app takes way longer.

i have had one instance where it misbehaved - its led light started flashing and though i could still *control* it via the ios app, it refused to provide updated energy usage data.  i had to physically unplug it from the wall socket, then re-plug it and wait a minute for it to reconnect to my wifi, to restore correct function.

the led light is pretty bright, and cannot be disabled short of hacks like putting tape over it.  if it's in a tv room, for example, it can be quite distracting when watching dark scenes with the lights off.  it's also impossible to tell if it's off or on by looking at it, despite the led, because the only difference is a subtle change in intensity - visible when you're toggling the state, but indeterminate in steady state.  luckily the included remote has dedicated buttons for both off and on, so there's no concerns with unintentionally toggling the state when it's already in the desired state.

the ios app is a bit limited.  its major flaw is that to get information on any given ihome smart plug - such as its energy usage history - you have to tap an 'info' button on the corresponding row in a list view.  but tapping *anywhere* else on the row causes the power state to toggle.  it misidentifies the intended tap target pretty easily, leading to unintentional sudden power loss (or gain), which is really unacceptable.

additionally, the ios app has no apparent way to export the energy usage data (nor is there any way to view it other than via the ihome mobile app, and that app only - other homekit apps don't have any access to that data, just the ability to detect the current on/off state, and to toggle that state).
summary: works most of the time, but the ios app is a bit awkward

reviewText: my review is with reference to the fit of the case for the galaxy tab a (2016).  the case is well made.  it is made of synthetic materials that will not crack at the corners like so many plastic cases do. it comes with a nice stylus pen.  there are two problems with the case.  first,  it does an excellent job of protecting the tablet,  but this is at the cost of being very bulky.  you will triple the width of the tablet when you put it in this case.  second,  the heavy strap that borders the tablet and holds it in place actually overlaps the screen along the bottom (landscape mode).  i had to trim about 1/8 inch of it away to see the edge of the screen. in addition,  the same strap gets in the way of easy access to the power and volume buttons.  i had to do some trimming there as well.  so,  if you are good with scissors and don't mind the added bulk and weight,  this is the case for you!

reviewText:
i bought the sangean to replace my sony walkman radio, which after ten years of brutal treatment, finally became unusable.  the little sony had been dropped, bashed up against hard objects, thrown into a bag and forgotten for months, left in the sun in the car -- you name it.  the belt clip broke a few years ago, but it kept ticking.  finally, i think there must be a crack in the circuit board, because it randomly just cuts off.  (it still works if i remain stationary).  it was time for a new one.

i came onto the web site to buy another sony, but saw that the sangean was available for slightly more money.  since i remembered the sangean commercials from the art bell show years ago, i decided to give that brand a whirl.  after two weeks of use, it seems to be doing well. no regrets, but i do note two possible negatives:

1. it does not appear to be as structurally strong as the sony.  it has a big plastic face that seems more vulnerable to "smashes" (which haven't occurred yet).  on the other hand, the belt clip on the sangean seems stronger than the sony.

2.  the controls seem to be a little more complicated than the sony -- so for the technically challenged, the sony might be a better buy.

i note no real difference in the reception.  it gets weak to nonexistent in the gym just like the sony did.  all in all, no regrets.  we'll see how well the sangean holds up.

fast forward to 2012:

i forgot that i had reviewed this radio.  it worked for a year or so, then broke.  it's been sitting broke in my junk drawer for a few years now. there is no comparison with the sony walkman.  my walkman lasted for ten years, including all of the abuse.  the sangean was a lightweight. i have reduced my rating to a two.

  but, a minor gripe considering the overall improvements: 140 to 141 model .

the product clearly states 150mbps speeds, but this is further from the truth.  calling tech support was a joke!!! they tell you to change the channel speed on your router, but to no avail.

overall, this was purchased no more than two weeks ago and was a failure. don't waste your money if you plan to utilize this product on a different floor within your home. however, if you plan to have it within the same floor, hopefully this will work out for you.

reviewText:
this transmitter would not work in my suzuki grand vitara. the external antenna is located at the rear of the vehilce, so maybe that was the problem. it just didn't seem to transmit with enough power to play on any frequency i tried. turning up the volume (power) made no difference. if i moved the ipod/transmitter around i got a little signal, but very, very  little. the limited movement of the unit prevents hanging from mirrors, placing on dashboards, moving to the back seat or other things one does to make these things work. also, the transmitter won't work unless plugged into the 12 volt outlet.

there were various rubber fixtures for the dc recepticle to help hold the ipod/transmitter steady, but these made the unit difficult to insert into the dc socket and much more difficult to remove. these rubber/plastic pieces are required because the transmitter/ipod ends up being really heavy on the end of the flexible mount and i'm sure they wanted to prevent damage (and lawsuits) to your 80g ipod. the pieces made for the collar of the dc recpticle did not fit at all unless you cut them.

the product fits every conceivable ipod ever made, but only one was labeled (they come in little cheap plastic baggy things that are only useful for keeping things together till you open the box). you have to figure out what fits what by trial and error.

i also tried the monster cable 200 fm wireless transmitter (w/best station scan) and the griffin road trip fm transmitter with dc charger. the monster cable transmitter didn't work at all (it wouldn't even scan correctly). the griffin road trip worked best in the suzuki, but only marginally. it seemed to be off the frequency a bit with a lot of static. things were clearer up or down band, but then the volume really decreased.

these three transmitters are top dollar units, so price doesn't mean anything. the only unit that has worked well in my suv is the belkin tunecast ii which is half the price or less of these units. you should try any transmitter you buy in your vehicle and return it if it doesn't work or sound good.

question: we have wifi routers and other transmitters that work extremely well, so why can't we buy a low cost fm transmitter that will work within a foot of our radios? is it fcc regulations or is it manufacturers who feel they can really soak consumer's for lots of $'s because it's made for an ipod? i'm getting sick of all this ipod bling that costs lots of bucks, but just doesn't work..

reviewText:
this is advertised as a plug-and-play network attached storage device, they just forgot to tell us that it only works with computers in a windows workgroup, and not on computers in a windows domain.

"does not work" is a bit harsh.  does not work as advertised or 'expected' is more accurate.

the drive does have dhcp, so it will automaitically obtain an address on your network, and you can give it a workgroup name, so that other computers in the same network should be able find it when you browse using windows network neighborhood.

unfortunately, if you install in on domain-based network it while it will get an ip address, it will not show in network neighborhood, as such you have to know the ip address to addess the device.

that said, once you access it, you can map a drive letter, but bear in mind that you have to do that from each pc.

the whole purpose of nas is to make it easy for people to access shared storage.

this issue was reported to seagate and confirmed by their support engineers.
 "unable to browse to the mssii through network neighborhood [incident: 080716-000554]

i give them 1 point because some folks must still be on workgroups, but then i can't imagine why they would be buying nas drives.

i also note that when you change the ip to a fixed address that there is a configuration.html file that does not get updated.  don't know what, if anything it is used for, and, ironically, neither do the seagate support technicians.

i also note the the url links to support and contact us in their web control panel do not work (as of this writing) [...]contact
... so zero more points for attention to details.
summary: does not show in browser on a domain

reviewText:
there's a reason these come with the 1/4" jack and not a minijack with an adapter - they're still designed to be used with a real rig. we're talking headphone amp, people.

about fifteen years back i purchased a pair from a record shop - someone must have found a few boxes in a stock closet somewhere. these were still in cherry condition, packed in the '70s-'80s era koss box with yellowed documentation, for about $90. i used them for recording and playback through an m-audio delta 66 & omni i/o combo on a pc built for recording sound, and they have been completely reliable staples of my recording setup ever since.

i've used them with vintage stereo heads, newer heads built to drive a pair of cans of this quality, 4-tracks, mixing boards, digital mastering stations, headphone-out on amplifiers, et cetera ad infinitum, and been completely satisfied the whole dang time. i've used other headphones for various reasons from time to time, and although i do like to wear lighter headgear, the sound from these guys always makes me happier. even the initial headaches have been worth it, plus now my neck muscles are at least 40% stronger!

long story short, if you want a set of decent headphones for your portable music device look elsewhere. if you want a set of ugly/awesome headphones for your pro audio rig, put these on your list.
summary: fantastic headphones, not for your mp3 player

reviewText: the dcr-trv140 is sony's lowest level digital camcorder, but it is not low-level at all. it records picture at a stunning 520 lines of resolution and sound in pcm digital stereo. you can truly see the difference in picture quality between digital and hi8 or vhs-c. the digital8 system records digital pictures on inexpensive hi8 tapes. it's got an incredibly large 20x optical zoom. optical zoom is the most important type of zoom because there is no loss of picture quality. it also has a 560x digital zoom which is less important because, the farther you zoom, the worse the picture quality gets. one of the most amazing features of this camcorder is the infrared super nightshot. what it does is project an infared light, invisible to the human eye, allowing you to see in no light at all. it also comes with various special effects and fade options. the fm30 infolithium battery allows use for 3 hours (1 hour w/lcd). it includes an i. link dv interface (ieee1394) for editing video on your computer. it also allows you to have streaming video via usb. this camcorder is a good, moderately priced introduction to digital video with features surpassing those of other brands.

reviewText:
after seeing these being cleared out for as low as fifty-five bucks i decided to blow some "toy money" to see how good (or awful) they are.  and the verdict is that they are darn good if your expectations are reasonable.

these are a generation or 2 old so you should be comparing them with the kindle fire (which i also own) or the nook color (which i have played with) - and not with the latest kindles, nooks, nexus or ipad.  but for these clearance prices, you are getting one for a fraction of a refurb of those models.

build quality:  a little lower than the kindle fire or nook color, but still perfectly acceptable.

speed and responsiveness:  not terribly quick, but comparable to others of its generation.  occasionally a really light tap of a button won't take and you have to do it again, but not a big deal.

screen:  very bright and uniform.  easily as good as the competition.  1024x600 resolution - same as the fire and color, but some newer tablets are higher res.  perfectly good for reading and surfing.

google play:  yep, you can get all the apps.  you can replace the launcher (home screen) to be more like a standard android tablet. go launcher ex seems to be a popular choice.  you can load the kindle and nook reading apps, if you like, or my favorite, fbreader, that lets you fine-tune margins and fonts and background color and such.

speaker:  only one and not that great, but ok in a pinch.  headphone jack works fine but its bottom placement means a cord in your lap if you are using it as a reader while listening to music.

microsd slot:  yep.  a lot of tablets don't give you this easy expansion option.  if you want to watch videos or listen to audiobooks, you'll be very glad to have this.

reading ebooks: excellent.  pick your app, set it up your way and enjoy the very uniform screen.

playing videos:  i've only played a couple of 720p .mp4 clips and they were perfect.

playing music:  very clean through headphones.  does not come with earbuds, so bring your own.

playing audiobooks:  works just fine.  i use the smart audiobook player app.

browsing the web:  seems to use the standard android browser and is as responsive as most other tablets.  you can, of course, pick other browsers from the google store.

wifi:  seems just as good as my other tablets.

what it doesn't have (these omissions, while typical of its competitors, are why i downgraded it to 4 stars because, otherwise, it's a great little tablet for the money):

--microphone
--gps (maps still show your location from wifi info)
--cameras
--blue tooth

obviously, if you need those, you don't want the kobo vox.

comes with ac charger, usb cable and an ok case.
summary: fine reader, decent tablet, dirt cheap

i had one of these cases for my x100 since 2012. in that time, it afforded decent protection for the camera against bumps and scrapes when traveling. i tend to use this all the time, putting the camera in a backpack inside it, and keeping it on nearly always when i'm walking around. it's very quick to open up, and you can shoot with the front flap hanging down with little problem.

this gave me a chance to confirm that this is indeed fake leather -- but it feels pretty good and didn't wear through.

also, i usually listen to live music once or twice a week (if not more) and love listening to recorded music at the same volume levels that i hear it live.  the panasonic does not even come close to delivering that level of sound.  its like listening to a live performance from the lobbey.
if you don't like loud music, this player is a good choice.  but if you like to hear the music at the same level you would at a concert or live performance, look elsewhere.

2 stars for now unless the next one proves to last much longer.

reviewText:
i bought 2 of these trendnet tpa-311 hpna adapters. cool idea, basically lets you create a super long ethernet cable by converting ethernet -> coax-> ethernet. doesn't use an ip address and just acts like one long ethernet cable.
last night, 1 just stopped working for no particular reason.
i am writing this review while on hold with their technical support... this is my second call to them...on hold 12 minutes so far this call. i called 2 hours ago, was routed to india (or maybe america where all reps coincidentally have indian accents), he took my name and number and said someone would call me right back... that was 2 hours ago. i called back, was on hold for a couple of minutes and same thing, routed to india, tried to do the "we'll call you back" and, having tried that, i refused and said i would hold...14 minutes now.
i bought 2 of these to connect my internet from where it enters my property, to my house 2000 feet away. one modem is at each end (obvious, right?). it is may 10 2018 and i bought these on jan 22 2018. i used 2000' (2 x 1000') rg6 gel filled, burial/uv rated coaxial cable to connect the modems. they worked fine from day one until last night when one just died - the lan1 port light on the unit in the house went out and my router did not show a device plugged into the port where the trendnet device was plugged in. i tried the other port and the light on the trendnet device lit up as did the light on the router port, but i couldn't get any response via ping from the other end. on hold 26 minutes now... because the device is basically invisible and doesn't use an ip address, there isn't (as far as i know) a way to log into the device and troubleshoot it. it either works or it doesn't. there are some indicator lights for pwr, lan1 lan2 and hpna. pwr is solid when on, lan1 and lan2 blink with traffic like a switch and my hpna seems to blink on and off right now at about 1 second intervals - i didn't notice what it did before, whether it stayed on solid, blinked at regular intervals or blinked with traffic. still on hold. 31 minutes now... oh, just got the ringing phone sound... and... back to music.
so a little about me....just kidding...
a little about my application. we live on acreage in a mountainous area. we get internet from a wireless isp - basically we have a 5ghz antenna  which connects to their centrally located tower. our property is on a mountain and we have a hill between the house and the wisp antenna, which means we can't just install a wisp antenna on the house, but we have visibility from the far corner of the property at the top of a hill. i originally used ubiquity networks' 900mhz nanostation but there were too many trees and whenever it rained or snowed, the connectivity would be bad. changed that out with this system and it worked great for a few months, but now it doesn't. (oh, indian guy is back after holding for 34 minutes - this seems to be the support guy)
ok, off the phone with tech support. total time 60 minutes, most of which seemed like an interrogation and him trying to find a way that it was somehow either not broken and i'm an idiot or it was a problem unrelated to the non-functioning adapter. convinced him that it was their product that sh*t the bed after less than 4 months and now i get to pay to ship it to them and we will see how long it takes for them to fix it, send me a new one or tell me it isn't really broken and send it back. judging from my support call, my money is on #3 at this point.
i have purchased about 5 trendnet products so far and all have worked fine. this is the first one i have had go bad. not impressed with their support or warranty so far. i did purchase the extended warranty - we will see how that works out...
in the mean time, i will begrudgingly order another one of these units as this is my main connection to the internet and i am guessing that this "support/warranty" thing isn't going to be quick and after running 2000' of coax, i'm kind of invested in this solution. oh to live in the country...
rating this unit 2 stars because one broke after only 3 1/2 months and so far their support/warranty has been a pain. if they amaze me and cross ship a new unit or something i might give them more stars because when it worked, it did work well...but i'm not holding my breath at this point.

i bought 2 of these to connect my internet from where it enters my property, to my house 2000 feet away. one modem is at each end (obvious, right?). it is may 10 2018 and i bought these on jan 22 2018. i used 2000' (2 x 1000') rg6 gel filled, burial/uv rated coaxial cable to connect the modems. they worked fine from day one until last night when one just died - the lan1 port light on the unit in the house went out and my router did not show a device plugged into the port where the trendnet device was plugged in. i tried the other port and the light on the trendnet device lit up as did the light on the router port, but i couldn't get any response via ping from the other end. on hold 26 minutes now... because the device is basically invisible and doesn't use an ip address, there isn't (as far as i know) a way to log into the device and troubleshoot it. it either works or it doesn't. there are some indicator lights for pwr, lan1 lan2 and hpna. pwr is solid when on, lan1 and lan2 blink with traffic like a switch and my hpna seems to blink on and off right now at about 1 second intervals - i didn't notice what it did before, whether it stayed on solid, blinked at regular intervals or blinked with traffic. still on hold. 31 minutes now... oh, just got the ringing phone sound... and... back to music.
so a little about me....just kidding...
a little about my application. we live on acreage in a mountainous area. we get internet from a wireless isp - basically we have a 5ghz antenna  which connects to their centrally located tower. our property is on a mountain and we have a hill between the house and the wisp antenna, which means we can't just install a wisp antenna on the house, but we have visibility from the far corner of the property at the top of a hill. i originally used ubiquity networks' 900mhz nanostation but there were too many trees and whenever it rained or snowed, the connectivity would be bad. changed that out with this system and it worked great for a few months, but now it doesn't. (oh, indian guy is back after holding for 34 minutes - this seems to be the support guy)
ok, off the phone with tech support. total time 60 minutes, most of which seemed like an interrogation and him trying to find a way that it was somehow either not broken and i'm an idiot or it was a problem unrelated to the non-functioning adapter. convinced him that it was their product that sh*t the bed after less than 4 months and now i get to pay to ship it to them and we will see how long it takes for them to fix it, send me a new one or tell me it isn't really broken and send it back. judging from my support call, my money is on #3 at this point.
i have purchased about 5 trendnet products so far and all have worked fine. this is the first one i have had go bad. not impressed with their support or warranty so far. i did purchase the extended warranty - we will see how that works out...
in the mean time, i will begrudgingly order another one of these units as this is my main connection to the internet and i am guessing that this "support/warranty" thing isn't going to be quick and after running 2000' of coax, i'm kind of invested in this solution. oh to live in the country...
rating this unit 2 stars because one broke after only 3 1/2 months and so far their support/warranty has been a pain. if they amaze me and cross ship a new unit or something i might give them more stars because when it worked, it did work well...but i'm not holding my breath at this point. worked great until it didn't and now i am experiencing their less than stellar support and warranty process.

i've owned two pairs of these sony headphones.  the sound in the right phone of my first pair mysteriously died after about six months.  i looked into it and a few other people online had the same problem.  some blamed it on yanking the phones out by the wires but i never did that.  i'm gentle as a lamb with my electronics and their accessories.  so i figured it was a fluke and i bought another pair.

it's been a bit more than six months and my latest pair just lost sound in the right phone.  i guess that's twice as long as the warranty but i'm not spending sixty bucks a year on headphones.

the sound quality is nice and they're comfortable.  but the lousy quality is so frustrating that i can't give more than two stars.

my advice - in-ear headphones are the only way to go for those of us who have a noisy commute on a subway or bus.  but stay away from sony fontopia.  i'm going to give the sennheiser cx 300s a shot.
summary: great sound, good fit, lousy construction

update may 19, 2014
i was able to buy a flash (perhaps the only one available in our city and over $400) and the wedding went well. i was trying to figure out what to do with the bower. i thought of just tossing it in the trash - $120 down the drain. but then i wondered if i could make it work as a slave flash.

there was a foot included in the box. i set it up, set the mode to s 0, and it fired as a slave. so i'll keep it. but it still gets one star for being broken.

update may 15, 2014
the wedding i'm going to shoot, and for which i purchased this flash, is in less than 48 hours.

i gathered up all of the equipment i'm going to use for this wedding and was testing it. the flash isn't working.

the flash constantly zooms in and out several times a minute once attached to the camer. you can hear the motor working and see the flash unit moving in and out. the unit will flash on command but it is constantly making noise. it is totally unusable to me. i've put 3 different sets of new alkaline batteries in it.

unfortunately i live in a small city and there are no flash units available for my sony cameras. i'm screwed.

i took perhaps 10 photos with this bower before it died. it has been sitting in a drawer for months with the batteries out waiting for this event.

i'm changing my review from 4 stars to 1.

original review...
i have decades of photo shooting, but i've seldom used a dedicated flash. this is a big weakness for me. i've been asked to take some shots at a small informal wedding that will be held indoors. i needed a decent flash.

i poked around, not knowing much about flash units, and read up as much as i could during a couple of hours. this one seemed to have a decent set of features for a reasonable price.

i was quite pleased when i locked it into the flash shoe and took a few photos. the handshake between the flash and camera took all of the work out of my hands. i took shots with my f/2.8 70-200mm and they came out fine. i took shots with my f/2.8 16-50mm and they came out fine. the flash has in internal motorized zoom that shifts as i twist the zoom ring on the lens. neat.

i took shots in a high school theater and the flash did a fine job of lighting up the whole large room.

my only complaint is two of my 50 shots were way overexposed. i have no idea what went wrong with those two shots.

i'm pretty happy with this external flash. i used it on both my sony a55 and a65.

reviewText:
the apc p74 has impressive specs for such a low cost multi-outlet strip.

the joules rating of a surge suppressor is over-hyped. more is fine but several hundred is usually enough, and thousands is overkill.
what is far more important is the key rating is the ul 1449 tvss ("transient voltage spike suppression" aka: clamping voltage) rating, and the specs on apc's website (at [...] ) state that the p74 has a maximum tvss of 330 volts.

the only problem is, the actual unit i got is far worse than that: 400 volts line-to-neutral, 400 volts neutral-to-ground and 500 volts line-to-ground. in fact, if you look closely at the second picture (of the back side) that has already been posted above, you can see those exact ratings. a good suppressor will have at most 400 volts on all three, and a better quality suppressor (like the p74 is supposed to be) will be 330v on all three.
____________

update: i have now been in contact with apc technical support. here is the answer that i got from "murli" at apc:

"thank you for contacting schneider electric. you have reached apc's customer care center email support on 05/17/2012 10:21 pm. i would be happy to assist you.
please be advised that p74 has a ul 1449 tvss rating of 330v.
if you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me by responding to this incident. it would be my pleasure to ensure that your issue is quickly resolved!"
__________

here's my response to apc tech support:

thanks for the reply. i appreciate your advisement that the p74 has a ul 1449 tvss rating of 330v.
however, the p74 i just bought has a tag on the back that clearly states the ul 1449 rating is 400volts ( l-n & n-g) and 500v ( l-g).
i have taken photos of the back of the p74, clearly showing that the ul 1449 rating on that tag is not 330v [photos were attached in the email, and also now posted on amazon]. as the above photos clearly show, the p74 i received from does not have a a ul 1449 rating of 330v as the specs state. the ratings tag shown in the second photo is unambiguous.

please advise how i can purchase a p74 that does have the advertised ul 1449 rating of 330volts.
summary: p74 actual specs are worse than as stated on apc's website

what is far more important is the key rating is the ul 1449 tvss ("transient voltage spike suppression" aka: clamping voltage) rating, and the specs on apc's website (at [...] ) state that the p74 has a maximum tvss of 330 volts.

the only problem is, the actual unit i got is far worse than that: 400 volts line-to-neutral, 400 volts neutral-to-ground and 500 volts line-to-ground. in fact, if you look closely at the second picture (of the back side) that has already been posted above, you can see those exact ratings. a good suppressor will have at most 400 volts on all three, and a better quality suppressor (like the p74 is supposed to be) will be 330v on all three.

my ultimate ears super.fi 5 pro earphones arrived a couple of weeks ago and i was psyched. i said to myself, "i am going to hear sound like i've never heard before based on all the raves in the amazon reviews plus the fact that they cost me as much as i paid for my portable dvd player or my digital media player." well...no.

look, these are good earphones, but you're paying for a secure fit that doesn't come with most alternatives. you're not paying for a sound that's far superior. is the sound different from the sound you get with the phones that came with your ipod? if you've got nice new foam on your ipod earbuds and they are nice and secure in your ear, the sound you get is really quite close to what you get with the ue super.fi's. so you need to ask yourself: is it worth paying the same cost of a media player for just headphones when the headphones that you have are good enough (and came free with your media player)?

on the other hand, it's very annoying to have to keep adjusting your earbuds to keep them from falling out of your ear (or for maximum sound). and standard earbuds are easily dislodged at the slightest touch. the ue super.fi's eliminate that problem completely. so if you're a musician (like me) that wears phones while playing or perhaps a jogger (or simply move around a lot while using phones), the super.fi's are a good solution.

the super.fi's are inserted into the ear canal versus the standard earbud fit to the ear opening. the super.fi's come with silicon reusable tips and foam tips. the silicon tips, once inserted properly, create a slight vacuum seal within the ear canal and provide a good bassy sound. they are reusable and should last a long time if you take care of them.

the foam tips are much more comfortable. the fit is ultimate because the foam molds to your ear as it expands after insertion. you don't feel like you're sticking the phones as deep into your ear canal with the softer foam as you do with the silicon, and they're just as secure--if not more--as the silicon. the "vacuum sensation" that is there with the silicon tips is gone with the foam. the only downfall to the foam is that after a lot of use you need to replace them and ultimate ears charges 20 bucks plus a fedex (only option) shipping charge (that puts the cost at over 50 bucks!) for a bag of 20 on their web site.

the sturdy "ear loop cables" are meant to be adjusted around the top and behind the ear for added stability. and, indeed, secure they are. the sound is consistently good. no disruption in sound due to a dislodged standard earbud.

so all in all, i am disappointed with the technology. i really expected a far superior sound with the ultimate ears super.fi's. the sound may be a bit better, but it's not far superior to a good pair of standard headphones or earbuds (that don't fall off/out). therefore, i'd say go for this excessive expense if your looking for quality that "won't fall out." if your just looking for better sound...well...you'll save some money if you just stick to adjusting your buds.
summary: they're good....but are they worth the price?

reviewText:
i am not one of those snobby audiophile people. i don't use all those silly terms and pretend i can hear some decreased audio quality at sound frequencies only my cat hears. but i do know crap when i hear it. so let's start off with the most basic function of these ear buds - to deliver decent quality sound to your ears. they fail at that. my crappy $[...] sony earbuds and the ones that came with my ipod both sound a lot better. (unfortunately for me, the dog chewed up both pairs, which is why i bought the philips buds to begin with.) and as for the "surround sound", well come on, you really didn't expect that for $15, did you?

in fact my expectations for ear buds are pretty low. the only criteria they have to meet is a.) delivering sound to my ears that's decent and b.) staying comfortably in my ears. that's it. so how does philips screw something so simple up?

besides the sub-par sound quality, let's look at the other shortfalls:

-ear piece is horribly designed, period. this alone made these earbuds completely non-functional for me. they won't stay in your ears. i get the concept of "in-ear" headphones, but philips doesn't. the headphones fall out while you are standing perfectly still. the only time they somewhat stay in is when you spend about five minutes pulling your ear into various configurations to shove them farther in the ear canal - which makes them uncomfortable to wear. even then, a quick turn of the head in any direction and they are coming out. they were completely unusable for jogging, biking or pretty much anything. the biggest issue is that the earpiece is just way, way to big to accommodate a normal adult ear. (i'm female, but still, i don't have particularly small or delicate ears, just averaged-sized ones.) i got all excited when i saw a second set of earpieces in the case, and then i realized those were even bigger. doh. to give you an idea of how bad these are at staying in, i tried to wear them while riding my vespa - yeah i know, a bad idea to wear any kind of earphones while on a motorbike, but i digress. even wearing these with my *very snug* helmet over them, they still fell out!

next: stupid features - wish they had spent more time worrying about function than form. philips spent too much time trying to design features to "wow" us, instead of actually making a simple product that functions well.  we are talking budget earbuds here, we don't want bells and whistles, we want something that just works.

-the cord for one ear is longer than the other. the idea behind this is that you can put the long one around the back of your head and somehow this is better than the typical y-style headphone. i found it annoying and the entire length of cord felt too short . the only good thing i can see about this design is that it allows you to differentiate the right and left earbud by touch alone - which is nice when it's dark. but i mostly just found it annoying.

-stupid case. i don't get the point of this case. unlike other ones, where there is a molded area to hold the earbuds, and then you wind the cord around the outside, this is just a stupid floppy piece of rubber over a plastic core. the holes you see in pictures are to hold the alternate earpieces, not the earbuds. you are supposed to wind the earbuds around the core too, so they get all tangled up. also, the packaging sucks. they knot the crap out of the cord. it seriously took me a good 15 minutes just to unknot the cord and get the stupid things off the spool. what purpose does that serve other than to annoy the crap out of people?

i was all set to return these, and of course, the dog destroyed them. you'd think i'd learn after three pairs? i am most likely going to replace these with the standard ipod earphones. the long cord on those seems a bit odd at first, but i've come to really like the extra length. and those actually stay in your ears.

reviewText: i just received my myvu glasses yesterday and tried them out on a 7 hour train ride today.  it was definitely a "trial run."  i purchased a competing product last year and returned it as the picture quality just wasn't there.  this product is definitely better.  the video quality is pretty good - say 7 stars out of 10.  the audio is really good. the soft ear pads allow good sound isolation.  i have bose noise cancelling headphones, and these compare well.  i watchced a 2 hour movie and they were very comfortable to wear - no pinching, or pressure points.  the build quality is good and gave me a feeling of an overall solid product. there is a small usb port on the ipod connector (small- like the ones on a digital camera). it allows you to charge the ipod while watching. i used a usb to 110 volt adapter and it worked great, and my ipod was fully charged after the 2 hour movie. i will keep the glasses this time. on long train rides i can handle looking like a geek, if i can enjoy movies.

reviewText:
portable dvd players are always great to have.  this model has some great extra features and one little power problem.  the problem is it only stores enough battery power for two hours (2200 mah), so unless it is plugged in, you are limited.  a plane trip might work, as it also has a headphone jack.  the sound is not loud and is slightly tinny with little bass.  the screen quality is very good with clear visibility.

the extras are amazing.  it plays tv, fm radio (it comes with an antennae), a usb slot, sd card reader, game function, swivel screen (just about any angle you want), a remote and a separate gaming remote and it plays mp5s.  it also will play 3d movies.  all the extra slots are on the right side and easily accessible.

the build is light inexpensive quality plastic and it feels like it would shatter if dropped.  the dvd lid is fragile.  the controls for channel changes and volume are on the left along in a circular button with buttons for lcd and r/l along with a separate button for menu and copy.  the right side has a circular control for previous, next, reverse and forward.  there is also a double button for setup and mode and another for stop and usb/sd.

essentially, it is an inexpensively made dvd player that has all the bells and whistles and a good screen quality.  you can do a lot with this device.  however, the battery just isn't very powerful, which is a surprise for this kind of machine.  for in home use while plugged it is very useful.  for the price, its about right and makes for a great teenagers or young kids gaming/movie play system.  product supplied for review.
summary: inexpensively made but full of bells & whistles

good bag overall, but with some flaws

i was looking for a sling style walkabout camera bag that in addition to rather bulky bags (domke 700-j2b, think tank retrospective 20) and backpacks  (kata r-103, kata bumblebee dl-210) i already own and actively use. the seems to fit the bill, so i gave it a try.

pros:
- clever design
- colored interior, good quality materiel and stitching
- adequate storage for small miscellaneous items like spare batteries, memory cards
- three different dividers with velcro tabs to quickly reconfigure the interior space
- holds  canon 5dmk3 with ef 24-105 f4l plus a wide zoom with some room to spare, or ef 20-200 f4l with tripod collar

cons:
- despite the product description canon 5dmk3 fits way too snugly at least until the bag is broken in. because of this the flaps tend to slide back and need to be secured by keeping the pull under the buckled flap
- shoulder strap and waist strap are too short for tall people. i'm 6'4" and i couldn't get the straps adjusted properly. in addition, this also made the bag tilting down more than i would like it, so the second zippered flap faced almost straight down, especially when the bag is moved from back to  front. this doesn't look safe if extra lenses are kept in this compartment.
- no raincover

bottom line
could be a good bag for someone with smaller frame. smaller camera body would also fit the interior dimensions better.

reviewText:
obviously, this is an older technology docsis 2.0 modem; however, unless you have the "super premium" broadband cable internet, the sb5120 is perfectly serviceable.  this used unit replaced an almost end-of-life motorola sb4200; our cable internet provider [cox communications] recommends at least docsis 2.0 for all levels of internet service, and docsis 3 for the top 2 service tiers.  this sb5120 is not on their "approved" list of modems, but it works, and they'll hook it up in a jiffy.  at my "cheapest" level of internet service, my download, upload, and ping numbers are essentially unchanged from the sb4200's performance, which is fine.  i have a wifi phone, and stream netflix, and have 4 computers connected.  this is a good, reliable modem for many people.

now, the bad news.  i bought this used, which [of course] is not refurbished, but the seller "state street deals" or ssdeals stated the condition as "used--very good."  no way!  they should have stated "working condition--below average/poor."  the modem i received had lived a tough life; it was beat up, with many chips, deep scratches, and lots of scuffing on the case.  also, there was a "rattling" sound from the inside; thankfully, it wasn't something critical.  there was also some adhesive(?) residue on the case, which i hoped wasn't biological.  i know this was a used modem, and we're not judging a beauty contest here, but a least wipe off some of the dirt before you put it a baggie, and proclaim its condition to be "used--very good."

good modem, but "state street deals" should improve their quality control.

i ordered two of these units (great price point!).  one works flawlessly but the other did not work at all.  turns out the female threads on the fuse holder simply fell out of the unit - which means the fuse wasn't being held in securely and was not getting contact with the yellow wire (to power the unit).  i used a little super glue to put the thread collar back into the unit (ensuring to maintain good contact with the yellow wire that's held in there by compression).  reading the other reviews, i expect the other unit to fail sometime in the near future.  the good thing about these is there isn't much to them and are easy to fix.  once you fix that cheap fuse holder (which seems to be the culprit on most of these units) they are solid units.

both units are working great now.  three stars because i had to repair one and let's face it...you shouldn't have to repair a brand new product.

with all that said, i would order another one.
summary: not bad...if you fix it first.

i abuse earphones, and wear them for hours every single day. these have lasted the longest and have the best sound, and are the most comfortable, and they stay in my ear, which is very rare for ear buds.

however, the molded soft plastic earpiece that attaches to the actual headphone slips off very easily, and i am constantly losing them. fortunately, they are bright blue and easy to spot in parking lots and on the floor, in my car, etc. they slip right off when you pick them up and one of them brushes against something, then its gone, and you can't use the ear buds without these molded pieces. i have tried gluing them on, but glue does not stick to silicone, so i'd love to have a source for replacing them, since the actual ear buds still work fine, but there is no way to fit them into your ears without these important pieces. that is a huge design flaw that needs to be addressed.

also, the rubberized cords are very sticky and they tangle at the slightest movement. when i take them off and set them on the table, then pick them up again they are hopelessly tangled, with the sticky silicone snagging on itself and the other cord, magically, it seems. if you wind them up carefully and put them in a pouch, they tangle when you take them out and unwind them, so that is of no help. i am seriously considering switching to some of the earbuds with fabric so they won't tangle and stick/snag to things (like a vinyl car seat). i wish the cords were covered with another material that wasn't so sticky.
summary: best i've ever used - but some problems

i bought these 5.5 mos. ago about 3 mos. ago i started noticing a popping sound when there was a deep, very deep bass sound in some movies, action movies like in everest & in the beginning of the fellowship of the ring! i troubleshooted the problem; changed speaker wire, changed speakers left to right, i even checked my a/v receiver for possible loose capacitor or something; couldn't find any (hard to check for me) i even changed a/v receivers! the problem remained & followed the speaker; i then contacted yamaha & they sent me a nfs form for a replacement speaker! more recently the other speaker is now doing the same! i did notice the serial numbers are consecutive, so that could mean that the batch was faulty in manufacturing! 03/25/16 got the replacements, finally after a month & several times contacting yamaha (the speakers are backordered but i rec'd refurbished speakers!) & they were not any better; same problem; someone commented @ pe, "maybe, just maybe, you're hitting them too hard with very low frequency bass. they're rated to 45 hz, but an 8" woofer trying desperately to reproduce 20 hz bass rumble will often make the noise you describe. make sure your bass settings are set to flat and, if you have one handy, try a sub. i think you'll like what you hear." actually i knew all the published specs on these! (my avr auto setup adjusts frequency signals to fit the speakers attached, so...) i replaced the woofers with grs 8pr-8 8" poly cone rubber surround woofer and whoa! big difference; there is a break-in period but with 2 days uses the new woofers are out-performing the paper coated ones that are on the ns-6490; they can handle more volume without that "pop" sound i was getting with the originals; i'll see how well they perform down the road! p.s. no subwoofer required for me!

06/24/16
update
warranty is over after 1 year; i checked the wiring inside the speaker box & found that the woofer had a red & red with black stripe wire, the midrange had a blue & blue with black stripe wire & the tweeter had yellow & a yellow with black stripe; looking at all the speaker terminals the black striped wire is connected to the negative or "common" terminal but, & this is big the red/black & the yellow/black are on to the same contact of the crossover board as the solid blue! so, either the midrange has mismarked terminals or the wiring is wrong, either way there is a huge mistake with these speakers; also noted; the negative terminals of the woofer & mid are on the same side of the speaker! so, these speakers have a problem!
06/25/16
contacted company by e-mail & by phone; i sent the pics of the crossovers! let's see what they will do!

06/30/16
spoke with yamaha; they say the wiring is correct; the midrange is suppose to be out of phase!
still getting some excellent bass from the poly woofers; considering if a port would help any! i will hold off for a while.
summary: not so awesome as first reviewed; crossed up crossover wiring on midrange!!

reviewText: this is a great replacement for the apple mouse, especially when the stupid little scroll ball finally stops working (which is pretty much a certainty if you use it for any length of time). the rocketfish optical mouse is plug and play with osx yosemite. the mouse came with a disc, presumably with drivers or whatever, but i haven't installed any additional software  it just works. one thing i'll note is that tilting the scroll wheel side-to-side doesn't have the same speed of responsiveness as scrolling up or down. after using it a while though i find i don't really use side scrolling all that much, nor do i miss it. the scroll wheel has soft detents or clicks while scrolling, which i prefer to the vague feel and jumpiness of the apple mouse's scroll ball. the only complaint i have is with the product packaging: this item comes heavily armored in one of those infernal finger-slicing plastic blister packs. it took a bit of work with a pair of scissors and needle nose pliers to free this thing from its unnecessarily difficult to open packing. otherwise i'm very happy with the product.

reviewText:
well, let's start with the pros of this item:  first, it's a true ram disk, so random i/o operations and file copies happen spooky fast.  and yes, i put my pagefile on it and it sped my system up quite a bit, despite all the millions of back and forth threads on that subject.  my system is an old pentium 900 series dual core but i need it for what it does, and this should add a few more years to it.  would it speed up a brand new penryn as much?  i don't know.  also, from what i have read on other sites, if you have a program that uses a scratch file or database file they will benefit enormously if placed on the ram disk.  second, it uses cheap ddr ram that runs about $30 per 1 gb stick from discounters.  no need for the fancy stuff, even the slowest ddr will saturate the sata i interface.  third, it only uses a pci slot for power.  it does not consume system resources.  fourth, it presents itself as a hard drive to the system bios.  no driver to load.  it truly does function as a hard drive as it has an onboard sata controller.  and as long as you leave your pc plugged in and the power supply not manually switched off, it will draw power and not use the battery backup when the system is shut down from the os.

now, the cons.  it's gonna spill over into an adjacent slot.  it's just too wide to occupy only one slot.  second, if your mb happens to have its usb/firewire/audio headers along the bottom row, as mine does, you won't be able to use that end pci slot, as the ram sticks will mash into the headers and header plugs.  second, it's only sata i so it maxes below sata ii and raid arrays for sustained transfers.  third, be careful, as the card is "hot" even if you remove it from the motherboard, since the battery is powering it.  you need to remove the battery according to the manual's directions to safely work with the card outside of the system.  needless to say, you then lose the contents of the ram disk as well.  this can also be a good thing if you want your browser files or other private data to be truly erasable.  no data remanance issues here.  fourth, it maxes at 4gb, which is not a lot of space these days.

needless to say, this item could be improved on in several ways.  first, in asia they sell a version of this item that is housed in a 5.25" form factor and fits into a standard bay.  that needs to happen here.  second, they need to update the controller to sata ii.  third, they need to update the product to handle ddr2 sticks up to 4gb each.  that would give it a capacity of 8-16gb which would be suitable for a no-frills system disk which would not suffer from the life-expectancy issues flash drives are going to face from the constant i/o action they will be subject to.  if you watch the videos of the boot times for this drive with xp installed, you'll be amazed.  windows xp loads in literally a few seconds.
summary: niche product, but if it's what you need...

ok. i just bought this adapter today for my pda cellphone.  the product integrates well with everything (my laptop - sony vaio, cellphone (siemens sx56, my panasonic cordless home phone (although with the panasonic, ppl complain about my voice being faint)).  but the issue is , i hear static crackling noises even if i'm not in a call. as soon as my bluetooth headset is connected to the a210 adapter, it produces faint-medium crackling noise. the noise is exactly like the one it produces when you move out of range.  but happens even at 1-2 feet distance.  i was initially confused on what is producing this.  the battery was fully charged on the adapter.  the bluetooth headset is not the issue, as it connects well with my laptop (which has integrated bluetooth).  then i figured, if i keep the adapter and phone closer (few inches away from my ear) to my headset, then everything works well. otherwise even at a distance of 2-3 feet , it starts the crackling.  i even switched modes (1,2,3) on the adapter and still the same issue.  although it works upto 20-25 feet, the crackling starts at a distance of 2 feet.  i even turned off my wireless networks to test this.  also exchanged it for a new one, to see if it was a item specific issue.  but even the 2nd one is having the same problem.  the manual says, that it is due to interference.  i think many 2.4 ghz can cause this inteference.  alhtough i turned off all of my wireles devices, it still caused the issue even in my car (slightly better, but not totally gone).
but in any case if you don't hear the crackling, it integrates very well with everything.  the crackling is heard only by you, not by the person on the other side.  so we can probably live with it.  there are not many bluetooth adapters that are available out there.
note: many reviewers here complain about this adpater not working well with home phones.  first of all, if you read the manual, this is not designed to work with home phones (if it works well with home phones, then you're lucky).  it is designed to work primarily for mobile phones only.
summary: crackling issues, but integrates well with many devices

reviewText:
i purchased the power castle and liked it so much that got the power mini as well.  both reviews below:

power mini 3000mah

the baby-flashlight sized power mini is all about ergonomics.  fits just fine while connected to my iphone 5 in my slim-fit pants but most of the time it slips into my sleeves while i use it.  it gets warm, not hot, and no more than my phone.  a non-issue but the flashlight is partially obstructed if you leave the usb dongle plugged in.  i keep a 4inch amazon lightning cable in at all times and then into my bag goes for my daily commutes.

power castle 11200mah

this guy isn't so much about ergonomics as it is about power.  it's bulky and moderately heavy meaning it "can" make it into a jacket or pouch but you'll feel it if you're walking/sightseeing. the best place for it is in your work locker or messenger bag along with your tablet which will charge fully a couple times over.

both batteries come with a cloth pouch so it won't rattle or scratch or can be used to keep the cables rolled up.  the power castle turns on automatically when you plug the usb cable however this won't work if you plug the phone while the cable is already connected.  the power mini needs a single tap to turn on.

both are complimentary travel companions.  when i travel to new york i pack an apple 12w adapter and an extension usb cable along.  on day to day i use them to powercycle my phone so that the batteries remain good for at least a couple more years.  highly recommended.
summary: power mini 3000mah and power castle 11200mah both
