reviewText:
i chose this kit because it had the right amount of outdoor cameras combined with two indoor cameras.  though more expensive than other systems, the convenience and reviews convinced me to go ahead and take the plunge.  thus far, here is the breakdown:

the arlo wire free camera's have worked flawlessly and were easy to sync to base station.  the batteries have last several weeks and i'm pleased with their overall performance.  i have them mounted on the walls outside my home and they give me a clear view of the activity around me.  i did not pay for the monitoring service so, i simply download the videos i want to keep (very rare i do) and delete the rest.  i figure, why keep videos of my entrance points unless i need them for the police.  so the basic plan works for me, no monthly fees.

no for the heartache and frustrating portion of this kit, hence the 2 stars.  the arlo q cameras are supposed to connect to my router without the need for the base.  this sounds ideal and just  convenient addition to the security kit.  however, before purchasing this kit please go through the troubleshooting issues with this model of arlo q's.  with an engineering background, i have gone through an extensive troubleshooting process with both cameras, 5.5 hours of my weekend dedicated to this process with no real solution, not even with the help desk.  customer service for arlo (chat session) is inconvenient with an unbelievable wait time of 20 minutes before getting someone to help on chat.  1.5 hours on chat and the technician was not able to mention any other solution found on the internet.

the issue with numerous arlo q cameras is that they fail to connect to the internet which makes updating the firmware possible.  what makes matters worse is there is no way to do a manual update such as connecting the camera usb to a laptop in order to resolve the issue.  this minor issue becomes a big one when the camera is rendered useless for lack of a connection.

my suggestion is to purchase a kit with the arlo wire free cameras and base station.  if you decide to purchase this one, keep the receipt.

in the case of trouble shooting (arlo q will not connect to internet):
method 1 (after failed attempt):
- unplug and re-plug arlo q camera
- use a pin and press reset until you hear the camera restart
- follow steps on app and re-attempt connection

method 2 (after failed attempt):
- open app
- when camera is flashing amber press wps on your router
- press sync button on camera until it flashes blue
- router and camera will signal successful connection
- press continue on app and skip scanning qr code
- if your camera is not faulty then your connection should be successful

method 3 (after failed attempt):
- attempt setup up using your laptop
- log onto arlo site and follow steps on your laptop

method 4 (after failed attempt):
- create a guest network on your router dedicated to 2.4ghz
- make sure your password is alphanumeric (no spaces or special characters)
- attempt arlo q setup utilizing laptop or phone app

method 5 (after failed attempt):
- attempt setup on a different wifi network
- after successful setup be sure to update firmware
- connect arlo q to your home network

method 6 (after failed attempt):
- if you've tried all above steps and are still unsuccessful...pick up the camera and drop kick it to the moon!!!
- just kidding, don't do that
- contact arlo customer support
- request to have rma for cameras
- keep in mind you will most likely get the rma's generated after going through troubleshooting with their technicians.  so be sure to have 1-2 hours of time for this.  be patient and grab a drink.

i hope this helps someone.

reviewText:
the simple truth is that i used to be so hung up on carrying my heavy professional equipment--or nothing--that many opportunities for capturing great memories passed me by.
i believe that having the right case means you will be more likely to take your camera with you often.

it wasn't until i purchased a lowepro rezo 15 that carrying a camera became a joy.
security and function are the hallmarks of this product.

there are many practical methods for securely carrying the case:

1.) i often need to put the case on as i am hurrying to go somewhere, which i do with my belt already on by unsnapping the fastened strap and pulling open the belt loop by the heavy-duty velcro at the bottom. i then slipping it over my belt (the same could be done around a purse or bag strap).
2.) the traditional  method of threading your belt or strap through the belt loop works too.
3.) the other method--that i use quite often--involves sliding two fingers through the loop while holding the case in my hand (especially effective if you are taking pictures often and want to still protect the camera in between shots).
4.) the neck strap that is included and clips to both sides of the case (allowing you to keep the case around your neck while removing the camera altogether).

the extra pocket is perfect for memory cards and/or a lens cloth (you could even make a cheat sheet of camera functions).

i have recommended this case to others and would definitely buy it again.
summary: if you have the right case...you'll carry your camera more often

reviewText: new update 12/3/2016 after having this since since 9/6/16 the right channel went out. i have contacted them several times so i can send it back for repair. received a email that says my return has been denied. seems sad that only after a few hours of working they do not want to repair it. my other one is over  2 1/2 years old and  still works fine. being a tech for most of my life it is a well known fact that most electronic items when they fail will happen in the first 1 or 2 months. i have owned a number of small fm transmitters for at least 8 years. i have used c crane,edm, etc. like any small fm transmitter you have to be careful that the rf output does not get back into the audio chain feeding the transmitter. because this unit is right next to my internet radio and classic ipod there was  some  rf hum in the signal. to reduce the amount of rf (hum) getting back into the audio input i moved the audio cables around to where the noise nulled out. i then put a 3' foot coax extension on the transmitter antenna output. i then adjusted the antenna length for the frequency i was using. i mounted the vertical antenna in the middle of my bedroom window..because of the high output 100/500 mills i decided not to use my outside ground plane  antenna. running 100 mills gets me out approx. 1.5 miles before the signal fades. the chinese fm transmitters have gotten a bad rap because of the amount of harmonics they sometimes emit on adjacent frequencies. i decided to broadcast at the extreme low end of the fm spectrum 87.9. i did check for some harmonics. there were a few i picked up because i was in the same room (normal)i then went into various rooms of the house and did not pick up any more  harmonics. i found a really good 12 volt 6 amp power supply for less then $11.00.($4.95 for the ps/$5.95 shipping)the audio quality of this unit i would say is top of the line. the build quality with its all aluminum construction can't be beat. i do not know of any other small fm transmitter that performs better then this one including the edm which is around $200.00 the edm fm transmitter has a 4 year quarantee. for less then $50.00 this one is a winner hands down.
summary: i have 2 of these units. one is silver and the other one is black. both are awesome units.

reviewText:
i bought this as an upgrade to a 7 year old 26" lcd monitor (which i still use).  i was looking for something mostly for gaming and watching movies.  i will say the colors on this monitor are great.  however, there is significant ghosting you'll have to adjust too.  first couple weeks i had this monitor gave me terrible headaches, but i adjusted.

i read 100s of reviews trying to decide on an ips monitor, one thing i want to address are the massive number of complaints about the controls everyone hates on these monitors.  yes, they are very sensitive, however not beyond control.  i didn't have any problems navigating the monitor controls using the touch sensitive buttons.

i have spent some time doing some calibrating on the monitor to help with the ghosting, but it's really unavoidable and noticeable side by side even an old 26" lcd which had an 8ms response time.  i was hoping it wasn't going to be significant.

outside of that, monitor is decent - didn't work out for my application, but at the time of purchase nothing really stood out as a perfect solution.
summary: not really for gaming - great for everything else.

included remote works great. however, i often have issues with the iphone app when attempting to power on and off devices from my phone.  i'm running it on an iphone 6, so there should be no delay from the phone side.  the app itself can take 10 seconds to load on my phone, then it takes another 30 seconds for the app itself to locate my harmony on the network, then another 30+ seconds for the power signals to be sent to the devices.  once that is all done, i'm often left with one or two devices not actually getting powered on correctly.  again - this only happens with the app, everything is fine with included remote.

additionally, when devices don't turn on correctly, the help option requires you to manually choose which device is not functioning - a step backwards from the "help me" button that was on previous harmony remotes where it would solve the issue for you automatically.

i bought this for the convenience of the mobile app and have been forced to always use the included physical remote to avoid delays and inconsistencies from the mobile remote app.  great idea/concept, but plenty of room for improvement.
summary: mobile app is more hassle than its worth.

reviewText:
i bought one of these for a desktop pc, i've found adapters like this tend to work better than the cards you install inside the pc. one advantage of this model is you do get a bundled cradle this allows you to move the position around and improve the signal pickup, and it also avoids the problem of having a dongle poking out of the pc (which can be vulnerable to damage)

for windows computers this works with xp, vista, 7, and 8 and is fully compatible with ieee 802.11 b/g/n 2.4ghz
this isn't the fastest adapter out there it sits mid range, but it's plenty fast enough for most uses

the software is straight forward and it's easy to set up the adapter quickly. once installed i had no problems with network connection, speeds were good and it picks up the wi-fi quickly after booting up. you do have a "one touch" connection button but i rarely use it.

the only real complaint i have is the build quality the plastics creak a bit, the usb end doesn't feel that strong and there is a bit of play in it, likewise the cradle has some wiggle in the usb input socket. i've not had any problems to date with the performance or reliability but it does look like a weaker point of the product. i would suggest using the cradle as this will help to keep it tucked away from knocks or damage.
summary: works quite well but the build quality could be better

this is a decent usit, but it could be better, especialy for the money.

1) capture performance

i have a p4 3.2ghz computer. 2gb ram. 100gb 7200 rpm hd. very fast. unfortunately, using the provided video capture software, it canot capture 640x480 @ 30 fps very well. it drops frames. by comparison, my digital camera does much better in movie mode. 640x480 @ 30fps is no problem for the camera.

2) capture quality

at night in my office there is no outside light, so i rely on my ceiling lights and desk lamps. this web cam does not do well with lower light levels. the software compensates somewhat, but the end result is not always consistent. by comparison, my digital camera has a movie mode that does much better in low light. my minidv camcorder also does much better, and it is about 5 years old.

i believe the software deserves much of the blame. it is a system hog that robs performance. this needs to be improved immediately. if there was a cheap or open source program that works with this webcam and can tap into all of its features, i would switch immediately.

reviewText:
i got the rose gold one. the earbud and lightening cable came in a little cardboard box, no fancy zip around case like some sellers offer. however, i appreciate the simple cardboard box because it is more environmental friendly and probably help the cost down for the actual product.

i like the quality of sound this earbud offers. it sounds clear and crisp. it comes with 2 additional silicone caps in different sizes, the casing is metal as described.

the volume rocker works differently than i expected. when it is on the plus (+) side, it gives you full sound at a set volume by your device. when you slide the rocker down to the minus sign, it fades the sound and mutes the sound at the end. so while you can decrease and mute the sound by simply moving it down, in order to increase the volume beyond the initial setting, you would have to do it directly on the device.

the white button you see on under the volume rocker can be flipped and when i flip it, it leads me to voice command on my phone while the sound plays hollow in the background.

i haven't tested the quality of microphone yet.

one bothersome thing about this earbud is how thin and fragile the cable looks. i wish they omitted the lightening cable and made a thicker cable for the earbud instead.

the lightening cable is made of nylon cable, much thicker and looks solid. it measures about 38".

again, i really like the clear sound it gives so i'm satisfied for that as of now.
summary: sound is clear, unique volume control, fragile looking cable, lightening cable is a bonus

reviewText: this review is aimed at those with eyeglasses and whose ears get pinched between the eyeglass arms and the earphones. i do not like to block up my ears with ear plugs all day for health concerns. i have bought and used these: sony mdr-cd230 sony mdr-v6 sony mdr-xd200 my ears are not real fussy on quality, nearly all headphones give my ears a problem by pressing them against my eyeglass arms and this hurts, usually after 10-20 minutes of listening. my hatsize if about 7.25, my ears are pretty normal in size, i am middle aged. all three of these headphones i own are the best i have tried on or read reviews by eyeglass wearers over past 2 years. headphones have a left and right side - the cord typically is attached to the left side, and the ear spaces, or cups, are oriented accordingly, to that the back of the ear lobe has more space to sit in than the front of the ear lobe. the sideways pressure (how hard they clamp onto your head) also is a secondary factor in whether my ears hurt. i wear wireframe glasses, and my use for headphones is background music while i program. $30 the cd230 is no longer available, that i could find (fall 2006), and i've used them for 5 years. they hurt my ears after 3-4 hours of continual use, but are good before that. they have cloth covered ear cushions, and relatively deep ear lobe spaces. this feature in all earphone seems to be the primary feature that determines whether my ears hurt or not. if you can find these, and like cloth covered headphones, you won't be unhappy. the sideways pressure is light for me. $64 the v6 stands out for 2 things - richness and accuracy of the sound and blocking out outside office noises. listening to classical music, not real loud, a co-worker can speak to my face and his voice is muffled pretty well. (women's voices too). overheard conversations are not overheard. i have used these occaisionally for a couple months and my ears/head get sore after 1-2 hours. the sideways pressure is noticeably more than the other two, but not excessive. they are well cushioned, with soft fake thin leather-like vinyl which i did not find causes sweating at all. but there is not a large space for the ear lobes to sit, and this is what causes pressure after a while to build up uncomfortably i am sure. if i did not have my eyeglasses on, then these are very comfortable. $26 the xd200 is a little lighter than the v6, it does not block out outside noises as well, which can be a benefit in the office because i can hear co-workers calling my name. the sideways pressure is light, the cushion is the same thickneess as the v6 but the ear space is much deeper for the earlobe, so for this reason it is the most comfortable of all headphones i've owned or tried. the cushions are covered in the thin leather-like vinyl like the v6 - this stuff feels like a paper much more than a plastic, it feels dry, not clammy. to my unprofessional ears the sound is great. if you wear eyeglasses, don't want to use ear plugs for hours at a stretch, then i think you will be happiest with the sony mdr-xd200 headphones. edited may 2013 to offer a still better option for those whoe ears get sore from headphones. the sony ultra lightweight mdr-w08l vertical in-the-ear headphones, which as of now costs $16, are very good, better for comfort than the over the ear headphones. these "in-the-ear" headphones really do not go *in* the ear, they rest on the outside and the head band is exceptionally light on pressure. now, every other so-called in-the-ear headphone does in fact go *in* the ear, but not these. these are flat disks that rest on the outside of the ear canal and allow air in and out. they will not block noise like the over-the-ear headphones, and that is a real factor in a noisy office, but for comfort i've found these the best for the past year, so that i no longer use my head phones.

reviewText:
this lasted a year of moderate use in my car's stereo system. it just stopped working the other day. after taking it apart and reassembling it, the issue is not mechanical or in the devices external wiring. the magnetic part of the adapter - the "write head" - is probably the culprit and it is truly dead.

audio quality:
the basses lost some of their definition - the sound was somewhat "boomy," which could be desirable in some cases - but overall the sound was pleasing. the 3.5mm plug was gold, which are typically found on higher-end connectors (even though they are quite similar to the nickel-plated plugs).

build quality:
my particular adapter gave up the ghost after a year. although i'm not surprised, for the price i hoped for a bit more. soldering was well-done and each channel well-connected. the problem was in the write head. there's no coming back from that one. i would estimate that i used it a total of 50 hours before it broke. of course, it was also subjected to both freezing and hot weather.

summary:
looks like cassette adapters are a balance between cost and longevity. buying too expensively can leave you with a broken piece of expensive hardware. i'd say the belkin xm is a nice balance of quality for the price. do plan on buying another in the future.
summary: broke up on our 1st year anniversary - but it was a good year

if your on a mac think twice before considering this product. my plan was to use this in jbod mode for an itunes media server.
i put two 1.5tb hard drives in the unit and it recognized them just fine as separate drives, but i wanted to use the drive in jbod mode.
it took me about five tries of having to flip the jbod switch on the drive unit (powering the unit down between switches) to get it to work on my mac pro running (osx 10.7.1),
i finally got it to take and then powered the hard drive enclosure down, unhooked the unit and took it over to my mac mini powered the unit up and the drive was not recognized properly, it did not hold the jbod mode that i had just set up and had basically reset it back to an initial drive set up. not wanting to trust my media files to a unit that's been this problematic to set up, i packed it back up and returned it. i should note that i had originally tried to set the unit up on my mac mini (osx 10.5.8) with no success, before getting it to format properly on my mac pro.

on the plus side the amazon no hassle return policy was great.
summary: nice package but doesn't play nice with macs

reviewText:
this mouse is pretty comfortable to use, i have big hands so i got a large. it doesn't take long to get used to it and in my opinion it doesn't take very long to find its 2 main flaws.

flaw #1 because it is very large and the way your hand lies on the mouse it is quite a pain to pick it up and reposition the mouse on the fly. i had read this complaint from others but i thought to myself i never pick up the mouse to reposition it so i should be good. when i started using this i quickly realized that from time to time i do pick up the mouse slightly to reposition it and put it back in that sweet spot. when i say slightly i mean slightly. usually when i reposition my normal mouse i'm only moving it 1/2 inch to 1 inch from its original position.

flaw #2 i have not had a mouse without the back and forward web buttons above the thumb rest in years. this mouse does not have them. meaning you have to make large mouse gestures to hit your browsers back and forward buttons. which ended up causing me to have to pick up the mouse and reposition it more often than i would have had to do if i was not forced to make such long gestures.

in the end i returned this mouse and i rarely return items to amazon, in the 5 years of buying items on a weekly basis i have returned less than 10 items.
summary: great idea but lacks the features of similar priced devices

i had great anticipation about this case.  the initial reviews looked positive and the price was right.  i purchased this online for $150 shipped.  installing the main board and components was easy.  but after firing up the newly built system, the problems started.  first, the lcd
screen dislodged and "fell" behind the front panel.  i removed the panel
and realigned the lcd panel.  within a day, the problem reappeared.  i finally glued it in place which appears to have resolved the problem.  next issue was a strange rebooting when i touched the front panel.  a little research on the internet revealed that static electricity easily causes a short.  even though i had the latest model with the "integrated ground wire", i could deliberately cause shorts by just touching the front panel.  after researching the problem more, i figured out that adding a heavy gauge ground wire between the front panel and power supply would fix everything.  next problem was a shorted wire which was caused by sharp edges inside the case.  some of the internal gussets are not finished and therefore very sharp - this seems ridiculous to me that antec can't spend a few bucks quality work.  here are some more problems:

-the imon drivers used to control the lcd screen are very buggy.

-vista occasionally shows the lcd screen "disconnected".  not sure if this is a software bug or hardware problem.

-even though the case is very big (much larger than my onkyo receiver), it's too short to fit most modern video cards.  i had to try four cards before i found one that fit.  it looks like the case just isn't tall enough.

-there are a lot of screws that go into plastic, of which can only be used a few times.  after that, you have stripped screw holes.  again, another unacceptable example of poor quality.

-the power supply makes an intermittent "buzzing" sound which appears to be related to a bad fan.

-customer support is very poor.  i called antec several times about these problems and they were not helpful at all.  responsiveness is slow and they put the burden on the customer to keep support issues progressing through their process.  i was never able to replace any of the defective components and i just gave up trying.

-it has a volume knob.  what is the point of this?  if this case is used as a htpc, then the receiver would control the volume.  in fact, if you connect your htpc to your receiver with hdmi and/or spdif, then the pc can't control the output volume.  so i'm not sure what the point of this knob is.

-the usb and firewire ports look unfinished.  why didn't antec put these behind a panel/door like most $39 dvd players?  again, very cheap quality.
summary: silent, affordable, but lots of problems

i ordered this keyboard to replace an aging k270. i'm a video game developer and computer consultant so i need a rock solid keyboard, which is why i choose logitech devices knowing they are solid, even at the budget level. ive ordered this model before from a different site, and have had no problems, so when the old one started to ware out, i chose the same one. ive had nothing but problems with the new one.

its weird. this new one won't work with the old ones receiver. the problem is, it doesn't have the orange gear logo on the bottom, showing that its part of the unifying "universal wireless system". when i try to connect to it with my unifying receiver using the special compatibility software, its detected as m510 mouse and then fails to install. the problem here is i cant use my better logitech mouse or any other unifying devices with the k270, or i will need to use 2 receivers, and i don't have any open usb ports, plus there's potential radio interference. i ended up having to ditch my other unifying devices and use the compact mouse it came with.

as if that weren't bad enough; it has a horrible lag between key-press and screen input, making it impossible to write with for any amount of time (writing this took some patience). here's an example; ill be playing a shooter game and all the sudden the w key stops working and i stop moving forward. i try to hit the escape key, nothing. then 10 seconds later it escapes. this bug pretty much indicates to me that its a counterfeit or at least an inferior transmitter.

its not the receiver, because ive had no problems with the m185 mouse. i have full use of the mouse - to open a virtual keyboard and finish typing one click at a time. its detected by the unifying software even without the orange unifying logo and never misses a beat with the new kb and receiver. i would notice any slight stutter in the mouse pointer.  its compact size is small for my hands and has a loud click, which is bad for in the living room. one other confusing thing: its labeled mk270 on the box; so shouldn't the mouse be a m270 rather than m185?  no such item exists.

why would they make 2 different versions of the same model? the only indication that its not the same is on the back and in 2mm fine print where its labeled k270 and below m/n: y-r0042. my old one is a k270 but m/n: y-r0015. ive read in the q&a; someone returned their y-r0042 and got the y-r0015 as a replacement.

the main point here: unless you want to risk receiving the incompatible and buggy version, don't try this product.
summary: not a unifying devaice and very buggy.

reviewText:
i've owned an iriver ifp series player for over a year. i've been pleased in general with their operation except for the issue that when the unit breaks (which yours may or may not) iriver has no facilities to repair a unit beyond its warranty period.

on the plus side:

+ small size

+ long battery life with single aa battery.

+ no oem battery that can't be replaced

+ audio good, and eq settings very flexible

+ many changable option features

+ software can be flash upgraded

on the negative side:

- the software for loading the device is only fair. the unit can supposedly be modified by software to act as an external drive, but i have not tried this.

- the need for an external cable is a hassle, nicer if it could just plug into a usb port without a cable

- fm radio is not very sensitive. only local stations are heard. the earphone cord is the antenna, so this accounts for the lack of sensitivity. the stereo decoding takes about 10db more signal so only strong signals will be heard in stereo

but, i bought this unit as an mp3 player, so the fm aspect isn't that important.

now... for the major problem with iriver.....

i had my unit for a little over a year. one day, while playing music, the unit just quit, and the display went dead. checking for the obvious problems, like a dead battery, nothing seemed to be wrong with the unit except that it wouldn't turn on or do anything.

i sent multiple emails to iriver and received no reply. i called their 800 number, and was informed that "they do not have a servive center, and make no repairs of the flash players"

i cannot give any higher rating than two stars to a company that charges $150-200 for a product and then expects it to just be thrown away as they don't service their product.

apparently, if the unit is still in warranty, they can send out a new unit as a replacement, but beyond the warranty period, you're out of luck as iriver won't touch the unit.

buy iriver at your own risk.

reviewText:
i use these at work for many hours at time for music and podcasts.

pros:

-good believable soundstage. the music sounds more like it is surrounding you rather than coming from between your ears.
-overall very pleasant, non-fatiguing sound, though little on the bright side.
-lightweight and very comfortable for long usage. very little pressure against the head, and easy on the ears.
-easy enough to drive with a portable player at decent volumes. no need for headphone amp.
-super long cord

cons:

-weak bass. not good for r&b/rap music unless you don't mind eqing or bass boosting to get the desired sound.
-"pleather" is not of very good quality and will likely flake over time.
-very plasticky construction, though it is to be expected at this price point
-non-foldable
-due to the lightweight and all-plastic construction, you can easily hear vibrations if anything is rubbing against the headphones or cord.
-cord coming from both sides of the headphones instead of only on the one side.
-the light pressure of the headphones and cheap foam padding doesn't allow for good sound isolation. at moderate music volume, you can still make out what the person next to you is saying.
-super long cord may not be ideal for portable usage.
-cables are rather thin and flimsy; durability is questionable here.

overall, a great set of cans and in terms of sound quality, i would put it up against anything $50 and under. the majority of the "cons" above are expected for cans that cost this much. my only real disappoint is the lack of the bass, which is the main reason why i gave it 4 stars instead of 5.
summary: great bang for the buck! comfortable!

reviewText:
i've gone through just about every kind of case, ranging from budget ($30 for case with power supply) to higher-end ($150 for case without power supply). i've purchased antec cases before and have always been impressed by their quality. for the price, this really isn't a 'budget-priced' case since it doesn't come with a power supply. a lot of good mid-range cases come with power supplies for around $75-$90.

the case has a lot of room for a mid-tower... room for six internal 3.5", one external 3.5", three external 5.25", and one bottom-mounted 2.5" ssd drive. all the drives are well spaced, however the specs mention room for 11 drives... there is barely enough room for the ssd drive with the lowest 3.5" internal bay used. the power supply is bottom-mounted and there's room for eight expansion slots.

first, the pros... the construction itself is excellent. the sheet metal is reasonably thick without being too heavy... an excellent balance between the two. the inside of the case looks great with everything blacked out and no exposed sharp edges. with two decent-sized fans (140mm at the top and 120mm at the rear) and room for three more (one on the side and two in the front), this case has a great amount of airflow. front audio in/out and four usb ports makes it convenient.

both sides and the front of the case are easily removable without tools and installing the motherboard was no problem at all, with plenty of room for the large video boards. there's also a cutout below the motherboard for easily installing/removing cpu fans and coolers without removing the board. there's two wire ties and several anchors to allow you to nicely route all the wiring underneath the board and out of sight.

as for the cons, there are a few. most notably is the top-mounted fan. it's a nice feature, and the fan does a decent job of moving the air, however you may notice that there are no pictures of the top of the case anywhere on amazon.com. if you go to antec's website, you'll find a vague picture of the top at a sharp angle. the reason for this is that the top of the case is quite ugly. there's an 'accessory tray' covering the front half of the top and the back half has the grill for the fan, which is so underwhelmingly designed that it sticks out like a sore thumb. it's clear that they put no more thought into this grill then they put into the fan on the back of the case... which you never see. obviously, antec thought it was ugly too because most of the pictures avoid showing the top. the ones that do either are at extremely sharp angles, or have the fan either blacked out or cut out completely. to me, it's the worst part about the case. a simply wire-mesh grill, like the front, would have been all that's needed.

there are also pop-outs for running an external cpu cooling system, but they offer no grommets. there are no extra wire ties for wire-routing and no expansion slot plates in case you pop open a slot and later need to close it back up. they offer dust filters, but they are cheaply held in place and only cover the top four bays, leaving the bottom five bays open to the elements. there's two lights upfront along with the audio in/out ports, but nothing's labeled, so unless you know the color coding for the audio, you'll be left scratching your head. lastly, there's no reset button. these problems here all fall under the title of 'cheap', which sadly doesn't reflect the rest of the case's intelligent internal design.

if you can find a picture of the top and don't mind the looks, or if you keep your computer hidden away under a desk, then this is a four-star case. it's well laid out, very conveniently designed, and quite sturdy. the only downside is some of the simple shortcomings of trimming the final cost. personally, the computer will be more out in the open, and i hate the top fan/grill's design, so i have to drop another star off it.

with a few cents worth of extras and the same amount of thought that went into the internal design, put into the external design, this case could easily be a five-star product. having bought cases within this same price range and getting all the missing elements that this case should have, i certainly know it's possible.
summary: could have been a great case

reviewText: if you manage to get a reliable board, you will be happy, but good luck with that. i initially had issues with the bmc management on this board. the ram voltages are hard-coded, so if you have low voltage ram installed, the bmc alarms would alert because low-voltage ram by default runs at lower voltage normally. so i couldn't use the bmc monitoring or i would have all these false alerts. contacted asrock support, no solution to customize the voltage alert level. then, intel has announced that some faulty silicon was used on the c2000 cpus which can result in premature failure. i rmad the board, and received the answer due to the bmc alarm issue they would replace it, but not necessarily for the intel-announced problem. so i receive the new board (i have to pay for the shipping to rma the board, asrock covers return shipping), and asrock support said that the board that has the replaced silicon is version 1.03 of the board, which is what i received. i rma'd version1.02 of the board. i install the board with all the same ram, hard drives, etc. and the board won't finish the post process, it is stuck on "system initializing." can't get to the bmc, can't get to the bios. googling this, apparently this is a common issue. some people say they have to rma their board. i found a forum posting that said to pull the cmos battery for 15 minutes and remove all the ram but 1 stick. put the cmos battery back in and then boot. this time it did finally boot after going through  one or two self-reboots. i powered off and added the 2nd stick of ram that was previously working in this system with no problems. back to being stuck on system initializing. i was thinking the 2nd stick of ram is bad (that would be odd but not impossible even though it was working with the old board), so i pulled the first stick and only used the second stick, and the system booted. so ram isn't bad. added the other stick of ram and this time the system booted. i would think i didn't have the ram seated properly, but its not like i am new at this, have built a fair number of servers and desktops. this board is finicky, and it wasn't cheap. i have zero confidence in this board. this is the first time i have purchased an asrock board, i usually get gigabyte or intel. i don't think i will be trying asrock again after using this board.

reviewText:
just bought mine last week and just like many other consumers, i was searching for cd-mp3-am-fm radio and remote.
advantages are:
1) the only smaller desktop unit that i found with cd-mp3-am-fm radio and remote.
2) has sleep timer 30 minutes, 60 minutes, 90 and 120 minutes. this is handy for cd's, mp3's and the radio.
3) fairly good sound for the money.
4) easy to use remote. (i leave mine next to the unit).
disadvantages are:
1) earphone plug in the back of the unit. when i want to plug in my earphone, it is hard to reach this and it is a poor design!
2) my biggest disappointment--no resume on cd or mp3! i listen to alot of audio books and i find this a real inconveince! i have to go to the track that i think i left off or write it down! (my panasonic mp3 cd small portable has this, why did they forget this in this one?).
3) terrible reception on am--static!
4) sound equalizer needs much improvement for the sound quality and ease of use.
i bought this because it is the only am/fm/cd/mp3/cassette unit with a timer and remote that i could find! since the am radio is so terrible, i ended up buying the sony icf-m410v so i can listen to my am talk shows. this one has a sleep timer up to 60 minutes, a clock and easy to use.
overall, i still give it a 4 because of it's many features and that it has a cassette for my older tapes. **and, i wish i would have bought it on amazon, not at radio shack (they were about $25 more). live and learn! if you are looking for a all in one with cd, mp3, cassette, remote and am-fm radio, this is about the only one that you will find and i looked for 3 months!
update: september 18, 2006: after owning this one month, i like it better and better! i love the sleep feature that you can use up to 120 minutes (2 hours) either on the radio or the cd! this automatically shuts the unit off. it is a great feature if you are listening to a cd that contains 40 hours of mp3's on it and you don't want it to play all night!
summary: good unit, however no resume on cd, rear earphones!

reviewText:
just received this rig today. i will post these first impressions and will try to follow up in a week or so when i've had a chance to work with it more. the photos are a bit deceiving, esp the one on the packaging that shows a blackmagic camera mounted on the rig. for the price, one can't complain too much, but there are some obvious things that could be done to improve this rig that wouldn't cost the mfg much.

the good
(1) it's very light and compact when folded. i bought this to put in my carryon for international travel and it's going to work well for that.

(2) the parts, though not heavy duty, seem well made and everything fits tightly. we'll see how long the adjustment knobs hold up to the torque, but the good news is that if they fail, they're simple to replace -- just carriage bolts run through pre-drilled holes and mated to knobs with nuts inside. pliable plastic washers are used to keep the knuckles tight. if those get compressed over time, they will have to be replaced.

the bad
(1) be aware that if you're using this for a black magic cinema camera (or the 4k production camera) that the camera will not fit within the cage as it's currently configured. the cage is wide enough, but in order to accommodate the canon 5d-7d bodies, which have their 1/4-20 mounting socket offset to the left, the front rod block on this rig has been shifted about 1.5" left of center. that moves the rods and camera mount to the left so that the left side of the bmcc body will not clear the left side of the cage. both the rod block and the right handle need to be moved. i plan to have a machine shop drill new holes in the cross-brace so i can shift the block to the right and center it.

(2) you can't turn the rear extension handle fully upright if you have the bmcc's sunshade in place. that's okay bc i tried handling it that way without the shade and it's really better to have the rear handle at a bit of an angle to steady the rig and use your other hand on the top of the cage to actually lift the camera. i will probably add a lift handle screwed directly to the taps in the top of the bmcc body.

(3) it's very, very light. and it is very compact when folded. however, the rod blocks are plastic and the aluminum struts are thin enough that, when i put on the bmcc with lens (~5 pounds), and held the rig by just one of the forward handles, the aluminum strut was flexing. not a lot, but enough to throw a shot off if you suddenly remove your hand to ride the focus. counterbalancing the camera so the weight isn't on the handles helps.

(4) the rods are short. they work, but they're short -- 10". on the bmcc, because the camera can't fit through the cage, you're forced to have the rear rod block back from the front block about 4", meaning there's not enough rod in front to mount a matte box or anything else. even a follow focus is going to be a tight fit.

the ugly
(1) the cage looks goofy. consider removing and adding a full cage or a top plate to carry the lift handle and provide attachment for monitor, recorder and microphone.

suggestions for the mfg
(1) heavier gauge aluminum. a little more weight would be welcome if it makes the rig stiffer.
(2) pre-drill holes to center the rod block and provide another hole for the right handle. the buyer can move the block to whichever position they prefer.
(3) the rear arm has an extension section and pulls out to about 14" -- another couple of inches would be very helpful so as to put a battery back there and get it far enough back to effectively counterbalance the camera.
(4) provide a real cage instead of that u-bracket and let the camera sit in the cage mounted to the rods, hopefully with room for a quick-release plate so the cage/handle/camera can come off the rod block and slide onto a tripod quickly. yes, the folding design is clever, but it's goofy and limits the forward travel of the camera on the rods.
(5) include rod extensions to lengthen the rods to 14-15".
(6) if you must use plastic on the rod blocks, how about delrin or nylon -- something a bit heftier and more durable.
summary: about what i expected with some flaws
text:
just received this rig today. i will post these first impressions and will try to follow up in a week or so when i've had a chance to work with it more. the photos are a bit deceiving, esp the one on the packaging that shows a blackmagic camera mounted on the rig. for the price, one can't complain too much, but there are some obvious things that could be done to improve this rig that wouldn't cost the mfg much.

the good
(1) it's very light and compact when folded. i bought this to put in my carryon for international travel and it's going to work well for that.

(2) the parts, though not heavy duty, seem well made and everything fits tightly. we'll see how long the adjustment knobs hold up to the torque, but the good news is that if they fail, they're simple to replace -- just carriage bolts run through pre-drilled holes and mated to knobs with nuts inside. pliable plastic washers are used to keep the knuckles tight. if those get compressed over time, they will have to be replaced.

the bad
(1) be aware that if you're using this for a black magic cinema camera (or the 4k production camera) that the camera will not fit within the cage as it's currently configured. the cage is wide enough, but in order to accommodate the canon 5d-7d bodies, which have their 1/4-20 mounting socket offset to the left, the front rod block on this rig has been shifted about 1.5" left of center. that moves the rods and camera mount to the left so that the left side of the bmcc body will not clear the left side of the cage. both the rod block and the right handle need to be moved. i plan to have a machine shop drill new holes in the cross-brace so i can shift the block to the right and center it.

(2) you can't turn the rear extension handle fully upright if you have the bmcc's sunshade in place. that's okay bc i tried handling it that way without the shade and it's really better to have the rear handle at a bit of an angle to steady the rig and use your other hand on the top of the cage to actually lift the camera. i will probably add a lift handle screwed directly to the taps in the top of the bmcc body.

(3) it's very, very light. and it is very compact when folded. however, the rod blocks are plastic and the aluminum struts are thin enough that, when i put on the bmcc with lens (~5 pounds), and held the rig by just one of the forward handles, the aluminum strut was flexing. not a lot, but enough to throw a shot off if you suddenly remove your hand to ride the focus. counterbalancing the camera so the weight isn't on the handles helps.

(4) the rods are short. they work, but they're short -- 10". on the bmcc, because the camera can't fit through the cage, you're forced to have the rear rod block back from the front block about 4", meaning there's not enough rod in front to mount a matte box or anything else. even a follow focus is going to be a tight fit.

the ugly
(1) the cage looks goofy. consider removing and adding a full cage or a top plate to carry the lift handle and provide attachment for monitor, recorder and microphone.

suggestions for the mfg
(1) heavier gauge aluminum. a little more weight would be welcome if it makes the rig stiffer.
(2) pre-drill holes to center the rod block and provide another hole for the right handle. the buyer can move the block to whichever position they prefer.
(3) the rear arm has an extension section and pulls out to about 14" -- another couple of inches would be very helpful so as to put a battery back there and get it far enough back to effectively counterbalance the camera.
(4) provide a real cage instead of that u-bracket and let the camera sit in the cage mounted to the rods, hopefully with room for a quick-release plate so the cage/handle/camera can come off the rod block and slide onto a tripod quickly. yes, the folding design is clever, but it's goofy and limits the forward travel of the camera on the rods.
(5) include rod extensions to lengthen the rods to 14-15".
(6) if you must use plastic on the rod blocks, how about delrin or nylon -- something a bit heftier and more durable. about what i expected with some flaws

i've had this device awhile now and have rigged it up a number of ways, downloaded a few trial apps, etc. i'm pretty good with this kind of thing, not a genius but better than average and i have not been able to defeat its incredible levels of crappiness.

basically, it ranks right after that screwy, apple peel-y device on my all time most hated devices list.

as many others have noted, the pop up keyboard app cannot be disabled by any means i've found so even with an external keyboard, you constantly have to close the onscreen keyboard.

there is a device explorer app that doesn't seem to do anything and navigation with a mouse is so clunky and slow it is maddening. i get that it is an android device but between smart phones and several tablets i think i've learned what their ui's look like and this device ui is much less effective.

i could make allowances if it at least loaded and streamed videos pretty well but no, streaming is just as bad as all the other features of this horrible device. netflix fails, amazon streaming video fails, amc.com, nbc.com, etc. all fail to load and/or stream without massive pixelization and loss of audio sync and big pauses for loading

it doesn't even perform well enough to use with a monitor just to do light internet  work.

it should work well based on the specs, maybe this particular one is a lemon, but i wouldn't recommend it to anyone for any purpose.

amazon fire tv, an old wii, xbox, or your old laptop will all do a better job depending on your needs. don't buy it.

reviewText:
i bought this item instead of the kindle fire or apple ipad.  in my non-geek opinion, it seemed to have more horsepower and flexibility.  there are some formats it cannot read but compared to the others, it's much more practical than any other i compared (which were many!).
i also bought the an ethernet adapter and an otg adapter to read micro/sd cards and which has a usb port.
(and i got a microcard so i can load up music, movies, etc., and take pics)
plug the otg adapter into the nexus, then the ethernet adapter and connect via ethernet cable directly to the internet (turn off the wi-fi in settings). or, use the usb port to view your external harddrive.  (or use an app called dropbox which can store 500gb i believe and go anywhere you want without having to carry an external.)

it comes with many apps already installed and if you don't want them, it's easy to delete them (unlike several reviews i've read..i had no problem.)  also, you cn join many apps into on folder; they merge to make a circle-shaped 'folder' you can then name (not all of them, but many did). i have a very uncluttered main screen after having downloaded quite a few apps.

it didn't have a filing system - i had to download a file manager.  i picked file manager hd. it suits my needs in a standard fashion and is not specifically limited to the cloud & dropbox web storage.  it's normal...for lack of better word.
i also downloaded cool reader; my text/pdf/epub files show up like real pages in a soft beige - really nice!

of course, download your favorite travel apps, weather, currency exchanger, some games, security apps, a wi-fi booster app, and 1tap cleaner to clean up caches. many apps are free. (thank you, awesome awesome developers!)
word of advice - it saves time if you research the apps first, be selective.  your nexus has play.google.com - once you purchase it and set up your gmail, it creates your account with google.  then you can use your pc to (more) quickly download/save all the apps you want. when you turn on your wireless (or use the ethernet cable to link directly), they'll all download at once.  saves lots of time.

there are some folks that had start-up battery charging issues at first - mine seemed to also, but only the first day...as if it needed to learn to walk it's first two-three times.  then it took off running - no problems since.
the nexus has a nice material on the back that makes it easy to hold.  the screen rotates, is very responsive, and has a very workable keyboard. i haven't tried out the speech-to-text yet - as a non-geek new android user, i'm sure there are many things i have not tried yet and excited to learn.  i'm reading many reviews and blogs to catch tips and tricks...one thing i've learned is not to ever think too quickly that something can't be done - someone found a way :)
 i watched a movie - colors were fantastic, sound was a bit quiet but volume control is on the side of the unit - very user friendly. then i read a book - these aging eyes were most relaxed. this ol gal is most pleased.

love the adjustability of the computer interface software. great back end stuff. youtube vids detail some incredible features. be that as it may, i need a camera where i am able to remotely access motion events stored on the sd card, which obviously remains in the camera (i opted for the reolink c1 pro-who assured me of this capability). i emailed foscam direct via amazon's link with this very question as i had come across mixed reviews. i will copy and paste their response as of 12/01/17 for your consideration:
 "if the camera and the account are setup for use within the united states viewing the stored videos from the foscam app currently is not supported. if the account is setup outside of the united states then it is possible to view the videos from the foscam app. viewing the stored apps via a macbook pro would require logging into a computer on the same network and viewing the sd card as a network drive from the computer on the network. this option is currently not officially supported by foscam and unless the network has high bandwidth capability the video would skip."

reviewText:
i've had this laptop for almost 3 years. it actually performs well for my needs. i have it on about 15 hours a day. it is still fast and does everything i need it to. i do not do any heavy gaming though, just web browsing, email, movies, music, online games like pogo, etc.

i paid 300 dollars for it brand new, on sale. it was an excellent laptop for the price, no doubt, as far as performance, but their are some build quality issues. the laptop around the battery area, on top and bottom gets super hot, super fast. the charger block gets very hot as well. the laptop would shut down on its own occasionally because it was overheating. this was not due to the fan being blocked or anything like that. the hottest part would be right at the area where the charger plugs in, which is on the left corner, by the hinge to open and close the laptop...

which brings me to my biggest issue with this laptop. about a year after owning it and getting multiple charging block/cord replacements, both by hp warranty replacements, as well as buying them on my own, one day the screen literally burst open on the left side by where the charger plugs in. so i was left with a laptop screen that is cracked open. the display still works, but i have to have it propped up against a wall, etc to use it. the hinge is completely busted and the framing around the screen just hangs open. i will upload a picture so you can see it. i have been using it this way still for awhile now. as i said, it still works perfectly fine, but the screen is just barely hanging on. of course it was out of warranty period so hp would not help at all, even after knowing all the issues i had with it overheating and them sending me replacement parts numerous times.

what i have ended up doing ever since the screen spontaneously combusted (lol) is remove the battery permanently and keep it plugged in nonstop. that totally rectified the overheating issue. it feels slightly warm at times at the charging area, but it is normal - not the super hot, burn my finger hot, that i used to experience.

other than that, it would have actually had a 5 star rating based on specs and price. i am still using it right now. i figure i will use it until it completely dies. i mean, it works, it's just not structurally sound as far as the screen is concerned. the battery life itself does leave a bit to be desired as well, but that didn't bother me so much really, because i am pretty much always near an outlet to charge it. you get about 40 minutes of use on a full charge.

as far as specs, it is a great laptop for a student, or someone like me who isn't into hardcore games. it is fast enough and runs any program i need. i can run multiple programs at a time without having it slow down on me. my antivirus runs while im watching videos and it doesn't slow down on me. i typically have about 5 tabs open at any given time on my browser (as i write this there are 7) and i never have any problems. i can burn cd's while i play online games and it still runs fine.

i haven't even looked at reviews to see if my issue is common or a fluke. if it weren't for the screen busting open, i would recommend it. i get the idea that hp/compaqs on the lower price range like this aren't built to last and not much thought or quality goes into the battery/charging/overheating. it is a shame too because they are great budget priced laptops that do everything a typical, everyday user would want/need... until it bursts apart.

reviewText:
i've had this remote for about two years... over the last six months or so it's been really quirky.
in the past i would have rated it a four; however, it's getting a two. it probably deserves a 2 and a half, but i can't do half ratings. logitech support is abysmal. i contacted them once asking if they had a different charger for this item, because it doesn't sit all the way in the cradle. i've often found that in order for the metal things on the charger to come into proper full contact with the bottom of the remote, you need to weight it down. they had no grasp of english, or of my problem. they asked me if my remote turns on and then said that they were considering the issue as solved. at one point i was also having problems with it being able to charge in the cradle turn on at all - there was a known issue that if the battery life gets too low it can't charge itself. i was able to fix that with a firmware update though. so that's one point for logitech. the battery has is unpredictable and the battery meter random - it will go from 2 bars to low battery, then sit for a little and go back to 2 bars - without being charged. the remote frequently forgets that it's in an activity and resets back to the activities menu. it also randomly freezes or restarts. i know i've had it for a while, but for such an expensive remote it shouldn't be doing this... and it's not like this remote has been abused or anything. and it does all these things while it's resting on the coffee table by itself. unfortunately, i'd probably buy it again at some point because there is nothing else that i've found necessarily to compete with it, but i would get an extended warranty for it. you're going to need it.

reviewText:
i had seen this smart phone accessory around and wanted to try it.
but first, i wasn't sure what it was or what it did by simply looking at the product photos. i think the photos could have given consumers more information about the product for advertising purposes.

so what is this product? it's basically a traditional phone looking earpiece (or headpiece) with a stand. i put my iphone on the stand and plug the audio cable on the headphone port and use it as if it's a traditional phone. it's nice for the person who spends lots of time on the desk. otherwise, it is not ideal as a regular headset.

so how did it work? it worked quite well on my iphone 4s, 3gs, ipad (basically all the ios devices), but not with nexus 4. the audio quality was good on any ios devices. i tried regular on a cell phone, skype, and talkatone. they worked all well without issues. however, when i tried with nexus 4 on skype, talkatone, grooveip, and regular cell phone, i had very inconsistent quality and connection. it worked fine sometimes and didn't work well other times. i tried to find what caused this inconsistent quality, but i couldn't figure out. i don't know if it's the hardware or software. interestingly, i didn't have this issue with my iphones.

my thoughts on this accessory are mixed. first, i wonder why they didn't make this bluetooth capable and get rid of all the cables. i don't know if the manufacturing cost was the issue, but bluetooth is widely used technology now, and i don't see what is so hard to incorporate to this design. if i just use this on the desk it's fine, but there are probably people who like to try this walking around the office or doing something else without carrying the wired iphone. secondly, i like the design. i didn't like it the first time. it was awkward and didn't seem as if it would hold the phone securely on the stand. i worried that my iphone would slide off the stand because there is no holding arms (like a car mount) or anything. but the rubber piece on the stand holds the phone and the two tiny rubber feet on the bottom stops the phone sliding off the stand. lastly, it is fun to use actually. it is easier to put on a shoulder and talk on this. and it reminds me 80s and 90s when we don't have smart phones. it's fun to be retro sometimes.

overall, this is a nice, fun headset, but if you're spoiled with wireless technology, you may not like using this headset. if you can manage both hand on and hand off technology, this headset will be perfect! on a side note, when my son saw me using this headset he asked, "why are you talking into that weird, boxy device?" since we do not own landlines and the style of the phone is classic, i understood his curiosity. are these types of phones still made?

this is one of the coolest gift i've gotten... next to my ipod touch. the av920 has a nice resolution. i've tried the lower resolution vuzix products, and others in stores, and (in my opinion) you should get the hr ones if you are going to spend the money. the av920 is hr.
if you can stand watching shows on your ipod, you'll love this. if you are a videophile, and expect to teleport into the movie, you're dreaming. it is very difficult to see the lines of resolution. you have to look for them. once in a while during the motion-comics you'll see them. in most shows, it's not a problem. you can even read subtitles.
i watch nature shows, animated movies, dramas, etc, and no issues.
i put them on every night when my gf wants to go to bed. she sleeps on my arm, and i watch shows.
she used to whine about me staying up late and her falling asleep alone. not anymore. all the controls can be used with one hand. the power, and volume control are the same knob. the only time i need to look under the glasses, is when i'm changing shows.
the glasses are a snug fit, but flex. the nose piece is ohkay. it gets a bit uncomfortable after an hour or so. it's fairly durable. i fell asleep with them on twice, and dropped them from about 1 meter onto marble, and no damage. the battery life lasts about a week for me. that's on and off watching. i'd guess it gets about 5 hours life. charges in about 2 hours.
the screen is plenty big for any show or movie. and good colors. these can also do 3d movies. there is no focus. not for each, nor for both. i don't like that, but my eyes are good, so its not an issue.
there's a  problem when using an outside display for the ipod-touch. this is an ipod problem, not the av920.
when connected using the dock connector, some of the controls disappear.
instead of the video playing on the ipod, it plays on the connected display, (the av920: this is expected), and displays the clip-art for the band, movie, or tv show i'm watching on the ipod. this is all fine.
problem is that the scrubber bar disappears. i am left with just rewind, play, and fast-forward,
the is very annoying. if i want to jump to a certain part of the show, and have to wait 8 minutes to fast-forward to get there.
i've had these for 3 months. no issues.
summary: very cool, but not really personal. you get approached a lot

reviewText:
even as a then mac bigot the lenovo (then ibm) thinkpad with a writing pad and touchscreen was one of the few times i had bought a windows laptop. fast forward to 2013 and i was given a brand new w530 for work and hate it (though much less than the lousy new hp ultrabook). i did not get this laptop from amazon but love reading amazon reviews and wanted fellow buyers here to have this review to help them buy something else from amazon other than this lenovo dumbbell set.

in 2013 a no touchscreen windows 8 laptop is funny enough, but it is designed by a team of truck designers or drivers. they put a 15 inch non-touch screen in a body bigger than most 17" laptops. and about as elegant.

warning: you need to buy a matching samsonite luggage set for this, not to protect the laptop but to protect other people's luggage from it. get a set of two, one for the boulder sized laptop and the other for the power adaptor just slightly lighter than a concrete block.

it has the weakest speakers on any laptop i have ever owned, and the world's most atrocious sandpaper textured touch pad that often requires multiple attempts to register movement.

and what can i say about the lenovo web site designed by those who were rejected for the mail room janitor jobs.... the site asks you for a 4-25 character id, which it later rejects because you used non-alphanumeric characters, like a period in the name. they of course do not state it before you have clicked submit. you write a short review and then the site does not accept it because it has "too much text"... but does not tell you what the text limit is. last time i will go to that site....

though windows 8 has been rock solid on this and i have not had any crashes at all since i got it, the hardware is the worst ever.

i cannot recommend this to anyone.... well, except my worst enemies. :-)

imran anwar

update 09/09/2013
------------------
as if things could not get worse, or as if to prove some latent tendency to feel pain and anger, i went to the lenovo web site to look for some updated firmware and drivers. the made-by-martians-for-saturnites-living-on-neptune interface would be funny if it did not make you cry for how you have to (or i had to) click on about a dozen or more links to display the drivers under various areas, and then to click on each of those to see what the issue date was. if the date was later than the purchase date i downloaded it. (i did not download all because some were not relevant to me). when all was said and done, i dutifully and painfully installed each one by one... until...

one of the update installers completed its work, asked for a reboot, which i allowed and then...

the lenovo w530 stopped booting. it just stopped going past the boot menu, but instead of showing the various usb stick, external disk or even windows2go on usb os plus the internal drive, it simply showed zero boot devices available. in the meantime, the utilities area allowed me to run disk tests on the internal drive and memory etc. all came back 100% but the machine remained unbeatable. so, after spending one day trying to resolve that, i had to go in for a technician to try everything he could, and he had no luck either. finally, the only way the machine was booted was with lan startup and formatting and reinstalling the os. that used up most of today. and now i have to dig for installers of all the files, not to mention the work in progress from the last few days that had not been backed up (since i am not at home in ny).

word to the wise, friends don't let friends buy lenovo.
summary: order 2 suitcases & anti-rage meds with these lousy lenovos

reviewText:
to repeat earlier reviews, the sound from this player is incredible.  using it as a source for a decent tivoli speaker system while in temporary lodging and the crispness and range of the sound has improved dramatically over my ipad.  i can't wait to try them with my excellent ear buds on my next flight.

i have not and do not plan to use the unit for video. so no comment on that.

but the ui.  come on cowon!  the bottom third of the unit is a touchscreen with some fairly cryptic symbols on it.  you need to follow the instructions showing on the upper portion of the screen - which is not touch sensitive - to determine which button to hit.  and calling them buttons is a real stretch. very small marks in strategic locations around the touch screen and in the center.

touchscreens being so ubiquitous, you will find yourself hitting the upper part of the screen frequently.  and the font on the screen giving you instructions is tiny.  i wonder how visible that will be in very low or high light conditions.  i may be able to adjust that font.  hope so.

after some trial and error, i finally figured out how to leave the album currently playing and return to the music list.  hit list, then go back using upper left button until you are back at the main music list.  not intuitive at all and quite frustrating.

would be nice to have a battery meter on screen and maybe something showing memory usage as well.  digging down into system data to find this information is a pain.

the unit is small, light and therefore somewhat plasticy feeling.  the power button is not very responsive through the jelly case i got for it.  this will easily fit in a pocket.  much smaller than an iphone for example.

i won't be returning this due to the sound quality.  in fact, i wish i had spent the money for 32 gigs of storage.  however, the ui is soooo frustrating and clunky that i cannot recommend this device strongly.

reviewText:
this would be perfect for someone who wants to monitor two areas of their home while they are home, or who would like to review clips from the unit's sd card when the motion sensor triggers the camera.  when you're home, the monitor can be set to beep and record when it senses motion. so this could be great to monitor children in another room, etc.

however, it's really not a great solution for remote monitoring. to set it up for remote monitoring you connect the unit to your computer and create a skype account for it. you will end up being able to call that skype number to view the camera. but this also means the other camera will not do anything at all.

i still use it, but i wish i had understood that because i probably wouldn't have purchased it.

otherwise, is easy to set up and the video quality is good. i have only used it indoors. i had a friend over and we actually put a camera on her baby as he was sleeping so that if he moved it would alert us. that was pretty cool so it may be a lot more useful if you have small kids or children. or even if you want to monitor pets, etc.

getting the thing out was a pain. looks like the issue is a combination of too-soft plastic for the housing, and a bulging rubber bit of molding where the clip presses against the connector.

i spent several weeks researching to find the best ball head for my tripod.  while i know there are some that are double the price of the acratech gp, i would bet good money that none exceed its quality and performance.  i am relatively new to advanced photography -- a step up from simple point and shoot.  however, as an engineer, i can easily weed out the junk.
i have done some pretty neat laser tests on the stability of my setup (camera, tripod, and ball mount), looking for the slightest indication of response to shutter shock or mirror slap.  my setup is so solid that i am actually surprised.

i love the layout of all the controls on this ball head.  they all have tensioning that gives vernier adjustment and the movement for panning, etc., is as smooth as glass. i also purchased the quick disconnect mounting plate from acratech that matches my camera.  as it too is machined instead of cast aluminum, it is definitely worth the price.

reviewText:
i'm a professional motorsports photographer and this is a "b" bag.  our main bags are gigantic tamrac expedition 8x (a $300+ bag).  this is a great little bag, because of the price.  i've only used it a dozen times out in the field, and so far it's done great.

it fits the gear easily, which is a 7d and 7d mark ii, each with battery grips, a sigma "bigma" 50-500mm lens, a canon 17-40mm f4 and two full size flashes.  it does close ok with the height of the cameras, both 1d pro bodies and 7d + battery grip fit.  it's a tight fit as the cameras stick up an inch or two above the zipper line, but it does close easily enough.

my concerns are it's longevity.  the zippers don't feel like the highest quality and that is the first part to fail on a bag in my experience.  nearly all my expedition 8x bags develop zipper problems over time, and they are much stouter than these zippers.

wish list:
* an inch more depth in main compartment
* clips on the sides for main compartment in case of zipper failure, then your gear will stay inside the bag (yes, it's happened with another bag).
* loops to attach lens pouches to on the side opposite the tripod (or monopod) holder.
* slightly larger pocket on tripod side, so a monopod slides in easier.
* in the front accessory pocket, on the "bag" side it needs some closable pouches either via zipper or velcro, in order to store batteries there.  in the "flap" side zipper pocket, it's kind of heavy when you have spare batteries in it and is mis-balanced a bit.

other complaints:
* the waist stap is too high, i'm 6'2" and it wraps around my lower ribs.  i could probably put a ton of slack in the shoulder straps to get it lower, but that's not without it's own drawbacks.

i don't use the laptop part, so i can't comment on that, looks fine though.

ultimately, if the zipper holds up over time, this is an excellent value bag.  i would pay up to twice the price for a bag with the features i want.  once you hit "pro" bag territory, the prices get ridiculous.  you could buy two of these a year and still be ahead of buying large pro bags which tend to last about 2-3 years of heavy use before falling apart.

reviewText:
this is a tough question because both primes are sharp wide open and both have reasonable price tags.  deciding which one is "better" will require weighing the fine differences.

if you've read anything about the sigma 35 1.4, you'll know that it is a highly regarded lens and most people on the boards say that it's sharper than the canon.  even the folks over at canonrumors.com decided to review the sigma 35 before the canon version, which is telling because they normally review canon's best lenses first.  but then again you'll always find people online who swear by their canon-branded gear.  roger cicala of lensrentals.com offers a nice analysis of the sigma and how it compares: [...]

so it seems like the sigma has these advantages over the canon:
1) sharper images
2) equally accurate and consistent auto-focus (yes, af accuracy from a sigma earns them points in my book)
3) about $300 less than the canon

the advantages from the canon appear to be:
1) smoother bokeh
2) resale value may be higher for the brand name since some sigma's have poor af performance

it doesn't seem like the canon has much of an advantage.  i have used the 35l and it is indeed sharp wide open with very pleasing colors.  i have not used the sigma but all i hear are good things and that it beats the 35l.  i also know that the 35l came out in 1998, whereas the sigma was released in 2012.  it kind of makes sense that the sigma would have an edge given that technology can move quite a bit in 14 years.

when canon offers their rebates, the price difference becomes less, so if you don't want to throw off your lens collection with one that doesn't have a red ring, then the 35l may be right for you.  but given how the 2012 sigma competes, i have to give this one four stars because the sigma has bumped it into second place.
summary: this or the sigma 35 f/1.4 dg art?

reviewText:
i bought this router specifically so i could hook up a usb 3.0 external drive and use as a media server but even with the most recent updates, the server doesn't play the most basic video formats, .avi or .mkv. the only video format i have been able to get to play on it is .mp4 files but the player's functionality is horrendous. worst of all, in full screen mode there is a large white line down the entire length of the right side of the screen. if you try and play any other format other than .mp4 (which is a horrific format for quality but great on file size), the player either does nothing or you get the error {"status":"fail","errno":5003} and that is through a web page.

what is also absolutely ridiculous is if you access the media server not through a web page but through the device under network locations, the videos will not play directly from the device. first the entire file is downloaded to some obscure temp file somewhere before it starts to play. why would anyone buy a media server to play video off of, when the file needs to be downloaded to your machine before you can play it? ridiculous!!!! you are by far, better off just getting an internal drive and sharing the media folder path on the network. at least that way it plays on the remote computer without downloading the file. with this "media server" if 5 different machines play the same video, that video is downloaded and copied onto those 5 machines. what a ridiculous waste of space!!!!!!!

the interface for managing the server is embarrassing. there is no way to copy media content directly to the external drive without "uploading" through the web browser interface. you can create folders through the interface, but there is no way to delete a folder, only media files themselves.

pros:
i've not nothing.... well i do like the look of it. the cylinder style is pretty cool looking. it looks by far better than the traditional piece of toast look.

cons:
1)  media server plays full screen with a huge white line down the right side of the screen.
2)  media server only plays .mp4 files and not basic video formats like mkv or avi.
3)  when not using a web browser to view the media on the media server, the video is first completely downloaded to your machine prior to playing.
4)  the media server management interface has not even the most basic functionality (no ability to delete folders or directly load media content not through a browser interface)
5)  playing video through the browser interface has no functionality. volume is the only thing you can adjust and rolling the mouse wheel does nothing. why doesn't the mouse wheel skip ahead???
6)  the interface for setting up qos is the least user friendly of any router i have ever seen. if you want to prioritize computers based on ip address, set one port as the lowest of all the priorities and have only video files located on one network machine (machine has low priority) have the highest priority when played on other machines forget it! good luck trying to figure that out with a d-jink router. any other router with qos would be easy.
7)  the router is so light that it will fall over with the slightest table bump because when apparently when d-link was considering weight, they didn't consider cables were going to be attached to the router.
8) no way to turn off the incredibly annoying lights. forget trying to watch a movie in the dark if this router is in the room. i had to put electrical tape over the lights.
9)  your wireless network will change names within 30 minutes of setting the wireless network name. i set my wireless network name to "don't blink" and then went around and connected the plethora of wireless devices to my network. after about 30 minutes my network which was named "don't blink" miraculously change to "don't blink" and all of my devices lost their connection. after numerous attempts to change it back, ii have given up. my network is now "don't blink" which is the stupidest thing ever but that is apparently d-link for you.
10+) there is more but i am getting tired of writing this and if you have read this far and are still considering buying this or any other d=link router then it doesn't matter what i write and i am wasting my time.

for all that is wrong with this router, the price is extremely high. if all the issues i listed above where fixed, the router would be under priced.
