reviewText:
this is a review of the jbl synchros s700....
i bought this directly from manufacturer on ebay for $79.....as of today they still are selling them....they are listed as refurbished and come in a different outer packaging.  the set i received has absolutely nothing wrong with it....all accessories and case are also included.
i have a few headphones in the $200-$300 price category (philips fidelio x2, bang & olufsen h6 and hifiman he4xx)....just so you know what i am comparing these to.
accessories-
case is great.  cables are terrible....thin and very springy.....and the cables are 2.5mm at headphone end but are 4 pole (4 contact points) for the microphone.  potential problem depending on source
build quality-
wow....the headphones themselves really are well built. they present as a very nice set in both appearance and tactile feel....i would happily pay regular price for this level of build quality.
comfort-
meh....not great.....a bit tight on clamp pressure and the headband is not very comfortable...it has padding but it puts pressure directly on top of skull...will take some getting used to.  cant see wearing these for long periods.
sound quality-
well....they are not great.  definitely worth $79 if you can get them for that price.  i would say the bass is a bit flabby and bleeds significantly into the midrange.  it does not sound awful and i will keep them as a limited use office headphone.  it does not compare favorably to the fidelio x2s or the b&o h6s.  i sold my he4xxs because they had anemic bass.
these definitely have bass....but its just not tight enough and is too boosted in the upper bass region which gives a sort of less than clear sound.
treble is ok, but can sound harsh when contrasted against the flabby bass,
 depending on the recording, i actually think live stage processing clears up much of the flabby bass issues.  at first i did not like it at all, but upon further listening, it presents the material with a dip in the upper bass where it meets the midrange.  this results (for me at least) with a much more clear midrange....and this function also creates a wider soundstage.  deep bass is still present as well.
verdict
a well built headphone that suffers from less than optimal driver tuning.  jbl could have had a real winner here if theyd just spent more time on getting the sound right.  the live stage function sounds better than the standard sound to me.
summary: great build.....average sound quality that improves with dsp turned on

reviewText:
in looking at the many reviews here, they run the gamut from disgust to great praise and i can completely understand why.  i've had my ds-213j for just over 6 weeks now, and there are days when i'm ready to send it back to amazon and others when i think that this is one of the best purchases i've ever made.  on balance, i think the days i'm happy outnumber the days that i'm not.  which group you'll end up in, depends on what your needs are and what your level of networking experience is.

i consider myself pretty experienced with computers, mostly on the mac side, and i know that networking is, for the most part, something i don't really understand.  so i purchased the 213j with a little bit of caution.  last summer i invested a lot of time into moving all of my digital media onto a western digital live media hub.  it had an internal 1tb drive and i bought a 3tb drive external usb drive for additional space.  it looked good in the beginning but as i got my files loaded, it slowed down to a crawl and got to the point where it was just too painful to deal with.  any time i added a new music album it would take several hours for it to re-index it's database.  and even once that was finished, navigating my way thru the music library was painfully slow and cumbersome.

it took about 3 hours to upload my library of almost 1tb of music to the synology and it finished indexing the library is less than 2 hours.  now adding a new album only takes a couple of minutes to merge into the database with this system as opposed to hours on the wd.  and the facilities that this server offers are much more robust.  there are apps for ios and android as well as roku and samsung smart tvs.  all of which i have.  so as it stands now, i've finally accomplished what i set out to do originally:  i can play my music anywhere in the house, or even outside in the yard and i can watch movies or the tv shows that i have on any tv in the house or on any smart device that i own.  or over the internet.

i've also moved 85gb of photos from my mac to the synology and i'm finding that browsing my photos is as easy with the included photostation app as using iphoto is.  however, the big difference is in the editing.  synology includes access to 3 different online editing programs but the experience that i've had in trying to use those apps hasn't been that great.  once i figured out how to use synology's bulk photo uploader utility, it was a piece of cake to transfer my photo library from the mac to the nas.  and moving new photos as they're taken now is just as easy.  but i suggest you do your editing before moving those photos to your nas.

so it managing and playing your media library is what you're interested in, you'll probably be very happy with a synology nas.  however, i do strongly recommend that you buy a copy of the "synology nas setup guide: based on dsm 5.0" by nick rushton.  it's only available as an ebook and is priced at $9.99, which i consider to be pretty high.  but it contains information that is critical for getting your nas up and running if you're a novice with networking and network storage systems.

and that brings me to the real problem with the synology systems.  there is no documentation included with these systems.  none.  zero, zilch, nothing at all.  you do get a small piece of paper that shows you how to install a drive into the synology box but you are on your own from there.  and, in my opinion, that is the root cause for the tremendous range of reviews of this product.

if you're an it literate person, who really knows networks and all of the various technologies that come into play with setting up network systems and software, you're gonna love this box.  you'll have it up and running, doing exactly what you need in no time.  or, if all you want is a network media hub, a super glorified appletv, and you've got just a little bit of computer smarts, you should be okay.  but if you're a network gimp and you'll really want to exercise all that the synology nas can do for you, you've got a big challenge in front of you.

rushton's book can get you started.  but it really only opens the door.  there are some very limited help files built into the dsm operating system and there is limited help contained in the synology online forums.  but much of that online help assumes that you know networking issues.  so if you're learning this stuff as you go, you may not go very far.

like i said at the beginning, you're milage may vary.  depending on your level of networking experience and the uses you plan for your nas purchase, you could be very happy or very frustrated.  or both on alternate days.

expensive.  competitors are not as proud of their offerings as bose is.  i've had other sets before and while the bose noise cancellation is better, it isn't worth the extra price.

reviewText: i have not been able to successfully build a windows 7 x64 pc with this motherboard. i've been building pcs for 20 years and even with that experience i am unable to complete the build and get windows successfully installed. first, this motherboard is somehow not compatible with the dc-dc power board in my mini pc case. the motherboard can be powered by other power supplies and the power supply can power other motherboards but the two are incompatible. since i also sell these mini pc cases it's turned into a customer support nightmare having to exchange power boards for customers. the asrock z68m-itx and a75m-itx work (among motherboards from all different brands) but the h67m-itx does not. i've never come across a power board/motherboard incompatibility before. this i was able to at least workaround with a different dc-dc power board or in my own build, a picopsu. i have no idea which is the issue, the motherboard or the power supply, but it takes the two together to cause the issue. the symptom is that the system turns on for about 1 second and then turns itself right back off. second, and most importantly since i can find no workaround, the graphics drivers included on the cd crash windows 7 on startup and the system has to be recovered. i tried all three graphics drivers on the cd, the latest from the asrock site and the latest from intel. i updated the bios as well. all attempts give the same result: bsod on startup just after "starting windows" and then it's off to system recovery. the bsod says "baddriver". i also tried hdmi and dvi-d since my research had shown some issue with bsods and hdmi with intel drivers but it was to no avail. the cabling didn't matter. strangely, windows 8 cp works right out of the box. windows 8 cp however isn't ready for production so i need windows 7 on my pc. i don't have this issue on a different board with the same cpu, ram and ssd. i see a lot of glowing reviews here so these incompatibilities seems very hit-or-miss. i cannot speculate why. besides these issues, my other issue has been the layout of the motherboard. the front panel connections are at the back of the board. this requires the front panel connections to be stretched across the board if they reach at all. of all the things that should to be at the front of the board, it should be the front panel connectors. i have never seen a motherboard with them at the back. thanks to amazon's wonderful return policy i can happily exchange it for a different motherboard. [update 18-may-2012] i received the gigabyte ga-h61n-usb3 motherboard today and put it together with the same ram, cpu, ssd and power supply. windows 7 x64 and all the drivers that came with the gigabyte driver cd installed without issue, including the graphics driver. no bsods / operating system corruption / bad driver issues.

reviewText:
this mouse looks like a great deal for those who need a vertical mouse, but after using it for an hour, i've returned it.

first off, the sensor works well enough and i didn't experience any tracking issues for normal desktop use. the real glaring issue is how stiff the mouse buttons are. every time you click, your mouse will literally move from where you are pointing since the buttons are on the side. you have to grip the mouse with your thumb and push against the mouse to stop it from moving. all this muscle strain defeats the purpose of an ergonomic mouse. i would've stuck it out and hoped the tension on the buttons would decrease with use, but there's an even bigger problem with this mouse.

the worst part is that the plastic on this mouse smells like burning plastic and the smell will transfer to your hand. i returned the mouse because i don't want to risk breathing in the plastic off-gassing or absorbing it through sweaty palms. i had high hopes for this mouse but it's not very usable and the plastic might even be a health hazard.

edit: big thumbs up to anker for their customer service. they saw this review and sent me a newer version of this mouse (https://www.amazon.com/dp/b018lr04b8/ref=psdc_11036491_t2_b00bifntmc). the mouse buttons are much softer so it eliminates the problem of mouse movement when you click, but the plastic still smells horribly. i've let it air out for about a week and it doesn't noticeably smell anymore unless you hold it close to your nose. it doesn't transfer to my hand, which is the most important part. the side mouse buttons (mouse4/mouse5) aren't the easiest to click, but it's acceptable enough that i'm willing to overlook that problem. i'd give this mouse a 4/5 overall.

the best part of this kit is the case.  it's a canvas-like bag with 3 pockets that unfolds and has a bit of padding for the filters.  it's soft enough that it can be folded in half and fit snugly into whatever space you have in your camera bag.

the filters themselves are usable, but be prepared to do color correction after the fact.  i had issues with both the grad and solid nd filters leaving color casts on the photos.  the non-gradient one in particular was consistently distorting the colors.  after using this set for about 2 months / 300ish photos i've decided to leave it at home and purchased something else.

there's a good chance if you're looking at this set you're thinking of doing landscape photography.  in the canon world at least i've noticed that most wide angle lenses have an area of about 77mm and these filters will fit over that space.  i used this set primarily with the tokina 11-16mm.  i didn't have a holder for the filters, i would just hold them by hand with the camera on a tripod.

on the positive side this set is so cheap that if you aren't sure if you want a gradient or nd filter it's really a low-cost way to see if it's something you'd like before investing in much more expensive filters.

i live in a difficult signal area and recently lost some channels with my old antenna and pre-amp setup, i tried a new antenna first and when that didn't get me reliable reception on one of the channels i wanted i figured i would try upgrading my old channel master spartan 3 pre-amp to the cm7777. i was able to improve signal strength on most of the channels but the one channel i was really having problems with would not come in at all now, i figured i might be having a signal overload problem so i ordered a 3db and a 6db attenuator today and decided to check all my signal strength readings so i would have something to compare them to when i get the attenuators, while checking this morning i lost all my channels. i read some of the bad reviews here about the cm7777 and saw where someone mentioned the power inserters could fail, i check the transformer without the power inserter and got a reading of 21 volts, i then checked the power inserter voltage and got 0 volts, so my 3 day old cm7777 was no longer working at all.

 i still had my old pre-amp power inserter and after checking to see if the voltages were the same i tried using it with the cm7777, it worked but i will wait and see if it lasts before modifying my rating.

**update november 8th***
lost all channels again, old power inserter still putting out 21 volts so i guess the mast mounted cm7777 pre-amp must be dead now. maybe i killed with the old channel master power inserter or maybe it was going to die anyways, i only know that i will not be buying anything from channel master again.
summary: power inserter failed after only 3 days

this review is for the ocz 126gb vector series vtr1-25sat3-128g. warning! do not buy ocz products. this ssd is a total piece of complete and utter crap. i had upgraded from this ssd which was working fine, about 3 years ago and have a couple very reliable, very solid and very dependable samsung 840 and 850 ssds. i had taken this piece of garbage out of service and put it on a shelf, in it's protective box.

three years later, after no use, i thought i'd see if i could use it as a cache for a new system. nope. the new asus mb could not see it. huh. so i tried it in the system i'd originally bought it for. nope. can't be seen. it's not even just lost data, which i've fortunately transferred to a newer ssd, it's completely and utterly dead. the system bios can't even see this garbage, yet it was working okay last time i used it. it just died in storage apparently. i can see it losing the data, maybe, but it's brains? no way should the brains of the thing be that volatile, that it can't even tell two systems what it is.

if you look around the web, you'll see a high failure rate for this crap and it's probably one of the reasons ocz went bankrupt and no longer exists. however toshiba did buy some of their assets and may still honor the 5 year warranty this piece of garbage came with. probably with a lot of restrictions though. do not trust any data to this ssd of doom.

they haven't been made for a while so i doubt you'll find any new. definitely stay away from any used ones!

i just had a lot of fun, pulling out the circuit board, wrapping it in layers of plastic to contain fragments and smashing every single blasted chip on it with a hammer.  good riddance. it's just not worth the trouble to go through the hassles of a proving a purchase date, and do warranty replacement, especially if it means i have to pay for return shipping. and what would the replacement be? i'd rather chose something with known reliability myself.

reviewText:
i purchased these headphones from bose when they first came out many years ago. the clarity was amazing and the noise cancellationn lived up to it's name because i could not hear anything, anything at all when i had them on, which further amplified the already amazing sound. then one day the headband broke at the swivel. i was extremely upset but i was about 19 years old when they broke so i didn't think to try to get a replacement; i just figured it was a loss, an expensive loss. besides, i was after the one year warranty so they wouldn't help me anyhow, right?

one day i was planning to move and found these in the back of my closet. i got curious and called bose to see if, after two years, they would assist me. not really expecting much i talked to a manager. to my surprise and delight the manager told me that the headband cracking was a known issue and that i could get a new pair shipped out and when i got the new one's to ship the old one's back in the box they came in. i was on a high! super happy! they came in 2 days by ups and i was up and running again.

when i looked at the new pair i noticed the look was a little different. i thought maybe they amped up the headband so i thought nothing about it. when i turned them on they were not as noise-cancelling as the others. the first pair made you feel like you were in a concert hall by yourself listening to a live performance and no one could break through the sound. with the new pair i heard everything in the background and the sound was not as sharp as the first one's. anyhow, i got over this minor blip and used them. after about 6 months the headband on the second one cracked and broke exactly where the first one's had, and alas i had no more headphones. eventually i purchased a pair from amazon for $130 used but the seller was very dishonest and sold me a pair that was broken like the one's i had and they would not refund my money, so beware if you must get these used.

all in all i am very disappointed in this product, not because of the sound so much but because of the construction. i know technology and sound takes a lot of money to produce, but a sturdier plastic would have made these a lot better and more able to last the test of time. to be honest i would have paid a bit more for a headphone i knew was going to last more than a few months, the sound was that good. i am back in the market for some really nice cans with fantastic sound as well as earbuds for one the run music listening but i do not dare go back to bose for cans because i know what the new style headphones look and sound like and in my opinion it's not worth the extra $31 markup that seems to be going on with amazon and not worth the $299 they used to be. i am looking at sennheiser or audio-technica but i cannot deal with this product again. if they decide to update the plastic band then i would give it another chance, but as it is i do not recommend this set to anyone and this product gets a 1/2 star from me because the sound means nothing if you can't even wear them and for this price bose should know better.

reviewText:
this was the first lens i bought for my nikon d90.  i got it used for $270 (march 2010) because i couldn't afford anything else at the time.  it was a great lens to learn how to use the manual features of my nikon d90 because the lens is so slow and difficult to get a good shot (especially indoors) unless you learn how to set the optimal settings of shutter speed, aperture, focus, and iso.  so i am thankful for my tamron lens because it taught me to appreciate the better features of better quality lenses.

good features:
1) great for outdoor shots.
2) great wide angle at 18mm (great for group pictures, landscapes, and capturing high rise buildings).

bad features:
1) terrible quality for indoor shots.
2) terribly slow when autofocusing and quite noisy (can disturb guests at a wedding or a public speaking event).
3) build quality is poor and plasticky.
4) the lens creeps a lot (meaning it slides out on its own when you point the lens downward).

i compared this tamron lens to the nikon stock lens that comes with many consumer nikon digital slrs and i didn't see a huge difference.  i think it is comparable.  but compared to the nikon 50mm f/1.4d and the nikon 85mm f/1.4d prime lenses, this lens simply doesn't capture anything close to the sharpness, detail, and great looking bokkeh of these more expensive lenses.  bottom line... i never use my tamron lens despite its multipurpose range since i purchased my 50mm 1.4d prime lens.

most of the time, i am taking portraits of people indoors.
summary: great range but the lens is painfully slow and terrible indoors!

p.s. i should note that when i said great price above, i paid only $10.09 for this though it seems to have gone up since then.

reviewText:
i got this adapter to be able to use a bluetooth headset with my pc.

the first bad experience is immediately incurred when you install the drivers for this device. the installation takes ages, literally more than 5 minutes probably closer to 8 min (doesn't seem long, but most driver installs are under the minute).

the second, and most important one, is that the audio quality with this device is just poor. it's like hearing a 24 kbs mp3, it's just bad. i tried both front and back ports (front ports generally receive less power than on board ones) and even had an extender cable so that the device was less than 1m away from the headset. still audio was bad, so bad that even spoken youtube videos were obviously being downgraded.

before somebody says it was the headset's fault, i paired it with my nexus 5 and the sound was perfect, even in another room from the phone.

the only positive thing is that pairing devices with it was easy.

if i could return the device without paying for shipping i would in a heartbeat, but because the cost of shipping it back will be close if not above the cost of the device, i will just pocket the loss.

stay away.
summary: not worth the money - stay away

reviewText:
i do a lot of phone tech support (and have for many years now), so i rely on my headset heavily. i need the sound to be loud and clear on both ends, and i need them to be comfortable enough to wear for many hours at a time.

it's hard to believe these $10 panasonic kx-tca60 headsets are still the best i've tried out of 8 different models / 4 different brands over the past 8+ years (and many of the ones i tried were much more expensive). for example, i've had $40+ plantronics models that could not match the volume level and clarity of these. even the uniden headset that came with my uniden 5.8ghz phones was inferior to the sound quality and volume of these.

i been using these kx-tca60's for years now and they're all i'll buy any more. i currently use mine with my uniden tru-9485 handsets and i'm extremely happy (so are my callers, since we hear each other loud & clear).

i will admit that i purchase them two at a time because i've had some kx-tca60's that only lasted a couple years (for example, the swivel for the boom does eventually get loose over a long period of time to the point where it won't stay where you've adjusted it) but that's after heavy use and abuse. that plus i tend to roll over the cord with my chair sometimes and it can only endure that so many times before you damage it, but overall these are really pretty rugged.

i would definitely recommend these to anyone who has handsets of any brand with headset jacks on them (like i said, these work better with my uniden phones than my uniden headset does!), and who spends long hours in calls each day. i hope panasonic never stops making these!!
summary: great value, surprisingly the best i've used with many brands of phones

reviewText:
===update===
i have recently installed openwrt on this "doorstop" (only works with versions 2 and versions 3 -- not the new version 4). it seems to have fixed many of the issues that i had with the product - except its range. now it is relatively stable and i can connect from all 5ghz devices that i have tried so far. it also has a much nicer gui interface and it has significantly more configuration options. i would only recommend this for the expert users as it could be easily misconfigured to allow security issues in a home network environment and it is not very "novice friendly" (ie. if you are not an it person in any form, avoid the advanced router firmwares like openwrt).

i am leaving the rating at 1-star as i really feel that no one should never have to struggle so much to make a "mainstream" home device for the end-user community function as advertised... and the fact that i lost 4 years to the crappy firmware and updated firmware that tp-link ships on the product (last tried new firmware in march 2018 with less compatibility that my initial review) and well as use of my 100usd.

for a good inexpensive router, i would recommend trendnet... for advanced features, i would recommend asus... and for easy of setup, use and frequency of updates, i would recommend netgear. steer clear of tp-link...
===
i purchased this in 2014 as my first ac-class router to provide better coverage in my new house at a bargain price of less than 100usd. after switching out my netgear n900 router for this to get better speed with devices in the 5ghz band, i started having disconnection issues with my 5ghz devices. since i assumed that they were vendor compatibility issues, i kept the router and waited for updates. after configuring this router for use as an access point and updating it numerous times, and having tried to connect products from netgear, belkin, linksys, and d-link... the connection for any single product i have tested with it has lasted less than 1hour -- neither can these products reconnect automatically. unfortunately, this is basically a doorstop. i never considered that a product from a reputable networking company would function so poorly, since their power-line products and their network switches have worked so well for me. i have since utilised ac products from belkin, netgear and linksys... all with wonderful results... but i am now "gun-shy" when it comes to tp-link wireless products. their stability will continue to remain suspect in my eyes... and especially now that they have blocked installing 3rd party software on their devices as well.

my recommendation with wireless products is to make sure you get a connectivity and stability rating from all reputable reviews before buying any products... i followed magazine reviews and blog posts without this reference.
summary: doorstop -- my first one star review ever!!!! needs to be a zero star though...

i would recommend due to build quality and ease of installation.

i'm pleased with the sound but i must give 3 stars at best purely for the ridiculous installation. the original reviewer complaining about the 'size of the screw' left us hanging as to what exactly the problem was. i will expand on what he said.

you are then left with a wobbly mount.

and forget wall anchors. the screw holes are so close on the mounting bracket that you can't put the wall anchors in the drywall without chewing up all the 'grip' area.

harmon kardon wall mount geniuses -- please include the screws to mount these things because i will probably have to get a machine shop to build me what i need.. gheez.

reviewText:
~further update, almost three years later~

well, i still own these headphones, and even though i don't use them very regularly, they've held up well over the years, still fit comfortably, and still deliver great sound! at this stage of the game, there are plenty of bluetooth headsets out there that run, price-wise, over, under, and around the same price that you'll find these at, but jabra always has (in my experience) and probably always will make good, quality, reliable products. this one is definitely worth the selling price, even in today's technologically updated market.

~update~

i've now owned my jabra headset for about two weeks, and i still love it! i used my phone and this headset to provide my music for my workout, and the headset stayed put perfectly, and delivered above-average sound quality throughout the duration of my workout. in travelling through numerous airports over the holiday season, it was the perfect way to drown out incessant background airport noise. i love this thing!

*~*

in my initial search for a headset for my phone, i was hoping to find a set that would give me good audio for my mp3s, as well as function well when i am on a call. as far as i can tell, after only owning this for a day, this headset more than adequately covers every requirement i had for it. i took a call yesterday on this, and had the call recipient complaining about the audio being too loud, which, to me, is a plus. i'm not stuck any more asking the standard "can you hear me now?" when on my cell phone using a hands-free set.

as far as the audio goes when listening to my mp3s, this definitely has stereo sound in my opinion, even if it is a bit lacking when it comes to bass. the volume and audio quality delivered by this jabra headset beats the poor quality audio that i was used to listening to from the cheapie-cheapie off-brand headset i'd spent thirteen bucks for at my local compusa a few months back. time and again, "you get what you pay for" has been proven to me to be true, and it seems to be the case once again here.

i wasn't even using my phone's mp3 feature prior to receiving this headset. now that i've got it, and see what my phone's mp3 player feature is truly capable of, i'm definitely looking forward to putting it to use in my travels, and exercise activities. jabra comes through for me once again!

please note, i am normally generous and lenient in my expectations of products on amazon. if you don't get a chance to see and feel it, there will always be some "error" involved. that said, i felt that you, my fellow consumer, needed to be warned about this one, as it has some major flaws.

here are the 2 major flaws i find:

1. as other reviews have said, the clip is not a "clip" because there's no spring tension. it really doesn't hold onto anything. if you try to use it your ipod will fall off, fall out, and fall down. so you'll be constantly testing the "protection" because the case meant to protect it is actually causing the dropping. ironic, right?

2. when you initially slide the ipod in there's a tiny node at the other end that's meant to stop it from sliding too far. however, the node is very small, and the ipod is able to slide past it. while it doesn't do it every time, it's still a problem because when it does move past it, the node leaves a scratch on my ipod. see the problem? the case that's meant to protect the ipod is actually damaging it! by plugging it in you are constantly pushing the device upwards, risking a scratch from a slide past that node. mine's been on there a week and there's a distinct mark on the pretty blue paint from the pesky node.

bottom line: this case will likely disappoint. it's certainly not worth $10. the protection from external damage may be adequate, but when the "protection" is the item that's actually causing the risk (i.e. because of the "clip" you'll drop it more, and the case itself may scratch your ipod) you have to question the value. as for myself, i will be looking for another case.
summary: 2 major flaws. better keep looking and not chance this one.

reviewText: so far, this card (the 4-port marvell 88se9235) is working quite well. i'm currently using this card in a supermicro sy-528ltn2, in the lone pcie 3.0 x16 slot, as i had already used two available sata 3 ports on the logic board, and simply needed more, to support some drives connected to the mid-tower's backplane. i'm not using any raid features of the card, i just needed the extra ports, with a spec to fully support the max bandwidth of multiple sata 3 drives, and anything over pcie 2.0 x2 is a bit expensive, for my needs. i will likely never use the raid features of this card, so the remainder of the review will be of the card, itself, sans any extra "stuff". out-of-the-box, it works with linux, at least under kernel 4.7.x and above. currently, i have two hitachi ultrastars connected to this card, and two connected to the logic board (a total of four, for testing, and in case one controller fails- i'd be able to easily identify whether it's the card or the controller/port on the logic board). so far, i don't notice any difference in speed, between the two drives connected to the card, and the two connected to the on-board sata iii ports (i wrote random data to all of the drives, via dd on linux, while tracking progress, and the speed across all four was nearly identical). so far, i haven't experienced any issues, and i run the card, as i do the machine it supports, 24/7. i'm not sure how well this setup would work with four ssds attached- my guess is it would be quite fast- nearly, but not quite, as fast as having four ssds connected to a logic board's on-board sata iii controller (for example, a samsung 850 evo peaks at around 552/532 mbps read/write, and the max theoretical bandwidth for pcie 2.0 x2 is 2000mbps, so you'd lose some speed, using the faster drives available). to those of you who don't have on-board sata iii, or not enough on-board sata iii, that probably makes no difference- this will certainly beat out your on-board sata ii connections. if what you need is is an inexpensive sata iii card, in a pcie slot fast enough to support it, this is probably the card to buy. if i experience any issues, i'll update my review. if i experience no issues, i'll update my rating to five stars.

i'm not brutal with equipment, but in a few short weeks, the flimsy plastic part that holds the ear pieces to the headset broke on one side. within a month or two the other side went as well forcing me to use office paper clamps to hold the whole thing together.
i use them in bed late at night when the household is asleep. a second convenient bedside charger would be nice. i tend to put them down on the bedside table before i doze off rather than get up and walk across the room hook it up for recharge. if you're a  late night tv watcher, you too might call this justifiable laziness. too many times i put them on the next night and find the battery's down.
i honestly think that before i replace them with another wireless, i'd find a way to sneak an extension wire across the room through attic or basement space and go with a standard wired headphone.

i wanted a thin folio to house my beloved surface pro 3, i also wanted something that was not pure black since i  tend to travel a lot, and misplace "pure black" colored devices in dark rental car trunks.  this product not only protects my surface, but looks professional, and the splash of color makes it visible enough that i won't lose it.  i really like that i can store my keyboard on the surface while in transit, and the cover stays on whether i use the keyboard or not.  why not 5 stars?  i deducted one star for the minor annoyance that the keyboard will not work in its "tilted" form with the cover still on - the cover at the bottom prevents the magnets from engaging the keyboard in its "elevated/tilted" mode.  this is not a huge problem, but keeps the product from being perfect.

the mi424wr-gen2 provided with my verizon fios account has weird wall-mounting slots in the back, which force you (that is, if you want to use them) to install the device with the antenna upside down. the signal propagation is terrible, worse with the metal studs in my condo.

there's no downside. i definitely recommend this to anyone that has a compatible router sitting in a less than optimal spot.
summary: very nice if you are forced to keep your router in an odd spot

reviewText:
when i got my hands on this headphones, i was surprised by how cheaply made it feels. the headbands were loose, and it seemed to be made of cheap plastic.
but it looks pretty cool. one point for style!

i connected it to the mini usb and charged it. it charged easily via usb and it was very intuitive.

after fully charged, i decided to give it a while. this headphones is very comforable, and you can wear it for a long time without discomfort. they also fit well over your head so it doesn't drop out of your head easily.

the bluetooth connected to my computer easily. it also connected to my phone easily. the volume control works well too.

i played with the headband. you can fold it in weird ways to make it more compact. the folding mechanics was very fun.

then, i turned on the music, and the sound sounded really bad. it did not have bass, and all the different sounds that you hear in music disappears. you can only hear the simple melody that you get with crappy earphones.

i decided to try this headphones for a day. on my way to school, i turned on the noise canceling. i took out my headphones, and then put it on again. there was no difference. the rumbling of the engine is just as loud.

as i walk around with it, the music skips at least twice every song. arrrgh!!!

i felt like i got cheated. i bought these headphones to listen to music, get rid of external noise, and get away from wires. but all of it didn't work out.

in conclusion
 pros: easy to charge, fun to fold the headphones and play, easy to pair with bluetooth, comfortable to wear, looks good.
cons: bad sound quality, no noise canceling, bad bluetooth connection.
summary: this is a toy. if you're trying to enjoy music i wouldn't recommend it

reviewText: i bought the tiffen 62mm approx. $30 polarizer from amazon.  when it arrived it was all smudged and dusty.  but even worse, it had a small scratch on the glass.  also the thread on the ring looked badly made, or else must have been scratched during transit, because if you looked closely you could see that the paint had come of from the edges and the edges themselves looked slightly jagged.  it made a disconcerting scraping noise when i put it on the lens, and that's when i decided i'm not going to use it because i'm afraid the unfinished edges will damage the threads on my lens.  i got a sigma uv filter along with this one and wow, what a difference in quality!  the glass on the sigma was smooth and clean and the ring and threads were very cleanly made.  you could just see how poor quality the tiffen was by comparison when you looked at the two rings side by side; the metal was all scratched looked like it had been crafted by hand with a hammer.  and both filters came in the same shipment so it wasn't the case that something happened to the tiffen during delivery.  i don't know if the problem is bad packaging on tiffen's part (the box did look like it would not hold the lens so securely as sigma's) or just poor quality control, but in any case i now seriously question the reliability of this brand.  i am returning it to amazon and buying a different brand.  i'm giving this 2 stars instead of 1 because the polarizing effect did seem to work pretty well, for what that's worth.

reviewText:
i caught these headphones on a deal of the day sale on amazon.  i normally don't buy anything without reading reviews, but these headphones had a total of five reviews at the time of my purchase and all of the reviews were pretty much suspect(fake).  i even checked online for reviews but could not find any thorough reviews of this product.  but the price was too good to pass up buying these so i pulled the trigger.  i am not an audiophile or sound expert, just a normal guy.

first, out of the box these headphones are nice.  very well made, and durable.  heavy but they fit comfortably on my head.  i can tell they will hold up to whatever abuse i put them through.  the cord is very nice, it's wrapped in this clothlike/braided material.  very nice touch.  also the design of the headphones are nice.  matte black look with bomb shelter type logos on the outside of the ears and on the inside. the connector that also bears the logo.  the coiled cord near the headphones can be detached from the longer cord.  the controller for your apple products is designed nicely.  all around, the most solid pair of headphones you can buy.

now for the sound.  again i'm not an audiophile.  i'm comparing these with my original pair of beats studio headphones.  i plugged these up to my hp envy beats edition laptop.  the bass sounds nice, very level and not overwhelming. vocals and treble all sound nice and balanced.  but, the one thing i noticed was that these headphones do not want to just blast off.  like the volume is stuck. i checked the volume on my laptop, and even at the highest volume, they aren't that loud.  i took them off and put on the beats studio and at half volume, the beats were louder to the point they were shaking.  i thought maybe this was just my laptop, so i switched to my ipod shuffle, and the sound was still lacking compared to the beats studios.  sidenote: the control works flawless on the ipod.

for my second problem,  i tried checking the sound using my phone (galaxy note 3), but i couldn't.  the reason being is because i have a heavy duty case.  due to the huge round connector on the headphones, i was unable to plug the headphones in.  this is a huge problem for anyone that uses a decent case on their phones. i'm not letting this effect my review, but thought buyers should be aware of this.  sound leaks heavily from these even though they aren't that loud.  they are not noise cancelling.

i like these headphones, but at full price ($299) i would be extremely disappointed in their performance.  for the half price deal i got these for, i'm satisfied.  you're paying for the styling, durability, and overall comfort.  everyone is walking around with the beats logo on their heads(including me), good to have something different that looks even better.  sound lacks compared to beats studio.  good job philips, but work on that sound.  maybe they need to be broken in first before they sound better, if they do, i will update my review.
summary: real review from a real person

reviewText:
i have been using my lenovo thinkpad i7 helix for 5 months now, i believe i was one of the first to get one when it went into production.

the pros:
1. the design - a fast processor laptop with a detachable touch screen is a great idea. lenovo should get credit for that.
2. the battery life is awesome, i can get up to 8 hours. the computer drains the battery in the keyboard section first, and then the one in the screen unit.

the cons:
1. the screen is really bad. there is a specific point near the middle of the screen where the screen intermittently reads a touch even when i am nowhere near the screen. that changes the cursor location if i happen to be typing, randomly presses displayed buttons on the app i am working on and plays havoc with the touch based controls in the apps. this is a bad enough experience for me as a regular user to stop using the helix and move to something else, like a surface pro 2.
2. the keyboard unit generates errors when restarting, the computer reads that as a hardware profile change, which triggers a bit locker error. the keyboard needs to be reset - there is a pinhole you need to shove a paper clip into for that.
3. seemingly randomly the computer does not hibernate when you close the lid. it stays on, and if you put it into a laptop bag, continues to run, and heat up. that makes the fan come on, blow hot air in the laptop bag and probably drain the battery very quickly. so the laptop is fully drained when you take it out of the laptop bag.

i do not recommend this computer.
summary: great design, poorly built, terrible hardware

reviewText:
i really love the idea of how this product should work.  i want to be able to send pictures to family members and surprise them with a cool picture and keep in touch more frequently without having to email photos or call.  once you have this thing set up, it works well.  however, if i had to send this photo frame to anyone without a clue of wireless networks or any adeptness with technology, i would seriously have to consider hiring someone to set it up for them.

i ordered this product to give to my husband's mother who is not tech-savvy at all.  i also bought a linksys router and then preconfigured the ssid and etc on to this product and personally found it lacking in usability features.  you had to use the remote or push buttons on the frame to select each individual letter which was timeconsuming as well as counter-intuitive.  the menus were also counter-intuitive.  i did like the fact that i could program this product to turn on at a certain time and turn off at another time.

as it turns out, she couldn't get the product to work so her daughter tried to get it setup and in the process, everything became so mis-configured, i had to wait until our next trip there to be able to re-configure it correctly.  i like it and recommend it to anyone who is tech-savvy.  if not, i wish you the best of luck!  i am waiting for a more user-friendly model to be released before i buy a second one.

reviewText:
this is a good standard telephoto zoom with solid, but average performance.  this particular lens features canon's micro ultra sonic motor; therefore, it does not have the same focusing performance of the standard usm designs.  optically, it is the same lens as the ef 75-300 iii, and performs roughly the same.  usually, this lens retails for more than the non-usm design, but i'd pay little more.  an oddity on amazon has often had the price of this lens lower, and that's a good deal.

as previously stated, the lens is a solid performer.  good lens speed, but not as fast of focusing as the ef 100-300.  additionally, the front of the lens rotates, which is not as nice when using filters such as polarizers.  the plastic barrels are ok, but zooming is a bit less smooth than desired.

canon also doesn't include much with the lens.  a lens shade is very useful for outdoors photography, and canon is very pricey on an accessory that most include.  canon's one-year warranty is also poor compared to most others.

for a good alternative, look at the tamron / promaster 70-300 ld lens which has closer focusing, includes the shade, and both offer longer warranties.  however, neither are as quiet as the canon lenses.

for an upgrade, look at the canon ef 100-300 usm, which offers a smoother, faster usm, and no filter rotation.

as previously stated, the lens is a solid performer.  good lens speed, but not as fast of focusing as the ef 100-300.  additionally, the front of the lens rotates, which is not as nice when using filters such as polarizers.  the plastic barrels are ok, but zooming is a bit less smooth than desired.

canon also doesn't include much with the lens.  a lens shade is very useful for outdoors photography, and canon is very pricey on an accessory that most include.  canon's one-year warranty is also poor compared to most others.

for a good alternative, look at the tamron / promaster 70-300 ld lens which has closer focusing, includes the shade, and both offer longer warranties.  however, neither are as quiet as the canon lenses.

for an upgrade, look at the canon ef 100-300 usm, which offers a smoother, faster usm, and no filter rotation. good, average telephoto zoom.

everything works well enough, but it's not exactly a quality piece of equipment.  the first thing i noticed was it's "limp" as it's feet were not of equal length.  this made for some unpleasent and noisy rocking, tipping and slamming every time i'd touch the thing (and with all those knobs, you are going to be touching it often).  with a bit of work with a rotary tool i filed down the oposing foot to match the shorter one to stop this.

next, we have the knobs, these are also cheap feeling plastic.  once you get past the look and feel of "premium quality" the knobs are well placed and have pretty good tolerances.

the preamp gain knob seems to give a pretty smooth power increase until around the last 2 "bars." after that it spikes uncontrollably.

the vu meter, honestly never worked reliably. sometimes showing nothing at all while the recording software was showing that i was speaking at -12 db.  sometimes it would show clipping when i was still seeing -8 db with totally normal waveforms.

now for for my biggest issue.  this is supposed to be a "low noise" device.  it introduces a very clear "mains hum" to the system.  leaving literally everything in place just removing this mixer and inserting another mixer in it's place and plugging the same cables into it removes the hum for me, and that's a problem.  a hum may be removable in post, but i should not have to remove anything from my recordings.  the other quality issues can be overlooked for budget cutting reasons, but impacting your recordings is where you should absolutely draw the line.  this is simply not acceptable.

this was my first behringer product, and i use this as a backup, but i don't see myself buying another one of these from them.
summary: cheaply made, wobbles on desk and adds "mains hum" to recordings.  not worth it.

reviewText:
this wire is extremely poor for crimping.  it's probably okay for screw terminals, though, or soldering, but it's very stiff and brittle.

i was looking for a four conductor 22 gauge wire to use in a project that would require many, many red quick disconnect wire terminals as well as those little tiny square housing crimps.  i grabbed this wire because it was less than half the cost of the copper west penn 241 wire i had been considering.  i wasn't even concerned that the logico is only aluminum, as i've used that without too many problems before.  unfortunately, this logico wire turned out to shred half the times i tried to strip the insulation for a crimp.  some of the strands would break and fall away, leaving too few to take a crimp.  i tried many techniques to improve this, yet nearly half of my crimps would suffer mechanical failure.  despite the strands being so fine, the wire also felt unnaturally stiff, even for aluminum wire.  if not handled carefully, it could easily fatigue and break internally.  that's probably not a concern for most, though, but i'm not just running this through walls.

i more recently ponied up for the wp 241 and haven't looked back.  it doesn't have any of the stripping or crimping problems this stuff did.  it's for that reason i feel confident in calling this one star, compared to an easy five for the good stuff.  turns out you get what you pay for.

as my title states, i believe this is worse than garbage.  from what i can find, the hardware seems to work about as it is supposed to. i say about, only because it is a slouch when it comes to pulling in the signal from the router.  the distance requirements are much more stringent than both my laptop, and desktop wireless cards.

 the software on the other hand is blatantly neglected by cisco. not neglected in the sense that the performance is sub par.  neglected to the extent it could impact future buying decisions between brands.  and the performance is sub par.  with two different vista computers (1 32, 1 64 bit) the utility would not even begin installing (stalled at 0% progress).  this is the software downloaded from linksys that reports it is compatible with windows vista.

i've had this piece of junk for quite some time, and revisited it this evening.  the only work around for vista that seems to work for most people, most of the time, is to actually use the software from another vender. i'm pretty sure that you're breaking the eula from the other vender, but it will load. the third party software is written by a monkey, so it consumes ~ 1.5gb of ram while viewing the settings of the utility.

after all of that is done, while using vista, you are guaranteed to have 1-2 second random gaps in your stream.  this is certainly not due to a high quality data stream stressing the router.  there seems to be some services running in vista that draws from the resources that are required for the driver, and when this happens, an audio void presents itself.  how often enough? sometimes several in one minute, sometimes a whole minute could pass.

if somebody offers to give you one of these for free, run. if you already bought one, return it.  the only thing missing from this turd is the steam.

reviewText:
pros:  reasonably good build quality
  decent terminals
  nice appearance
  ease of handling

cons: actual internal volume is only 0.666 cubic feet
  carpet is not actually carpet, it is just felt with no backing.
  inset sides interfere with mounting screws.
  speaker cutout 1/8 inch off center

probably for appearance and ease of handling, the manufacturer chose to inset two of the sides about 5/8 of an inch.  while this does those things, it also decreases the internal volume of the box.  the measured internal dimensions are 11  x 10 7/8 x 9 5/8.  that comes to about 1151.4 cubic inches, or .666 cubic feet.  close is not really good enough in speaker design.  getting the tuning right requires accuracy, and nothing about the presentation of this product on this site reflects a concern with accuracy.

don't try cutting the "carpet" and peeling it off to make a clean sealing surface for your sub.  it is just felt glued directly to the mdf and all you'll do is make a lumpy mess out of it.  you might just want to use some rtv between your speaker gasket and the felt and just hope it seals.

the inset sides also interfere with screw placement.  you can't use tee nuts on the back side if you want your speaker to go in with the logo parallel to the floor.  the inset sides don't leave enough room for anything other than light duty mdf screws for the lateral midline speaker screws- not what you want to hold back a 15 pound sub pushing 350 watts.

all in all, the decision to inset the sides pretty much ruins this box.
summary: not .77 cubic feet, inset sides interfere with speaker mounting, cheap felt covering

reviewText:
though it's not mentioned anywhere the usb, sd, and cassette deck are all in stereo. the fm however is not. the tape deck records in stereo as well (though there is only one built in microphone so that's mono, of course).

the sound can be a bit on the shrill side, but the good news is that it has a tone knob that takes the edge off quite a bit. because of that it's not bad. of course at this price it's not exactly going to be top notch high fidelity, but for what it is it's just fine.

sd and usb slots:
the most basic of functions is the name of the game here. it has buttons for next track, previous track, and play/pause. that's it. of course there's no screen.
it does not scan through a track when you hold down the "next" or "prev" buttons. it does remember the last track plaid and will start back on that track after you turn it off or switch to another function however it starts at the beginning of the track.
it is hcsd (more than 2gb) compatible.

the tuner:
the tuner is a bit better than the other quatum fx, supersonic, etcetera radios of this type and class that i've tried, though not top notch. the fm is quite sensitive and selective (perhaps a touch better than average), mw/am performance is about average, and the sw bands are about what you would expect from something in this price class, if not a bit better.

cassette deck:
it runs at the correct speed and stays there, the head azimuth is spot on, and surprisingly enough the built in microphone is reasonably sensitive yet pics up very little noise from the deck itself. it will record from the sd and usb slots in stereo. the quality of the recordings is about average for an auto level control deck.
the fast forward and rewind buttons do not function as cue and review (you can't hear the tape go backward or forwards).

lights?
*laughs* yes, it has flashing lights. no, they do not change by/with whatever you're playing.

all in all for the price it's fun and it does what it should.

runs on 6 d cells, 9v barrel plug, or ac power (switchable 110/220 volts).

reviewText:
i have a magellan 5045 in my truck and thought i'd throw a separate gps in the wife's car. i saw this was the #1 gps on amazon, and decided to give it a try. i ultimately returned it.

pros: easy to read interface. easy to customize voices and display (to a degree). quicker response time than my magellan.

cons: often gives wrong side of street for addresses. many layers of menu needed to turn volume down or alter route. cradle/mount was cheap and did not keep the cord in place. aftermarket cradles and mounts all use the same crappy ball joint system that has no cable mount.

two hands are required to plug in the usb cable and then mount this gps. this is a great gps if you program it while sitting in a parking lot, pulled over at the side of the road, or have the time to assemble the apparatus and navigate through the multiple layers of menu to input your destination.  it is horrible if you need to pull it from the glove compartment, plug it in, and mount it single-handedly. it is horrible if you need to suddenly switch your destination from one common/saved destination to another common/saved destination.

in essence, i had to return this because it was much more unsafe to operate in the vehicle than my magellan 5045.  i have since purchased another magellan 5045.

reviewText:
i was looking for an inexpensive way to get some of my many record albums and 45's into itunes.  these seemed to fit the bill.  not the cheapest one, but far from the most expensive.

i want to qualify this review with a couple of facts up front.  first, i bought this in 2012; secondly, i only paid $88.70 for it.  at the time, there were similar one that cost $99.00, $119.00 and about $139.00.  were i do get a "do-over", i would have sprung for the $139.00 model and would probably have a gotten a superior product with better sound quality.

first is the sound quality is reproduces from my records.  only fair to average.  it's difficult to adjust the pitch to get the original quality sound.  it either plays the records slightly too fast or slightly too slow, which distorts the sound quality.

secondly, even given that it's an inexpensive model, it seems really cheaply built, even give it's price.  one minor bump, i am sure the plastic construction will crack.

i've imported about three albums so far.  the quality is passable, but barely.  i'd like to see a little better quality without having to break the bank.

addendum update november 2016:  as noted above, i would like to point out to any readers of this review that when i purchased this unit, the price was only 88.00.  the current price is listed at over $200.00, which is ridiculous.  i definately would not pay more than the $89.00 i paid a few years back.  no way would i fork over $200.00 for this substandard product.  for that money, you easliy can get a way better usb turntable than this one.  if i were buying this now, there is no way i would spend over $230.00 for this machine.  it simply is not worth anywhere near that kind of money.

in a nutshell, look for a higher quality product for around $200 or a bit less.  you'll surely get a better quality product at a much better price.
summary: cheap product that does ok, but really is lacking in quality ** note my 2016 addendum at the end of this review

responsive keys

overall, i'm in love with this bluetooth keyboard. i used it with a 3g and 4g ipad. it fit both well, with very little movement in the case. my ipad felt very secure. when the ipad is placed into the typing position, the magnet engages and powers up the keyboard. when you remove it, the keyboard powers down. much easier to use than yet another on/off switch. my devices paired quickly and maintained connection to the keyboard while i was using it. i have tried a few other keyboards and discarded them. the one piece construction along with the firm hold in typing position make this one a keeper. the caveats are that this is a very solid feeling accessory and you pay for that in weight. my ipad felt more than twice as heavy with the folio on. i'd like to slip it on and off for the day depending on what my expected needs will be but putting in the folio is much easier than removing it. i have some issues with hand strength and i ended up asking for assistance in popping it back out. on the other hand, while it was in the folio the ipad was extremely secure, it was an exceptional fit on the 4g and very good on the 2g as well. the external fabric is a nice bright color. it offers some grip to the hand without feeling scratchy or cheap. it's pleasant to hold or view. the interior keyboard is not fabric, but a rubberized material that feels almost like typing on an old stretch armstrong toy. the keys feel solid and respond well. it was just like a standard keyboard. within seconds i wasn't looking at it at all but typing naturally. (i wish it were quieter but keyboard makers seem to have filed typing noise under feature instead of bug.) while this wasn't the perfect accessory for me it is absolutely the best keyboard i've used. great item.

reviewText:
don't buy this if you are going to hold the thing!

after two days of trying to like this tablet, i decided that i've had enough.

there is a real home button at the bottom, which works well. there is also a back button and menu button, which don't work fine.

actually they work too fine. because they are capacitive and not real buttons (like the home button is), just touching the bottom of the tablet almost anywhere triggers one of these buttons. the back button will take you back when you don't want to, and the menu button will sometimes pop up a menu, but more often pops up a search box over the entire screen.

touching the menu button again makes the search box go away, but i've had enough. a huge waste of my time that makes using this tablet very frustrating. every time i use it!

i didn't buy the case for it initially. but i ordered some cases, so maybe holding it by the case will help?

other than that the tablet works ok. it's light and thin. the screen looks great. it's pretty fast and has a built-in gps that works ok. the sound is pretty loud. scrolling on the screen is smooth.

but hitting one or the other capacitive buttons ...once or twice every minute... while holding this thing makes it useless for me.

i have a galaxy tab 7.0 (the original) that just didn't want to run most new programs (they aren't even offered in the play store because the tablet is so old), so i bought this tablet. the original tab has four capacitive buttons along the bottom, but i didn't have the problem with them. you have to touch right on the actual icon.

on the tab 8 you can touch anywhere around the button. it has a bubble sound when you touch one of those "buttons" so you know you just screwed up.

there doesn't seem to be a setting for how sensitive the button is. i don't have a samsung phone which i understand this is a copy of. maybe it's not an issue on a phone because you normally hold it in portrait mode. i always hold a tablet in landscape mode.

update: the three cases i've tried didn't help much. samsung can fix this if they program the buttons to be less sensitive, or require that the button be touched for half a second. but they don't seem to care.

this is the last samsung product i'm going to buy. it is unusable if you have to hold it in your hands in landscape (portrait is essentially impossible because of the tiny edges before the screen starts, you keep touching something on the screen).

if you leave it on a desk or glued to a wall, and never try to pick it up, it's ok.

reviewText:
i bought these speakers a year ago, and i'm continually amazed. these are some great speakers. if you're not familiar with mirage and their omnisat / nanosat series, there's a design feature that sets them apart from most other "surround system in a box" speaker packages: they have a unique radiating system, with a drive mounted upwards towards a reflector. the resulting sound field is more "spread out" than other conventional speakers, and so the sound image becomes more transparent. if you set them up well, and turn on an audio source with decent imaging, you'll be amazed at how hard it is to localize where the speakers are. sound imaging is astoundingly accurate.

then there's the sound quality. some people don't much care for the subwoofer and its set crossover, but i don't mind. just set the crossover point on your amp (the manual says to 120hz), and you're good to go. the sub itself is decently powerful, but not muddled. the speakers themselves produce great highs and decent mids. they can be a little bright sometimes, but that's a common problem with small speakers thanks to a lack of any significant enclosure. if i turn the volume up, they get plenty loud and never distort.

definitely one of the best speaker deals out there...i'd highly recommend them for anyone with an apartment or small livingroom setup that needs unobtrusive speakers and doesn't want to just settle for the run-of-the-mill consumer crap.

reviewText: i've owned mine for over a year & have been impressed with it in several ways. first is the new, lowered price; real digital cameras at such a nice price are quite a development! the applications this camera seems best suited to are: e-mailing photos, webpage posting or limited photo printing (4" x 6" max), as in school papers or nonprofessional grade work reports. the resolution is up to these tasks, but not much more. it has no zoom lens, which limits its usefulness. it does have a good indoor flash, and it has an expandable memory (multimediacards, generally harder to find & a bit higher cost than other memory formats). the camera will download into the pc via usb (forget about painfully slow serial port options), but the only way to fly is to use a separate mmc card reader (a little more $, but no battery use and much better speed). all in all, this is a great camera for younger students and beginners whose main interest is computer-based digital photography.

i bought this grip a year ago after shooting homecoming weekend at my school, central michigan university.

the pain it saved my wrist being able to shoot sports vertically without having to hang my hand over the top of my camera was a huge relief.

recently though, after a year of solid use, i've been having problems with it. there will be days that my camera will suddenly say my batteries are dry - after charging them the day before. i've checked, and my grip is not part of the series that was recalled for a similar problem.

i have to actually removed the grip, and the batteries, and restart the camera to correct the problem. --this is a big problem in the middle of a sports match--

however, the grip is a great addition to the 20d/30d models. it's not the same feel as using a 1d, but it's as close are you're going to get. and for $150, you can't go wrong with the vertical shooting and doubled battery life. it also simply evens out the weight of the camera, especially with the heavier l-glass lenses on your camera.

reviewText:
----pros:
* color is outstanding... it's like the festival of colors in india no matter what you're looking at. your eyes will smile. i am not a designer, i simply wanted the color for viewing brilliant photos, games, and especially movies (we use my pc as our media center). this monitor delivers fully. once you see 10-bit color in something like a pixar film (wall-e), every other display you see, including 8-bit ips, plasma screens, and even movie theater projectors will look dull and washed out. heck, even most of the real world isn't as exciting to look at as this screen. i don't notice any banding in the stuff i spend time on. my girlfriend also appreciates the color in films and is always jealous when we're looking at the same thing on my screen vs her tn panel.
* it has emulation of more limited color spaces for times you don't want the saturation.
* 2560x1440 at 27" is significantly crisper than 1920x1200 at 24" (i've had two quality screens of different makes at that resolution). x1080 has always looked blurry to me over 22", but it's especially noticeable after adjusting to this. even when you lean in really close, the sharpness stands out. i've also had the 30" 1600p (u3014) version of this; they're about comparable in sharpness, maybe a slight edge to the 27" but it's such a close call if you're looking for a tie-breaker between the two 10-bits...
* easy to navigate menu, mostly good options. some options limit other settings for no apparent reason.
* smooth and easy ergonomic adjustments.
* deeper blacks than many ips screens. no noticeable glow. haven't spotted dead pixels. ag coating doesn't make things look grainy, though glare with a window right behind me can get bad during the sunniest part of the day.
* i sit at this screen and/or a 24" ultrasharp most of the day and my eyes don't get dry or unusually tired. there's no known pwm flicker with this screen, and its brightness goes down very far to keep things easy on your eyes. i previously would get very tired eyes looking at a hp zr24w (ccfl backlight, 1200p) on lowest brightness in a well-lit room and have noticed the improvement with this screen.

----cons:
* like its big brother u3014, this panel has terrible overshoot. even scrolling up and down webpages, the you can see a double/shadow of everything on screen including text. it's harder to see in video but in general motion looks blurry. -1 star
* why are there no physical buttons? the touch buttons suck. they are overly sensitive and difficult to use. often they register multiple presses when i'm slightly grazing the button, other times they won't register anything at all. a strong breeze (like air from the ac ceiling vent) or nearby electronics like phones or a moving mouse will set off the touch illumination -- not exaggerating. i use other dell ultrasharp screens which have the physical buttons and they are infinitely easier and more reliable. touch buttons are not a high-end "feature," they are a needless annoyance. they will strongly discourage me from future dell monitor purchases. they're a bigger deal than you think, unless you never change any settings including brightness and you are not easily distracted by flashing lights in the bottom right of your vision. -1 star
* displayport no longer works. the port no longer detects a signal. using dvi instead. i'd take a star but the thing has so many ports it's hard to fault it for one failing...
* build quality is ok (all plastic except metal spine and plate under the plastic of the stand). pretty bland otherwise, no samsung 9 series here. smudges/fingerprints easily. i modified the inside of my stand with a rotary cutter so it rotates 360* (the base is attached to my desk, otherwise would tip over when swung past about 150*), but otherwise only rotates about 45* each way.
* i have not tried dedicated usb 3.0 devices to test other reviewers' claims. however, the sd card reader isn't working on the one card i have available to test.
* overall, too many issues for a monitor priced at $800-1000. i would expect a monitor with the bugs and quirks of this screen to be significantly cheaper and would not buy again. -1 star. as more competition in the 1440p+ resolution opens up, these screens will be a hard sell. that said, i am grateful to have one and enjoy it every day, just wouldn't choose this one over others if able to go back.

* i sit at this screen and/or a 24" ultrasharp most of the day and my eyes don't get dry or unusually tired. there's no known pwm flicker with this screen, and its brightness goes down very far to keep things easy on your eyes. i previously would get very tired eyes looking at a hp zr24w (ccfl backlight, 1200p) on lowest brightness in a well-lit room and have noticed the improvement with this screen.

----cons:
* like its big brother u3014, this panel has terrible overshoot. even scrolling up and down webpages, the you can see a double/shadow of everything on screen including text. it's harder to see in video but in general motion looks blurry. -1 star
* why are there no physical buttons? the touch buttons suck. they are overly sensitive and difficult to use. often they register multiple presses when i'm slightly grazing the button, other times they won't register anything at all. a strong breeze (like air from the ac ceiling vent) or nearby electronics like phones or a moving mouse will set off the touch illumination -- not exaggerating. i use other dell ultrasharp screens which have the physical buttons and they are infinitely easier and more reliable. touch buttons are not a high-end "feature," they are a needless annoyance. they will strongly discourage me from future dell monitor purchases. they're a bigger deal than you think, unless you never change any settings including brightness and you are not easily distracted by flashing lights in the bottom right of your vision. -1 star
* displayport no longer works. the port no longer detects a signal. using dvi instead. i'd take a star but the thing has so many ports it's hard to fault it for one failing...
* build quality is ok (all plastic except metal spine and plate under the plastic of the stand). pretty bland otherwise, no samsung 9 series here. smudges/fingerprints easily. i modified the inside of my stand with a rotary cutter so it rotates 360* (the base is attached to my desk, otherwise would tip over when swung past about 150*), but otherwise only rotates about 45* each way.
* i have not tried dedicated usb 3.0 devices to test other reviewers' claims. however, the sd card reader isn't working on the one card i have available to test.
