reviewText:
i'm a recent fan of pentax cameras, having within the last year purchased my first two from the brand (a q and the much maligned but excellent k-01).  i like the fact that pentax is a bit quirky, with their own style and way of building cameras.  you need look no further than the fact pentax included brass top and bottom plates for this modern digital camera, harkening back to the late, great film cameras of old.  being a not-so-youngster myself, i have some of those film cameras, and a little brass showing beneath paint reminds me of all the nice memories i have made while using the camera.  i believe that's exactly what pentax was after here, and i really like the sentiment, especially in today's throw-away newer-is-better society.

the question is, though: would you keep this camera long enough to wear through the paint, exposing that lovely brass?  or was this just a chic move by the marketing team of pentax?

the answer isn't simple, unfortunately.  certainly, the image quality of the camera is "good enough" for the vast majority of common photographic pursuits.  we are living in good times, and "digital" has (imo) finally caught up with where the average point-and-shoot film camera left us after many decades of innovation.  i'd be willing to say that if you are a typical photographer who never prints larger than 11x14 or so, wants to grow your photographic skills but doesn't have a specific pursuit that this camera won't handle well (you will know this already), and doesn't have any specific notion that a camera should operate in a particular manner, this could very well be your "everything" camera for enough years that you will wear the paint off the brass.

however, as a photography enthusiast with many years of film (and digital) under my belt, i was left a bit confused by the mx-1 as the body made promises i didn't feel the camera kept.  the retro styling suggests that this camera will handle and flow like an old film camera; in my admittedly short exposure to the mx-1 i didn't find this to be the case.  although the interface and user experience was good, it felt decidedly "modern" to me, which was jarring in the face of the very retro styling.  looking at the camera, i was expecting something like a fuji x10, x100, or xpro 1, but in operation this was more like an olympus xz-1 or xz-2 than a fuji x10.  for me, unlike the aforementioned fuji's, it didn't "flow" as well.  additionally, the effort put into the styling and brass plates made me think this was an enthusiast's special, but i was a little perplexed as there are fewer options for customization than the q and k01.  this left the camera feeling a bit less like the enthusiast camera it seems to be positioned as.  why "dumb it down" comapred to the other pentax cameras?  it was a but puzzling, and like the juxtaposition of old and modern, during the time i had the camera i was perpexed as to who exactly this camera was marketed to.

that said, when i finally viewed the images on screen i found the photo quality very good.  using lightroom 4.4 to convert the raw files, i was very impressed with the resolution at base iso, displaying a crisp, colorful image with excellent contrast, even in harsh lighting.  dynamic range was also quite good, particularly when pulled and pushed a bit from raw.  with respect to image quality, it is a notable step above older high-end compacts i have had experience with such as the canon g9, ricoh grd-iv, as well as pentax's own q.  at high iso (>=1600), it was notably better than the q, the grd-iv, and also the brand-new and otherwise excellent fuji x20.  it matches or bests the olympus xz-1 in good light, and while that camera falls apart above iso400, the mx-1 holds up quite well.  i don't have my sony rx100 any more to compare, but i was fine using the mx-1 around iso1600 as the grain had a nice fine, tight pattern to it, and detail was retained quite well. with the fast lens, a good image stabilization system, and iso1600, i'd suggest you can successfully use this camera in any light you care to photograph in.

the mx-1 also has some nice features: the tilting screen is handy at times, and the display itself is very smooth with excellent color, brightness, and tonal gradations (several orders of magnitude better than the q!).  the exposure compensation wheel, popular on throwback cameras right now, is quite helpful and easy to access.  the battery life also seemed quite good, although i didn't have it long enough to fully judge battery capacity, i think it's enough for a nice day of shooting as you travel, etc.  i also liked the lens; i believe it is shared with the olympus xz-1 and xz-2, and although we all would like bespoke lenses on our cameras (makes you feel "special" somehow!), as far as compact camera lenses go, this one is worth sharing between manufacturers.  you can somewhat play with depth of field, and bokeh is smoother than expected, even besting the x20 in certain circumstances.  it's a bit soft in the corners at wide angle and wide open, but stop down a little for landscapes and you won't notice.  although it doesn't necessarily have the "character" of some vintage and modern lenses, that will actually be a plus in the minds of many.

so that's where we're left, then: a compact that by "looks" promises retro charm, character, and charisma, yet manages to be fully modern in implementation and feel.  will you wear that paint off to expose the pretty brass underneath?  that depends upon whether you view this mashup of "old" and "new" as positive, or negative.  if you want "new" with a little retro charm, then by all means, this is as good of a camera as many highly-touted models on the market.  the price is also quite aggressive, competing with models costing quite a bit more.  however, if you desire a retro approach in form and function, with a more old-school photographer-centric (vs technology-centric) flow, and perhaps a bit more "charm and character" in your images, then i would suggest taking a pass on the mx-1.
summary: you gotta love pentax: brass on a modern camera?!?

something occurred when i put this unit into service.  it seemed to alter the frequency on the overhead door opener unit.
my door opener was an older unit so the manufacturer no longer made the exact replacement keypad for it.  this keypad was the one sent to work with my older model opener.  after installing this keypad my door began opening when my neighbor (some 200 feet from my house) would drive into her garage.  her opener was an entirely different brand that has been in her garage for over 20 years with no changes made to it recently.. my hand held opener would not work on her door.  it was a bit unsettling as my door opened while we were away on a trip.  fortunately another neighbor noticed & put the door down for me.  a family member responded to my panic call for assistance & unplugged the opener & removed the battery from the keypad.  i did not put the battery back into the keypad but did plug the opener back in.  i experienced the ghost openings several more times & called a service person to check the door.  he removed the inside wall opener thinking that a wire may have shorted in it to cause the issue.  again ~ ghost openings so i decided to resort to replacing the over 20 year old opener for security reasons.  certainly a big mystery.
so in conclusion ~ i would reconsider purchasing a new keypad opener for an old opener if the exact replacement keypad is not available.

my door opener was an older unit so the manufacturer no longer made the exact replacement keypad for it.  this keypad was the one sent to work with my older model opener.  after installing this keypad my door began opening when my neighbor (some 200 feet from my house) would drive into her garage.  her opener was an entirely different brand that has been in her garage for over 20 years with no changes made to it recently.. my hand held opener would not work on her door.  it was a bit unsettling as my door opened while we were away on a trip.  fortunately another neighbor noticed & put the door down for me.  a family member responded to my panic call for assistance & unplugged the opener & removed the battery from the keypad.  i did not put the battery back into the keypad but did plug the opener back in.  i experienced the ghost openings several more times & called a service person to check the door.  he removed the inside wall opener thinking that a wire may have shorted in it to cause the issue.  again ~ ghost openings so i decided to resort to replacing the over 20 year old opener for security reasons.  certainly a big mystery.
so in conclusion ~ i would reconsider purchasing a new keypad opener for an old opener if the exact replacement keypad is not available. caused a mystery.

reviewText:
i recently purchased two of these yongnuo 300 led video lights to use on indoor interviews for budget conscious company videos.

pros:
- they come on, work nicely, and produce quite a bit of light (i can't say how much, but plenty for my purposes.)
- built-in barn doors are a great addition
- easy to adjust power levels (with "coarse" and "fine" adjustment options, but i never use the "fine" option)
- color gels (4) are a nice value added bonus
- very light weight, even with the battery (so you can use inexpensive light stands)
- uses readily available sony np-f550 (or similar) style batteries
- battery level indicator is really helpful

cons:
- the lights don't come with a battery or power adapter, so you need to buy batteries (generic sony np-f550 style)
- would be nice to have full power adjustment, it only goes from 100% output down to about 40% output (by my visual estimation)

neutral:
- the lights come with a little 6" handle, a plastic cold shoe angle attachment, 4 color gels, and a nice cloth bag. the bag is too small for all the equipment, and barely even fits the light, so it's not much good - but i will find another use for it.
- be very careful with the plastic angle attachment because that's the only way to "mount" the lights. if it breaks, we're going to have fun coming up with a new way to mount the lights to stands - lol.
- not surprisingly, the light is fairly harsh and specular when bare, and even with the color diffuser. simply aim it through a cheap white photo umbrella to diffuse the light (or into a silver umbrella.)
- the lights come with a remote to control power output and (apparently) it can even function as a remote shutter release for certain cameras - i haven't tried this out yet (even for power output) but it would be cool to have a compatible camera

as for battery usage, it's hard to say how long batteries last because you have to buy your own (generic) batteries and total output is all over the board with those. i would estimate about 30-45 minutes of full power output with the generic np-f550's i purchased. i recommend you purchase several np-f550 batteries, or the higher capacity 770 versions.

overall i'm very pleased with the lights and highly recommend them for anyone shooting simple "interview style" videos on a budget.
summary: excellent value - plenty of light output

reviewText:
i rated this "its okay" because the price is great for the power this is capable of but you will be wanting for more soon.

i bought this telescope for my young son who has a lot of interest in the solar system and planets/stars near us.  the supplied "high power" 4mm lens was pretty much garbage.  i bought the collimation eyepiece tool for it as well to make sure all the optics were aligned but nothing i did would let me see even remotely clearly with that lens.  celestron is going to send me another lens to see if that helps.

you will learn quickly that this is an entry level rig.  you will want better and more varied lenses and color filters right away for better stargazing which can cost big $$$ when the time comes.  you will also find the mount shaky.  i am going to go over every bolt/hole there is and make sure they are as tight as they can possibly be with no play to provide greater stabilization.

the finder scope is not great but it has gotten me close enough that even with the 4mm lens i can find the "blob" of light in that lens pretty quickly.  i have seen a lot of bad reviews on here about said scope but i could get by with it.

if a more costly setup with good lenses of greater variety is an alternative for you i would suggest you take it if you remotely think you will stay interested in stargazing.  i just dumped another $300 on this for a fair to good imager and lens/filter set.  time will tell.  thank goodness it all came from amazon on my prime account as i can return it all....
summary: gets you in to the hobby but it doesnt take long to realize about triple the price would have yielded much more satisfaction

reviewText:
i was a happy owner of dcrhc30 for first 10 months, and felt that we made a wise purchase.

until recently, we found out that the rec/standby button sometimes did not respond, and it happened more and more frequently. when it happens, i have difficult time to make it record, or i had to power it off to stop recording. when i contact sony customer serivce, i found the warranttee for labor is only 90 days, though part is 1 year (fyi: labor is way more expensive than part!).

cs rep gives me an estimate of flat labor rate $269, plus shipping and handling to/from the repair center in ct. that's 60% of the purchase price of the hc30!

we had already spent extra $100+ for sony accessaries (like batteries, memory cards, etc), which normally are not compatible with other brands of camcorders/cameras by design (a typical sony strategy following the proven-unsuccessful footsteps of apple computers decade ago). i can pretty much say good-bye to these accessaries as well...

when purchasing sony, be aware of its warranttee policy and think twice. there is a reason that the company has been losing ground to its competitor for years, and not likely can the newly-appointed u.s. ceo overturn the trend!

we will definitely avoid sony products in the future.
summary: poor warranttee policy (90-day labor) + expensive repair

what we have here is quite simply a compact g5.  forget the swivel lcd screen - for me not at all useful, the only thing missing of any consequence from the g5 in my opinion is the flash shoe, otherwise you basically have a g5 in a much smaller more functional package.

the pictures are quite simply fantastic!  only minimal purple fringing and only noticeable to the most discerning (read nit-picking).

the camera still suffers from the digital point and shoot shutter lag which for the most part plagues all point and shoots.  it is certainly no worse than the g5.

one clear advantage over the previous s50 is its smaller size.  the camera still has the sliding lens cover which some object to but i find no problem whatsoever.

the only dilemma facing the prospective buyer is whether to purchase this camera or the significantly smaller s500.  the s60 being a more capable complete camera than the s60.  my advice:  if this is your only digital camera, buy the s60.  if you have a digital slr then buy the s500 for true portability.  the good news is that whatever decision you make you should be very pleased because both are great cameras.

if you haven't taken the digital plunge, then take it from one who resisted much too long.  go out and buy a digital camera today!!  it will reawaken you interest in photography.  imo, digital photography is the current killer app for pc's right behind the internet.  good luck.

reviewText:
i really like the sound signature of these headphones, it's similar to their big brother the triple drivers (my favorite earbuds). their sound isn't identical, but the mix appears to be the same, and it's a perfect wireless option for my gym use. the audio quality is above anything else near this price point in my opinion. they are also well built and stylish. the ibfree would be my favorite bluetooth earbuds (and i have a drawer full of them), but unfortunately they have two significant problems:

1. they come with 3 sets of tips and none fits my ears perfectly. the triple drivers come with 9. this is probably an easily resolved issue with aftermarket tips so not that big of a deal, but it would be nice if they came with everything i need. i didn't take any stars off for this.

2. the bigger problem is connectivity issues. they pair quickly and easily but suffer from what appears to be signal strength issues on my iphone 7 plus. they frequently stutter or cut out music even with the phone only 1-2 feet away with no obstructions (such as sitting on the desk in front of me while i type this). this makes the headphones more or less unusable, which is a shame because i really like them when they work. this isn't an issue with my other bluetooth headphones, including bottom-of-the-barrel $10 sets.
summary: connectivity issues ruin an otherwise great product

2. the bigger problem is connectivity issues. they pair quickly and easily but suffer from what appears to be signal strength issues on my iphone 7 plus. they frequently stutter or cut out music even with the phone only 1-2 feet away with no obstructions (such as sitting on the desk in front of me while i type this). this makes the headphones more or less unusable, which is a shame because i really like them when they work. this isn't an issue with my other bluetooth headphones, including bottom-of-the-barrel $10 sets. connectivity issues ruin an otherwise great product

i really wanted to like this lens.  i read so many positive reviews and so many reports showing excellent performance.  specifically, i was wanting the sharpest lens with the most detail.  i don't expect to be upgrading to a full-frame soon, so the range fit my needs better than any of the current l offerings.  i purchased the ef-s 17-55 to replace a sigma 17-70 lens with which i wasn't entirely happy.  even though a lot of people complained about build quality, i wasn't that concerned with that aspect; but while i found the lens to be solid, the zoom ring did not turn smoothly at all.  the biggest problem, though, was that the lens was softer at any aperture and focal length than my ef-s 10-22, my sigma 17-70 or even my old 18-55 kit lens.  i don't know whether i received a dud copy or whether it became messed up in shipping.  in either case, i just didn't think it was worth $1000 for a lens that was either that poor from the factory or so fragile that the overnight trip completely threw it out of alignment.

the two stars is for the lens.  i would like to have given amazon 0 stars for their packaging.  the box containing the lens had a single (1), small inflatable pillow leaving 3/4 of the box empty for the lens to slide around in.  i paid $1000 for a lens and $20 for overnight shipping, surely they could have afforded to use a couple more air pillows.  i'm sticking with adorama from now on.

i am only now calm enough to write a review after installing this hours earlier.  in the end, it all works and fits in place, but i cannot in good conscience not warn folks of the horrible instructions on this.  i mean, near worthless.

you *will* be cutting parts of this off. and the parts are not made so they can snap off, you have to cut them using metal or garden shears or perhaps a dremel w/ a cutting attachment.  you will throw away enough of this kit that you'll wonder multiple times if you've forgotten something important.  you'll remove the radio again several times to get the fit "right".  you'll wonder how somebody can not only write bad english, but also screw up the drawings as if those required translations too.

in the end, just take the thing and hold it up to your original mounts to note which pieces will match up to the original radio mounts.  then cut off everything else.  out 8 tabs on the front faceplate i removed all 8 (idiotic...why?).  out of ~5 tabs on each side i removed all but 2 on each side.  i removed the radio more times than i could count as i realized it would "fit" but now i couldn't reach the screws or i didn't get the front faceplate on first or now with all the pulling i've disconnected something...

it costs someone almost nothing to do a video showing how to install this w/ some general guidelines and put it on youtube.  i'd do it but i'd rather stab myself in the eye with the many pieces of plastic now littering the floor of my car than do a favor for this manufacturer.

in the end, once mounted, it looks ok.  just have lots of patience and nobody around to hear you cursing at whatever idiots wrote the install guide.

reviewText:
the device is difficult to set up, and not really useful.

the idea of the verbatim mediashare wireless mini is great: load a micro sd card with movies and music, and have it available to the entire family on mobile devices, whether at home or in a flight. however the execution was quite short from the idea.

setting up is difficult. i downloaded the verbatim mediashare mini app to my google nexus 6 phone, loaded a microsd card with music and video, and turned on the new device. the app could not find the mediashare wireless mini initially because even though it asked for permission to change my wi-fi setting, it did not do that. the instruction tells me to manually connect to a hot spot created by the mediashare mini, but that was buried in the small prints. i did that and the phone connected, but complained immediately that it had no internet connection, and the app still could not find the device. this was because when the phone detected no internet from the wi-fi, it continued to use lte from the cell service. i had to put the phone into airplane mode, turn wi-fi back on, and then the app finally connected to the mediashare device.

to make it usable at home, i had to configure the mediashare to have wi-fi access to my home router. the manual calls this "bridge" mode which i hope it really is, but it is actually a "router" mode - my home network becomes the "outside" or "wan", and the mediashare hot spot becomes the "inside" or "lan". the configuration timed out many times, but i eventually managed to get it to work. while this got internet access back for my phone while connected to the mediashare device, it separated my phone from my home network so it lost access to other devices on the network such as printers and nas.

the app has a music player, but only supports mp3. i tried higher quality flac and apple m4a files and none of those worked. the interface is really poor. no way to order the songs by album or artist.

there is no video player built into the app. instead the native video player of the phone is used, and in my case it was the "google photo" app that came with the nexus phone. i dug a little bit deeper and found that the video was provided via a "http" url. there was no adaptive streaming or any other streaming techniques, just a plain old http session. although the video played, it was difficult to use the progress bar to jump to a certain location - any movement of the playback marker required long buffering time. i blame it to the http protocol used.

a dlna server appeared on my network from the mediashare device, but there was no video or music served from the server at all. this was strange because if the contents could be served over dlna rather than http, it would be much easier to use.

after all these testing, i decided to toss the device - too much trouble to set up, and not really usable after setting it up. two star instead of one because it at least actually worked.

reviewText: i had a tamrac pro 8 but i quickly outgrew it and wanted to upgrade.  i generally carry two dslrs, an assortment of lenses and filters, a flash unit, and a host of cleaning supplies and various other gadgets.  based upon other reviews, i felt that carrying anything larger than the pro 12 would increase the risk of bag checking requirements with the airlines, so i chose this bag.  it's expensive for a bag, but if you've ever owned a tamrac photo bag, you can easily see the quality, strength and durability for which you are paying.  there are plenty of pockets and compartments in this bag to store most everything for a professional photographer (which i am not).  imo, if you need a larger photographer's bag than this, you will likely be too weighted down, are probably carrying too much gear, and likely need to practice more discretion in what you carry.  anyway, the one drawback is that the bag does not include a rain cover.  it's not enough to knock it down a star but i would expect that to be included at this price.  however, you may do as i do and carry a trash bag or two in one of the many pockets to protect the bag and your gear from a sudden downpour. all in all, i am very pleased with this bag and highly recommend.

i have used the g3 for about 1.5yr now and really don't see a size advantage over a full sized dslr camera.
can't possible put it in any normal pocket, and usually carry a bag to drag this and related equipment around.
on the neck it fits better under a jacket and is lighter, but that is it.
the kit lense is ok, but could benefit from a bit more zoom.
in low light photos are ok, but expect trouble focusing.
videos and sound are good.
outdoors is it's forte, but that is true with every digital camera.
battery life is great if you don't use the lcd monitor, but the view finder leaves something to be desired.
i bought a lumix lx7 at the same time, and frankly find this camera much more flexable in use and better for indoor photography.
i am an amateur photo nut who has owned many cameras over the years. i don't aspire to greatness. i just want great photos of personal interest. i want the camera to work, not me.
full sized dslrs are intrusive but my question is this; if you want super photos why stop here? buy a 24mp machine and face the music.
i gave it 4 stars for the build quality,features and price.

reviewText: i love my 2 megapixel canon elph. small, sharp and reliable - during its time, it was all i could ask for.  i even sold a couple of its pictures to magazines, so what's not to love?  while i have not discarded my elph, i recently moved up to the g5 because it's better in every way. with a fast 4x optical zoom (all the way out to a 35mm-camera-equivalent of 140mm) and 5 megapixel chip, it could easily become my new favorite camera. the manual is thick but it uses a lot of illustrations and the text is surprisingly clear and simple so the reader should not be intimidated. not being one to read manuals, i was able to take the g5 out of the box and immediately shoot pictures without cracking the book (the battery came out of the box with a decent charge too - how cool is that?) that's how simple and intuitive the camera is. i have already made a few 8x10 prints on my canon color printer and they are sharp, show excellent contrast and have good color balance too. like most auto-focus digital cameras there is a brief shutter lag. it's not too bad but the shutter release is certainly not as quick as one of my 35mm leicas. speaking of leica, the shape and size of the g5 is very close to that of the classic leica m series cameras. and the clever design of the battery case allows it to serve as a grip - i found it comfortable and secure. (note: a similar grip is a [$$$]option on a 35mm rangefinder leica!) i don't like the fact that you can't screw a uv, skylight or other kind of filter on the front of the lens. i like to have a good quality filter on the front of my lenses for protection - but that's me. for the average camera user, there are 2 auto exposure settings that should cover the vast majority of shooting situations. (i used "p" and got an "included in the box" 32mb compact flash card full of great exposures.) for the advanced photographer, the g5 comes with just about every manual control you could need or want - similar to those on their excellent eos 1v pro camera. one cool feature is the ability to capture a shot in both raw and jpeg at the same time. this feature will give you a "pure" file with no data loss due to compression and will allow you to make the largest, sharpest print possible. (the manual says that the raw file is compressed, but there is no data loss - must be a new form of japanese magic!) bottom line, the raw format will give you the biggest file with the most information. i suspect that a raw file will allow the careful user (i.e., one who is fussy about focus, exposure and camera shake) to make an 11x14 inch print that is as good as any 35mm camera (maybe better!)  when compared against the many excellent digital cameras out there, the canon is a stand out. its size, resolution, simplicity, and canon's excellent reputation for reliability made it and easy choice for me.
summary: the sweet spot for digital point and shoots

i really wanted to like the samsung galaxy note 8.0. there is such a great feel to the touchscreen and the way it allows you to move back and forth within the applications. however, as much as i wanted to like this product and learn how to work it i continue to have difficulty. i purchased it approximately two weeks ago and have worked with it for short periods everyday. the purchase was made so that i could keep it at the office and watch my favorite show on amazon prime during lunch break. (i can do this on my ipad) as well as take notes during meetings.

i quickly found watching my programs on amazon prime wasn't an option as you need adobe acrobat in order to watch tv, movies or video particularly from amazon prime (almost unlimited tv, movies with my $80/year membership). unfortunately, this system isn't compatible with adobe. so, i tried searching the internet for a fix and found a suggestion to download "mx player"  which would supposedly give me the ability to play any video. oops, didn't work....still can't play tv or movies unless i purchase them from google play. okay, so nix that. how about i concentrate on the note taking feature with the app s note. i figure i can still use the pad to take notes during our companies endless meetings.

well, the s note application would be wonderful to take notes in if i could just figure out how to work its many features. the basics of writing on the pad are obvious. but, getting too much further than writing and flipping to a new page starts to get a little more complicated. so that's when i started looking, in earnest, for a user manual since my search through the internet wasn't yielding much help. voila, i googled and found the user manual on-line by searching through samsung's website. (it was hidden pretty deep). once i found the on-line manual, i also realized there's a user manual on the pad itself. however, since theres no "search" option on the samsung galaxy note i didn't actually "find" the user manual - i just happened up on it. okay, so i started browsing through the user manual and found the following helps for s note: select a note template, compose notes, insert multimedia files, using productivity tools, browsing notes, viewing notes. great - but nothing on how to save a note, change the name of a note, save to a particular day, event, etc. so that if i need to find my notes from a particular meeting i'm still not sure how to do this. i tried to change the name of a note and couldn't do it. neither the on-line user manual nor the samsung user manual helped me with this very necessary feature. while that's frustrating enough,  i'm sure there are even more features i will need help on that hasn't even occurred to me yet - and i don't have time to muddle through and find out how to use the details of this system by trial and error.

there are many neat features on this pad. if you have time to play around and figure it out then go for it. if you have $400.00 to spend though, i would suggest an ipad or kindle fire. either will give you the features you find on this system plus more. as i said, i wanted to like the samsung galaxy 8.0, but am sorry to say i'm packing it up and shipping it back.
summary: vague, incomprehensible and a sore disappointment

reviewText:
i purchased these binoculars for night sky viewing.  i had a pair of 10x50 bushnell binoculars and i was impressed with what i was able to see through those so i bought these for even more in depth viewing and they have not let me down.  they are ideal as supplements to a telescope or if you don't have a telescope, these are great for your first introduction to optics that will open up the night sky to you.  they are much easier to use than a telescope and you can see all kinds of neat things.  i viewed such things as the orion nebula, the andromeda galaxy, the pleiades, and double stars such as mizar and alcor in ursa major with relative ease and they looked stunning.  focus these binoculars in on the milky way and you will see tons of stars you wouldn't be able to see otherwise.  i was even able to look at saturn and with some steadying of the binoculars against my chest, could slightly make out the definition of the rings.  these binoculars also do a magnificent job of viewing the moon.
i had read some reviews that they are really heavy and bulky, but i found that they were surprisingly light and easy to steady free handed.  they are quite large, which means that they will take up more space than a normal binocular, but this is to be expected.  mine did come with a carrying case and a tripod adapter (which i haven't used yet, so i cannot comment on its quality).
overall, for the price, you can't go wrong.  i've used these binoculars in the daytime and they are great--crystal clear optics.  they also seem very durable and with some care, will probably last you many many years.  if you are new to stargazing and are considering a good pair of binoculars that will show you all kinds of wonderous things, look no further than the celestron skymasters--you will not be disappointed.

reviewText:
i live in a rural area that has a co-op as our electricity provider.  basically, power in our area is quite unreliable.  we get frequent dips in our power which are like blackouts that last only a few seconds.

i purchased this particular ups for my entertainment center.  this consists of a vizio 47" lcd hdtv, a pioneer receiver which powers my 5.2 surround sound audio setup, a pc with a 430 watt power supply (basically a home theater pc), an hd homerun prime cable receiver (also purchased from amazon), a tp link 5-port gigbit ethernet switch (for internet access to various devices), and lastly my xbox one (also purchased from amazon).

i calculated that i needed 500 watts, at peak usage, to keep all of my devices powered.  it didn't need to power them for more than a few minutes; just long enough to keep everything from resetting during a power dip.  this ups has fit that role perfectly!  it has a usb interface which allows the pc to configure and monitor the ups.  it continually monitors my power usage (about 400 watts continuous with the xbox powered off, and 450 - 500 watts continuous with the xbox on and in use).  at 400 watts, the ups widget on the pc tells me that i've got about 7 minutes of backup power.  at peak usage of 500 watts, that drops down to about 5 minutes.

since i purchased this, i've had nearly half a dozen power dip events.  the first time happened when i was playing an online game on my xbox.  i heard a click, and then a beeping from the unit, but my game continued and i wouldn't have even noticed if it weren't for the audio notifications (i should mention i have a bit smaller of a cyberpower ups for my internet cable modem, firewall, wifi router, and 24-port gigabit switch in my network closet--the cable signal from comcast appears to be unaffected by power outages).  the widget showed a 4 second power outage during that event.  every subsequent power dip has been exactly the same--except for the audio notification, we didn't even notice the power had dropped.

this unit has done exactly what i wanted it to, and has performed to my complete satisfaction.  i will definitely by cyberpower products again for any future ups needs.
summary: excellent ups backup for my home theater setup!

reviewText:
let me say first that i absolutely love the tivoli model two radio.  it is one of the best purchases i have ever made.  the selectivity of the tuner is phenomenal and the sound from the speakers is wonderful for listening.

the optional subwoofer, on the other hand, is such a mess that it nearly seems like a work of sabotage.

another reviewer remarked that the subwoofer extends unnecessarily upward into the mid-range frequencies - this is absolutely true, a fact which completely annihilates mid and upper range tone and renders music totally unlistenable.  it's like trying to have a conversation with someone who keeps interrupting you, or to use a culinary image putting ketchup in your coffee.  spoils everything.  the tone of the bass from this subwoofer is so bossy and undefined that i actually became angry while listening to it, and i'm not an angry guy.  i tried adjusting the volume level of the output, and i even put the subwoofer in several different positions - on the floor, on a shelf, under a chair, even next to the main component - to no avail.  like a mosquito buzzing in your ear that terrible, obtrusive tone just wouldn't go away.

thank goodness the tivoli model two radio has sufficient bass on its own through the stereophonic speakers to reproduce naturalistic low tones for the type of music i listen to - mostly jazz.

i really can't understand how tivoli thought this product was a good idea.  it's a sonic catastrophe.

reviewText:
this is the third bluetooth portable speaker system i've owned. by all accounts it is the coolest one yet. this system is a glimpse at the future where, hopefully, power will be free for larger things like cars as long as the sun is shining. first off it's much smaller then i thought it was going to be. this is good, and once you hear the sound you will not mind. for a system you can chuck in your backpack or leave in your cars windshield small is definitely better. bluetooth hook up was extremely simple. hold the button down for 3 seconds. select the unit with your phone/comp and that's it. major bonus for this unit is that it'll not only charge itself but it will charge most usb devices. my iphone 5 was sucking up sunlight by simply connecting the usb cable to the back and hitting a button. 2 rugged, like the name says, plastic loops on the unit will allow for attachment to a backpack so it can face the sun and charge while hiking.

so far i can only think of a few minor issues. * no radio: a old school radio in this would have been great. * scratch prone: the solar pannel had a clear plastic film over it for protection. i pealed it off using the small tab. once off the urge to touch the solar pannel was accompanied by shock as my fingers caused tiny scratch marks. although not a defect this is going to make the otherwise rugged unit look pretty delicate very fast.

aside from those 2 minor points this unit is great. the ability to charge external usb devices gives it a double whammy double plus good appeal. this is gonna be with me everywhere this spring and summer.

reviewText:
i had two sr2016 switches installed--one at our business and one at home.  both died in exactly the same way, the first in about six months and the second in about 12 months.  unfortunately, they don't fail suddenly and completely.  rather, they die slowly and intermittently.  the symptom is that random and seemingly inexplicable errors occur on the network, together with what appear to be dhcp failures between the switch and the router.  attached devices will intermittently appear to have network service, but with random failures.  frequently, the attached devices "lock up" and need to be rebooted to clear the problem.  the symptoms gradually worsen until failure is complete.  it took me a long time to figure out that the switch was the problem, since in a complex network it's hard to troubleshoot this kind of failure.

stay away from this product--there is something systematically wrong with either the design or the construction.  this is unfortunate, because it works very well until the trouble starts.
summary: dies slowly and creates huge problems as it dies

reviewText:
the official leather cover looks nice, but being 1/3 the price of the kindle (2015 paperwhite) itself was hard to justify.

after an exhaustive research of various kindle paperwhite cases, i'm extremely happy with this moko case with "map h" design.

my cover is centered differently than shown on the product picture; mine has full australia in the upper left quarter and the ship in the lower center of the front cover, which i actually prefer (check my review pictures).

pros:
+ bargain price
+ interesting, unique design
+ magnetic flap keeps cover closed and turns kindle on/off when opened/closed
+ protects entire kindle when closed, aside from bottom usb pottery and power button
+ front cover flipped behind to be grasped between right index and middle finger serves to keep entire kindle secure in hand (great for reading while walking or lying in bed)
+ barely adds thickness or weight

cons:
- pleather, but textured and perfectly fine
- a little bit of dried glue by magnetic clasp, but easily scraped off with fingernail

100% recommended, and i did not get reduced price or anything shady like that.
summary: excellent bargain and actually makes kindle easier to use

reviewText:
do not get me wrong. ultra makes very good power supplies. i purchased five lsp750s in 2008 - all had lifetime warranties. two went bad in 2015.
.
the problem is customer service; it is non-existent. numerous emails for warranty service go unanswered. more important, phone calls are never answered. the user is placed on "hold." after two hours, the line is disconnected. calling back will achieve the same results.
.
adding insult to injury, the company's website page prides itself on customer service. in addition, the phone recording always begins with "your call is very important to us. . . . " such claims are pure fantasies.
.
.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
.
.
update 1
.
on the ninth day of phone calling and waiting for hours, a service representative finally answered. according to the gentleman, any rma request must be referenced to an id number, which i did not have at the moment. so, i had to search my computer for the old ultra email. luckily, it was found.
.
a few more days of phone calling and hours of waiting connected to a second representative. he wanted to know the vendor's name, date of purchase, and invoice number. after 20 minutes of checking, the man said that zipzoomfly.com was not an authorized seller and no longer in business. as a result, the warranty was no good.
.
in return, i argued that company was authorized in 2008. if it were not, why did ultra give me a registration number? . . . he finally agreed with that logic.
.
the agent next tried to transfer responsibility to the company's customer service department. my response was that i already emailed the department with my request and necessary documents two weeks ago. it never responded. so, i re-emailed with similar results. . . trying to obtain warranty work from it was "an exercise in futility."
.
to shut me up, the man said that he will personally handle the case. "just email me the original invoice and a copy of the factory registration. i will contact you within 24 hours."
.
the designated time came and went. in fact, nothing arrived after a week. despite two personal emails, there were no replies.
.
as the reader can see, ultra warranties are meaningless - the company will not honor its commitments. once the firm has your money, it is gone. the customer is left with "runarounds" and silence.
.
.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
.
.
update 2
.
here is the final record. i left five emailings on the ultra customer service website. failing to get responses, i telephoned. after many days of disconnecting calls and waiting hours for someone to answer, i was able to talk to three representatives on different days. one finally took my case and promised a response within 24 hours. when no reply came, i emailed him four times. failing to get responses, i wrote a complaint to the company ceo. after waiting a week, nothing transpired.
.
the moral to the story is simple. once you purchased an ultra product, your money is gone. if the item fail, the warranty will never be honored. contrary to the stated warranty on the box, user booklet, and website page, the real company policy is to do nothing and never respond to any user request for an rma.  my experiences support this fact.
summary: try getting warranty service. it is impossible!

reviewText: i really love my pebble time steel. i am a previous owner of the original pebble steel, pebble time, apple watch, and now pebble time steel. i actually traded in my apple watch to get this one. though my apple watch was feature packed, i finally got sick and tired of having to charge it every single day. i am able to get 7 days on a charge with my pebble. this makes my life so much more convenient. i can now finally get daily sleep tracking! this was not possible with my apple watch since i had to charge it while i was sleeping. not to mention, any type of sleep tracking app would have drained the battery even worse. i am quite pleased with the app selection of the pebble store. it seems to be continually growing and adding more useful apps daily. i also love the many different watch faces you can choose from. now the color e-ink is a nice step up from the previous black/white screens but nothing to rave about. color e-ink has no comparison to the vivid colors on an apple watch, but i would still rather have the 7 day battery life anyday. the bluetooth connection is pretty solid for the most part. i might lose connection temporarily once every few days if that. what i really love about my pebble most are the new health functions that are now built in! i use these daily and am thrilled with how accurate and comprehensive they are. sleep tracking tends to be very accurate and the step/distance tracker seems to be accurate enough for my own needs. one thing that i do not like is the big black ugly bezel that is an eyesore. this looks to be just a massive amount of wasted and valuable screen space. last, but not least, the included strap is terrible. the leather strap gets dirty very easily and starts turning a nasty color within days of wearing it. i replaced my strap within the first couple of weeks and am now pleased with the overall look of my pebble. overall, i am very pleased with my pebble time steel.

this is my initial review for the tianshili bluetooth hands-free sun visor in-car speakerphone as i've only been using it a week. the device is a good size, it's approximately 3"x4" and has a metal clip to secure it to your visor. the sound quality is good. i've had no complaints of people not being able to hear me and my callers come through loud and clear. the unit does have two volume control buttons, up and down. the button, with the picture of the handset, is used to disconnect a call. the light is used as the main indicator for the unit. the light will change color or flash frequency for a number of different things, including the low power indication. the unit does have a voice indicator, so far i've only heard power on, power off, pairing indicator and paired notification.

according to the instructions this will support dual phone connection. however, i have not tried this. the instructions also state the standby time for the device is 1400 hours/60 days and will last 17-20 hours working time.

i like the performance and the look of this device. my main complaint is it does not have a battery level indicator on the unit. it only has a time to charge indicator. also per the instructions, you are supposed to keep the device away from high or low temperature environments. i live in las vegas, nv, according to my outdoor thermostat it's 118 degrees right now, so i can't leave this in my car.

reviewText:
i needed an inexpensive 2 channel amp for a console stereo rebuild i was working on and saw some good reviews of this product so i figured id give it a try.

on the positive side, the power of the amp and the sound quality are great.  for the money, i don't know that you could find a better sounding 2 channel amp in this power range for the money.  it also supports up to 2 inputs (i only needed one) and has an ac passthrough in case you need an extra outlet for some type of input device.

however, the reason for the docked stars is that the biggest feature that i liked about this unit is the auto-power feature that turns the amp off when there is no signal.  since this amp was going to be located inside of a console, it would not be easy to gain access to turn on and off.  i liked that the unit would power itself down when it was not in use.

sadly, this isn't exactly how it works.  when the auto-sensing feature is enabled (you can turn it off with a switch in the back), the amp measures the signal strength and once it reaches below a certain level, it cuts the power to the amp.  the problem is that it is way too sensitive to drops in the signal.  if you are playing a song with a quiet passage, the amp turns off in the middle of the song.  it also turns itself off in between every song.  when this happens, there is usually about a 1-2 second delay before it comes back on at the beginning of the next song, cutting off the beginning of every song you play.  in addition to this, i think that the unnecessarily high amount of times the relay has to click on and off could lead to premature failure.

since this was a primary reason for buying this particular model, i had to dock 2 stars.  i disabled the auto-sensing feature and now the amp works like you would expect it to, but i have to leave it on 24/7.  the manual does not list the power usage at idle, and while i doubt its very high, its still wasted energy.  if you are very "green" conscious, you might not want this device.

reviewText:
i purchased this lens for my sony hdr-xr550v handycam. the camera has a native 10x optical zoom (26.3mm wide angle) and a 37mm thread.

the raynox hd-5050pro seems well made. it is not heavy and it is difficult to tell whether the body is made from metal or plastic. the image quality is good and it works well for the most part. the only issue is the vignetting (see below). a note for users with the sony: the lens blocks both the flash (above the lens opening on the camera) and the ir lamp (for "nightshot" to the right and below the lens opening). so these functions are not operational with the raynox lens attached.

the rear lens in the raynox lens is slightly convex and extends beyond the threads all the way across the diameter. the manual recommends that even though the lens is 37mm native thread, that it be used with a 37 to 37 mm adapter. i've tried it with and without the adapter and there is vignetting in either case. i can't tell if the lens itself is contacting the face of the camera when i don't use the adapter or whether the threads are bottoming out.

with the 37 to 37mm adapter:
as you would expect, the vignetting is worse. the raynox lens works well over the telephoto end of the range, but there is substantial vignetting at the last 20% or so of the wide angle end of the range. the vignetting is substantially more noticeable when in the photograph mode (as opposed to the video mode).

without the 37 to 37mm adapter:
the vignetting is reduced in both modes. in the video mode, the vignetting is noticeable over the last 10% of the wide angle range. again, it is much more noticeable in the photo mode.

overall, the lens does substantially expand the wide angle capability of the sony camera, but i was expecting that the raynox would perform over the full range of the camera.

reviewText: i bought this unit based on my previous experience with apc products.  i've had excellent luck with their ups's up to this point and i decided to buy this unit for its claimed runtime and the automatic voltage regulation (avr).  i installed the powerchute software and plugged it in to charge the batteries overnight.  the next morning i plugged it in and set up my workstation pc.  the unit worked perfectly for 11 months then the "overload" light came on and the ups would not produce ac power in any outlet.  i did get power again by unplugging the battery, switching on the power (battery is "hot-swappable") waiting for the green "on-line" led to light and i plugged in the battery and all seemed well until i decided to run the powerchute software's "self-test" feature, at this point the power to my pc quit instantly.  i contacted apc by e-mail and got a response that indicated that perhaps they didn't read my message so i called their customer assistance number.  the tech i spoke to was very helpful and he "cross-shipped" me a replacement unit, i did have to pay shipping to send my defective unit back though.  i thought all would be well at this point; however, two weeks later i had the same problem!! again tech support at apc was very helpful, they "cross-shipped" another one, this time they paid the shipping back to apc of my defective (second) unit.  this is not the end unfortunately...  my third one died after only two days of "service"!!!  if i have any warranty left (i'll find out tuesday) i'll take the fourth one and sell it on ebay!  i'm not going to even attempt to use another one of these, it's a real shame because their software (powerchute personal edition) works so nicely and their customer service people are genuinely helpful.  a friend of mine suggested that i must have a power  problem at my house, all i could say to that is "i thought that's what i bought it for!"  i actually don't have a wiring fault and my voltage varies by only about plus or minus 4 volts from 120 volts.  i just don't think this unit is a reliable back-up power source-find another device!!  the problems i've had with the second and third ups's are identical to the first one and powerchute software indicated that i could still attach more equipment to this device.  my inexpensive es500 from apc is more reliable than this expensive model, i admit it does not have anywhere near the capacity of the bx1000 but at least it works!  i'm going to shop other brands this time... i'm more than a little gun-shy!
summary: high expectations, big disappointment!!  don't buy this one!!

i think at this point i've reviewed every startech kvm that is available on vines.  i am being really hard and please read before taking my 3 starts as an insult to it.  the problem i have with it is that it's just two ports and tha'ts not enough.  with windows 10 i use wireless mode and we bought a bunch of smart tvs that let us, but we still have quite a few monitors and investments in them. so starting with the biggest and working to the smaller ones i tried each.

by now, i know the installation with my eyes closed.  just remember the type of switch you're using, i don't have a huge need for the ps2 features although our main domain controller at the house is a few years old and i'm too lazy to install more usb and sata ports.  if you have older equipment or just a small amount of items you need, it's splendid.

first, it's light. it's very light and size wize it's tiny as far as kvm's with box form factor go. it's extremely light.  the transfer rates are excellent, i've had to tighten things once just b/c i was lazy but this isn't startech's fauilt at all.  i can't mention the monitors or the audio system but the monitors were all top of the line when i bought them and the speakers are among the best you can buy for pro-sumer purposes.  usb works well although another few ports would have been nice.

ok, so here's my only issue.  most people don't need kvm switches these days and if they do, they need more ports.  for the price, you are getting a steal.  it's easy to set up. this isn't even something that you really need to read the manual with and the first one, (can't mention model but their largest one) would have been hard to setup were it not for reading the instructions first.  yes, i'm a data scientist with over 15 primary computers in my house, and a good 50 by the time i'm done including peripherals like those really awesome led bulbs beginning with an h (if you don't own those, do yourself a favor and deck your house out in them or buy them for holiday presents, they are must have items) and in spite of that i'm complaining about trivial matters that could be solved by reading the manual on a different version of the item.

on this one, it'll take you longer to unpack then it will to set up. it is intuitive to a fault, easy and quick to use and i swear, i never really knew of startech until vines introduced me to them, but i have a tremendous amount of respect for the company.

everything you need is included unless but just know what you're getting.  this isn't bleeding edge kvm equipment. it's rock solid stuff for legacy or older devices and it is a tremendous value and rock solid.  just do your homework like you would with anything so you know what you're getting into.
summary: my 3 star rating is too harsh, i'd gladly recommend this to anyone.

 these would probably work best if you're in your own small area. the sound degrades, the louder you turn it up. the speakers have a cute design and an ok battery life but i am just not satisfied with this set, with all of the variety that is currently out there. they are not wireless speakers, they are external speakers that have to be charged individually. the way the speakers are set up, i would maybe use this for a couple weeks and then switch to something more convenient.

reviewText:
this is my review of the 3 pack - cat5e 15ft networking rj45 ethernet patch cable from cables direct online.

i wanted to get my printer out from under my desk and on a nearby filing cabinet so i needed something longer than my current 6ft patch cable and felt 15ft would be enough and since i might want to move other things opted for a 3-pack.

so the cables were safely shipped individually wrapped in vinyl bag protected by air pockets in a box.

upon opening the cable pack i noted how thin/flexible the shielding was at which point i went back to the packaging and saw that these are utp cables (unshielded twisted pair) so it wasn't that the shielding was thin its non-existent. this means i just have to be a bit more mindful to avoid routing the cables around anything with significant emi such as power bricks/transformers and/or some speakers.

i liked that the connectors have protective tabs over the connecting tabs, it helps with orienting the cables which sometimes has to be done blindly, made removing them much easier as i just had to locate the large plastic tab as opposed to the small tab that i normally depress with a fingertip/fingernail. so after moving my printer and verifying no issues i am confident these cables will work for me on my gigabit network.

while the product description mentions these adhere to the eia/tia-568b category 5e compliance standards, i would like to see a note added explaining that these are unshielded to reduce confusion.

i recommend these cables to anyone that needs unshielded patch cables of these length.

i received these at a discount for fair and unbiased review.
summary: great unshielded twisted pair patch cables for my gigabit network!

reviewText: i was looking for a bag that would be big enough to carry my nikon d300, 18-200, 70-300, 28-70 and 17-35 lenses.  not to mention assorted filters, batteries, flash cards, etc.  i thought, after doing quite a bit of research, that this bag would suffice.  and i suppose it might, if you carefully tucked everything away in the bag and never actually tried to get at anything.  sure, the bag will hold a bunch of 'skinny' lenses (problems stuffing in my 17-35), but those lenses are buried under layers of padding velcroed in such a way that makes all but the exposed camera and attached lens readily accessible.  for example, the camera and attached lens has to sit on the 'second tier' of padding in order to use the 'lens gate'.  under the body, totally hidden, might be another lens.  another problem with the body and lens sitting high up, is that the bag's center of gravity is higher up and more prone to dump out your gear.  and speaking of velcro, trying to rearrange the pads is sort of like herding cats.  another problem are the storage spaces- there simply aren't enough zippered compartments to hold loose items.  the front compartment is less of a pouch and more of a sleeve.  the side pockets only velcro shut, good luck if it rains.  and inside the top lid?  great for storing pieces of paper, that's about it.  the bag comes down to personal preference.  i misfired by choosing this one.

while the first few images developed just fine, the 4th and 5th images developed with a blob at the top where the developer in the picture's built-in envelope just ran out, leaving a section at the top of the image where it was exposed but not developed. it's easy to spot the manufacturing defect here and i can only hope that the impossible project takes a look at their developer formula and can reconfigure it to be the correct amount of chemical.

reviewText:
***this device is almost identical to the foscam fi8098w, but this is the cheap chinese knock-off version.***

the camera takes very low quality pictures and movies, it does not take hd videos (480p, 720p, 1080i). it's basically an 8mp camera with a wireless adapter. it has very low resolution settings - the maximum resolution is 640x800. this camera does not have an optical zoom or digital zoom feature. this camera does not have an auto-focus feature. the camera does have a built-in microphone, and a speaker so you can use it as a 2-way radio or baby monitor.

the manufacturer says this camera does up to 30 frames per second, but i found out that is only while using the lowest resolution setting. when you increase the resolution the video begins to lag and is very choppy. so you have to choose between having 'a blurry image with smooth video' -- or 'a sharper image with choppy video'.

this camera does have ir beams for night vision -- it actually takes better images and video during the night than during the day. however, there is no option to turn off the night vision, so it stays on even when there is light in the room -- this reduces the quality and color of the images, and makes it difficult when adjusting the brightness and contrast.

___unpacking this device:___

the manufacturer did include:
-an ethernet cable
-a wireless antenna
-a camera mount/bracket
-a few small mounting screws

they also included a 5v power adapter..but it was a chinese wall plug!...ugh. i live in america so obviously, the adapter wouldn't work for me. the 5v adapters we have in america won't plug into the camera, so i had to splice the manufacturers adapter and solder their cord onto an american adapter. that worked fine.

***the manufacturer did not include any drivers or software, i had to find these items online.***

___configuring this device: ___

i've spent the last 24 hours installing, configuring and testing this device, with very little help from the manufacturer. that's because the instruction manual is 100% chinese! the support website is also 100% chinese!! i don't speak or read chinese, so i was dumbfounded once i opened the box. i did a google search, and found an english manual online then i was ok from there.

so once i found the english manual, made an american adapter, and found the drivers and software online - i was ready to begin configuring the device. so i then:
-powered the camera on
-plugged the camera into my router
-used the search utility to find the camera
-added the camera onto my wireless network
-and then set the camera's ip address.

i was finally able to view the camera by putting the camera's ip address into my web browser. but i cannot view the camera outside of my local network. i'm still trying to figure out how to setup remote viewing without exposing my entire home network. since the manufacturer doesn't provide instructions for this, it will be an uphill battle.

at the end of the day, it really wasn't worth going through all that trouble.. i saved about $20 on the camera, and $10 on the adapter. next time i will gladly spend an extra $30 to get a higher quality camera, an american adapter and at least an american instruction manual and support website.

i would not recommend this item to anyone in america.

thanks,
c. cole phd
summary: not high quality, just a wireless 8mp webcam

reviewText:
some of the best computer monitors i have ever used were viewsonic monitors so i was very interested in trying out the viewsonic pjd5232l projector and seeing if the company is also capable of making good projection equipment. i have an excellent proving ground  the sanctuary of a small church with a retractable screen as well as  access to the computer there, which is the kind of environment where one might use this kind of projector. so far i have been very pleased though i have not used this projector very long at all.

first things first  i was a little surprised at how light this projector is. i expected to be a bit heavier and therefore harder to manage when moving it or mounting it somewhere. the lighter weight means that mounting it from a ceiling-suspended rack or on a wall shelf requires less anchoring and reinforcement right out of the box. this is a very good thing.

this particular projector supports inputs from two computers as well as s-video and composite plugs. what is missing is newer input standards like hdmi. this means that this is the wrong projector if you are using it with a system that does not support the older inputs unless you use an adapter. this may or may not be a big deal depending on the specific setup but it does mean that with the most modern computers it probably will not connect right out of the box. keep this in mind.

the resolution is 1024x768 which is not considered high-definition  by todays measure but it is fine for putting presentations up or for watching a movie. to move up to a higher resolution will cost a lot more. the color and clarity of images this projector puts out are excellent. i have used other projectors where the colors diffuse into drab or washed-out hues but this projector seems to suffer less from that than some of the others.

one of the great aggravations that has bothered me about projectors is the short range and uselessness of the remote that come with them. a remote control is not helpful if it requires being a foot away from the projector to work. this remote is better, giving better range than some that i have used in the past, and it is also fairly self-explanatory. now with that said, it would have been nice to have better documentation with it.

overall, this is a very nice projector and viewsonic has done a nice job with it. it projects bright, colorful images and it is very lightweight which makes mounting easy. my main complaints are the lack of modern input options (and no adapters) and sub-par documentation; otherwise, this is a 5-star projector worth its asking price.

i was in need of a pair of headphones for some vo i was recording with a tascam hd-p2
  while searching at usual suspects sony $99 blue mofi $350, i saw these on sale at $12.99. i figured if anything i can use these in the field if they at least work.  when they arrived i did a test and they sound great!  the voice tone and level are decent.  i read some reviews that these don't last to long but i just got them so we'll see.  my second test was playing hall & oates song "man eater". i played the song off an iphone 5 and compared the th02, a pair of bose in ear head phones and a jambox.  that's when i heared the difference.  the bose and jambox both were crisp and you could hear the subtle reverb on the instruments.  the th02 you can't.
so for checking mic placement and if sound is getting to your equipment you can't go wrong with the th02....
but if your need is to mix an album or do fine audio adjustments, get a better pair of headphones and use these for the "car" tests.
summary: good for checking sound, not good for fine adjustment.

reviewText:
i don't doubt that this monster brand unit is probably the best built of all the brands of fm transmitters, but i did notice that it cuts off the high end significantly. i have a portable device with a built-in eq, and even with the top end boosted all the way it didn't sound quite right. it reduces the overall sound quality to fm quality (or less) and i noticed occasional chuffing noise in the background during quiet songs. the transmitted music is quieter than real fm broadcasts, which is true of all fm transmitters - they really should build in a small line-level amplifier to these things, it wouldn't be that hard to do. on the upside, the transmitter never "lost" the signal.

in summary, this is a good cheap temporary solution if you don't have any other recourse, like if you're going on a long trip (maybe in a rental car) and don't want to be driven crazy by bad fm programming, but it's not at all equivalent to a basic line level radio input.

reviewText:
for a stereo pair of computer speakers, these aren't too bad (which is rarely the case with bose, but we won't let my opinion of the company get in the way with my opinion of the product).  they do indeed sound quite decent for a fairly small set of computer speakers.  bass is present, unlike most small speakers, and they have a reasonably full sound.
they also have a nifty feature that some people might put to great use - they have 2 audio inputs, and can actually mix them together (and you can control the volume levels of both of them), which is as far as i know, a unique feature to computer speakers.  this is nifty because you could do something like run your tv's audio output into them while having the computer plugged into them too, so you get somewhat better sound than cheap tv speakers and can still hear the sound from the computer.
the problem is for the price, you can get significantly better sound with some monsoons or other similar computer speakers, which not only sound a bit better in the mids and treble, they also include small subwoofers that handle bass better than the mediamates.
overall, these aren't a great deal for most people, but if you are looking for a powered stereo pair of speakers and plan on using the mixer feature, they are your only choice.  if you don't plan on using the mixer feature, i reccomend you compare them to other speakers in the price range, especially if you have the room for a small subwoofer.
summary: overpriced, but some will find good use in them

reviewText:
i bought this hdmi switch as an addition (not a replacement)  to the one pictured, which i purchased in april 2009. this older one still works fine, and so i was displeased to receive the new one, to find it has a different configuration: one of the five  "in"  ports is on the front of the unit, rather than in the rear along with the other 4 ports,  the hdmi "out"  and the power adapter plug.

this redesign reduces the width of the unit, which may actually be a plus for some buyers (its not for me). but its not the one shown in the ad, and i don't like the 5th port sticking out of the front. this unit is actually about 6" wide;  the old unit was about 8.75" wide.

the indicator lights on this one are bright enough to guide planes landing at jfk (why this ridiculous brightness on a device thats probably going to used in a darkened room?).

the new remote is quite similar to the one pictured. i've never much liked it, as its so small that  its easy to get lost (i once almost threw it out with the sunday paper). anyway, i've  taped a "handle" to it, extending its length somewhat). but of course some folks might like a remote this size (1.5" by 3 1/8")

finally, no where in the box or on the device or in the poorly written instructions is the name of the manufacturer shown, nor is there any information about the warranty, or who to contact for tech support.  not a good sign.

if this device were much cheaper than other 5 port switches, i'd acknowlege a trade-off. but its not--there are others in the same price range. i'm giving it 2 stars because i have owned another switch (apparently) by the same manufacturer and its operated fine for almost 3 years.

but caveat emptor for sure.
summary: product does not match ad - no warranty info

i had a 30+ year old sony "boom box" model cfs-209 that finally crapped out after schlepping it hundreds of times to the beach in florida over the years.  now that was a great quality sony...substantial case, real bass, every button labeled, wonderful sound and quality.  and not much bigger than the new one.

now i needed a replacement to listen to cassettes of my now deceased mother playing the organ, and reciting scriptures.  as well, i was a professional "pop" organist and made a lot of different tapes since the 70's.  i bought this because it is a sony.  unfortunately, it does not come up to the quality or sound of the old one.  the plastic case is light and flimsy, cassette buttons not labeled, the handle is hollow plastic, the volume is button controlled, so when you push them, you push the unit away from you...and i couldn't hear much of a change with bass reflex on.  the sound is "tinny", but everything works.  i think the price is a bit too much for this kind of quality.  the batteries did not come with it.  after several attempts at tuning the fm, i've decided to return it.  when tunred off, it does not remember last station, but returns to 87.5, and you have to go through the laborious task of searching and stopping at every strong signal to get to the one you want.  you can set presets, but there are not enough.  too bad.  i'm going to purchase an emerson at 2/3 the cost, that at least has labels and a tuning wheel.

i've been pleased with the casecrown cases for the various kindles i own, so decided to get this one for my ipad air 2.  it's well made, and fits the ipad very nicely.  i had a little trouble with the little flap that needs to fold under the ipad (after it's been inserted) and then be attached to the bottom with velcro -- but with a bit of trial and error i got it in snugly, and have had no problem since.

it's nearly perfect for my daily use, and i have only two minor criticisms.
(1)  the case looks a little askew, as if the pieces weren't cut exactly right.  makes finding the power button a teeny bit more work. but it's a minor defect.  no other problems with the various ports and buttons, they're all easily accessible.
(2)  the triangle "stand" position i make with the front folded back and pushed into a little flap on the back, requires a little fiddling, and doesn't always sit quite right.  making the flap a bit wider & deeper might have helped.

finally, the wakeup/sleep function for the ipad works just fine, i've not had any problems with it.

unless you're willing to pay up a lot more (i wasn't), this is a very fine option.
summary: very nice option for an ipad air 2, at a reasonable price
